ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER NO. 2025-4
 
ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER AMENDING THE OGDEN CITY EMPLOYEE POLICIES AND PROCEDURES
MANUAL.
 
   WHEREAS, the Ogden City desires to amend Section 4-10 Military Leave, of the
Employee Policies and Procedures Manual to provide more flexibility in the use
of military leave.
 
   NOW, THEREFORE, I, Benjamin K. Nadolski, Mayor of Ogden, as Chief Executive
Officer and pursuant to the authority granted me by Section 2-6-1 of the Ogden
Municipal Code, and pursuant to the procedures outlined in Ogden City
Administrative Policy No. 1702, hereby order that the Ogden City Employee
Policies and Procedures Manual be amended as follows:
   SECTION 1.   Section amended. Section 4-10 of the Ogden City Employee
Policies and Procedures Manual is hereby amended to read and provide as
follows:
4-10: MILITARY LEAVE:
 
A.   Authorized Employees: Military leave[s of absence] may be approved for
[full time]full-time employees, as provided herein.
 
B.   [Time Allowed]Paid Military Leave: Eligible employees who are members of a
reserve unit of any branch of the armed forces may[, on presentation of a copy
of official travel orders to the Human Resources Office, take] use available
military leave with pay for attendance at a scheduled[,] military assignment,
including training. [annual two (2) week training assignment up to fifteen (15)
consecutive calendar days including holidays. Only one period of paid military
leave shall be allowed during the fiscal year. Employees may request use of
available vacation leave, compensatory time or unpaid time off for any
additional reserve duty or training. Employees on military leave shall receive
only the base rate of pay for the respective position.] Eligible employees will
be provisionally credited 120 hours (168 for Sworn Fire) of paid military leave
each fiscal year to attend required military assignments. Paid military leave
may only be taken when a military assignment conflicts with the employee’s
regular work schedule. Employees on paid military leave shall receive pay at
their current rate for their current position, with a maximum of 40 hours per
week (max of 56 per week for sworn fire). Paid military leave will be credited
each fiscal year and will only be available for use in the same fiscal year. At
the end of the fiscal year, no paid military leave will roll over into a new
fiscal year nor be available as a paid-out benefit. Time not used in the fiscal
year will be lost effective June 30th of each year. Employees may request use
of vacation leave, compensatory time, or unpaid time off for any additional
military assignments not covered by paid military leave. Previously used leave
cannot be redesignated as paid military leave or another type of leave after
the fact.
 
C.   Eligibility: Eligible Employees who are active members of any reserve unit
of any branch of the armed forces may submit proof of current military service
each fiscal year to the Human Resources Division and be provisionally credited
the allotted hours of annual paid military leave.
 
D.   Notice of Military Service: An employee receiving orders for military duty
should give notice to their supervisor as well as the Human Resources Division
as far in advance as is reasonable under the circumstances. Notice may be
verbal or written by the employee. The city may also contact an appropriate
commanding officer for clarification and/or confirmation of the employee’s
orders.
 
[C]E.Return To Work: Employees on scheduled, annual, [active duty]active-duty
[training]military assignments are required to return to work for the first
regularly scheduled shift after the end of [training]assignment, allowing
reasonable travel time.
 
[D]F. Unpaid, Long Term Military Leave: During a national emergency, eligible
employees who voluntarily enlist, who are drafted into the armed forces or who
are called into active military duty, will be granted unpaid, long term
military leave. The granting of unpaid, long term military leave shall entitle
the employee to the following:
 
1.   Reinstatement rights shall be retained in accordance with all applicable
State and Federal laws, provided reinstatement is requested within ninety (90)
calendar days of the end of military duty and the employee is honorably
discharged.
 
2.   Every reasonable effort will be made to return eligible employees to the
same or comparable position.
 
3.   Any vacation leave, sick leave, and compensatory time accrued as of the
commencement of leave will remain to the credit of the employee for use upon
return to full employment. Further accrual of vacation and sick leave will be
suspended at the commencement of [active duty]active-duty status. If requested,
accrued vacation leave and compensatory time can be disbursed during [active
duty]active-duty status.
 
4.   Although no benefits shall accrue during the period of leave, a reinstated
employee will be treated as though they were continuously employed for purposes
of determining benefits based on length of service, such as the rate of
vacation accrual, promotional considerations and job seniority rights.
 
5.   A reinstated employee shall not be subject to any introductory period.
 
6.   Long Term Military Leave employees will not be required to submit
verification of active-duty status while away on long term active duty.
However, paid military leave may be provisionally credited to the employee with
Department Executive Director approval and used as set forth in this section.
 
[E]G.    Working During Leave: No employee on military leave shall work his or
her own, or another Ogden City employee's, job for any kind of compensation
[;]. [provided, that if an employee is serving locally and is available for
City work during the leave period, the applicable department director or
division manager may authorize City work with a corresponding reduction in the
military leave.] Once active duty has been completed, the employee may return
to work. 
 
DATED this 25th day of August 2025.
 
 
                                        /s/ Benjamin K. Nadolski            
         Benjamin K. Nadolski, Mayor
ATTEST:
/s/ Tracy Hansen         
Tracy Hansen, City Recorder
 
 
APPROVED AS TO FORM: /s/ AMB   08/25/25
          Legal Date      
 
 
ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER NO. 2025-7
 
ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER AMENDING THE OGDEN CITY PERSONNEL POLICIES AND PROCEDURES
MANUAL.
 
   WHEREAS, the Ogden City personnel policy manual requires amendments to
Section 4-1; Holiday Leave; Paid Time Off.
 
   NOW, THEREFORE, I, Benjamin K. Nadolski, Mayor of Ogden, as Chief Executive
Officer and pursuant to the authority granted me by Section 2-6-1 of the Ogden
Municipal Code, and pursuant to the procedures outlined in Ogden City
Administrative Policy No. 1702, hereby order that the Ogden City Personnel
Policies and Procedures Manual be amended as follows:
   SECTION 1.   Section amended. Section 4.1 of the Ogden City Personnel
Policies and Procedures Manual is hereby amended to read and provide as
follows:
4-1: [HOLIDAY LEAVE; PAID TIME OFF:]
   
A.      [Eligible Employees:] The [City]city provides paid time off or
additional compensation, as provided in the holiday pay policy, to all eligible
employees for holidays designated by the [City]city. Employees in the following
employment classification(s) are eligible for this benefit:
      
1.      Full time employees.
      
2.      Nonmerit, special employees.
      
3.      Introductory employees in the above classifications.
   
B.      [Holidays Designated:] The holidays designated by the [City]city for
this benefit are:
 
 
Holiday                        Calendar Date
New Year's Day                 January 1
Martin Luther King, Jr. Day    Third Monday in January
Presidents' Day                Third Monday in February
Arbor Day                      Personal preference day (see vacation policy)
Memorial Day                   Last Monday in May
Junteenth National Freedom Day June 19 if a Monday (see subsection D)
Independence Day               July 4
Pioneer Day                    July 24
Labor Day                      First Monday in September
Veterans Day                   November 11
Thanksgiving Day               Fourth Thursday in November
Day after Thanksgiving         Fourth Friday in November
Christmas Day                  December 25
 
   
C.      [When Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve fall on a Monday, Tuesday,
Wednesday or Thursday, city offices will close at 1:00 p.m. Merit employees and
non-sworn merit employees in the police and fire departments will receive up to
four (4) hours of holiday pay per the holiday pay policy according to the
employee's normal work schedule on that day (e.g., two and a half (2.5) hours
of holiday pay if the employee normally works until 3:30 p.m. on that day; four
(4) hours of holiday pay if the employee normally works until 5:00 p.m. on that
day.) This subsection 4-1.C does not apply when the CAO or department director
determines that coverage is required to meet the needs of the department, or to
provide emergency services.] When Christmas Eve or New Year’s Eve falls on a
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday, City offices may close at 12:00 p.m.
Merit employees, including non-sworn merit employees in the Police and Fire
Departments, may receive up to four hours of administrative pay, based on the
employee’s normal work schedule for that day (e.g., an employee who normally
works until 3:30 p.m. will receive two and a half hours of administrative pay,
and an employee who normally works until 5:00 p.m. will receive four hours of
administrative pay).
 
Closing City offices on these dates is done as a convenience to the city and is
not guaranteed from year to year. Accordingly, this administrative pay is not
considered holiday pay and will not be included in the designated holiday
schedule in Chapter 4.
 
Subsection 4-1.C does not apply when the CAO or an executive director
determines that staffing is required to meet operational needs or to provide
emergency services.
   
D.      When June 19 falls on a Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, or Friday,
Juneteenth will be observed on the immediately preceding Monday. When June 19
falls on a Saturday or Sunday, Juneteenth will be observed on the immediately
following Monday.
   
E.      [Saturdays [And]and Sundays:] For purposes of paid time off, a holiday
that falls on a Saturday is observed on the preceding Friday and a holiday that
falls on a Sunday is observed on the following Monday. (Notwithstanding the
above, holiday pay will be based on the actual holiday for "employees working
shift work", as provided in the holiday pay policy section.)
   
F.      [Equivalent Hours:] Paid time off or additional compensation for
holidays is provided to all eligible employees immediately upon assignment to
an eligible employment classification. For all eligible employees, except sworn
fire personnel working [twenty four (24)]24 hour shifts, a holiday is
equivalent to eight [(8)] hours of regularly scheduled work.
   
G.      [Calculation:] Paid time off is calculated based on the employee's base
pay rate at the time of the holiday and does not include any special forms of
compensation, such as incentives, commissions or bonuses. Paid time off for
holidays is not considered hours worked for the purposes of calculating
overtime (notwithstanding the above, holiday time off may be considered hours
worked as provided in the holiday pay section).
   
H.      [Sworn Fire Personnel:] Sworn fire personnel working [twenty four
(24)]24 hour shifts are compensated for working holidays at their regular rate
of pay, as if the day were not a holiday. In lieu of holiday pay, these
employees receive additional paid time off by accruing six [(6)] hours of
holiday leave each pay period to be utilized as additional vacation leave
(which includes benefit for Arbor Day). The provision of such additional paid
time off for holidays shall be prorated to adjust for any changes during the
year from, or to, shift work assignments.
   
I.      [Paid Absences:] If a designated holiday falls during an eligible
employee's paid absence (i.e., vacation or sick leave), holiday paid time off
will still be granted for the applicable holiday, rather than vacation or sick
leave.
   
J.      [Unpaid Absences; Eligible Employees:] Applicable to merit, non-merit,
and sworn police employees, if a designated holiday falls during an eligible
employee's unpaid absence, holiday paid time off will still be granted for the
applicable holiday unless the employee does not work any hours within the pay
period which includes the holiday.
   
K.      [Personal Preference Day:] As indicated in the schedule above, eligible
employees will receive one additional vacation day in each calendar year in
lieu of Arbor Day. To be eligible, employees must be employed to work in the
pay period during which Arbor Day occurs. (See vacation benefits policy in this
manual.)
   
L.      [Shift Work; Work Required:] See [section]Section 5-5 [of this manual]
regarding holiday pay for employees working shift work and other employees
required to work on a holiday.
 
DATED this 17th day of December, 2025.
                                        /s/ Benjamin K. Nadolski            
         Benjamin K. Nadolski, Mayor
ATTEST:
/s/ Tracy Hansen         
City Recorder

CHAPTER 1
GENERAL EMPLOYMENT POLICIES
SECTION:
1-1: Title Changes
1-2: Nature Of Employment
1-3: Professional Goals And Standards
1-4: Employee Relations
1-5: Equal Employment Opportunity
1-6: Residency And Commuting Requirements
1-7: Hiring Of Relatives; Personal Conflicts
1-8: Employee Medical Information And Examinations
1-9: Immigration Law Compliance
1-10: Conflicts Of Interest
1-11: Acceptance Of Gifts
1-12: Outside Employment
1-13: Hiring Authority And Placement
1-14: Nondisclosure
1-1: TITLE CHANGES:
Effective upon passage of the FY25 budget, dated August 6, 2024, every
reference in this policy manual to a division manager or a manager of a
specified division, shall hereafter mean a division director or director of the
specified division. Every reference in this policy manual to a department
director or a director of a specified department shall hereafter mean a
department executive director or an executive director of the specified
department. (Adm. Order 2024-7, 11-19-2024)
1-2: NATURE OF EMPLOYMENT:
   A.   Voluntary: Employment with the city is voluntarily entered into and the
employee is free to resign at will at any time. Similarly, the city may
terminate the employment relationship at will at any time, subject to
applicable laws and adopted policies and procedures. The city can terminate the
employment relationship under certain conditions related to cause or financial
necessity. Moreover, the city reserves the right to terminate an employee
subject only to the notice and grievance rights of certain employees as
described in this manual.
   B.   Policy Intent: Policies set forth in this manual are not intended to
create a contract, nor are they to be construed to constitute contractual
obligations of any kind or a contract of employment between the city and any of
its employees. The provisions of the manual have been developed at the
discretion of the administration of the city and may be amended or canceled at
any time, at the city's sole discretion, subject to the requirements of
federal, state or local law. Employees are encouraged to ask questions, raise
issues and voice concerns about any condition of their employment without fear
of reprisal.
   C.   Existing Policies: These provisions supersede all existing policies and
practices and may not be amended or added to without the express written
approval of the mayor. (Adm. Order 2015-3, 6-2-2015; Adm. Order 2024-7, 11-19-
2024)
1-3: PROFESSIONAL GOALS AND STANDARDS:
   A.   Public Service: Ogden City was incorporated in February 1851. Its
history and traditions serve as the foundations of strength, integrity, and
professionalism for all our employees. It is in this background and setting
that we strive to provide continued excellence in public service to our patrons
and the community.
   B.   Recognition: The city has a strong desire to recognize people as
individuals who have individual needs and desires. This recognition is best
observed when we treat each other and the public whom we are called to serve
with respect and interact with one another in a spirit of good faith and
cooperation.
   C.   Defined Guidelines: The city believes that employees function in a more
efficient and effective manner when they have clearly defined guidelines in
which to work and appropriate objectives and standards to achieve in the
performance of their duties.
   D.   Off Duty Conduct: Employees represent the city both on and off duty
through their behaviors and interactions while engaged in work activity, as
well as their conduct off work which reflects on the city's public mission and
the public interest. As stated elsewhere in this manual, there are certain
standards regarding off duty conduct which employees are expected to uphold.
Employees reflect the city's interest and efforts in providing service to the
public to protect people's well-being, their property, and their lives.
   E.   Community and Civic Affairs: It is the intent of the city to encourage
employees to be involved in community and civic affairs, and to be an active,
successful part of our community. Moreover, the city expects all employees to
meet its standards of professional work and service in a manner which reflects
integrity, honesty, openness, and a sense of interest and attention to their
jobs and work functions.
   F.   Volunteer Work: Notwithstanding the above, employees are not to perform
volunteer work for the city in such a manner that would deprive them of
otherwise legitimate compensation. The city desires to reward and compensate
all employees based on the city's pay plan and equivalent values for their
work. (Adm. Order 2015-3, 6-2-2015; Adm. Order 2024-7, 11-19-2024)
1-4: EMPLOYEE RELATIONS:
   A.   Conditions; Compensation: The city believes that the work conditions,
wages, and benefits it offers to its employees are competitive with those
offered in this area in public employment. If employees have concerns about
work conditions or compensation, they are strongly encouraged to voice these
concerns openly and directly to their supervisors in a spirit of respect and
cooperation.
   B.   Dealing with Supervisors: Our experience has shown that when employees
deal openly, respectfully, and directly with supervisors, in a spirit of good
faith, the work environment can be excellent, communications can be clear, and
attitudes can be positive. We believe that the city amply demonstrates its
commitment to employees by responding effectively to employee concerns.
   C.   Interaction: It is the intent of the city to encourage an open, good
faith, respectful manner of interaction when employees deal with each other
within the work environment.
   D.   Personal Behavior: The city believes that, as a matter of public
mission, each employee represents the city in their work setting, as well as
when away from work, when attending to, or acting in connection with, city
business. Likewise, how each employee acts in their personal life can affect
the best interests of the city, in its public mission role, as the employee's
behaviors are perceived to have an effect or impact on the city's role to
provide for the safety and security of the public's lives, property, and best
interests.
   E.   Employee Participation: Under certain conditions and within certain
parameters, it is the policy of the city to encourage employees' involvement
and participation in a variety of activities and programs which promote a high
level of morale and an increased spirit of teamwork within and between
departments. This participation provides an employee or employees with
opportunities for input into policy and decision making, feedback on current
systems, communication to all levels of the organization, expression of
creativity, increased personal growth and the development of new interests. In
addition, this employee participation encourages increased interaction between
employees, thus improving working relationships and the sense of belonging. In
furtherance of this policy, however, the following guidelines should be
followed:
      1.   The city prohibits employees from volunteering their work and
service which stem from their normal job functions, in order to comply with
federal and state laws governing the proper and timely payment of compensation
and overtime earned within their employment.
      2.   It is the intent of the city that employees' participation in off
duty, city related activities, organizations, and programs occur in a manner
which is safe and protective of their own and others' health and the best
interests of our community. The city reserves the right to withhold its support
and encouragement of any activity, group, or event whenever the safety or
health of its employees or the public may be placed at unnecessary or
unwarranted risk. (Adm. Order 2015-3, 6-2-2015; Adm. Order 2024-7, 11-19-2024)
1-5: EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY:
   A.   Statement: In order to provide equal employment and advancement
opportunities to all individuals, employment decisions at the city will be
based on merit, qualifications, and abilities. The city does not discriminate
in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, religion,
sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability,
genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law. The city has
an affirmative action plan that it follows to actively recruit, hire, train,
and promote individuals in a protected group.
   B.   Disabilities; Accommodations: The city will make reasonable
accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities unless doing
so would result in an undue hardship on the city. This policy governs all
aspects of employment, including selection, job assignment, compensation,
discipline, termination, and access to benefits and training.
   C.   Veterans' Preference: The city adheres to applicable federal and state
law regarding veterans' preference criteria when making decisions with respect
to initial, new hires. It is city policy that veterans' preference does not
apply to promotional opportunities. Applicants for initial employment with the
city shall be required to provide reasonable documentation and records of
verification as proof of any claimed veterans' preference. For example, such
documentation may include, but not be limited to, a form DD-214, or equivalent
discharge or other official record from the armed services of the United
States.
   D.   Job Description; Duty Rosters: The city develops job descriptions, duty
rosters and other guidelines for each employee's job. These shall be used in
determining whether an employee meets the qualifications and standards of
performance on which decisions of initial employment or continued employment
conditions are based. Job site evaluations and other evaluative and analytical
processes and procedures may be used in addition to other written documents
pertaining to job duties in order to better assist employees, supervisors, and
appropriate professionals in determining job duties and work demands.
   E.   Questions; Concerns: Employees with questions or concerns about any
types of discrimination in the workplace are encouraged to bring these issues
to the attention of their immediate supervisor, division director, or the human
resources office. Employees can raise concerns and make reports without fear of
reprisal. Anyone found to be engaging in any type of unlawful discrimination
will be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of
employment. (Adm. Order 2015-3, 6-2-2015; Adm. Order 2024-7, 11-19-2024)
1-6: RESIDENCY AND COMMUTING REQUIREMENTS:
While the city provides equal opportunity to all individuals applying for
employment, it also requires as a condition of employment that employees in
certain identified jobs or positions reside within the city or within a
required commuting time or distance from their place of employment. Employees
subject to the following residency requirements are required to maintain a
record of ongoing residency with the human resources office:
   A.   Commuting Requirement: Those positions requiring the employee's place
of residence to be within a designated commuting time or distance from their
place of employment shall be those positions for which it has been determined
that the job functions, duties, or tasks place urgent or emergency demands of
attention or service upon the completion of work assignment(s).
      1.   Identified positions for such requirements include, but are not
limited to, division directors, sworn police officers, sworn firefighters,
emergency medical technicians and employees receiving on call pay. Other
positions for which such a requirement may be imposed shall be identified upon
the recommendation of the applicable department executive director and with
review and approval by the chief administrative officer.
      2.   For purpose of this policy, department executive directors shall
establish the applicable time or distance requirements which will provide
adequate work response times. Notwithstanding the above, the commuting time or
distance requirement for division directors shall be within a reasonable amount
of time no longer than 45 minutes. Department executive directors shall
establish reasonable time limits within which new employees or employees in
newly identified positions in their respective departments must comply with the
terms of this policy. Employees who do not meet these requirements shall be
subject to termination.
   B.   Department Executive Directors: Department executive directors are
required to live within the city limits. However, this policy will only be
applied to those who already reside outside of the city at such time as the
employee moves from their current residence. As a condition of employment with
Ogden City, department executive directors who move while employed in these
positions must move to reside within the city's political boundaries that are
established by code and ordinance. These employees who move are required to
maintain a record with the city of ongoing residency with the human resources
office. (Adm. Order 2015-3, 6-2-2015; Adm. Order 2024-7, 11-19-2024)
1-7: HIRING OF RELATIVES; PERSONAL CONFLICTS:
The employment of relatives in the same organization or in the same area of an
organization may cause serious conflicts and problems with favoritism and
employee morale. In addition to claims of partiality in treatment at work,
personal conflicts from outside the work environment can be carried into day-
to-day working relationships.
   A.   Hiring of Relatives:
      1.   With respect to the employment of relatives, state law prohibits the
hiring of relatives under certain circumstances. Utah Code Annotated Title 52
Chapter 3. The city has adopted an ordinance which implements the minimum
requirements of state law and also adopts additional rules, beyond the minimum
requirements of state law, regarding the hiring of relatives. (See city code
Section
2-6-15.)
      2.   In addition to the minimum requirements of state law, it is
unlawful, under city ordinance, for the mayor, chief administrative officer, or
a department executive director to knowingly appoint any prospective officer or
employee, who is a relative of the mayor or chief administrative officer, to a
position of employment within the city, or for a department executive director
to knowingly appoint any prospective officer or employee who is a relative of
the department executive director to a position of employment within that
executive director's department. It is also unlawful for the mayor, chief
administrative officer, or a department executive director to knowingly appoint
any prospective officer or employee to a position of employment within the city
when the officer or employee will be directly supervised by a relative.
      3.   "Relative", for purposes of the ordinance prohibitions, means a
father, mother, husband, wife, son, daughter, sister, brother, uncle, aunt,
niece, nephew, first cousin, mother-in-law, father-in-law, brother-in-law,
sister-in-law, son-in-law, daughter-in-law, grandparent, grandchild, half-
brother or half-sister to the prospective officer or employee. Relative, for
purposes of the additional policies or restrictions adopted under this city
policy, shall also include stepchildren, stepsiblings, or stepparents.
      4.   “Subordinate”, for the purposes of this policy, is defined as any
employee who occupies a position that is lower in the organizational hierarchy
than a supervisor, regardless of whether the supervisor directly manages the
employee.
      5.   Applicants for employment, promotions, and transfers shall be
required to disclose any familial relationships with other employees of the
city. It shall be grounds for immediate discharge if such applicant willfully
withholds or gives false information regarding such familial relationships.
   6.   Employees should also understand that violations of state laws and city
ordinances regarding nepotism are misdemeanors. Employees with questions about
the provisions of state law or city ordinance, and the provisions of this
policy, may contact their department executive director or the human resources
office of the city.
   B.   Relatives within Division:
      1.   Effective July 1, 2006, it is a violation of city policy for any two
relatives to be assigned to work in: a) the same bureau or squad within the
police department; b) the same 24-hour shift within the fire department; or c)
the same division within any other city department, except as provided for in
Subsection B2.
      2.   Unless there otherwise exists a personal conflict as described in
subsection C, the following exceptions apply:
         a.   Relatives may be assigned to work in the same division if they
are assigned to different operating units within that division, e.g., streets
and solid waste within the division of public works/operations, and no
supervisory relationship exists between the employees.
         b.   Relatives may be assigned to work as school crossing guards in
different locations. When necessary to meet staffing needs, related crossing
guards may work at the same location.
         c.   Relatives may be assigned to work occasional extra duty periods
of two to 24 hours to meet the staffing needs of the fire department. These
assignments shall be voluntary and not part of an employee's permanent shift
assignment. The shift commander during that period of time shall not assign the
relatives to the same station and/or crew.
         d.   Assignments pursuant to Subsection B2 require prior written
approval by the department executive director.
      3.   Relatives found to be working together in violation of this
subsection will be separated by reassignment or terminated from employment.
Previously unrelated employees who become relatives by a marriage occurring
during the course of employment with the city are subject to the prohibitions
of this subsection. Employees are required to notify their immediate supervisor
and the human resources office if they are assigned to work with a relative in
violation of this subsection. This subsection shall be applied prospectively
from the effective date of this policy, and shall not require reassignment of
relatives who were currently assigned to work together as of the effective
date, unless there otherwise exists a personal conflict as described in
Subsection C. Notwithstanding the above, the chief administrative officer may
grant permission for particular relatives to work together on a temporary basis
for short periods of time, provided it is not unlawful, if the chief
administrative officer deems it necessary to meet the city's short term
staffing needs.
   C.   Personal Conflicts: As with other management rights to set work
standards and rules, in cases where a conflict or the potential for conflict in
the work force arises, including, romantic or dating relationships, familial
relationships or other relationships which may impact the workplace, even if
there is no supervisory relationship involved, the parties may be separated by
reassignment or terminated from employment. A conflict may exist when a
department executive director determines that a relationship between two
employees interferes with the ability to effectively direct work assignments
within the department or interferes with the performance of work in a manner
which fails to meet the standards and expectations reasonably associated with
the job functions and work assignments of employees. Romantic or dating
relationships between a supervisor and a subordinate are prohibited. (Adm.
Order 2015-3, 6-2-2015; Adm. Order 2024-6, 10-4-2024; Adm. Order 2024-7, 11-19-
2024)
1-8: EMPLOYEE MEDICAL INFORMATION AND EXAMINATIONS:
To help ensure that employees can perform their duties safely, medical
examinations and/or the exchange of medical information about an employee's
ability to perform the essential functions of their job are required.
   A.   Postoffer Examination: After an offer has been made to an applicant
entering any job category, a medical examination will be performed at the
city's expense by a health professional of the city's choice. The offer of
employment and assignment to duties is contingent upon satisfactory completion
of the exam. This exam includes test(s) to determine the presence or absence of
drugs or alcohol in the applicant. The city subscribes to a drug free
workplace. Accordingly, applicants shall not be hired who test positive for the
presence of drugs or alcohol, in accordance with the drug and alcohol, drug
testing, and fitness for duty policies in this manual, as a result of this
medical exam and testing procedure. (See drug and alcohol, drug testing and
fitness for duty policies in this manual.)
   B.   Fitness For Duty Examinations: The city believes it is important to
provide for the safety and health of its employees and the public for whom the
city provides services to protect the public's lives and property. Whenever a
question arises based on work performance or related observation and/or
evidence, about an employee's ability to adequately perform the essential
functions of their job, they may be required to take medical examinations to
determine fitness for duty and their continued ability to safely and adequately
perform the essential functions of their job. Such examinations will be at the
city's expense and will be conducted pursuant to the drug and alcohol, drug
testing, and fitness for duty policies in this manual.
   C.   Obtaining Current Information: The city reserves the right to obtain
medical information from any medical practitioner about an employee's current
health, physical condition, or treatment, as a condition of initial and/or
continuing employment to determine whether the employee is able to safely and
adequately perform the essential functions of their job and in a condition fit
for work. This extends to conditions that may relate to either specific health
issues, or to questions about "fitness for duty" related to drug/alcohol use.
(See drug and alcohol, drug testing, and fitness for duty policies in this
manual.)
   D.   Confidentiality: Specific information on an employee's medical
condition or history will be kept separate from other employee information and
maintained confidentially. Access to this information will be limited to those
who have a legitimate need to know. Notwithstanding this confidential record,
the existence of medical condition(s) or history may be referred to within
other records related to work performance, job standards, and work expectations
within an employee's personnel file to properly document any issues,
conditions, or accommodations with respect to the employee's work performance
and continued conditions of employment. (Adm. Order 2015-3, 6-2-2015; Adm.
Order 2024-7, 11-19-2024)
1-9: IMMIGRATION LAW COMPLIANCE:
   A.   Statement: The city is committed to employing only United States
citizens and those who are authorized to work in the United States and does not
unlawfully discriminate on the basis of citizenship or national origin. In
compliance with the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986, each new
employee, as a condition of employment, must complete the employment
eligibility verification form I-9 and present documentation establishing
identity and employment eligibility. Failure to present proper or adequate
documentation required within three working days from the date of hire will
result in termination of employment. Former employees who are rehired must also
complete I-9 form.
   B.   Questions; Information: Employees with questions or seeking more
information on immigration law issues are encouraged to contact the human
resources office. Employees may raise questions or complaints about immigration
law compliance without fear of reprisal. (Adm. Order 2015-3, 6-2-2015; Adm.
Order 2024-7, 11-19-2024)
1-10: CONFLICTS OF INTEREST:
   A.   Applicability: The appointed officers and employees of the city (as
well as elected officials and persons serving on city boards, committees,
commissions, or agencies) are subject to the Utah municipal officers' and
employees' ethics act. The provisions of this act have also been adopted under
city ordinance (Title 2, Chapter 7 of the Ogden municipal code).
   B.   Prohibited Acts: The law has prohibitions regarding the use of the
employee's position for personal benefit by prohibiting:
      1.   The improper use of private, controlled, or protected information;
      2.   The securing of special privileges or exemptions;
      3.   The use or attempting to use the employee's official position to
secure special privileges for the employee or others;
      4.   The acceptance or solicitation of gifts or loans if the gift or loan
tends to influence the employee in the discharge of the employee's duties.
(Exemptions for certain gifts are referred to in the acceptance of gifts
policy.)
   C.   Disclosure and Filing Requirements: Beyond these prohibitions the law
imposes certain disclosure and filing requirements for relationships of the
employee which involve:
      1.   The receipt of compensation for assisting in a transaction involving
the city;
      2.   Having an interest in a business entity regulated by the city;
      3.   Having an interest in a business entity doing business with the
city;
      4.   Having a personal interest or investment which creates a conflict
between the employee's personal interests and the employee's public duties.
         (Note: The above interests can include interests held by spouses or
minor children, or may arise through ownership or the holding of certain
positions in the applicable entity.)
   D.   Contracts: In addition to the requirements of state law, the city
prohibits, by ordinance (Section 2-7-7 of city code), employees from
participating on behalf of the city in the process of making, recommending,
approving, or preparing any contract in which the employee or any member of the
employee's family has any private pecuniary interest; or in making any
discretionary decision with regards to such contract.
   E.   Financial Interests: Employees should also be aware that a prohibition
against interest exists under the city's contracting and purchasing ordinances
(Section 4-2A-12 of the Ogden municipal code). No purchase order or contract of
the city may be approved in which a city employee is financially interested
(including interests of spouses and children). Under certain circumstances the
mayor may waive this prohibition and allow the city to proceed with the
purchasing or contract; however, the employee's obligations not to participate
in the process, as described above, are still applicable.
   F.   Violation: Conduct found in violation of these provisions shall subject
the employee to termination and/or criminal penalties. Employees desiring more
information about state law or the city ordinances, or who have questions about
conflicts of interest, may request further information from the human resources
office or the city attorney's office. (Adm. Order 2015-3, 6-2-2015; Adm. Order
2024-7, 11-19-2024)
1-11: ACCEPTANCE OF GIFTS:
   A.   Prohibited: The Utah municipal officers' and employees' ethics act and
city ordinance (Section 2-7-4 of the Ogden municipal code) prohibits the
acceptance of certain gifts by employees. Under these provisions, no employee
shall knowingly receive, accept, take, seek, or solicit, directly or
indirectly, any gift or loan for the employee or for another person, if the
gift or loan tends to influence the employee in the discharge of official
duties.
   B.   Exceptions: There are exceptions under these laws, including:
      1.   An occasional nonpecuniary gift having a value of less than $50;
      2.   An award publicly presented;
      3.   Any bona fide loan made in the ordinary course of business; or
      4.   Political campaign contributions actually used in a political
campaign.
         (Note: Although the acceptance of political contributions may not
violate these ethics provisions, restrictions exist regarding political
activity of employees under Section 2-6-13 of city Code.)
   C.   Violation: Violation of these laws and/or ordinances shall subject an
employee to termination and/or criminal penalties. Employees desiring more
information about these provisions may contact the human resources office or
the city attorney's office. (Adm. Order 2015-3, 6-2-2015; Adm. Order 2024-7,
11-19-2024)
1-12: OUTSIDE EMPLOYMENT:
   A.   Conditions: Employees may hold outside jobs as long as they meet the
performance standards of their job with the city. All employees will be judged
by the performance standards of their city job and will be subject to the
city's scheduling demands, regardless of any existing outside work
requirements. An employee's job with the city will be considered to be the
primary priority of the employee among any and all jobs of the employee. No
employee shall receive special treatment or accommodations due to any outside
job.
   B.   Conflicts Prohibited: Outside employment that constitutes a conflict of
interest is prohibited. Employees may not receive any income or material gain
from others outside the city for materials produced or services rendered while
performing their jobs with the city.
   C.   Department Policy: Individual departments within the city may establish
additional policies and rules regarding outside employment of various employees
within their department, provided said policies and rules are not inconsistent
with the provisions of federal, state, and local laws, or Ogden City
ordinances, administrative rules or policies. (Adm. Order 2015-3, 6-2-2015;
Adm. Order 2024-7, 11-19-2024)
1-13: HIRING AUTHORITY AND PLACEMENT:
   A.   Policy Statement: It is the policy of the city to fill vacancies with
qualified individuals who are able to perform job functions properly,
appropriately, and adequately. This policy extends to all aspects and phases of
the employment life cycle, from job announcement, recruitment, hiring,
performance evaluation, discipline, and separation. While the city generally
recruits and hires from within existing employment ranks, the city reserves the
right to accept applications from non-city employees.
   B.   Sworn Public Safety Employees: All full-time sworn employees within the
police and fire departments, except the heads of the departments, deputy chiefs
of the fire department, and deputy chiefs of the police department, are sworn
public safety employees and shall be recruited, selected, and appointed
pursuant to rules and regulations adopted by the mayor and by the chiefs of the
police and fire department consistent with administrative policy.
   C.   Merit and Sworn Public Safety Positions: The following guidelines are
those the city will generally use and consider when taking action to fill a job
vacancy in a merit and sworn public safety position:
      1.   Former employees with reinstatement rights will be considered
pursuant to the reinstatement rights policy in this manual.
      2.   Vacant positions will be posted for a minimum of five working days
in the human resources office and may be advertised in appropriate internal and
external employment websites. Announcements will also be distributed via email
and may be distributed to the general public. Applications will then be
accepted from current employees, as well as nonemployees, when applicable, on-
line through the human resources office until midnight on the closing date
contained in the vacancy announcement.
      3.   Testing procedures applicable to job position qualifications, which
serve to apply knowledge, skill, and ability to demonstrate successful
completion of essential job functions, and as outlined in these rules and
procedures, shall be conducted by the human resources office, or under their
direction and guidance.
      4.   An eligibility list shall be compiled and the top five eligible
candidates shall be certified by the human resources office to the appointing
authority for selection to the vacant position. The appointing authority may
select any person on the certified eligibility list for appointment. In the
event the appointing authority has less than five available persons from which
to make a selection and no additional names can then be certified, the
appointing authority may choose from the certified names available, may elect
to postpone filling the vacancy until the names of at least five available
persons can be certified (including that the vacancy be opened up to non-city
employees), or may fill the position by a temporary appointment. For entry
level sworn police and fire vacant positions, the names of ten eligible
candidates shall be certified, with one additional name for each vacant
position. The appointing authority may select from among any of the certified
candidates to fill a vacancy in an entry level position.
      5.   An eligibility list shall become effective upon certification by the
human resources office that the list represents the relative ratings of the
names appearing thereon. Eligibility lists shall remain in effect for one year
unless sooner cancelled by the human resources office and may be extended by
the human resources office for additional six month periods. No list shall
remain in effect for more than two years. At any time during the effective term
of an eligibility list, the human resources office may add thereto the names of
new eligible candidates. These new names shall be added and merged with the
existing list in order of final ratings of those added and those already on the
list.
      6.   Division directors of the city may make recommendation for selection
to the department executive director. Subject to the terms and conditions of
this hiring procedure and guideline, the department executive director shall
otherwise have final authority in the hiring process. Only those applicants
properly certified by the human resources office will be considered for
appointment.
      7.   Anyone who believes these procedures were not followed or who wishes
to make an inquiry or raise a concern or issue about the proper and appropriate
application of these procedures, may contact the human resources office and
file a written inquiry or protest. Any inquiry or protest by an applicant shall
be filed within five days from the date a hiring decision has been made or
shall not be considered.
      8.   After a period of not more than 14 calendar days from the date of
receipt of a written inquiry or protest, the human resources office shall make
a written reply to the petitioner, and a copy of that reply shall be filed with
the chief administrative officer and the department executive director.
      9.   The city reserves the right to investigate any hiring procedure or
process, evaluate and analyze data and information received, and otherwise
modify, amend, or set aside any hiring decision which violates any policy or
the best interests of the city. Such investigations shall be performed as
directed by the chief administrative officer.
      10.   Prior to placement in a position and commencement of work activity
for any newly hired employee, a drug and alcohol test shall be performed and
completed to determine and verify fitness for duty. (See medical information
and examination policy in this manual.)
   D.   Nonmerit, Special Employees: Nonmerit, special employees within the
mayor's administration shall be appointed by the mayor, subject to any advice
and consent proceedings that may be required by law, except as follows:
      1.   The chief administrative officer shall appoint division directors
and assistants and staff to the chief administrative officer.
      2.   A department executive director may appoint a deputy department
exective director, and a chief within the police or fire departments may
appoint a deputy chief, upon approval of the chief administrative officer.
(Adm. Order 2019-3, 3-26-2019; amd. Adm. Order 2022-4, 4-8-2022; Adm. Order
2024-7, 11-19-2024)
1-14: NONDISCLOSURE:
   A.   Intent: The city adheres to the open records and public records laws
and regulations as established by law. It is the intent of the city to provide
an open, direct public access to all appropriate and covered public information
it handles and with which it is entrusted. This includes adherence to open,
public meetings and publication of agendas. Nonetheless, the city also
recognizes that some information and records within the city may be
confidential in nature and not subject to disclosure.
   B.   Classified Records: Records classified as private, protected or
controlled under the Government Records Access and Management Act (which has
been implemented by the city under Title 4, Chapter 5 of the Ogden Municipal
Code) have statutory limitations on disclosure. Improper disclosure of such
records may subject an employee to criminal penalties, as well as disciplinary
action, up to and including termination. A good example of private records
under the Act are certain records contained in a personnel file, if properly
classified.
   C.   Proprietary Information: The city may also develop proprietary
procedures, processes, and functions that are and have been accomplished at the
expense of financial and professional resources, and for which the city has
both a responsibility and a right to protect from the unauthorized, "free", and
otherwise uncontrolled dissemination to others. The protection of certain of
these confidential and valued information is vital to the interests and the
success of the city. The city may also acquire access to the proprietary
property of third parties through license agreements which create certain
obligations on the part of the city limiting its use. Common types of
proprietary information include, but are not limited to, the following
examples:
      1.   New materials research.
      2.   Proprietary production processes.
      3.   Scientific formula or process.
      4.   Technological data, including computer software and programs.
      5.   Technological prototypes.
      6.   Training and research materials.
      7.   Departmental research, design and graphics records.
      8.   Patented or copyright materials.
      9.   Trademarks.
   D.   Highly Sensitive Data: In addition to classified records and
proprietary information, other data may be considered highly sensitive. Access
to highly sensitive data shall be approved by the department executive
director, city attorney, chief administrative officer, or mayor. The following
procedure shall be followed when moving or copying highly sensitive data to a
mobile storage device:
      1.   The employee shall state in writing that such storage is an
essential business need and shall file a signed electronic access agreement
with the human resources division.
      2.   The data shall be securely encrypted and password protected on the
storage device according to encryption methods established by the information
technology division.
      3.   The data shall be deleted from the mobile storage device or the
mobile storage device shall be destroyed as soon as the data is no longer
required.
   E.   File Accessing: All files created by city employees are owned by Ogden
City. Employees shall not gain remote access to city servers, files, and data
without the approval of the infromation technology division. Employees shall
not access another employee's e-mail or "C" or "H" drive without their
permission, except as approved by the owning department's executive director,
city attorney, chief administrative officer, or mayor.
   F.   Disciplinary Action: Any employee who improperly uses or discloses the
city's confidential business information will be subject to disciplinary
action, up to and including termination of employment and legal action, even if
the employee does not actually benefit from the disclosed information. (Adm.
Order 2015-3, 6-2-2015; Adm. Order 2024-7, 11-19-2024)
