3-1: EMPLOYMENT BENEFITS; INTRODUCTION:
   A.   Scope; Coverage: Eligible employees at the City are provided a wide
range of benefits. A number of the programs (such as social security, workers'
compensation and unemployment insurance) cover most or all employees in the
manner prescribed by law.
   B.   Eligibility: Benefits eligibility is dependent upon a variety of
factors, including employee classification. Your supervisor or the Human
Resources Office can identify the programs for which you are eligible. Details
of many of these programs can be found elsewhere in the Personnel Policy and
Procedures Manual.
   C.   Programs: The benefit programs included in this chapter are available
to eligible employees.
   D.   Employee Contributions: Some benefit programs require contributions
from the employee, but many are fully paid by the City, subject to the terms
and eligibility conditions as defined and controlled within each benefit
policy.
   E.   Amendments; Modifications: All benefits, conditions and terms of
employment with the City are contingent upon the availability of revenues and
resources with which to carry out or otherwise maintain those operations,
benefits and/or privileges described or referred to in this manual. The City
reserves the right to amend, modify or set aside any and all benefits subject
to the decision(s) of the Mayor and/or the City Council. (Adm. Order 2018-10,
11-29-2018)
3-2: EMPLOYEE ASSISTANCE PROGRAM:
   A.   Provided: Subject to the terms, limitations and conditions of the
benefits and coverages provided under this policy, the City provides for an
employee assistance program as a health and work benefit for eligible
employees.
   B.   Eligibility: All full time employees are eligible for the employee
assistance program.
   C.   Availability: The employee assistance program (EAP) is a confidential
assistance service offered to full time Ogden City employees and their
families. It is a counseling service made available to employees who are
experiencing personal or medical problems.
   D.   Job Performance Issue: The program is also available to supervisors,
who may refer an employee when job performance is an issue with respect to the
employee's ability to continue to meet conditions of employment and job
standards. The City recognizes that many personal problems may detract from a
person's effectiveness and can seriously impair job performance (e.g., stress,
drug/alcohol abuse, legal or financial problems, family or emotional upsets,
etc.). The employee assistance program (EAP) offers counseling and referral to
attempt to successfully resolve these problems.
   E.   Supervisor Referral: A referral to the EAP by a supervisor due to job
performance issues may reflect a serious matter with respect to the employee's
work performance, depending on the circumstances. Yet, such a referral also
offers a real opportunity for the employee to obtain professional counseling or
other help.
   F.   Scheduling: The EAP coordinator's phone number is posted in written and
posted material distributed throughout departments of the City. Appointments
are scheduled for the employee or the employee's family member to meet with the
EAP coordinator/counselor at the first opportunity. In a crisis, immediate help
can be provided.
   G.   Confidentiality; Participation: All contacts are confidential and are
generally based on voluntary participation. There may be occasion when the
department director requires that an employee see the EAP coordinator as a
continuing condition and part of employment. Since the program is confidential,
the directive to meet with the EAP staff shall be viewed as necessary to help
the employee resolve any issue(s) or problem(s) as a first good faith step in
addressing work performance issues.
   H.   Outside Referrals: Outside referrals may be recommended by the EAP
counselor and the employee's health insurance may be utilized for the extra
cost for these services.
   I.   Questions: Employees are encouraged to raise questions and discuss
issues involving this program and referrals to the EAP without fear of
reprisal. The Human Resources Office may be contacted for more information
regarding the employee assistance program. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018)
3-3: UNEMPLOYMENT INSURANCE BENEFITS:
   A.   Intent: In accordance with State law, the City participates in the
State unemployment insurance program. Employees who are separated from
employment with the City may be eligible for unemployment insurance benefits.
The intent of the unemployment insurance program is to assist employees who are
temporarily out of work through no fault of their own.
   B.   Purpose: Established as part of a nationwide effort, the unemployment
insurance system has as its main purpose, the economic stabilization of
businesses and communities in times of unexpected or high unemployment.
   C.   Eligibility: Generally, employees who voluntarily quit without good
cause or who are discharged for misconduct under certain "for cause" reasons,
do not qualify for unemployment. The sole authority in determining a worker's
eligibility for unemployment benefits rests with the State unemployment
insurance agency. Claims may be filed and benefits determined and coordinated
through the local Utah Department of Workforce Services. (Adm. Order 2018-10,
11-29-2018)
3-4: WORKERS' COMPENSATION:
   A.   Provided: In accordance with Utah State law, the City provides workers'
compensation. Subject to applicable legal requirements, this program generally
covers injury or illness sustained in the course of employment that requires
medical treatment.
   B.   Benefits: Generally, workers' compensation benefits may include
payments for: medical treatment, temporary total disability income and
permanent partial disability benefits. More information about workers'
compensation and its benefits can be obtained through the Ogden City Risk
Management Division.
   C.   Report To Supervisor: Employees who sustain work related injuries or
illnesses should inform their supervisor immediately. No matter how minor an on
the job injury may appear, it is important that it be reported as quickly as
possible. It is the policy of the City to investigate all accidents or
injuries, no matter how slight, to determine the cause of the accident or
injury.
   D.   Forms: Upon notification that an accident or injury has occurred
related to an employee's work, the supervisor and/or the employee completes the
first report of injury or illness form and the City's supervisor's
investigation report form, and forwards these with any additional information
to the City's Risk Management Division.
   E.   Procedures Established: Employees injured on the job while working for
the City, who need medical treatment and services, are required to follow the
City's established procedures. These procedures are posted at City work sites.
Proper procedures must be followed before payments for medical treatment will
be made.
   F.   Notification Requirements: Under applicable State law, an injured
employee is required to give notice of an accident or injury immediately upon
first knowledge of such, and not later than one hundred eighty (180) calendar
days after such occurrence. If an appropriate supervisor completes an
employer's first report of injury form, written notice from the employee is not
necessary. However, claims not meeting statutory notification requirements can
be denied under workers' compensation laws.
   G.   Reductions In Compensation: Workers' compensation laws provide
reductions in compensation for failure to properly report an accident, or for
failure to meet safe work requirements under applicable law and regulation.
   H.   Paid Leave (Vacation or Sick Leave Use): Ogden City policies allow
employees to use available vacation or sick leave to supplement workers'
compensation disability amounts up to the employee's total net (after taxes)
pay. (See workers' compensation policy in the leaves section of this manual.)
Ogden City employees, who take time off work as a result of an injury sustained
at other employment, are not eligible to use any accrued sick leave while
receiving workers' compensation disability benefits based on other employment.
   I.   Policy; Enforcement: The City reserves the right to act in accordance
with its own safety and risk management policies to determine appropriate
action with respect to the work force, procedures, internal controls and even
disciplinary action, in order to enforce its own safety and risk management
policies.
   J.   Third Party Recovery: As provided by applicable State law, the City
retains the right to legally pursue against any third party to recover workers'
compensation costs paid on behalf of an injured employee.
   K.   Liability For Off Duty Injuries: Neither the City nor the workers'
compensation carrier will be liable for the payment of workers' compensation
for injuries that occur during an employee's voluntary participation in any off
duty recreational, social or athletic activity sponsored by the City. (Adm.
Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018; Adm. Order 2023-5, 7-13-2023)
3-5: SICK LEAVE PAYMENT UPON DEATH:
It is the policy of the City that upon the death of an employee with accrued
sick leave, regardless of the cause of death, the City will pay a lump sum
benefit to the surviving heir(s) based on the employee's accrued, unused sick
leave. Upon the employee's death, the benefit is calculated and paid on the
same basis as if the employee retired from service with the City. (Adm. Order
2018-10, 11-29-2018)
3-6: MEDICAL HEALTH INSURANCE:
   A.   Eligible Employment Classifications: Subject to the terms and
conditions of the group health insurance plan offered by the City and as
provided by an approved plan provider, the City offers several options of
coverage for medical health insurance benefits for employees in eligible
employment classifications. Eligible employment classifications are:
      1.   Full time employees.
      2.   Nonmerit, special employees.
      3.   Introductory employees in the above classifications.
   B.   Eligibility Under The Patient Protection And Affordable Health Care
Act:
      1.   This subsection applies only to casual or seasonal employees.
      2.   There is an established twelve (12) month initial measurement period
for determining whether a casual or seasonal employee is considered to be
eligible for medical health insurance benefits for a particular coverage period
in order to be in compliance with the Patient Protection and Affordable Health
Care Act. Information regarding the measurement period can be obtained through
the Human Resources Division. If an employee works an average of thirty (30) or
more hours per week over this measurement period, the employee is considered to
be a full time employee for purposes of medical health insurance benefits only.
      3.   If an employee is determined to be an eligible employee during the
measurement period, the employee must be offered medical health insurance
benefits during the next twelve (12) months (stability period) regardless of
how much the employee actually works during the stability period. If during the
measurement period it is determined that an employee is not an eligible
employee then the employee will not be entitled to medical health insurance
benefits during the stability period regardless of how many hours the employee
works during the year.
      4.   For new hires, the measurement period to determine if the employee
is considered to be full time and eligible for benefits begins on the date of
hire and continues for one year. For every year after that initial year, the
measurement period will occur immediately after the hiring date and continue
annually in conjunction with the City's measurement period.
   C.   Enrollment: Eligible employees may elect to participate in a group
health insurance plan during annual open enrollment, or during any of the
following life events:
      1.   Marriage, divorce or separation (marital status change).
      2.   Birth, death or adoption of a child (dependent status change).
      3.   Death of an employee or spouse.
      4.   The spouse begins or terminates employment, effecting benefit
coverages.
      5.   The spouse loses health insurance coverage through his/her employer.
      6.   Employment separation (for any reason).
      7.   Employment status change of an employee (i.e., moving into an
eligible employment classification or reemployment from long-term military
service).
   D.   Eligibility Conditions: The City sponsors one or more group medical
health insurance plans, which are organized and administered through the terms
and conditions of each plan. Employees granted coverage under any terms or
agreement, must also meet the conditions of eligibility as established by the
plan provider. Information about each available plan (benefits, costs, etc.) is
provided to eligible employees during open enrollment, upon hire or through the
City's Human Resources Office.
   E.   Coverage Established: Subject to the terms and conditions of the
approved insurance plan, the City sponsors medical insurance coverage and
services through medical insurance plans. Group medical health insurance
coverage begins upon entering an eligible employment classification and upon
meeting the designated waiting period as determined by the plan document.
Enrollment is established through the proper and timely completion of certain
written forms and records. If no selection is made by the employee upon
entering an eligible classification or during "open enrollment" periods in the
calendar year, the City will provide at least minimum core coverage through a
specific group plan. Once notified, employees who fail to turn in their plan
enrollment form when due, will only be eligible for minimum core coverage until
the next available qualifying enrollment period.
   F.   Plan Coverage: Under the terms and conditions of the group medical plan
coverages and benefits, certain medical services and costs may not be covered
or provided for in a plan or through a plan provider, depending upon the type
of plan the employee selects. The specific plan provisions, including premium
costs, copayment amounts, deductibles and other factors related to plan
coverage, are subject to change depending upon any plan provider which the City
approves and selects.
   G.   Retirees:
      1.   For the purpose of this section, "retirees" means employees who have
either: a) met the conditions for retirement as determined and defined by the
Utah State Retirement Board or another City sponsored retirement plan; or b)
employees who have left City employment as the result of a disability and who
were eligible to receive benefits under the City's long term disability
program.
      2.   Retirees may elect to continue their health insurance coverage upon
retirement, which they had prior to their retirement date. In such case, those
retirees shall be required to pay the full premium for this group insurance
coverage, plus an administration fee, under COBRA, for a period of up to
eighteen (18) months. (See also benefits continuation "COBRA" policy in this
manual.)
   H.   Retirees After Eighteen Months: After eighteen (18) months, qualifying
retirees may elect to continue their health insurance coverage under the terms
and conditions of the group health insurance plan sponsored by the City for
retirees for a period of up to ten (10) years or until the retiree qualifies
for medicare, whichever occurs sooner. In such case, those retirees shall be
required to pay a monthly premium amount as determined and charged by the
insurance plan provider of the City.
   I.   Changes; Modifications: The City reserves the right to change, modify
or set aside, medical group insurance, should insufficient resources and
revenues be available to continue to provide such. While not anticipated, it is
important to note this possibility, inasmuch as medical insurance, as with all
other conditions of employment and benefit packages, is subject to the
resources and ability to provide such for employees. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-
29-2018)
3-7: DENTAL INSURANCE BENEFITS:
   A.   Eligible Employees: Subject to the terms and conditions of any approved
insurance plan, the City sponsors dental insurance coverage and services
through dental insurance plans. Employees in eligible classifications may
select the dental insurance coverage they wish. Eligible employees are:
      1.   Full-time employees.
      2.   Nonmerit, special employees.
      3.   Introductory employees in the above classifications.
   B.   Enrollment: Eligible employees may elect to participate in a dental
insurance plan during annual open enrollment, or during any of the following
life events:
      1.   Marriage, divorce or separation (marital status change).
      2.   Birth, death or adoption of a child (dependent status change).
      3.   Death of an employee or spouse.
      4.   The spouse begins or terminates employment, effecting benefit
coverages.
      5.   The spouse loses health insurance coverage through his/her employer.
      6.   Employment separation (for any reason).
      7.   Employment status change of an employee (e.g., moving into an
eligible employment classification or reemployment from long-term military
leave).
   C.   Plan Information: The City sponsors one or more group dental insurance
plans, which are organized and administered through the terms and conditions of
each plan. Information about each available plan (benefits, costs, etc.) is
provided through the City's Human Resources Office.
   D.   Coverage Granted: Group dental insurance coverage begins upon entering
an eligible employment classification and upon meeting the designated waiting
period as determined by the plan document. Enrollment is established through
the proper and timely completion of certain written forms and records.
Employees granted coverage under any terms or agreement, must also meet the
conditions of eligibility as established by the plan provider.
   E.   Coverage And Benefits: Under the terms and conditions of the group
medical plan coverages and benefits, certain dental services and costs may not
be covered or provided for in a plan or through a plan provider, depending upon
the type of plan the employee selects. Certain costs related to dental
services, prosthesis and products are borne directly by the employee or a
covered participant in a selected plan. Additionally, the employee is
responsible for certain amounts or portions of fees charged; such as deductible
amounts and copayment amounts. The specific plan provisions, including premium
costs, copayment amounts, deductibles and other factors related to plan
coverage, are subject to change depending upon any plan provider which the City
approves and selects.
   F.   Changes; Modifications: The City reserves the right to change, modify
or set aside, dental insurance, should insufficient resources and revenues be
available to continue to provide such. While not anticipated, it is important
to note this possibility, inasmuch as dental insurance, as with all other
conditions of employment and benefit packages, is subject to the resources and
ability to provide such for employees. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018)
3-8: VISION CARE COVERAGE AND SERVICES DISCOUNT:
   A.   Provided: Subject to the terms and conditions of any approved insurance
plan, employees may purchase vision care coverage and services through a plan
provider for employees in eligible classifications. Some available, group
medical insurance plans offer limited vision care benefits related to a
specific medical service.
   B.   Eligible Employees: In addition to any specific vision care service
covered or provided through a medical insurance plan, employees may purchase a
vision care discount program for eligible employees. Eligible employees are:
      1.   Full-time employees.
      2.   Nonmerit, special employees.
      3.   Introductory employees in the above classifications.
   C.   Membership; Premium: Under the vision care discount program, employees
pay the entire cost of an annual membership fee to the applicable program. In
return for the fee, vision care and services are available at generally
significant discounts to the covered employee and their covered dependents. The
employee pays one hundred percent (100%) of the discounted vision care premium
and vision care services provided under the plan.
   D.   Limitations: Certain limitations on the covered costs of services as
well as qualifications or limitations on the amount of discounts available may
exist and are directed and controlled through the terms and conditions of
coverage in the plan.
   E.   Enrollment: Employees may enroll in the plan upon meeting the
designated waiting period as determined by the plan document, or during certain
times of the calendar year, known as open enrollment(s). More information is
available in the Human Resources Office. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018)
3-9: BENEFITS CONTINUATION (COBRA):
   A.   Qualifying Events: The Federal Consolidated Omnibus Budget
Reconciliation Act (COBRA) gives employees and their qualified beneficiaries
the opportunity to continue health insurance coverage under the City's health
plan when a "qualifying event" would normally result in the loss of
eligibility. Some common qualifying events are resignation, termination of
employment, retirement or death of an employee; a reduction in an employee's
hours, long term military leave or a leave of absence; an employee's divorce or
legal separation; a dependent child no longer meeting eligibility requirements;
and termination of family or medical leave.
   B.   Terms And Conditions: Subject to the terms and conditions of the group
policy and applicable legal standards for extensions of insurance coverage
under the law, employees, their spouses, dependents and divorced or separated
spouses may continue the group insurance plan benefits for periods of time
beyond the last date of work of the employee for the City. The terms,
limitations, conditions and length of extensions of coverage are specific in
each individual case. Employees, dependents, spouses and ex-spouses are
encouraged to make inquiry of the City through the Human Resources Office to
obtain further information.
   C.   Cost Of Coverage: Under COBRA, the employee or beneficiary pays the
full cost of coverage at the City's group rates, plus an administration fee.
   D.   Notice To Employee: The City or its designee provides each eligible
employee with a written notice describing rights granted under COBRA when the
employee becomes eligible for coverage under the City's health insurance plan.
The notice contains important information about the employee's rights and
obligations.
   E.   Retirees:
      1.   For the purpose of this section, "retirees" means employees who have
either: a) met the conditions for retirement as determined and defined by the
Utah State Retirement Board or another City-sponsored retirement plan; or b)
employees who have left City employment as the result of a disability and who
were eligible to receive benefits under the City's long- term disability
program.
      2.   Retirees may elect to continue their health insurance coverage upon
retirement, which they had prior to their retirement date. In such case, those
retirees shall be required to pay the full premium for this group insurance
coverage, plus an administration fee, under COBRA, for a period of up to
eighteen (18) months.
   F.   Retirees After Eighteen Months: After eighteen (18) months, qualifying
retirees may elect to continue their health insurance coverage under the terms
and conditions of the group health insurance plan sponsored by the City for
retirees for a period of up to ten (10) years or until the retiree qualifies
for Medicare, whichever occurs first. In such case, those retirees shall be
required to pay a monthly premium amount as determined and charged by the
insurance plan provider of the City.
   G.   Coordination Of Coverage; Information: Continuation of health insurance
coverage must be coordinated with the City's Human Resources Office under the
terms and conditions established by and through the plan provider. Employees
interested in more information about the continued health insurance coverage
under this policy should contact the Human Resources Office. (Adm. Order 2018-
10, 11-29-2018)
3-10: FLEXIBLE SPENDING ACCOUNTS; CAFETERIA PLANNING:
   A.   Provided: In an effort to help eligible employees with the costs of
medical expenses and dependent care coverages and premiums, the City sponsors
flexible spending accounts, which reserves a certain amount of compensation
each year and sets it aside for the purpose of medical insurance payments and
coverage costs/fees. This reserved amount is then excluded from reporting for
the purposes of taxable income.
   B.   Defined; Control: Flexible spending accounts (FSA) are benefits which
have been developed under the meaning of a qualified cafeteria plan as defined
and controlled by the U.S. Internal Revenue Service. Thus, as IRS rules change
or are amended, an FSA is also subject to change or amendment to maintain
conformity to law. While sponsored by the City, specific terms, coverages and
the administration of an FSA is developed and administered through a plan
administrator.
   C.   Eligible Employees: Subject to certain qualifying conditions and hours
of work, eligible employees, referred to as plan participants in the flexible
spending accounts, include:
      1.   Full-time employees.
      2.   Nonmerit, special employees.
      3.   Introductory employees in the above classifications.
   D.   Requirements For Employees: FSA's function similarly to a personal
checking account held for the purposes described above and in the written
policy and plan coverage information. Money from the employee's compensation is
deposited throughout the year. FSA's have three (3) unique requirements for
employees:
      1.   The employee decides before the beginning of each year how much
their total deposit for the year in the FSA will be;
      2.   The employee uses the money set aside in the FSA only to pay for
their eligible dependent care costs and medical/dental fees/costs; and
      3.   The money deposited in the employee's account is deducted from their
compensation before it is taxed, thus providing a benefit of some immediate tax
relief.
   E.   Changes In Coverage: Once an employee makes an election for benefit
coverage, that election is set for one year and may be changed only upon any of
the following qualifying life events:
      1.   Marriage, divorce or separation (marital status change).
      2.   Birth, death or adoption of a child (dependent status change).
      3.   Death of an employee or spouse.
      4.   The spouse begins or terminates employment, affecting benefit
coverages.
      5.   The spouse loses health insurance coverage through his/her employer.
      6.   Employment separation (for any reason).
      7.   Employment status change of an employee (e.g., moving into an
eligible employment classification or reemployment from long-term military
leave).
   F.   Information: Plan information and written summaries and plan documents
are available from the City. Employees interested in participating in flexible
spending accounts should contact the Human Resources Office for written plan
information, appropriate enrollment application(s) and forms and other
pertinent information. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018)
3-11: LIFE INSURANCE:
   A.   Eligible Employees: The City sponsors a life insurance policy for
employees in eligible employment classifications. The City pays for the premium
cost of the individual policy as provided under the terms and conditions of a
group life insurance policy plan as provided by the City's plan provider.
Eligible employment classifications are:
      1.   Full-time employees.
      2.   Nonmerit, special employees.
      3.   Introductory employees in the above classifications.
   B.   Coverage: The life insurance coverage provides a lump sum benefit in
the event of an employee's death. Additionally, should the reason for the
employee's death be due to an accident, the face value of the benefit is
increased.
   C.   Spouses And Dependents: Spouses and dependents of eligible employees
are covered by the City's plan provider under the terms and conditions of the
individual life insurance policy. The policy coverage provides a lump sum
benefit for the spouse or each covered dependent of the employee. No additional
accidental death benefit is provided. As one condition of coverage, spouses and
dependents of eligible employees are required to be listed on enrollment cards,
available in the Human Resources Office.
   D.   Additional Insurance Available: Additional group term life insurance is
available. This benefit can be added or deleted during initial eligibility and
open enrollment periods. Employees are encouraged to contact the Human
Resources Office for more information regarding additional term life insurance
available to employees. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018)
3-12: SHORT TERM DISABILITY:
   A.   Provided; Purpose: Subject to the terms and conditions established and
controlled by the plan provider and/or other disability plan provider(s), the
City sponsors short term disability insurance coverage for employees in
eligible classifications for the purpose of providing income protection against
the loss of an employee's ability to work and earn income for periods of time
exceeding certain short term periods and conditions.
   B.   Eligible Employees: Eligible employment classifications are:
      1.   Full time employees.
      2.   Nonmerit, special employees.
      3.   Introductory employees in the above classifications.
   C.   Enrollment: Enrollment in short term disability insurance plans may
occur upon meeting the designated waiting period as determined by the plan
document or during annual, open enrollment periods. Enrollment is subject to
these specific times and the cost(s) of the premium is paid by the employee.
More information about respective coverage, plan costs or plan participation is
available in the Human Resources Office. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018)
3-13: LONG TERM DISABILITY:
   A.   Provided; Purpose: Subject to the terms and conditions established and
controlled by the plan provider and/or other disability plan provider(s), the
City sponsors long term disability insurance coverage for employees in eligible
classifications for the purpose of providing income protection against the loss
of an employee's ability to work and earn income for periods of time exceeding
certain long term periods and conditions.
   B.   Eligible Employees: Eligible employment classifications are:
      1.   Full time employees.
      2.   Nonmerit, special employees.
      3.   Introductory employees in full time positions in the above
classifications.
   C.   Other Eligible Employees: Other eligible employee classifications which
might be provided long term disability insurance coverage are those for whom
contributions are made by the City into the Utah State retirement system.
   D.   Fire Personnel: Subject to the terms and conditions established and
controlled by the firefighters retirement system(s), long term disability
insurance plan and coverage is provided for sworn fire personnel through that
retirement program.
   E.   Waiting Period: Under the long term disability insurance plan, there is
a waiting period, generally one hundred twenty (120) days, before benefits
begin.
   F.   Premiums; Information: The City pays for the premium cost(s) associated
with the respective long term disability insurance plans and policy provisions
for covered employees. More information about respective coverage or plan
participation may be obtained through the Human Resources Office. (Adm. Order
2018-10, 11-29-2018)
3-14: RETIREMENT PLANS AND SOCIAL SECURITY COVERAGE:
The City offers three (3) types of retirement programs to employees in eligible
employment classifications which are funded in part by the City, and in part by
those eligible employees. Eligible employment classifications are specific to
each type program, subject to the terms and conditions as described in this
policy.
   A.   Social Security:
      1.   Eligible employees are covered under the Federal social security
program. Social security is designed to provide supplemental income to workers
who retire, and was not designed to provide full retirement benefits. Eligible
employment classifications are all employees, except sworn police officers and
firefighters.
      2.   Federal law provides the exemption from taxation of employees'
compensation for the purpose of election of coverage under the Social Security
Act for retirement purposes, where preexisting retirement plans exist for
certain, qualified plans and public administrative employees. The City's
retirement plan under the Utah State Retirement Board qualifies for such an
exemption. Certain sworn police officers and firefighters are covered with
respect to Medicaid/Medicare Tax under the law. Employees may inquire further
of the Human Resources Office or the Payroll Department, if they wish more
information about this exemption or coverage.
   B.   Utah State Retirement:
      1.   Coverage: Subject to the terms, conditions and limitations as
defined and regulated by the Utah State Retirement Board, the City provides
coverage for employees in eligible employment classifications in the Utah State
retirement system. For membership eligibility, contact the Utah State
Retirement Office.
      2.   Rate And Manner Of Contributions: The rate and manner of
contributions into the State retirement system vary depending upon the type of
program under which the employee qualifies and is covered.
      3.   Rate Of Compensation To Qualify: The rate of compensation required
for elected or appointed officials to qualify for retirement coverage is
determined by the Utah State Retirement Board and will change annually based
upon the consumer price index, and as determined and administered by the Utah
State Retirement Board.
      4.   Information: Information about coverages, contributions, benefits
and programs may be obtained through the Human Resources Office or the Utah
State Retirement Office in Salt Lake City, Utah.
      5.   Exempt Out Of State Retirement: Some nonmerit, special employees may
choose to exempt out of the State retirement system, and have their
contribution deposited into an alternative retirement program, which is
available through the City. Individuals must meet criteria established by URS
and not be entitled to merit or civil service protection. Interested employees
should contact the Human Resources Office.
      6.   Tier 2 Retirement System: Appointed officials whose position is full
time, as certified and documented with the Utah retirement system, who
initially begin employment on or after July 1, 2011, participate in the tier 2
retirement system. All tier 2 participants must make an election to participate
in either the tier 2 hybrid retirement system or the tier 2 defined
contribution (DC) plan within the first twelve (12) months of employment.
      7.   Eligibility Requirements For Elected Officials: Like appointed
officials, tier 1 elected officials who meet the minimum earnings requirement
for membership, and are not entitled to merit protection, may be certified
online as either eligible for, or exempt from, retirement coverage. Elected
officials whose position is full time, and who initially begin employment on or
after July 1, 2011, participate in the tier 2 retirement system. (Elected
officials are only eligible to participate in the tier 2 defined contribution
(DC) plan.) Part time elected officials whose initial employment begin on or
after July 1, 2011, are not eligible for retirement coverage. For purposes of
URS coverage, the City classifies all elected City Council members as part time
employees and the elected Mayor as a full time employee.
   C.   Compensation Deferral Program: In addition to the State retirement
system coverage, the City sponsors a program which provides a form of
compensation deferral for eligible employees. This program allows a certain
amount of an employee's compensation to be set aside in a Retirement Fund or
investment pool without being taxed. Eligible employees may elect to deposit a
portion of their compensation into a tax deferred savings/retirement program
administered by approved plan sponsors. This program should be viewed primarily
as a long term savings or retirement program, since the funds within the
qualifying program cannot be withdrawn without meeting specific criteria and
guidelines as outlined by the plan sponsor, until termination of employment or
retirement from the City. Information and necessary enrollment forms for the
City's compensation deferral program can be obtained in the Human Resources
Office. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018)
3-15: QUALIFIED SAVINGS PLANS 1 :
   A.   Provided: As a benefit to employees, and to help plan for employees'
retirement and long term financial security, the City offers several qualified
savings plans to eligible employees subject to certain qualifications and
limitations.
   B.   Taxes: Subject to the terms and conditions of these plans, the amounts
employees save are not initially taxed. In many cases these nontaxable
contributions or savings can provide real benefits to the employee. Since less
taxes are taken out of the employee's paycheck, generally their "take home" pay
is not significantly affected.
   C.   Enrollment Information: Eligible employees may elect this benefit and
can sign up any time during the year by contacting the Human Resources Office.
More information about the plans and their terms and conditions can be obtained
from the Human Resources Office. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018)
 
Notes
  1. The City encourages all employees to save for their future, to meet
  personal goals and to plan for solid financial health. As with any financial
1 investment, risks exist that you should be aware of. Yet, the qualified
  savings plans sponsored by the City can be excellent tools for employees to
  accomplish their own financial health and success. Employees are strongly
  encouraged to consider and participate in these qualified savings plans.
3-16: EDUCATIONAL ASSISTANCE:
   A.   Scope: The City recognizes that the skills and knowledge of its
employees are critical to the success of the organization. The City's
educational assistance program encourages personal development through formal
education so that employees can maintain and improve job related skills.
   B.   Assistance Granted: The City may provide educational assistance up to
fifty percent (50%) of the cost of tuition, fees and books for up to six (6)
semester credit hours, or nine (9) quarter credit hours (or the equivalent time
within approved, qualified training or certification programs) per semester or
quarter to all eligible employees. The total amount of assistance granted any
employee shall not exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000.00) per fiscal year.
   C.   Eligible Employees: Eligible employees are all full time employees.
   D.   Maintaining Eligibility: To maintain eligibility, employees must remain
on the active payroll and be performing their job satisfactorily through
completion of each course.
   E.   Availability: Educational assistance is available to eligible employees
to attain a high school degree (diploma) or a college degree, so long as the
degree and course work relate to the employee's career path, and it is
reasonably expected that the City will derive a benefit of increased
productivity and effectiveness from the employee's successful attainment of the
diploma or degree.
   F.   Courses Eligible: This policy is not designed to cover all courses
which may be required as part of a degree program in a postsecondary, higher
education curriculum. Additionally, individual courses or courses that are part
of a degree, licensing or certification program, must be related to the
employee's current job duties.
   G.   Approval: The City has the sole discretion to determine approval for
any educational assistance requested. Approval must occur first through the
department director and next through the Human Resources Officer, and prior to
enrollment in the course, training or class offering.
   H.   Advancement; Pay Increases: While educational assistance is expected to
enhance employees' performance and professional abilities, the City cannot
guarantee that participation in formal education will entitle the employee to
automatic advancement, a different job assignment or pay increases.
   I.   Right Of Refusal: The City retains the right to refuse educational
assistance if, based upon the availability of funds as appropriated by the City
Council, there are insufficient financial resources to adequately provide for a
request for educational assistance. Accordingly, allocation of reimbursement
funds will be based on the value of course work to the City as recommended by a
Joint Labor Management Committee.
   J.   Reimbursement: It is a requirement of the City under this policy that
costs of tuition, fees or books are generally reimbursed upon successful
completion of approved training, certification, class or course work. Where a
grade is given and/or inherent in the nature of the approved course, the
employee is required to successfully complete said course with a grade of "C",
its equivalent (e.g., a grade point of 2.0 within a 4.0 scale), or better.
Within thirty (30) days of the successful completion of any approved course,
the City requires the employee to submit a completed request for reimbursement
to the Human Resources Office on proper form(s) available from the Human
Resources Office.
   K.   Reimbursement Exception: The City may make an exception to the
reimbursement policy when the course offering is in the nature of training or
certification type work, and the course is limited in both time of offering as
well as its length (e.g., a 1 day seminar or a 1 week training and
certification course). In such exception, the City may pay for the course
directly, subject to the recommendation of the department director and the
written approval of the Human Resources Office and the Chief Administrative
Officer.
   L.   Separation From Employment: If an employee voluntarily separates from
the City's employment within one year after completion of any course, the
amount of educational financial assistance for that course(s) will be
considered only a loan. Accordingly, the employee shall be required to repay up
to one hundred percent (100%) of the educational assistance amount for any
course(s) taken within the last twelve (12) months from the date of
termination. Exceptions to this repayment requirement may be made at the
discretion of the Chief Administrative Officer, and generally are limited to
compelling circumstance(s) beyond the immediate control of the employee and for
which a reasonable accommodation is requested.
   M.   Changed Or Modified Course: If a course is changed, modified or deleted
as a curriculum offering after the employee has obtained approval for
reimbursement, the employee is required to notify the Human Resources Office
and their department director of the change immediately upon first knowledge of
the change, modification or deletion. New, changed or modified course(s) must
receive written approval in order to receive reimbursement.
   N.   Information: Employees should contact the Human Resources Office for
more information or questions about educational assistance. (Adm. Order 2018-
10, 11-29-2018; Adm. Order 2023-2, 2-13-2023)
3-17: EMPLOYEE RECOGNITION:
   A.   Intent: It is the intent of the City to recognize those employees whose
loyalty and dedication to public service are reflected in their length of
service to the City. The City expresses this recognition and attempts to show a
measure of its appreciation through an annual employee service awards program.
   B.   Eligible Employees: As part of the annual employee service awards
program, the City presents those eligible employees with awards based upon the
number of continuous, uninterrupted years of service. Eligible employees are:
      1.   Full-time employees.
   C.   Changes; Modifications: The City reserves the right to change, add or
modify its specific service awards to eligible employees. As with all other
benefits provided and paid for by the City, the employee service awards program
is subject to the availability of funds and may be limited in scope or
frequency during times of substantial budget restrictions due to lack of
revenues, economic downturn or other significant operational requirements of
the City. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018)
3-18: CLOTHING ALLOWANCE:
It is the policy of the City to assist employees with applicable costs of
uniforms and clothing accessories required of them in the performance of their
duties. This assistance is provided in the way of financial assistance or
allowance for the purpose of ensuring employees maintain clean, neat and proper
uniform and appearance in their role(s) of representing the City and its
reputation and interests. The purpose of the clothing and accessories allowance
is to cover the acquisition, repair, cleaning, upkeep and replacement of
required and appropriate uniforms and clothing accessories as may be directed
and controlled through employees' respective departments and department
directors.
   A.   Payments Considered Separate: The amount of financial assistance
provided through and under this clothing allowance policy shall be specifically
treated and considered a separate and distinct matter apart from any other
compensation, pay, wage adjustment, benefit or overtime consideration otherwise
due a covered employee, and are processed for payment on a bi- weekly basis
through the payroll process, unless provided otherwise in this policy.
   B.   Taxable Income: All financial assistance provided to employees in those
positions covered by this policy, is considered income under State and Federal
law and is subject to Social Security Taxes. Social Security Tax is deducted
from clothing allowances and Income Taxes are withheld at the time of payment
to the employee. Payments for clothing allowances and Social Security Tax will
be included as taxable income and listed on the employee's annual W-2 and other
income and withholding information reported to appropriate taxing authority. It
is the intent of the City to report clothing allowance as income in order to
provide employees with the opportunity to deduct actual clothing expenses
subject to applicable State and Federal law. It is the employee's
responsibility to check with their own accountant or other sources to obtain
information on income and tax law that might affect their personal
circumstances.
   C.   Departments Covered: See specific department policies for available
allowances.
   D.   Protective Clothing: Each employee, who is determined by their division
manager to be involved in work which requires or warrants protective clothing,
shall be provided by the City proper protective clothing and other proper
safety gear/wear on an appropriate basis. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018)
3-19: TOOL ALLOWANCE:
   A.   Policy: It is the policy of the City that employees hired as mechanics
are expected to provide their own tools and be compensated on a bi-weekly basis
for the use, repair and/or replacement of those tools they use at work and on
the job for the purpose of completing job duties and duty assignments.
   B.   Separate From Other Pay: The amount of financial assistance provided
through and under this tool allowance policy shall be specifically treated and
considered a separate and distinct matter apart from any other pay,
compensation, wage adjustment, benefit or overtime considerations otherwise due
a covered employee.
   C.   Amount; Payments: The City shall provide each mechanic a bi-weekly tool
allowance of forty-six dollars and fifteen cents ($46.15). Mechanics will
receive an initial tool allowance of five hundred dollars ($500.00) to purchase
the required equipment to begin work. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018; amd.
Adm. Order 2022-10, 12-6-2022)
3-20: EMPLOYEE LOAN PROGRAM:
   A.   Intent: It is the intent of Ogden City to assist interested employees
with the purchase of technology devices, exercise equipment, bicycles, or
emergency preparedness items.
      1.   Technology Devices: To help increase the productivity of our
employees and elevate employees' technology literacy by assisting eligible
employees with the purchase of personal devices.
      2.   Bicycle: To increase health and wellness, offer economical
transportation and emphasize our responsibility to our environment by assisting
eligible employees with the purchase of a bicycle and associated safety
equipment.
      3.   Exercise Equipment: To increase health and wellness by assisting
eligible employees with the purchase of exercise equipment.
      4.   Emergency Preparedness: To encourage disaster preparation, and
facilitate employee capability to respond to City duties in an emergency,
emergency preparedness items will be offered for purchase through the Ogden
City Fire Department.
   B.   Eligible Employees: Any full time benefit eligible City employee, who
has completed his/her introductory period, is eligible for a loan under this
program. Participants must agree to comply with the requirements and provisions
of the plan. Participants will be eligible for only one loan at a time.
   C.   Loan Fund: Subject to the terms and conditions of this policy, eligible
employees may obtain a direct, interest free loan from the City to purchase or
upgrade a technology device, bicycle, exercise equipment or emergency
preparedness items. Loans are made from a Loan Fund created by the City.
Currently the Loan Fund is capped at one hundred thousand dollars
($100,000.00). Based on a first come, first served basis, and thereafter based
on a waiting list employees may obtain a direct loan from the Loan Fund up to
the maximum of:
      1.   Technology device: Two thousand dollars ($2,000.00).
      2.   Bicycle: Two thousand dollars ($2,000.00).
      3.   Exercise equipment: One thousand dollars ($1,000.00).
      4.   Emergency preparedness items: Two thousand dollars ($2,000) (if
purchasing a generator, the employee must match 50% of the loan for a total
purchase of $4,000).
Upon proper approval, funds shall be made available for purchases with a
purchase order and a check made payable to the employee and a vendor for the
proper amount. All loans must be approved by the Management Services Director.
   D.   Equipment Requirements:
      1.   Technology Devices: Employees are required to purchase a technology
device that has an industry standard OS and the devices cannot be older than
two (2) years old. Employees may purchase any type of device that is a
computer, tablet, cell phone and/or a wearable device. Employees may use the
device purchased through this loan program only for themselves or their
immediate family. When possible, devices should be purchased from a vendor
located within Ogden City. All device purchases must be approved by the IT
Manager.
      2.   Bicycle Equipment: Bicycle equipment should be purchased from a
vendor located within Ogden City. A bicycle purchased through this program
should only be for use by the employee or the employee's immediate family. All
bicycle purchases must be approved by the HR Manager.
      3.   Exercise Equipment: Exercise equipment should be purchased from a
vendor located within Ogden City. Exercise equipment purchased through this
program should only be for use by the employee or the employee's immediate
family. All exercise equipment purchases must be approved by the HR Manager.
      4.   Emergency Preparedness: When possible, seventy-two (72) hour kits
and other preparedness items should be purchased from a vendor within Ogden
City. Supplies purchased through this program should only be used by the
employee or the employee's immediate family. All seventy- two (72) hour kits
and other preparedness items must be approved by the Ogden City Emergency
Management Coordinator.
   E.   Procedures And Requirements: In order to make a purchase, the employee
must contact the Human Resources, IT Division or Emergency Management
Coordinator to initiate the proper procedures and paperwork for obtaining a
loan. Employees will be required to sign agreements to repay the loan, perfect
a security interest for the loan and abide by the terms and conditions of the
loan policy.
   F.   Insurance: Equipment purchased with a loan under this policy must be
properly insured as determined by proper proof of such coverage, and may not be
reassigned or transferred to another. The equipment purchased under this policy
may be subject to taxation and employees are responsible for any and all taxes
otherwise due under this policy.
   G.   Repayment: Loan repayments will be made through payroll deductions on a
biweekly basis. The actual amount of the payroll deductions will be sufficient
to pay for the entire loan in equal amounts over a maximum of fifty two (52)
consecutive pay periods immediately following the issuance of the loan.
   H.   Termination From Employment: Under the terms and conditions of this
policy and the formal agreement the employee signs, upon termination from
employment any remaining balance on any outstanding loan becomes immediately
due and can be deducted from the employee's final pay. (Adm. Order 2019-1, 2-
27-2019; amd. Adm. Order 2021-6, 10-25-2021)

4-1: HOLIDAY LEAVE; PAID TIME OFF:
   A.   Eligible Employees: The city provides paid time off or additional
compensation, as provided in the holiday pay policy, to all eligible employees
for holidays designated by the city. Employees in the following employment
classification(s) are eligible for this benefit:
      1.   Full time employees.
      2.   Nonmerit, special employees.
      3.   Introductory employees in the above classifications.
   B.   Holidays Designated: The holidays designated by the city for this
benefit are:
Holiday Calendar Date
Holiday                        Calendar Date
New Year's Day                 January 1
Martin Luther King, Jr. Day    Third Monday in January
Presidents' Day                Third Monday in February
Arbor Day                      Personal preference day (see vacation policy)
Memorial Day                   Last Monday in May
Junteenth National Freedom Day June 19 if a Monday (see subsection D)
Independence Day               July 4
Pioneer Day                    July 24
Labor Day                      First Monday in September
Veterans Day                   November 11
Thanksgiving Day               Fourth Thursday in November
Day after Thanksgiving         Fourth Friday in November
Christmas Day                  December 25
 
   C.   When Christmas Eve or New Year's Eve falls on a Monday, Tuesday,
Wednesday, or Thursday, City offices may close at 12:00 p.m. Merit employees,
including non-sworn merit employees in the Police and Fire Departments, may
receive up to four hours of administrative pay, based on the employee's normal
work schedule for that day (e.g., an employee who normally works until 3:30
p.m. will receive two and a half hours of administrative pay, and an employee
who normally works until 5:00 p.m. will receive four hours of administrative
pay).
      Closing City offices on these dates is done as a convenience to the city
and is not guaranteed from year to year. Accordingly, this administrative pay
is not considered holiday pay and will not be included in the designated
holiday schedule in Chapter 4.
      Subsection
4-1.C does not apply when the CAO or an executive director determines that
staffing is required to meet operational needs or to provide emergency
services.
   D.   When June 19 falls on a Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, or Friday,
Juneteenth will be observed on the immediately preceding Monday. When June 19
falls on a Saturday or Sunday, Juneteenth will be observed on the immediately
following Monday.
   E.   Saturdays and Sundays: For purposes of paid time off, a holiday that
falls on a Saturday is observed on the preceding Friday and a holiday that
falls on a Sunday is observed on the following Monday. (Notwithstanding the
above, holiday pay will be based on the actual holiday for "employees working
shift work", as provided in the holiday pay policy section.)
   F.   Equivalent Hours: Paid time off or additional compensation for holidays
is provided to all eligible employees immediately upon assignment to an
eligible employment classification. For all eligible employees, except sworn
fire personnel working 24 hour shifts, a holiday is equivalent to eight hours
of regularly scheduled work.
   G.   Calculation: Paid time off is calculated based on the employee's base
pay rate at the time of the holiday and does not include any special forms of
compensation, such as incentives, commissions or bonuses. Paid time off for
holidays is not considered hours worked for the purposes of calculating
overtime (notwithstanding the above, holiday time off may be considered hours
worked as provided in the holiday pay section).
   H.   Sworn Fire Personnel: Sworn fire personnel working 24 hour shifts are
compensated for working holidays at their regular rate of pay, as if the day
were not a holiday. In lieu of holiday pay, these employees receive additional
paid time off by accruing six hours of holiday leave each pay period to be
utilized as additional vacation leave (which includes benefit for Arbor Day).
The provision of such additional paid time off for holidays shall be prorated
to adjust for any changes during the year from, or to, shift work assignments.
   I.   Paid Absences: If a designated holiday falls during an eligible
employee's paid absence (i.e., vacation or sick leave), holiday paid time off
will still be granted for the applicable holiday, rather than vacation or sick
leave.
   J.   Unpaid Absences; Eligible Employees: Applicable to merit, non-merit,
and sworn police employees, if a designated holiday falls during an eligible
employee's unpaid absence, holiday paid time off will still be granted for the
applicable holiday unless the employee does not work any hours within the pay
period which includes the holiday.
   K.   Personal Preference Day: As indicated in the schedule above, eligible
employees will receive one additional vacation day in each calendar year in
lieu of Arbor Day. To be eligible, employees must be employed to work in the
pay period during which Arbor Day occurs. (See vacation benefits policy in this
manual.)
   L.   Shift Work; Work Required: See Section
5-5 regarding holiday pay for employees working shift work and other employees
required to work on a holiday. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018; Adm. Order
2019-7, 10-31-2019; Adm. Order 2022-5, 6-16-2022; Adm. Order 2025-7, 12-17-
2025)

   C.   Additional Vacation Pay; Converting Sick Leave: In addition to the
vacation accrual rates described above, employees may also accrue additional
vacation pay by converting certain accrued sick leave to vacation leave (see
sick leave policies of this manual).
   D.   Personal Preference Day: Employees who would otherwise qualify for
holiday pay also accrue one day of vacation time annually as a personal
preference day in lieu of Arbor Day. (See also holiday policy.) For most
employees, this personal preference day accrues at eight (8) hours of vacation
time in the pay period in April in which Arbor Day falls (i.e., the last Friday
in April). Employees may schedule the use of this time in accordance with
normal vacation procedures, once accrual of the additional time/day has
occurred. Sworn fire personnel and other employees designated as working shift
work for the purpose of the holiday policy, receive this time as described in
the holiday pay policy found elsewhere in this manual. (See holiday and holiday
pay policies in this manual.)
   E.   The following full time nonmerit, special employees are credited one
hundred sixty (160) hours of vacation pay annually on January 1 of each year:
the Mayor and all administrative employees described in subsection
2-1B3b of this manual, Executive Assistants to the Mayor and the CAO, Executive
Director and City Council staff, Police Division Commanders, Police
Lieutenants, and Fire Battalion Chiefs. Fire Battalion Chiefs working twenty
four (24) hour shifts are credited three hundred sixty eight (368) hours of
vacation pay annually on January 1 of each year. If an employee described in
this subsection is hired after January 1, the number of hours of vacation pay
credited on the date of hire will be prorated based on the months remaining in
the year. All other full time nonmerit, special employees not described in this
subsection shall receive vacation leave benefits equal to that of full time
merit employees. Part time nonmerit, special employees are not eligible to
receive vacation leave benefits.
   F.   Carrying Forward: In the event that available vacation is not used by
the end of the calendar year, employees may carry unused vacation time forward
to the next calendar year. However, if the amount of unused, accrued or
credited vacation time at the end of the first complete pay period in January,
except for hours accrued in the new calendar year, has exceeded a "cap" of two
hundred forty (240) hours for full time and nonmerit, special employees, or
four hundred eighty (480) hours for sworn fire personnel, the excess balance
will be paid as part of the payroll process. The vacation time will be paid out
at straight time based on the employee's rate of pay at the time of payout.
Carry over payout will not count toward the vacation buyback policy.
   G.   Information: For more information on the procedures and conditions used
to take vacation time off, refer to vacation; purposes, procedures, conditions
policy found in this manual.
   H.   Vacation Leave Donation:
      1.   Purpose: The City desires to allow an employee to donate vacation
hours for use by another employee in defined cases when the recipient
employee's compensatory time, accrued sick leave and vacation leave are
exhausted.
      2.   Eligibility: An employee is eligible to receive donations when that
employee has a qualifying event, as defined under the Family Medical Leave Act,
that is not caused by an on the job injury. Additionally, the recipient
employee is expected to be able to return to work and has exhausted all other
paid leave.
      3.   Amount Of Donated Leave: An eligible employee can receive up to four
hundred eighty (480) hours (12 weeks) of donated leave. Donated leave shall run
concurrent with any approved family medical leave or personal leave.
      4.   Approval Process: An employee desiring to donate vacation hours to
another employee shall submit a request to the Human Resources Office using a
form provided by the HR Division. HR shall review the request for compliance
with this policy and shall submit the request to the recipient employee's
department director for approval. The donating employee shall be notified of
the approval or denial of his or her request.
      5.   Approval Of Recipient's Department Director; Appeal: All leave
donations must be approved by the recipient employee's department director. The
decision of the department director may be appealed to the CAO by the donating
or recipient employee. The decision of the CAO is final and not subject to
further grievance or appeal.
      6.   Confidentiality: The name of any donating employee and the amount of
time donated shall be kept confidential. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018; amd.
Adm. Order 2022-11, 12-12-2022)
4-3: VACATION; PURPOSES, PROCEDURES, CONDITIONS:
   A.   Purpose: The City provides vacation benefits to eligible employees in
order to provide opportunities for rest, relaxation and personal pursuits. The
eligibility and rates of vacation accrual are described in the vacation
benefits policy above.
   B.   Calculation Policies And Procedures:
      1.   The length of eligible service to determine the vacation rate of
accrual is calculated on the basis of a twelve (12) month period that begins on
the date of hire for the eligible classification. Any unpaid leave of absence
will not count toward the twelve (12) month period except for a military leave
of absence. Military leave has no effect on this calculation. (See individual
leave of absence policies in this manual for more information.)
      2.   Vacation time off is paid at the employee's base pay rate at the
time of vacation. Base rate of pay does not include overtime or any special
forms of compensation such as incentives, commissions, bonuses. Paid vacation
time shall be accounted for in minimum increments of one-fourth (1/4) hour.
   C.   Requests For Leave: To take vacation, employees must request approval
at least two (2) weeks in advance from the supervisor who is authorized to
receive and review requests. Exceptions to this advance notice requirement may
only be granted by the department director, division manager or immediate
supervisor if authorized by the department director. Requests will be reviewed
and either denied or approved based on a number of factors, including business
needs and staffing requirements.
   D.   Exempt Employees: Due to FLSA requirements concerning employees who are
not eligible for overtime, exempt employees who are off work for less than one-
half (1/2) of a full workday, shall not have their vacation leave deducted for
vacation time taken. Paid vacation time shall be accounted for in minimum
increments of four (4) hours (fire and battalion chiefs working twenty-four
(24) hour shifts shall account for time in twelve (12) increments). They are
subject to the same conditions and limitations applicable to the qualified and
proper use of vacation leave.
   E.   FMLA: Employees may use vacation leave in connection with the care and
support of themselves or another under conditions described in the family and
medical leave policy in this manual. Employees, supervisors and department
directors are required to notify the Human Resources Office whenever paid
vacation leave is used for a serious health condition or a condition covered
under the family and medical leave policy in this manual.
   F.   Policy Terms And Conditions: As with all benefits of the City, the
terms and conditions of the vacation benefit and leave policies are subject to
continued funding and appropriate City Council authorization. These benefits
are provided subject to a variety of conditions and factors, including, but not
limited to, the financial ability of the City and the resources available to
the City to continue to fund the cost of vacation accrual and use.
   G.   Vacation Buy Back: An employee may request to have the City buy back
unused vacation time twice per fiscal year (July 1 to June 30) as long as the
employee will have a minimum of forty (40) hours of accrued vacation time
remaining after any buy back. For firefighters, the buy back time frame is
based on the Fire Department vacation planning year. Firefighters must have a
minimum of fifty six (56) hours of accrued vacation time remaining after any
buy back. Eligible employees requesting one or two (2) buy backs within a
fiscal year (Fire Department vacation planning year for firefighters) are
expected to use a minimum of forty (40) hours of vacation time (56 hours for
firefighters) in that fiscal year. Any exceptions must be approved by the Chief
Administrative Officer. The vacation time will be paid out at straight time
based on the employee's rate of pay at the time of the buy back. The employee
shall submit a written request for vacation buy back to the employee's
department director for approval and then to the Human Resources Division for
processing. Vacation carry over payout will not count toward this policy. (Adm.
Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018; amd. Adm. Order 2022-11, 12-12-2022)
4-4: SICK LEAVE BENEFITS:
   A.   Eligible Employees: The City provides paid sick leave benefits to all
eligible employees for periods of temporary absence due to illnesses or
injuries. Sick leave may also be available as death benefit or for bereavement
leave. Employees in the following employment classification(s) are eligible to
earn and use sick leave time as described in the sick leave and other
applicable policies in this manual:
      1.   Full time employees.
      2.   Nonmerit, special employees.
      3.   Introductory employees in above classifications.
   B.   Rate Of Accrual: Eligible employees will accrue sick leave benefits at
the rate of 3.70 hours biweekly (5.18 hours biweekly for sworn fire personnel).
   C.   Calculation: Sick leave benefits will be calculated based on the
employee's base pay rate at the time of absence and will not include any
special forms of compensation, such as incentives, commissions, bonuses.
   D.   Sick Leave Accrual Limitations, Conversions And Payments:
      1.   The City allows employees to benefit from a certain amount of unused
sick leave each year. After employees accrue two hundred forty (240) hours of
sick leave (336 hours for sworn fire personnel), they may elect to convert
twenty five percent (25%) of their additional unused hours earned in that
calendar year to vacation leave each calendar year at the end of the first
complete pay period in January. For employees retiring with State retirement
benefits or other City approved retirement program benefits during a calendar
year, conversion to vacation leave benefits will occur upon the effective date
of retirement.
      2.   The maximum number of hours of sick leave allowed under this policy
are one thousand three hundred forty four (1,344) hours for sworn fire
personnel and nine hundred sixty (960) hours for all other eligible employees.
Additional sick leave over the maximum shall be allowed to accrue for the
purpose of converting all such leave time to earned vacation leave.
      3.   At the beginning of each calendar year and by January 31, all sick
leave hours over nine hundred sixty (960) (1,344 hours for sworn fire
personnel) accrued by an employee shall be converted to an equal number of
earned vacation leave hours. Such converted vacation leave shall be subject to
the provisions of subsection
4-2F of this chapter during the calendar year in which it was converted.
      4.   Accrued sick leave benefits described and controlled in applicable
policies in this manual are intended solely to provide income protection in the
event of death, illness or injury or conversion to vacation as allowed in this
policy. Unused sick leave benefits will not be paid as direct compensation to
employees while they are employed or upon termination of employment except as
otherwise stated in this manual. (See policies regarding bereavement and
death.)
      5.   It is the intent of the City to provide some additional compensation
for employees retiring from public service, by paying the employee for a
portion of their accrued, unused sick leave. Subject to the terms, requirements
and controls of any City approved retirement system program, an employee
retiring under the system may be paid the value of one-half (1/2) his/her
unused, accumulated sick leave up to the maximum allowable number of hours for
their respective position (1,344 hours for sworn fire personnel and 960 hours
for other, eligible employees). Therefore, the maximum payment made to an
employee retiring with retirement benefits would be up to six hundred seventy
two (672) hours for sworn fire personnel and four hundred eighty (480) hours
for other, eligible employees. Such payment shall be based on the hourly or
equivalent base rate of pay in effect at retirement. A nonmerit, special
employee who is exempted from retirement coverage by Utah retirement systems,
upon voluntary termination of employment with the City may be paid the value of
one-half (1/2) his/her unused, accumulated sick leave up to the maximum
allowable number of hours for his/her respective position.
      6.   Except for employees retiring with State retirement benefits, or
other City approved retirement program benefits, the City shall not pay an
employee for any amount of accrued, unused sick leave upon separation from
their employment with the City under any reason other than by death. In the
event that a retiree has sick leave benefits reinstated at time of rehire, the
City shall not pay any accrued, unused sick leave upon separation from their
employment for any reason.
      7.   Full time employees who are rehired by the City within ten (10)
years of termination of their employment with the City pursuant to the
reinstatement provisions as otherwise stated in this manual, shall have sick
leave balances restored to them as such balances existed on the date of their
termination. This provision shall be effective for all full time employees.
   E.   Conversion Of Sick Leave To Volunteer Leave:
      1.   Purpose: The City desires to encourage employees to provide
volunteer service that benefits the community and recognizes that employees
would benefit from having the opportunity to perform volunteer service during
working hours when they are not required to meet other obligations.
      2.   Conversion Of Hours: After an employee accrues two hundred forty
(240) hours of sick leave (336 hours for sworn fire personnel) an employee may
elect to convert two (2) hours of sick leave into one hour of volunteer leave,
up to a maximum of sixteen (16) hours of sick leave (8 hours of volunteer
leave) per month, which leave may be used to provide volunteer service during
working hours, or taken as "credit" for volunteer service provided outside of
working hours. Volunteer leave must be approved by the employee's supervisor.
Additional hours over the maximum of eight (8) hours of volunteer leave per
month may be taken upon the approval of the employee's supervisor and the CAO.
      3.   Approval Process: An employee desiring to provide volunteer service
during working hours shall submit a request to his or her supervisor at least
two (2) weeks prior to the requested volunteer dates using a form provided by
the Human Resources Division, containing at least the following information:
the nature of the volunteer activity and the dates and times of the volunteer
service. The supervisor shall review the request and either approve it or deny
it taking into consideration the business needs of the division or area, and
the employee's work history, including employee performance, attendance and
disciplinary action, and other information about the employee's performance.
The employee shall be notified of the approval or denial of his or her request.
Approval of leave time on an individual basis does not imply all future
requests will be granted or create an expectation that approval is automatic.
There may be occasions where approval for an individual request needs to be
rescinded because of an operational need.
      4.   Other Options: Employees with less than two hundred forty (240)
hours of sick leave accumulated may have other options available to pursue
volunteer service during working hours, such as utilizing vacation leave,
compensatory time, or taking unpaid leave, and should consult their supervisor
or the Human Resources Department.
      5.   Definition Of Volunteer: For the purposes of this policy,
"volunteer" means a person who performs or gives services of his or her own
free will without monetary compensation.
      6.   Permitted Activities For Use Of Volunteer Leave:
         a.   Volunteering for a school within Ogden City boundaries;
         b.   Volunteering for Ogden City sponsored events;
         c.   Volunteering to assist with local disaster relief efforts.
         d.   Under no circumstances shall permitted activities be of the same
nature of duties that fall within the employee's normal job duties,
responsibilities, and assigned tasks, nor shall they include an employee's
participation in a City sponsored event, e.g., running in the Ogden Marathon.
      7.   Use Of City Facilities And Equipment: Employees may not use City
facilities and equipment for volunteer activities without the prior approval of
the employee's division manager.
      8.   Recognition For Volunteerism: Department Directors, division
managers and supervisors are encouraged to recognize their employees who
provide volunteer services, and may wish to report employee volunteer
activities in the Inside Track, or nominate employees for awards through the
Mayor's Office and/or Statewide award programs.
      9.   Unused Volunteer Leave: There is no payment for unused volunteer
leave upon an employee's separation from employment with the City. However, any
unused volunteer leave may be converted back to sick leave (2 sick leave hours
per 1 volunteer leave hour) for utilization as sick leave, or for pay out upon
separation from employment, consistent with City policy. (Adm. Order 2018-10,
11-29-2018; Adm. Order 2020-9, 12-24-2020)
4-5: SICK LEAVE; PURPOSES, PROCEDURES, CONDITIONS:
   A.   Purpose: The City provides paid sick leave benefits to eligible
employees in order to provide time off away from work to care for the medical
needs of the employee and the employee's qualified family members as defined
herein. The method and rate of sick leave accrual are described in the sick
leave benefits policy above. Employees are encouraged to accrue sick leave in
amounts sufficient to provide them financial security and regular income during
periods of extended sickness or injury, such as may be the case during surgery
and postsurgical recovery periods.
   B.   Use; Increments: Eligible employees may use sick leave benefits for an
absence due to their own illness, injury or bereavement leave. Employees may
also use sick leave to care for the illness or injury of the following
qualified family members of the employee: the employee's spouse, child,
stepchild, foster child, guardian child, parent, spouse's parent, grandchild,
grandparent, sibling, brother-in-law or sister-in-law. Use of employee sick
leave to care for the illness or injury of qualified family members described
herein shall be limited to nine hundred sixty (960) hours (1,344 hours in the
case of sworn fire personnel) in any twelve (12) month period. Paid sick leave
shall be accounted for in minimum increments of one-fourth (1/4) hour. Sick
leave cannot be used to increase the total number of hours an employee is
compensated for to more than forty (40) hours in a week (56 hours for
firefighters). For example, if an employee works thirty six (36) hours in a
week and takes eight (8) hours of sick leave, only four (4) hours of sick leave
will be utilized, and the employee will be compensated for a total of forty
(40) hours for that week. Parents cannot use sick leave to "bond" with a
newborn or newly adopted child. The federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA)
allows leave for bonding purposes, refer to FMLA policy in this manual.
   C.   Due to FLSA requirements concerning employees who are not eligible for
overtime, exempt employees who are off work for less than one-half (1/2) of a
full workday, shall not have their sick leave deducted for sick time taken.
Paid sick time shall be accounted for in minimum increments of four (4) hours
(fire battalion chiefs working twenty-four (24) hour shifts shall account for
