time in twelve (12) increments). Exempt employees are subject to the same
conditions and limitations applicable to the qualified and proper use of sick
leave for illness, injury or bereavement.
   D.   Notification: Subject to procedures established by department
directors, an employee who is unable to report to work due to illness or injury
of the employee or the employee's qualified family member should notify the
immediate supervisor or other designated individual. The direct supervisor
should also be contacted on each additional day of absence.
   E.   Advance Requests; Verification: Except in the case of an emergency or
unexpected illness, employees should request time off at least two (2) weeks in
advance of the beginning date of an extended period of sick leave. Verification
of illness or injury may be requested for sick leave absences and may be
required as a condition to receiving sick leave benefits.
      1.   If an employee is absent for more than three (3) consecutive days,
(or 2 consecutive shifts for sworn fire personnel) due to illness or injury of
the employee or employee's qualified family member, a physician's statement may
be requested verifying the disability and its beginning and expected ending
dates.
      2.   An employee may also be requested to provide a physician's statement
identifying whether they can return to work, and what, if any, work
restrictions or limitations exist. (See family and medical leave and fitness
for duty policies in this manual.)
      3.   Employees returning from sick leave may be required to provide a
physician's statement upon their return to work. See Family Medical Leave Act
policy found elsewhere in this manual.
      4.   Additionally, where a pattern of sick leave use presents itself, or
a question arises as to the legitimate use of accrued sick leave, department
directors shall have the right to inquire of proper use of sick leave, make
inquiry of the employee as to their ability to perform essential functions of
the job, and otherwise request that medical information for the employee or the
employee's qualified family member be provided to the Human Resources Division.
   F.   FMLA: Employees, supervisors and department directors are required to
notify the Human Resources Office whenever paid sick leave is used for a
medical disability or serious health condition of the employee. A "serious
health condition" means an illness, injury, impairment or a physical or mental
condition that involves an absence of three (3) days or longer under the care
of a healthcare provider, inpatient care in a hospital, hospice or residential
medical care facility; or continuing treatment by a healthcare provider.
   G.   Reporting: The City has developed a reporting form to be completed by
the employee and submitted to both the employee's department director and the
Human Resources Office. This form is used to determine the effective date of
any medical disability or serious health condition of the employee and the
period of available leave (paid and unpaid) benefits for the employee. If the
proper form is not completed, the City Human Resources Office will determine
the effective date of any serious health condition and the period of available
leave (paid and unpaid), based on the first date the employee was granted any
leave related to, and/or in connection with, the employee's medical disability
or serious health condition.
   H.   Notice Of Resignation: Upon notice of resignation, sick leave will not
be available for use unless an employee has a qualifying event under the Family
and Medical Leave Act or provided a doctor's note.
   I.   Policy Terms And Conditions: As with all benefits of the City, the
terms and conditions of the sick leave and other policies are subject to
continued funding and appropriate City Council authorization. These benefits
are provided subject to a variety of conditions and factors, including, but not
limited to, the financial ability of the City and the resources available to
the City to continue to fund the cost of sick leave accrual and use. (Adm.
Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018; amd. Adm. Order 2022-11, 12-12-2022)
4-6: BEREAVEMENT LEAVE:
   A.   Authorized; Notification To Supervisor: Employees who are eligible for
sick leave may use accrued sick leave to take time off from work to attend to
those matters normally associated with the death and funeral of a family
member. If an employee wishes to take time off due to the death of an immediate
family member, the employee should notify his or her supervisor immediately.
   B.   Use Specified: Employees who are eligible for sick leave may use
accrued sick leave for bereavement leave purposes, in the following manner:
 
                                                                              Sworn     All
                                                                             Fire      Others
                                                                              Personnel
Death of an employee’s spouse or child                                      112 hours 80
                                                                                        hours
Death of an employee’s parents, spouse’s parents, grandchildren, sibling, 56 hours  40
grandparents, brother-in-law or sister-in- law                                          hours
 
   C.   Death By Miscarriage Or Stillbirth Of A Child: In accordance with Utah
State law, the City provides three (3) consecutive work days of paid
bereavement leave for an employee, employee's spouse, or partner, following the
end of the employee's pregnancy by way of miscarriage or stillbirth regardless
of employment category (Utah Code §10-3-1103).
   D.   Discretion For Other Persons: In the discretion of the department
director, special consideration may be given for the death of any other person
whose association with the employee was similar to any of the above
relationships.
   E.   Vacation Use: Any employee may, with approval, use any available paid
vacation leave for additional time off as necessary when a compelling
circumstance occurs.
   F.   Leave Without Pay: If an employee has no accrued vacation or sick
leave, or if the employee is not an eligible employee for purposes of vacation
or sick leave, the employee may request bereavement leave without pay, in the
same manner as provided for other requests for leave without pay, for the same
periods of time allowed above for the use of sick leave.
   G.   Death Of A Co-Worker: An employee may use up to two (2) hours of
administrative leave with pay, and at the discretion of the department director
or CAO if appropriate, up to two (2) additional hours of sick leave, to attend
the funeral and related services of a co-worker or a person who dies within six
(6) months of being employed at Ogden City. At the discretion of the CAO, City
vehicles and other City resources may be utilized to assist with services. This
policy does not supersede customary procedures in the event of the death of a
public safety officer. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018; Adm. Order 2020-3, 4-
16-2020; amd. Adm. Order 2022-11, 12-12-2022)
4-7: WORKERS' COMPENSATION; LEAVES OF ABSENCE:
   A.   Scope: In accordance with Utah State law, the City provides workers'
compensation. Subject to applicable legal requirements, this program generally
covers injury or illness sustained in the course of employment that requires
medical treatment. The purpose and a brief description of workers' compensation
and its benefits are found in the workers' compensation policy found elsewhere
in this manual.
   B.   Unpaid Leave; Length: Unless the employee is terminated or separated
from the City, it is the policy of the City to provide an unpaid leave of
absence to any employee, who is unable to work as a consequence of a work
compensable injury, accident or illness. Generally, the length of time of this
leave is determined by both the medical condition of the employee and the
employee's ability to return to work in a capacity for which a medical
practitioner has approved and provided a release to such duty. The length of
this leave is discussed in the medical termination policy under the employment
separations section in this manual.
   C.   Request For Time: As with any other time off from scheduled work,
employees are required to complete a request for time off to their supervisor.
Employees have an obligation to request the time off work, keep their
supervisors informed of their whereabouts and otherwise keep the City apprised
of their intentions and availability to return to work.
   D.   Payments: During the leave period, temporary disability payments are
paid in accordance with applicable law, and paid as a specific amount based on
the employee's earnings and eligibility. Employees may qualify for family and
medical leave as part of a workers' compensation leave, or as a separate leave
altogether. (See also family and medical leave policy in this manual.)
   E.   Vacation and Sick Leave Use: If an employee is on an approved workers'
compensation leave and is receiving a temporary disability benefit, he or she
may use any available vacation or sick leave to supplement the workers'
compensation amount up to one hundred percent (100%) of the average net pay the
employee was receiving during the last thirteen (13) weeks of service for the
city immediately preceding the workers' compensation injury.
   F.   Information; Employee Responsibility: The City has specific policies
and procedures for handling workers' compensation claims. Safety programs have
been established to properly address safe working conditions and environments.
Employees are responsible for obtaining information about, and adhering to
direction on, the City's safety programs. (See safety policy in this manual.)
   G.   Failure To Return; Termination: If an employee fails to report to work
promptly at the end of an approved leave related to workers' compensation, the
City will assume the employee has resigned. Employees may be terminated for
work related reasons even though they receive workers' compensation. (Adm.
Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018; amd. Adm. Order 2022-11, 12-12-2022; Adm. Ord. 2023-
5, 7-13-2023)
4-8: FAMILY AND MEDICAL LEAVE:
   A.   Conditions: The City provides family and medical leaves of absence in
accordance with Federal law. The existing Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA)
allows eligible employees to take leave if they are temporarily unable to work
due to any of the following:
      1.   For incapacity due to pregnancy, prenatal medical care or
childbirth;
      2.   To care for the employee's child after birth, or placement of a
child with the employee for adoption or foster care, and to bond with the
newborn or newly-placed child;
      3.   To care for the employee's spouse, son, daughter or parent with a
serious health condition;
      4.   Because a serious health condition makes the employee unable to
perform one or more of the essential functions of his or her job;
      5.   To care for a qualifying family member who is injured or becomes ill
while in active military service; or
      6.   To assist a spouse, son, daughter, or parent with qualifying
exigencies as a result of a call to active duty.
   B.   Policies And Procedures: In implementing the Family and Medical Leave
Act and in accordance with Federal law, the City has adopted the following
policies and procedures:
      1.   Time Allowed: As determined by the Human Resources Officer and in
accordance with existing law, except for military caregiver leave, as provided
for below, eligible employees may take up to twelve (12) weeks of leave in a
twelve (12) month period for reasons stated above. For purposes of determining
the twelve (12) month period, up until November 15, 1998, the City will use a
calendar year. After November 16, 1998, the twelve (12) month period shall be a
rolling twelve (12) month period measured backward from the date an employee
uses any FMLA leave. Eligible employees may take up to twenty six (26) weeks of
leave to care for a qualifying family member who has a serious illness or
injury incurred while on active military duty. For military caregiver leave,
the twelve (12) month period begins on the first day the employee takes
military caregiver leave and ends twelve (12) months after that date. An
eligible employee is entitled to a combined maximum of twenty six (26) weeks of
military caregiver leave and leave for any other FMLA qualifying reason during
the twelve (12) month period calculated for military caregiver leave. Under
certain circumstances, a husband and wife both working for the City may have a
combined maximum of twelve (12) weeks of FMLA leave, or a combined maximum of
up to twenty six (26) weeks for military caregiver leave.
      2.   Paid Leave Substitution Required: Employees are required to
substitute appropriate paid leave, if the employee has earned or accrued it.
Consistent with the sick leave policies in this manual, sick leave may be used
to care for the medical needs of the employee who has accrued the sick leave,
or a qualified family member.
      3.   Absences More Than Three Days: Any period of incapacity requiring
absence from work or other regular daily activities of more than three (3)
consecutive days may qualify as a serious health condition under FMLA.
      4.   Disclosure; Forms: As soon as an employee, or the employee's
supervisor, becomes aware that a request for time off may meet a qualification
for FMLA leave, the employee must state that qualification and disclose general
information on the request for time off. In addition to the request for time
off, the employee should complete a request for family and medical leave form
that is available from the Human Resources Office.
      5.   Requests In Advance: Requests for FMLA leave should be in writing in
advance of foreseeable events and as soon as possible for unforeseeable events.
To the extent possible, any leave for a foreseeable event must be requested at
least thirty (30) calendar days in advance in writing. Employees are required
to complete a request for time off form and a request for family and medical
leave form and immediately submit copies directly to their supervisor,
department director and the Human Resources Office.
      6.   Review; Decision: Request for family and medical leave forms and
request for time off indicating potential FMLA leave qualifying circumstances
are reviewed by the Human Resources Office. The Human Resources Office shall
determine what, if any, additional documentation is needed on which to base a
written decision approving or denying the leave under FMLA. The employee is
responsible for providing the Human Resources Office requested documentation. A
written decision is issued by the Human Resources Office to the employee. If
approved, the Human Resources Office will also inform the employee of the
applicable conditions of the leave, the reason for the leave and the beginning
and ending dates of the leave.
      7.   Health Insurance Benefits: As required, the City will continue to
provide health insurance benefits for the full period of FMLA leave on the same
basis that any insurance benefit coverage was available and in place prior to
the leave commencing. An exception would be a change in health insurance
benefits for all employees or a change in the type of plan available to all
employees. Employees responsible to pay any portion of the applicable monthly
insurance premium are required to continue to do so while on FMLA leave.
      8.   Benefit Accruals: Benefit accruals, such as vacation, sick leave,
holiday benefits and seniority will continue during any paid portion of FMLA
leave. However, benefit accruals, such as vacation, sick leave and holiday
benefits, will be suspended during any unpaid FMLA leave and will resume upon
return to active employment. Likewise, seniority will not continue to accrue
during any unpaid FMLA leave, except for disabilities of the employee covered
by the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA), but will resume upon return to
active employment.
      9.   Verification Of Fitness: Employees returning from FMLA leave may be
required to provide a physician's verification of fitness to return to work
before the employee will be allowed or permitted to return to any work
activity. In order to properly schedule work, employees on leave are expected
to provide the City with at least two (2) weeks' advance notice of the date
they intend to return to work. When the leave ends, the employee is required to
report for work on time and ready for work.
      10.   Failure To Return: If an employee fails to report to work promptly
at the end of the leave, the City will assume that the employee has resigned.
Under circumstances where the employee fails without cause related to any
medical condition to report back after the leave ends, the employee may be
required to reimburse the City for the health insurance premium costs paid on
their behalf during the entire period of the leave.
      11.   Work Related Injuries/Accidents: Any period of approved worker"
compensation leave will be considered as part of the maximum of twelve (12)
weeks available under the FMLA leave policy during the twelve (12) month period
described above. While on approved workers' compensation leave, an employee is
not eligible to substitue other paid leave to comply with FMLA leave policies.
   C.   Information: Employees are encouraged to talk with their supervisors or
department director, or to contact the Human Resources Office and make inquiry,
raise concerns and seek information about the Family and Medical Leave Act, or
their working conditions related to taking such leave, without fear of
retaliation. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018; amd. Adm. Order 2022-11, 12-12-
2022; Adm. Ord. 2023-5, 7-13-2023)
4-9: PERSONAL LEAVE:
   A.   Allowed; Request: The City may grant leaves of absence without pay to
eligible employees who wish to take time off from work duties to fulfill
personal obligations upon the approval of the Chief Administrative Officer.
Only full time employees are eligible to request personal leave as described in
this policy. As soon as eligible employees become aware of the need for
personal leave of absence, they should request a leave from their supervisor
through appropriate leave procedures.
   B.   Time Granted: Personal leave may be granted for a period of up to
thirty (30) consecutive calendar days for every one year. If this initial
period of absence proves insufficient, consideration will be given to a written
request for a single extension of no more than sixty (60) consecutive calendar
days. An employee is required to take any applicable and available paid leave
during the commencement of any personal leave.
   C.   Evaluation: Requests for personal leave will be evaluated based on a
number of factors, including anticipated workload requirements and staffing
considerations during the proposed period of absence.
   D.   Health Insurance: Subject to the terms, conditions and limitations of
the applicable plans, the City will continue to provide health insurance
benefits for the first thirty (30) days of the approved personal leave.
   E.   Benefit Accruals: Benefit accruals, such as vacation, sick leave or
holiday benefits, will be suspended during the leave and will resume upon
return to active employment. Seniority will not continue to accrue during any
unpaid leave, including personal leave.
   F.   Reinstatement: When a personal leave ends, every reasonable effort will
be made to return the employee to the same position, if it is available, or to
a similar available position for which the employee is qualified. However, the
City cannot guarantee reinstatement in all cases.
   G.   Failure To Return: If an employee fails to report to work promptly at
the expiration of the approved leave period, the City will assume the employee
has resigned. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018; amd. Adm. Order 2022-11, 12-12-
2022)
4-10: MILITARY LEAVE:
   A.   Authorized Employees: Military leave may be approved for full-time
employees, as provided herein.
   B.   Paid Military Leave: Eligible employees who are members of a reserve
unit of any branch of the armed forces may use available military leave with
pay for attendance at a scheduled military assignment, including training.
Eligible employees will be provisionally credited 120 hours (168 for Sworn
Fire) of paid military leave each fiscal year to attend required military
assignments. Paid military leave may only be taken when a military assignment
conflicts with the employee's regular work schedule. Employees on paid military
leave shall receive pay at their current rate for their current position, with
a maximum of 40 hours per week (max of 56 per week for sworn fire). Paid
military leave will be credited each fiscal year and will only be available for
use in the same fiscal year. At the end of the fiscal year, no paid military
leave will roll over into a new fiscal year nor be available as a paid-out
benefit. Time not used in the fiscal year will be lost effective June 30 of
each year. Employees may request use of vacation leave, compensatory time, or
unpaid time off for any additional military assignments not covered by paid
military leave. Previously used leave cannot be redesignated as paid military
leave or another type of leave after the fact.
   C.   Eligibility: Eligible Employees who are active members of any reserve
unit of any branch of the armed forces may submit proof of current military
service each fiscal year to the Human Resources Division and be provisionally
credited the allotted hours of annual paid military leave.
   D.   Notice Of Military Service: An employee receiving orders for military
duty should give notice to their supervisor as well as the Human Resources
Division as far in advance as is reasonable under the circumstances. Notice may
be verbal or written by the employee. The city may also contact an appropriate
commanding officer for clarification and/or confirmation of the employee's
orders.
   E.   Return To Work: Employees on scheduled, annual, active-duty military
assignments are required to return to work for the first regularly scheduled
shift after the end of assignment, allowing reasonable travel time.
   F.   Unpaid, Long Term Military Leave: During a national emergency, eligible
employees who voluntarily enlist, who are drafted into the armed forces or who
are called into active military duty, will be granted unpaid, long term
military leave. The granting of unpaid, long term military leave shall entitle
the employee to the following:
      1.   Reinstatement rights shall be retained in accordance with all
applicable State and Federal laws, provided reinstatement is requested within
ninety (90) calendar days of the end of military duty and the employee is
honorably discharged.
      2.   Every reasonable effort will be made to return eligible employees to
the same or comparable position.
      3.   Any vacation leave, sick leave, and compensatory time accrued as of
the commencement of leave will remain to the credit of the employee for use
upon return to full employment. Further accrual of vacation and sick leave will
be suspended at the commencement of active-duty status. If requested, accrued
vacation leave and compensatory time can be disbursed during active-duty
status.
      4.   Although no benefits shall accrue during the period of leave, a
reinstated employee will be treated as though they were continuously employed
for purposes of determining benefits based on length of service, such as the
rate of vacation accrual, promotional considerations and job seniority rights.
      5.   A reinstated employee shall not be subject to any introductory
period.
      6.   Long Term Military Leave employees will not be required to submit
verification of active-duty status while away on long term active duty.
However, paid military leave may be provisionally credited to the employee with
Department Executive Director approval and used as set forth in this section.
   G.   Working During Leave: No employee on military leave shall work his or
her own, or another Ogden City employee's, job for any kind of compensation.
Once active duty has been completed, the employee may return to work. (Adm.
Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018; amd. Adm. Order 2025-4, 8-25-2025)
4-11: JURY DUTY:
   A.   Intent; Fees Earned: It is the intent of the City to guarantee that an
employee who is called to serve on a jury will not have a loss of pay while
serving on such jury. Employees called for jury duty will receive paid time off
for any periods of time for which the required jury duty and the employee's
regularly scheduled work hours coincide. Any fees earned as a result of that
jury duty, for which the employee has received paid time off, will be returned
to the City Treasurer within one week of their receipt.
   B.   Excuse Request: Either the City or the employee may request an excuse
from jury duty if, in the City's judgment, the employee's absence would create
serious operational difficulties.
   C.   Notification To Supervisor: Employees must show the jury duty summons
to their supervisor as soon as possible so that the supervisor may make
arrangements to accommodate their absence. Of course, employees are expected to
report for work whenever the court schedule permits. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-
29-2018)
4-12: WITNESS DUTY:
   A.   Paid Time Off; Fees Earned: Except as otherwise provided below,
employees subpoenaed as a witness in a case outside the scope of their job
assignments during the employee's normal working hours will be allowed paid
time off for any periods of time for which the required witness duty and the
employee's regularly scheduled work hours coincide. Any fees received as a
result of that court appearance as a witness, for which the employee has
received paid time off, will be returned to the City Treasurer within one week
of its receipt.
   B.   Exceptions: This policy shall not apply if an employee is required to
appear in court in the employee's own behalf (e.g., paying a fine, as party to
a lawsuit, etc.). In addition, the City does not compensate employees for court
time due to events arising from noncity employment. In such cases, the employee
shall take vacation leave or unpaid leave.
   C.   Personal Time: Employees called as a witness in a case outside the
scope of their job assignments, on the employee's personal time, will not
receive full pay for such appearance and any fees received as a result of such
service may be retained by the employee.
   D.   Notification To Supervisor: Employees must show the witness subpoena to
their supervisor as soon as possible so that the supervisor may make
arrangements to accommodate their absence. Of course, employees are expected to
report for work whenever the court schedule permits. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-
29-2018)
4-13: TIME OFF TO VOTE:
   A.   Hours Allowed: The City encourages employees to fulfill their civic
responsibilities by participating in elections. Generally, employees are able
to find time to vote either before or after their regular work schedule. If
employees are unable to vote in an election during their nonworking hours,
their department director may grant a reasonable amount of paid time off, up to
two (2) hours, for employees to vote.
   B.   Advance Notice: Employees should request time off to vote from their
supervisor at least two (2) working days prior to the election day. Advance
notice and prior approval is required so that the necessary time off can be
scheduled at the beginning or end of the work shift, whichever provides the
least disruption to the normal work schedule. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018)
4-14: EMERGENCY CLOSINGS:
   A.   Extent: At times, emergencies such as severe weather, fires, power
failures or earthquakes, can disrupt City operations. In extreme cases, these
circumstances may require the closing of a work facility. In the event that
such an emergency occurs during nonworking hours, notifications will be
announced through all available means.
   B.   Notification; Paid Time Off: When the decision to close a work facility
is made, employees will receive official notification from a supervisor.
Supervisors and department directors are responsible for scheduling employees
and work assignments. When an emergency occurs, under the authority of the
Chief Administrative Officer of the City, department directors and supervisors
will determine how time missed away from work will be handled. Under these
circumstances, missed time away from work may be paid time off, worked at
another time during the work period, or paid out as paid leave time where such
leave is accrued and available.
   C.   Essential Operations Employees: Employees in essential operations may
be asked to work on a day when operations are officially closed. In these
circumstances, employees who work will receive regular pay. Where applicable,
overtime pay or compensatory time will apply. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018;
amd. Adm. Order 2022-11, 12-12-2022)
4-15: LEAVE FOR EMPLOYEE ASSOCIATION MEETINGS; BUSINESS:
   A.   State Or National Association Meetings: Subject to the completion of
the City's request for time off form and upon the approval of the employee's
department director and the Chief Administrative Officer of the City, one
elected representative of an employee association shall be granted eight (8)
hours of paid leave during any calendar year for the purpose of attending one
employee association meeting sponsored by its State or national affiliation.
Except, in the case of sworn fire personnel, the President of the Fire
Association shall be granted two (2) 24-hour shifts of paid leave per calendar
year, and a single board member of the Fire Association shall be granted one
(1) 24-hour shift of paid leave per calendar year, to attend Fire Association
or professional development meetings or conferences.
   B.   Local Association Business: Subject to the completion of the City's
request for time off and upon the approval of the employee's division manager,
all elected representatives of an employee association shall be provided up to
one hour per month of paid leave time off for the purpose of attending local
employee association business.
   C.   Unused Time: Any paid leave time provided in this policy, which is not
used during either the month or calendar year in which it was available as
described above, shall not accrue for other use at any time. Any such paid
leave time unused will be forfeited after the respective month or calendar year
in which it was available.
   D.   Additional Time Request: Additional paid leave time away from work may
be granted to one or more association representative(s), if requested by the
administration to attend official meetings called by the City's administration
for the purpose of discussing terms and conditions of employment. Such
additional paid leave time shall be in addition to any paid leave time granted
for attending employee association meetings or business, as described above.
   E.   Other Circumstances; Approval: For any other circumstance(s) involving
employee association business for which either attendance by an association
representative has not been requested by the City, or are not covered in this
policy, an employee association representative must obtain approval from his/
her respective supervisor to take available paid leave time off work. Examples
of these other circumstances include, but are not necessarily limited to:
appearing as a witness in a grievance matter; or, discussing terms and
conditions of employment not initiated by the administration.
   F.   Unpaid Time; Request: Elected representatives of recognized employee
associations in the City may request unpaid time off work. (See personal leave
policy.) Employees who are not elected representatives of recognized employee
associations in the City must use any available and applicable leave (paid or
unpaid) for all association business.
   G.   Other Activities Not Allowed: No other activities will be allowed on
City time or using City facilities without written approval by the Chief
Administrative Officer. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018; amd. Adm. Order 2022-
11, 12-12-2022)
4-16: LEGISLATIVE LEAVE:
The City may grant leaves of absence for employees who are duly elected or
appointed to serve as members of the Utah State Senate or House of
Representatives under the following conditions:
   A.   Eligibility: Only full time employees are eligible to request paid
legislative leave as described in this policy.
   B.   Paid Leave: In any one calendar year, eligible employees who are duly
elected or appointed members of the Utah State Legislature may take legislative
leave with pay to fulfill their legislative duties in an amount equal to the
regular working hours in a single pay period applicable to that employee. (As
example, the paid legislative leave available for an employee not working
shifts would be 80 hours; for sworn fire personnel working shifts, the
available paid legislative leave would be 96 hours.)
   C.   Leave Of Absence: Employees who are duly elected or appointed members
of the Utah State Legislature may take unpaid leaves of absence to fulfill
their legislative duties. Such unpaid leave will only be granted for time
during which the employee receives compensation for service in the legislative
office. An employee may take available vacation leave or accrued compensatory
time during any leave of absence.
   D.   Health Insurance: Subject to the terms, conditions and limitations of
the applicable plans, the City will continue to provide health insurance
benefits for the period of legislative leave, whether paid or unpaid.
   E.   Benefits: Benefit accruals such as vacation, sick leave or holiday
benefits will be suspended during the period of legislative leave for the
period of the general legislative session only and will resume upon return to
active employment. Seniority will not continue to accrue during any unpaid
leave including personal leave.
   F.   Use Of Other Available Leave: An employee is required to take any
applicable and available paid leave (exclusive of sick leave), including
accrued compensatory time before the commencement of any paid legislative
leave. However, an employee may retain a balance of eighty (80) hours (112
hours for sworn firefighters) in the employee's vacation leave account (and
still use legislative leave as provided herein), which vacation leave may be
held by the employee for nonlegislative uses.
   G.   Flex Schedule: If it is in the best interest of the City and approved
by the department director, an employee who serves in the State Legislature may
work a flexible schedule during the period of any legislative leave to minimize
the use of legislative leave.
   H.   Approval: The use of paid legislative leave is subject to the approval
of the Chief Administrative Officer who shall not refuse such approval unless
the absence of the employee from City service for legislative leave creates an
undue hardship in a critical area. Employees considering running for State
Legislative Office are encouraged to consult with the Chief Administrative
Officer and their department director to determine if their absence would
create such a hardship.
   I.   Exempt Employees: Nonmerit, special employees with FLSA exempt status
who continue to carry on their daily management duties intermittently while
also engaged in legislative activities, may upon approval of the Mayor, receive
their regular City salary for those workdays in which they are involved in both
legislative and City duties. As a condition of this accommodation, the employee
shall agree to pay to the City any legislative salary received for workdays for
which the employee is paid a City salary, less actual expenses incurred by the
employee for lodging near the Capitol during the general legislative session
that is not reimbursed by the State of Utah. The Mayor may withdraw approval
for this accommodation at any time if the Mayor determines that the
accommodation is unduly interfering with the employee's management duties.
   J.   Failure To Return; Termination: If an employee fails to report to work
promptly at the expiration of the approved leave period, the City will assume
that the employee has resigned. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018)
4-17: RESERVED:
(Reserved by Adm. Ord. 2023-5, 7-13-2023)
4-18: DISASTER SERVICE VOLUNTEER LEAVE:
   A.   Definitions: As used in this chapter:
   CERTIFIED DISASTER SERVICE VOLUNTEER: Any person who has completed the
necessary training for and has been certified as a disaster service specialist
by the American Red Cross, other approved Volunteer Organization Active in
Disasters (VOAD), or government agency.
   CITY: Any City office, officer, official, department, board, commission,
institution, bureau, agency, division, or unit of the City, including those
within the legislative branch of the City government.
   DISASTER: Any declared disaster or disaster designated at level III or
higher in the American National Red Cross regulations and procedures.
   VOLUNTEER ORGANIZATION: A member of the National Volunteer Organizations
Active in Disasters.
   B.   Leave Of Absence; Request For Leave; Approval By City:
      1.   A City employee who is a certified disaster service volunteer may be
granted leave from work with pay to participate in disaster relief services for
a volunteer organization in connection with any disaster, upon the request of
the volunteer organization for such employee's services. An employee will be
allowed up to one hundred twenty (120) hours of volunteer leave in any twelve
(12) month period. No additional costs will be provided, including but not
limited to overtime, per diem, or travel reimbursement. A City employee
requesting leave under this section shall file a written request with the
employee's supervisor, which includes:
         a.   The anticipated duration of the leave of absence;
         b.   The type of service the employee is to provide on behalf of the
volunteer organization;
         c.   The nature and location of the disaster where the employee's
services will be provided; and
         d.   A copy of the written agreement for the employee's services from
an official of the volunteer organization or government agency.
The employee agrees to present a report based on their disaster service leave
experience to the EOC and, if requested, to the department directors.
      2.   This leave will be approved by the Mayor or CAO upon recommendation
of the employee's department director. Factors included in the evaluation of
the leave shall include employee participation in the Ogden City EOC, benefit
to the employee, benefit to the City, and cost to the City of the employee's
absence. Nothing contained in this section shall be construed to require the
City to grant a City employee's request for voluntary disaster service leave if
the City determines, in its sole discretion, that the grant of leave would pose
a hardship on the City.
      3.   Volunteer service leave time will not be considered hours worked for
overtime purposes, and an employee on volunteer service leave will be
considered off-duty for purposes of worker's compensation and entitlement to
light duty.
      4.   A City employee requesting leave under this section shall complete a
Disaster Leave Request Form, on file with Human Resources, and get appropriate
approval signatures. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018)
4-19: ADDITIONAL LEAVE OF ABSENCE:
Additional unpaid leave of absence may be requested in writing and granted to
an employee at the discretion of the department director subject to other leave
policies in this manual. All available leave must be exhausted prior to unpaid
leave being approved. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018)
4-20: LEAVE ACCRUALS:
   A.   Accrual Of Paid Leave Benefits During Paid Leave: Eligible employees
who are actively at work or on paid leave, such as vacation leave, sick leave
or compensatory time, will continue to accrue paid leave benefits provided by
Ogden City.
   B.   Accrual Of Paid Leave Benefits During Unpaid Leave: Employees on unpaid
leave are not entitled to accrue paid- leave benefits. This includes employees
who are receiving income replacement benefits from a source other than Ogden
City payroll such as short-term disability, long-term disability, or workers'
compensation insurance. Accrual benefits will be pro-rated based on base hours
worked during the pay period cycle. (Adm. Order 2018-10, 11-29-2018)
CHAPTER 5
COMPENSATION
SECTION:
5-1: Pay Plan/Pay For Performance
5-2: Job Classifications
5-3: Pay For Certifications
5-4: Longevity/Loyalty Pay
5-5: Holiday Pay
5-6: Acting Positions; Qualifications
5-7: On Call Duty Pay
5-8: Callback Duty Pay
5-9: Overtime
5-10: Compensatory Time
5-11: Other Compensation Considerations
5-12: Canine Corps Pay
5-13: Differential Pay
5-14: Total Remuneration
5-15: Employee Referral Recruitment Incentive
5-1: PAY PLAN/PAY FOR PERFORMANCE:
   A.   Established: The city has a pay plan which is used to determine the
compensation range within specific limits for each employee's position.
Additionally, the compensation is broken down on a monthly, biweekly (which is
commensurate with the city's pay periods) and equivalent hourly. The city has
adopted a pay for performance system whereby an employee's compensation within
the pay range for the employee's position may be increased based on the results
of an annual performance evaluation.
   B.   Work Periods; Hours: The city provides differing work periods and/or
hours of work for employees in certain departments, such as police officers and
firefighters. These hours of work and work periods may not be the same as the
biweekly pay period.
   C.   Information Public Record: Specific compensation information on
individual employees is a matter of public record. Employees who have questions
about their present pay range for their position should contact the human
resources office. Supervisors may also review the pay plan information
regarding their staff upon request to the human resources office.
   D.   Pay Ranges: Ranges within job classifications establish a minimum and a
maximum base compensation which may otherwise be paid an employee, except for
other legitimate, authorized payments incidental to the performance of work
duties, such as overtime, on call and callback time, reimbursements for
approved educational assistance and business expenses, etc. The human resources
manager or the manager’s designee shall evaluate positions to determine whether
the pay range for a particular position should be adjusted based on
benchmarking of comparable Wasatch Front salaries. The human resources manager
shall report to the management services director any recommendations for pay
range adjustments to be considered in the annual budget.
   E.   Compensation Upon Initial Appointment: Except for certain qualified
reinstatement rights for eligible employees (see reinstatement rights policy in
this manual), initial appointment to any position in any range shall be made at
the lowest point of that range; provided, however, that the department director
may appoint a new hire to any point within the range specified for the
position, if it has been determined by the department director and the human
resources manager that there has been demonstrated an inability to recruit at
the minimum rate of pay or the new employee possesses qualifications warranting
employment at a higher rate in the pay range. Warranted qualifications may
include prior service, special skills or abilities, additional levels of
education, or other unique qualifications.
   F.   Performance Pay Increases/Bonuses:
      1.   Requirements Must Be Met: Performance pay increases or bonuses may
be granted to those employees who meet the requirements specified for such
increases or bonuses.
      2.   Eligibility For Salary Increase: A full time employee, other than an
elected official whose compensation is established by Ogden Municipal Code, who
meets or exceeds expectations based on his or her performance evaluation, and
who is not compensated at the top of the pay range for that employee's
position, may receive a salary or step increase. Where a performance pay
increase as determined by a department director would result in an employee's
compensation exceeding the range for that employee's position, the employee
shall receive the maximum possible salary increase without exceeding the range.
      3.   Eligibility For Bonus: A full time employee, other than an elected
official whose compensation is established by Ogden Municipal Code, who exceeds
expectations based on his or her performance evaluation, and who is compensated
at the top of the pay range for that employee's position, may receive a onetime
bonus. Bonuses may be spread out over the number of pay periods for that fiscal
year.
      4.   Determination Of Pay Increases/Bonuses: Subject to budgetary
constraints, the management services director shall recommend to the mayor and
the mayor shall recommend to the city council a fixed amount for an increase in
employee compensation, including salary increases and bonuses, with the
administration's annual proposed budget. Based on the amount appropriated by
the city council, department directors shall receive an allocation of funds
representing the department's proportion of compensation for authorized
positions in such department. Department directors shall apportion the funds
for salary increases or bonuses to eligible employees according to the range of
eligible performance evaluation scores. The management services director or
designee shall review performance evaluations for all city departments. In the
event of specific policy violations, the management services director may
recommend changes to the distribution of salary increases and bonuses upon
discussion with the responsible department director. The mayor or chief
administrative officer shall conduct a final review of the distribution of
salary increases and bonuses prior to implementation at the beginning of the
fiscal year.
      5.   Request For Review: Employees wishing to request a review of a
performance based salary decision shall be required to file such request for
review directly with their department director and with a copy to the human
resources office within five (5) days of the effective date of notification of
such salary increase or bonus, or within five (5) days of the first pay period
of the fiscal year, whichever is sooner, or they shall forfeit any and all
rights of grievance, appeal or review under this or any other policy provision
of the city contained in this manual. In the case of specific and more serious
matters, including, but not limited to, unlawful harassment or illegal
discrimination, the employee may file a written request for an administrative
hearing within fourteen (14) days from the final decision of the department
director. Such request shall be filed with the city recorder on a form
available through the city recorder's office. The procedure for administrative
hearings is discussed elsewhere in this manual.
   G.   Compensation Upon Promotion:
      1.   Full Time Merit And Non-Merit: Upon promotion to a higher job
classification, an employee shall be moved to the point in the new pay range
which is closest to a five percent (5%) increase in the employee's base
compensation that was in effect immediately prior to the promotion; provided,
however, that the department director may move the employee to any point within
the range specified for the position, if it has been determined by the
department director and the human resources manager that the promoted employee
possesses special skills, qualifications or experience warranting employment at
the higher rate in the pay range and the adjustment is commensurate with prior
adjustments provided to new hires currently filling the same position within
the same department.
      2.   Full Time Sworn Public Safety: Upon promotion to a higher sworn
public safety job classification an employee shall be moved to the first step
of the new pay range of the new position; provided, however, that the
department may move the employee to any step within the range specified for the
position. If it has been determined by the department director and the human
resources manager that the promoted employee possesses special skills,
qualifications or experience warranting employment at the higher rate in the
pay range and the adjustment is commensurate with prior adjustments provided to
new hires currently filling the same position within the same department.
   H.   Compensation Upon Demotion:
      1.   An employee, who is demoted to a job classification in a lower
compensation range than they last held immediately prior to the demotion, shall
be placed at a point in the new pay range which is closest to the compensation
that they were receiving prior to the demotion. The responsibility for ensuring
compliance with the terms and conditions of this policy shall lie with the
human resources officer.
   I.   Compensation Upon Transfer: An employee, who is the subject of a job
transfer from one position to another, shall be moved to an equivalent point in
the pay range of the newly held position.
   J.   Compensation Upon Upward Reclassification:
      1.   Full Time Merit And Non-Merit: An employee, who is the subject of a
job reclassification which moves the employee's job class at least one
classification higher in the pay plan, shall be moved to a point in the pay
range of the new job classification which is at least two and one-half percent
(2.5%) more than the compensation the employee was receiving immediately prior
to the reclassification.
      2.   Full Time Sworn Public Safety: An employee, who is the subject of a
job reclassification which moves the employee’s job class at least one
classification higher in the pay plan, shall be moved to a step in the pay
range of the new job classification which is at least two and one half percent
(2.5%) more than the compensation the employee was receiving immediately prior
to the reclassification. Specialty or differential pay will not be considered
for purposes of calculating placement in the new pay range.
   K.   Compensation Upon Downward Reclassification: An employee, who is the
subject of a job reclassification which moves their position at least one
classification lower in the compensation plan, shall have their rate of pay
frozen until such time as the range for that position is increased based on
benchmarking. Such employees are eligible for a bonus under the pay for
performance program. (See the performance pay increase/bonus policy in this
manual.)
   L.   Nonmonetary Compensation:
      1.   Employees who receive nonmonetary compensation in the form of
lodging, utilities or other similar elements of value, may have an equivalent
dollar amount deducted from their regular compensation. The city will rely upon
usual and customary accounting practices to the extent that any compensation
value is assigned for goods or products received as an outgrowth of work and
service performed on behalf of the city. Some guidelines are established by the
IRS as to what reasonable value should be assigned in such cases.
      2.   When employees receive nonmonetary compensation on a regular or
recurring basis, the reasonable value assigned shall be either deducted from
the employee's compensation, or that value may be added to the employee's total
taxable, reportable income for the year. The department of management services
is responsible for determining both value and proper reporting requirements.
Employees affected by this policy provision should direct their questions or
concerns to the comptroller's office. (Adm. Order 2010-4, 5-5-2010; Adm. Order
2019-6, 9-10-2019; Adm. Order 2020-8, 12-24-2020)
5-2: JOB CLASSIFICATIONS:
   A.   Classification Plan Description:
      1.   The classification plan of the city includes job descriptions for
each position within a department of the city. The classification plan reflects
the increasing complexity, demands and value of positions within the city. In
turn, the classification plan serves as a basis for establishing the pay plan
of the city, as each pay range is related to the nature of the work performed
in each position.
      2.   Within the classification plan, class levels or differing pay ranges
are established for certain positions reflecting the types and levels of
training, knowledge and experience required for certain maintenance, clerical,
managerial, technical, professional and administrative positions within the
city.
      3.   The relationship between related jobs and their attending pay ranges
helps establish training requirements to advance within jobs and work areas.
Similar relationships between jobs, or job "classes", help establish job
"families". Job families generally reflect those job descriptions and attending
pay ranges that can be grouped according to job functions. Examples of job
families include:
         a.   Clerical Jobs: These jobs exist within several departments, and
can be classed together to show the relationship between an entry level, a
journey level (greater knowledge) and an advanced journey level (greater
knowledge, experience and training) for a clerical job in any department of the
city.
         b.   Supervisory Jobs: These jobs exist within most departments, and
can be classed together to show the relationship between an entry level
(supervisory), manager (more supervision and responsibility) and director
(responsibility over entire departments and employees) job in any department of
the city.
      4.   The city uses specific job families and job classes to help identify
common levels of difficulty, responsibility and knowledge in jobs that will
compare similarly with each other, in order to help establish pay rates and pay
ranges for positions.
Employees are encouraged to find out more about their own job class or job
family by inquiring of their department director or the human resources office.
(Adm. Order 2010-4, 5-5-2010; Adm. Order 2019-6, 9-10-2019; Adm. Order 2020-8,
12-24-2020)
5-3: PAY FOR CERTIFICATIONS:
Spanish And American Sign Language Fluency: All nonmerit, special; full time;
part time; and special temporary employees, are eligible to receive one hundred
dollars ($100.00) per month upon demonstrating fluency in Spanish or American
Sign Language (ASL) and agreeing to utilize their Spanish or ASL speaking
skills in the workplace from time to time as needed. Certification will be
obtained under rules and procedures established by the Director of Management
Services. The additional compensation will be paid bi-weekly. An employee may
only receive certification for one language.
Employees interested in more information about the qualifications for, and
amounts of, certification pay are encouraged to contact their Department
Director or the Human Resources Office. (Adm. Order 2007-14, 5-15-2007; Adm.
Order 2019-6, 9-10-2019; Adm. Order 2020-8, 12-24-2020)
5-4: LONGEVITY/LOYALTY PAY:
   A.   Eligibility: Subject to the terms and conditions of this policy, all
full time merit (non-sworn) employees, who complete at least ten (10)
consecutive (or cumulative, except for breaks of service of not less than 6
months) years of employment for the City, shall be compensated with an
additional amount paid biweekly.
   B.   Compensation: Beginning on the tenth anniversary date of employment, an
eligible full-time merit (non-sworn) employee will be compensated at a rate of
ten dollars ($10.00) per month in longevity pay. Beginning on the eighteenth
anniversary date of employment, an eligible employee will be compensated an
additional ten dollars ($10.00) per month in longevity pay. Therefore,
beginning on the eighteenth anniversary date, the employee shall be compensated
at a total rate of twenty dollars ($20.00) per month in longevity pay.
   C.   Loyalty Pay; Full Time Sworn Public Safety: Sworn public safety
officers may receive loyalty pay incentives according to department policy. In
order to be eligible for the incentive, the employee must be a full-time
employee of the Ogden Police or Fire Department and must not be under
investigation for a disciplinary issue at the time the incentive is due.
Employees that separate from the Ogden City Police Department and are rehired
may be eligible to have previous service applied towards years of service for
the loyalty program with approval of the Human Resources Manager and Chief
Administrative Officer. (Adm. Order 2017-2, 4-17-2017; Adm. Order 2019-6, 9-10-
2019; Adm. Order 2020-8, 12-24-2020)
5-5: HOLIDAY PAY:
   A.   Additional Compensation For Specific Employees: Eligible "employees
working shift work", other than sworn fire personnel and certain eligible
employees required to work on a holiday, receive additional compensation as
holiday pay. (The designation of holidays and the definition of eligibility is
provided in the holiday policy of the leave section of this manual.)
   B.   Shift Work Employees Defined: For the purposes of this policy,
"employees working shift work" are merit employees or sworn public safety
employees, other than sworn fire personnel, who are assigned to work holidays
as part of their regular work assignment in order to provide required City
services.
   C.   Availability; Calculation: Additional compensation for holidays is
provided to all eligible employees immediately upon assignment to an eligible
employment classification. Additional compensation is calculated based on the
employee's base pay rate at the time of the holiday and does not include any
special forms of compensation, such as incentives, commissions or bonuses.
   D.   Pay Based On Actual Holiday: Although paid time off may be provided on
an observed rather than an actual holiday, holiday pay will be based on the
actual holiday for "employees working shift work", as defined herein.
   E.   Rate Of Pay: Except for "employees working shift work", if an eligible
employee is required to work on an observed holiday, hours worked are paid at a
rate of one and one-half (11/2) times their straight time, base pay rate, in
addition to receiving eight (8) hours of straight time pay for the holiday. If
such an employee is required to work on an actual holiday that falls on the
employee's regularly scheduled day off, hours worked are paid at a rate of one
and one-half (1 1/2) times their straight time, base pay rate.
   F.   Shift Employees: "Employees working shifts" in other than the Police
and Fire Departments, are compensated for holidays as follows: If such employee
works on an observed holiday, which falls on the employee's regularly scheduled
workday, the employee shall be paid for working the observed holiday at their
regular rate of pay plus eight (8) hours at a rate of one and one-half (1 1/2)
times their straight time, base pay rate. If such employee works on an observed
holiday that does not fall on the employee's regularly scheduled workday, the
employee shall be paid at the rate of one and one-half (1 1/2) times their
straight time, base pay rate, for the actual hours worked, plus eight (8) hours
of straight time holiday pay. The employee will be paid the greater of actual
hours worked on the holiday or all hours worked after the 40 hour overtime rule
has been met. If such employee does not work on the observed holiday, such
employee shall receive eight (8) hours of straight time holiday pay. (The
latter circumstance may arise due to use of vacation or sick leave or because
the employee's regularly scheduled workday does not fall on the observed
holiday.)
   G.   Sworn Police Officers: Sworn police officers working shifts are
compensated for holidays (excluding Arbor Day benefit) falling within their
regular work period, whether worked or not, by receiving one and one-half (1 1/
2) times their straight time, base pay rate for the eight (8) hour holiday.
   H.   Two Day Shift: If "employees working shifts" work a shift that spans a
two (2) day period, one (1) of which is a holiday, any holiday pay, as provided
above, for working on a holiday shall be limited to the hours falling within
the twenty four (24) hours constituting the applicable holiday.
   I.   Sworn Fire Personnel: Sworn fire personnel working two thousand nine
hundred twelve (2,912) annual hours are compensated for working holidays at
their regular rate of pay, as if the day were not a holiday. These employees
receive additional paid time off for holidays as provided in the holiday policy
found in the leave section of this manual.
   J.   Exempt Employees: Exempt employees are paid on the basis of set
compensation and are compensated for all holidays based on that compensation.
If an exempt employee works on a holiday, they are not compensated additionally
for such work. Notwithstanding the above, Lieutenants in the Police Department,
who are regularly assigned to work as watch commanders, shall receive holiday
pay equal to sworn police officers working shifts for any holiday falling
within any work period in which such assignment as a watch commander is
effective. Lieutenants not assigned as watch commanders (i.e., Staff
Lieutenants) shall be treated as other exempt employees.
   K.   Terms And Conditions: As with all benefits of the City, the terms and
conditions of holiday pay are subject to continued funding and appropriate City
Council authorization. These benefits are provided subject to a variety of
conditions and factors including, but not limited to, the financial ability of
the City and the resources available to the City to continue to fund the cost
of holiday benefits.
   L.   Policy: For the purpose of implementation and clarification of the
above policies, a department policy may be established, if it is not in
conflict with this policy and is approved in writing by the Chief
Administrative Officer. (Eff. 6-1-1996; Adm. Order 2005-2, 2-23-2005; Adm.
Order 2019-6, 9-10-2019; Adm. Order 2020-8, 12-24-2020)
5-6: ACTING POSITIONS; QUALIFICATIONS:
Subject to the terms and conditions of this policy, it is the intent of the
City to provide a framework and guideline within which eligible employees may
be appointed to acting positions.
   A.   Applicability: This policy applies only to merit service and sworn
public safety service employees who are being appointed to acting positions.
This does not include temporary change of assignment in the Police or Fire
Departments even where there is a change of remuneration.
   B.   Placement Decision: The decision to place an employee in an acting
position of another person or position shall be made by the Department
Director, except where the acting position is subject to appointment by the
Chief Administrative Officer or the Mayor. An employee is appointed temporarily
(due to a vacancy or the temporary absence of an incumbent) to an acting
position of higher compensation and authority, only when he/she assumes all the
functions and authority of the higher position. Appointments shall be reflected
by approval of a personnel action form.
   C.   Compensation; Full Time Merit And Non-Merit: Subject to the terms and
conditions of this policy, an employee performing work and service within the
scope and role of an acting position, as provided herein, shall enjoy the
benefit of additional compensation for such work and service. When additional
compensation is allowed for such service, an employee shall be compensated at
the lowest point in the pay range for the acting position that results in a
minimum of a five percent (5%) increase in the employee's base compensation
that was in effect immediately prior to the temporary appointment or to the
minimum of the pay range of an acting position if greater than five percent
(5%). Except for certain employees working shift work within the sworn public
safety service as provided below, an employee shall be compensated only for
service in an acting position if the time in service equals or exceeds thirty
(30) consecutive days. Employees who meet the thirty (30) day requirement in an
acting position will be eligible for acting pay starting on day thirty one
(31). Acting pay will not be retroactive to the first day in the acting
position.
      1.   Sworn police personnel performing service in an acting position
which is assigned to a ten (10) hour work shift, shall be compensated only for
service in an acting position if the time in service equals at least four (4)
consecutive full ten (10) hour shifts. Once this criteria is met, the
additional compensation begins from the first hour of the acting assignment and
will subsequently be paid for any consecutive work hours. Employee shall be
compensated at the first step of the acting position.
      2.   Sworn fire personnel performing service in an acting position which
is assigned to a forty eight (48) hour work shift, shall be compensated only
for service in an acting position if the time in service equals at least one
(1) full twenty four (24) hour shift. Once this criteria is met, the additional
compensation begins from the first hour of the acting assignment and will
subsequently be paid for any consecutive work hours.
   D.   Prohibited Employees: It is the policy of the City to prohibit any
employee from serving in any acting role, position or capacity, who is the
subject of any current, ongoing or open disciplinary investigation, review or
action, or who has been the subject of any disciplinary action within ninety
(90) days preceding any consideration for any acting role, position or
capacity.
   E.   Maximum Time: The maximum length of time any employee shall be allowed
to perform work and service in an acting position or capacity is twelve (12)
consecutive months. Should the position still be open at the end of twelve (12)
consecutive months, the Department Director, the Chief Administrative Officer
or the Mayor, as applicable, shall act to either fill the position or it shall
cease to exist as applicable. (Adm. Order 2017-2, 4-17-2017; Adm. Order 2019-6,
9-10-2019; Adm. Order 2020-8, 12-24-2020)
5-7: ON CALL DUTY PAY:
   A.   Applicable Employees: This policy applies to employees of the City who
are required to serve in an "on call" status and be available for a call back
to work for up to a week at a time during otherwise unscheduled, off duty
hours. These employees are generally assigned communication devices and
procedures, and are allowed to drive City vehicles home after working hours to
aid in response time for any call to work. On call employees are expected to
comply with the City's fitness for duty policy during this on call period. (See
also overtime policy, Administrative Policy Manual, as applicable.)
   B.   Compensation: It is the policy of the City to pay these specifically
designated on call employees a minimum of sixteen (16) hours of overtime for
each week in which they serve in a paid on call or callback status. If the
employee serves less than one (1) full workweek in this status, the number of
hours of applicable overtime will be prorated. When and if an employee in this
capacity performs actual work and service as a result of being called back to
work, they will be paid any additional overtime for hours worked in excess of
the first sixteen (16) hours. Information Technology Division nonexempt
employees will receive two (2) hours of overtime for being on call from 17:00
to 08:00 and three (3) hours for being "on call" from 08:00 to 08:00 (full 24
hours). When and if an IT employee in this capacity performs actual work and
service as a result of being called back to work, they will be paid any
additional overtime for hours worked in excess of the first two (2), or three
(3), hours of overtime, as specified above.
Departments and/or divisions may have additional on call or callback procedures
if department policy is approved and on file with the human resources office.
Policy must be approved by the department director and Chief Administrative
Officer in conjunction with the human resources division. (Adm. Order 2012-17,
12-7-2012; Adm. Order 2019-6, 9-10-2019; Adm. Order 2020-8, 12-24-2020)
5-8: CALLBACK DUTY PAY:
Sworn public safety and merit employees shall receive a two (2) hour minimum
amount of paid work time for any call back to duty during an otherwise
scheduled off duty workday, except that police officers providing scheduled
telephone testimony shall receive a one (1) hour minimum amount of paid work
time. If such callback time places the employee in an overtime situation, then
overtime is otherwise payable. Telephone calls from work to an off duty
employee are not considered callback duty, however, calls of fifteen (15)
minutes or longer may be eligible for compensation as paid work time. (See also
compensatory time off policy, work schedules and compensation plan policies in
this manual.) (Adm. Order 2017-2, 4-17-2017; Adm. Order 2019-6, 9-10-2019; Adm.
Order 2019-6, 9-10-2019)
5-9: OVERTIME:
   A.   Authority: When operating requirements or other needs cannot be met
during regular working hours, employees may be scheduled to work overtime
hours. When possible, advance notification of these mandatory assignments will
be provided. All overtime work must receive the Supervisor's prior
authorization. Overtime assignments will be distributed as equitably as
practical to all employees qualified to perform the required work.
   B.   Disciplinary Actions; Conditions: Failure to work scheduled overtime or
overtime worked without prior authorization from the Supervisor may result in
disciplinary action, up to and including possible termination of employment.
   C.   Eligible Employees: Overtime compensation is paid to all nonexempt
employees in accordance with Federal and State wage and hour restrictions. The
Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) sets forth certain conditions and procedures
under which overtime is to be determined. However, certain positions as defined
by FLSA may not require the payment of overtime, even if the employees in these
positions work over forty (40) hours in a week. Classification under FLSA must
be approved by the human resources office. Notwithstanding the above,
Lieutenants in the Police Department, who are regularly assigned to work as
watch commanders, shall receive overtime compensation equal to sworn police
officers for any work period in which such assignment as a watch commander is
effective. Lieutenants not assigned as watch commanders (i.e., Staff
Lieutenants) shall be treated as other exempt employees.
   D.   Rate Of Pay: All work and service activity performed for the City under
the direction and with the approval of supervisory staff shall be considered
compensable hours of work for the purposes of determining hours of work and
overtime calculations. Overtime shall be paid at a rate of time and one-half (1
1/2) the equivalent hourly, base wage rate.
   E.   Calculation Basis; Actual Hours Worked: Overtime pay is based on actual
hours worked. Paid time off, such as sick leave, vacation leave, holidays or
any other leave of absence will not be considered hours worked for purposes of
performing overtime calculations. Additional compensation, such as callback
duty pay or holiday pay that does not reflect actual hours worked or additional
compensation for special duty that already reflects overtime compensation shall
not be used to calculate additional overtime pay. Notwithstanding the above,
the following time may be used in the calculation of hours worked for purposes
of overtime:
      1.   Employees subject to callback and call out requirements in their
job, shall be allowed to include reasonable travel time directly associated
with travel to perform emergency or additional duties in the computation of
hours worked.
      2.   See also snow removal and overtime policies, Administrative Policy
Manual, as applicable.
   F.   Work Periods:
      1.   Sworn Fire Personnel: Sworn fire personnel (i.e., those employees
hired to provide direct fire suppression and emergency relief services) shall
be paid overtime based on FLSA guidelines for those hours over ninety one (91)
actually worked in a twelve (12) day work period. Overtime for these employees
will be paid on the first regularly scheduled payday falling at least one (1)
week after the end of the twelve (12) day work period in which the overtime
occurred.
      2.   Sworn Police Officers: Sworn police officers are paid overtime based
on FLSA guidelines for those hours over forty (40) actually worked in a seven
(7) day work period.
      3.   Other Nonexempt Employees: Other nonexempt employees (except sworn
fire personnel) are paid overtime based on those hours over forty (40) actually
worked in a seven (7) day work period. (See also work schedules; work periods
policy in this manual.) (Adm. Order 2012-17, 12-7-2012; Adm. Order 2019-6, 9-
10-2019; Adm. Order 2020-8, 12-24-2020)
5-10: COMPENSATORY TIME:
   A.   Development Of Policy: This compensatory time policy has been developed
through management-employee discussions and review. This policy reflects the
final "understanding" of management and employees regarding the City's existing
compensatory time policy.
   B.   Defined: "Compensatory time" is defined as the accrued time credits an
employee may use as paid time off work, subject to department and City policy,
at the employee's normal, regular base pay rate. Like the cash equivalent under
the City's overtime policy, employees earn one and one-half (1½) hours of
compensatory time for every hour worked after minimum overtime requirements
have been met.
   C.   Payout Option: Accumulated compensatory time may be paid out annually.
Any accumulated compensatory time that has not been used as of the final day of
the pay period which includes March 15, or December 15, depending on which date
is designated by the Department Director, may be paid out to the employee at
his/her regular base pay rate on the payday following the pay period which
includes March 15 or December 15. Department Directors shall designate in
writing which payout period is in effect for each division eligible to receive
compensatory time in lieu of overtime. Compensatory time may be carried forward
to a new calendar year or fiscal budget cycle but cannot exceed the stated
maximum as outlined below.
   D.   Merit Employees: Department Directors may choose by division to
compensate merit employees for overtime worked with cash or compensatory time.
Eligible employees accrue compensatory time in one-fourth (¼) increments at one
and one-half (1½) times their regular base pay rate for hours worked over forty
(40) in a workweek. Compensatory time for merit employees is allowed to
accumulate up to a maximum of one hundred (100) hours. When this maximum is
reached, all additional overtime hours worked must be paid in the payroll
period in which it was earned.
   E.   Sworn Police Officers: Full time sworn police officers accrue
compensatory time in one-fourth (¼) hour increments at time and one-half (1½)
of their regular base pay rate for hours worked over forty (40) in a work week.
Compensatory time for Police Department employees is allowed to accumulate up
to a maximum of one hundred twenty (120) hours. When this maximum is reached,
all additional overtime hours worked must be paid in the payroll period in
which it was earned. Accumulated compensatory time may be used at any time
pursuant to department leave usage requirements.
   F.   Full Time Public Services Employees: Compensatory time off is only
accrued in one-fourth (¼) hour increments at a rate of one and one-half (1½)
times the employee's base rate for hours worked over forty (40) in a workweek.
Compensatory time off is allowed to accumulate up to a maximum of two hundred
(200) hours. When this maximum is reached, all additional overtime hours worked
must be paid in the payroll period in which it was earned.
   G.   Time Off Plans:
      1.   As allowed under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), Ogden City's
policy allows the Supervisor of a nonexempt employee to schedule the employee
to work a differing number of hours during a pay period. This generally means
the employee works more hours during one (1) portion of a pay period, and less
hours during another portion of the same pay period. Time off plans are
designed to control or limit the accumulation, accrual or payment of earned
compensatory time or overtime pay by one (1) or more employees. Employees
benefit with reduced work periods while still earning their full time
compensation.
      2.   Department Directors can implement time off plans for one (1) or
more of their respective employees as a tool to better manage the time, staff,
money and other resources available to their department.
      3.   The following is an example of a time off plan:
      If the employee works fifty (50) hours in the first week of the pay
period, the first forty (40) hours are at straight time pay and the remaining
ten (10) hours must be credited at time and one-half (1½), or fifteen (15)
hours equivalent to straight time pay. In the second week of the pay period,
the employee is scheduled to work twenty five (25) hours only, and is off the
rest of the week. The employee earns full compensation, since fifteen (15)
hours of equivalent straight time pay is carried into the second week from the
first week. (Adm. Order 2017-2, 4-17-2017; Adm. Order 2019-6, 9-10-2019; Adm.
Order 2020-8, 12-24-2020; Ord. 2021-2, 7-13-2021; Adm. Order 2022-8, 11-15-
2022; Adm. Order 2023-3, 5-4-2023)
5-11: OTHER COMPENSATION CONSIDERATIONS:
   A.   Additional Work And Service: Employees who are eligible for overtime
compensation may be required to perform additional work and service outside
their regular job duties that relate to and support the functions of their
primary job duties and the needs of the department.
   B.   Approval; Assignment: Additional work and service outside regular job
duties may be approved and assigned through established authority and performed
while at work and/or during scheduled work times. Such additional work or
service shall be compensated as part of the employee's regular pay or
compensation and is subject to applicable overtime based on the employee's
regular, base pay rate. While not all inclusive, examples of additional duties
and services are: training or instruction (on a formal or informal basis);
assisting another employee in completion of their own duties; or, temporary
work performed outside the normal duties and functions within an employee's job
description. A special consideration is given to police officers who train,
handle and board a member of the City's Canine Corps on their own time and at
their own residence. (See Canine Corps pay policy in this manual.) (Eff. 6-1-
1996; Adm. Order 2019-6, 9-10-2019)
5-12: CANINE CORPS PAY:
   A.   Rate Of Compensation: The City provides additional compensation to
police officers who are assigned the care, training and handling of any member
(s) of the City's Canine Corps. This compensation is based on an overtime pay
rate of time and one-half (11/2) the employee's regular, base pay rate. The
assigned officer is compensated at a rate equivalent to five (5) hours of
overtime each week, which is otherwise stated as seven and one-half (71/2)
hours of equivalent straight time pay.
   B.   Pay Irrespective Of Hours Worked: Since the care, training and handling
of any member(s) of the Canine Corps generally occurs at the police officer's
