place of residence, and includes hours outside the normal work schedule, the
City pays this equivalent overtime rate each week irrespective of the actual
hours the employee works, and irrespective of whether the employee is on
vacation or other paid time off during each week. (Eff. 6-1-1996; Adm. Order
2019-6, 9-10-2019)
5-13: DIFFERENTIAL PAY:
   A.   Rate of Compensation: The city provides additional compensation to
employees who are assigned specific afternoon and graveyard shifts. This
compensation is a percentage based on the employee's base pay wages.
Definitions of a primary, afternoon, and graveyard shift schedules are
determined by the Department Director and approved by the Chief Administrative
Officer.
   B.   Approval; Assignment: Differential compensation may be approved and
assigned through established authority and subject to budgetary restrictions.
For the purpose of implementation and clarification of the differential policy,
a department policy may be established, if it is not in conflict with this
policy and is approved in writing by the Chief Administrative Officer. (Adm.
Order 2019-6, 9-10-2019)
5-14: TOTAL REMUNERATION:
It is the policy of the City that employees are compensated based on an adopted
pay plan and approved compensation and benefits. Each compensation rate
established in the pay plan for any position shall represent the total
remuneration for that position, exclusive of any other additional pay,
reimbursement or compensation authorized by City policy or ordinance. Employees
shall receive pay from the City based on the compensation authorized in the pay
plan and in compliance with applicable policy/ordinance, for services rendered
by the employee, either in the discharge of the employee's ordinary duties or
of any additional duties that may be assigned. No employee shall be paid based
on any service or activity which the employee may volunteer to perform outside
those authorized and approved by established policy or procedure. Likewise, no
employee shall be allowed or suffered to work in his/her assigned job or duties
without receiving or being paid applicable compensation for such work. These
restrictions shall not prevent payment of funds to, or for the benefit of,
employees for retirement benefits, medical insurance or any other benefit
approved in the Ogden City budget.
(Eff. 6-1-1996; Adm. Order 2019-6, 9-10-2019)
5-15: EMPLOYEE REFERRAL RECRUITMENT INCENTIVE:
   A.   Ogden City employee referral program: A one thousand six hundred
dollars ($1,600.00) tiered incentive will be awarded to any eligible full-time
employee who refers an individual for employment as a full-time employee. In
order to qualify for the first tier of incentive pay, the referred individual
must complete the hiring process and commence city employment; this does not
include "conditional" job offers.
   B.   Eligible Employees: All full-time employees are eligible to receive the
referral incentive, except department directors, division managers, employees
directly involved in community outreach, or those who participate in department
authorized recruiting events.
   C.   Tiered Incentive: An eligible employee who referred a new city employee
may receive a total of one thousand six hundred dollars ($1,600.00) in referral
incentive, with a tiered payout based on progress of the referred employee:
      1.   An eligible referring employee will receive six hundred dollars
($600.00) upon commencement of city employment by the referred employee. A
"conditional" job offer, without actual employment, does not qualify.
      2.   An eligible referring employee will receive five hundred dollars
($500.00) at the completion of a referred employee's one hundred and eighty
(180) calendar day introductory period.
      3.   An eligible referring employee will receive five hundred dollars
($500.00) upon the completion of a referred employee's one-year anniversary of
hire.
   D.   Procedure:
      1.   An employee wanting to make a referral shall complete an employee
referral form. The form must be submitted to the HR office for approval prior
to the applicant completing an online application.
      2.   The form must be submitted to the HR office to verify eligibility
and to track the hiring process. The department director will approve payments
to the referring employee upon timeline completions of referred employee.
      Employees interested in more information about the qualifications for,
and amounts of, recruitment pay are encouraged to contact their Department
Director, or the Human Resources Office.
   E.   Policy: For the purpose of implementation and clarification of the
above policy, a department may establish a supplementary policy, if it is not
in conflict with this policy and is approved in writing by the Chief
Administrative Officer.
(Adm. Order 2023-6, 10-11-2023)
CHAPTER 6
TIMEKEEPING; PAYROLL
SECTION:
6-1: Timekeeping
6-2: Work Schedules; Work Periods
6-3: Flexible Scheduling; Time-Off Plans

6-5: Rest And Meal Periods
6-6: Travel Time

6-9: Pay Deductions And Setoffs
6-10: Administrative Pay Corrections
6-11: Direct Deposit
6-12: Telecommuting
6-1: TIMEKEEPING:
   A.   Employee Responsibility: Accurately recording time worked is the
responsibility of every nonexempt employee. Federal and state laws require the
city to keep an accurate record of time worked in order to calculate employee
pay and benefits. Time worked is all the time actually spent on the job
performing assigned duties.
   B.   Accurate Records: Nonexempt employees should accurately record the time
they begin and end their work, as well as the beginning and ending time of each
meal period. They should also record the beginning and ending time of any split
shift or departure from work for personal reasons. Overtime work must always be
approved before it is performed.
   C.   Altering Or Tampering: Altering, falsifying, tampering with time
records or one employee recording their time on another employee's time record
may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of
employment.
   D.   Scheduled Time: Nonexempt employees should report to work in sufficient
time to be at work and work ready when scheduled. These employees are not
permitted to stay after their scheduled stop time without expressed prior
authorization from their supervisor.
   E.   Review; Corrections Or Modifications: It is the employee's
responsibility to record his or her time to verify the accuracy of all time
recorded. The supervisor will review and then initial the time record before
submitting it for payroll processing. In addition, if corrections or
modifications are made to the time record, both the employee and the supervisor
must verify the accuracy of the changes by initialing the time record. (Eff. 6-
1-1996)
6-2: WORK SCHEDULES; WORK PERIODS:
   A.   Normal Work Schedule: The normal work schedule for most employees is
eight (8) hours a day, five (5) days a week. Generally, these employees are
scheduled to begin work at eight o'clock (8:00) A.M. and end work at five
o'clock (5:00) P.M., Monday through Friday. However, these hours or days may
vary, depending upon the nature of work requirements and departmental
functions. Work schedules which vary from the above general rule may be
established by the applicable department director or supervisor. Examples of
differing work schedules would commonly involve shift work, such as in public
safety or public works, or could involve flexible scheduling under flexible
scheduling/time-off plans policy found elsewhere in this manual.
   B.   Pay Period: The city's pay period for all employees is based on two (2)
consecutive weekly periods each which begins at one minute after twelve o'clock
(12:01) A.M. on Saturday and ends on the next Friday at twelve o'clock (12:00)
midnight. Due to operating requirements and work demands, each employee's own
work period may vary from the city's defined pay period.
   C.   Work Periods:
      1.   Except for sworn fire personnel working shifts, the work period for
all employees is based on a seven (7) day period, with no more than forty (40)
hours regularly scheduled within such seven (7) day period. Unless an
alternative seven (7) day work period has been established, an employee's work
period under conditions governed by the federal fair labor standards act (FLSA)
shall begin at one minute after twelve o'clock (12:01) A.M. on Saturday and end
at twelve o'clock (12:00) midnight on the following Friday. A department
director may establish a different beginning and ending date and time for such
seven (7) day period. Department directors shall inform the personnel manager,
in writing, of the beginning and ending day and time for any such seven (7) day
work period that varies from the general rule above. Information regarding the
establishment of alternative work periods shall be maintained in each
employee's personnel file.
      2.   The work period for all sworn fire personnel working shifts is a
twelve (12) day work period. The twelve (12) day work period is based upon a
work schedule of four (4), 24-hour shifts in a consecutive twelve (12) day
period, which shall begin at one minute after twelve o'clock (12:01) A.M. on
the beginning day of the twelve (12) day period established by the department
and end at twelve o'clock (12:00) midnight on the twelfth day, unless another
time is established by the fire chief. (This equates to 96 hours of time worked
in that scheduled work period. Under the standards established by the federal
fair labor standards act (FLSA), overtime hours actually worked above 91 hours
for these employees will be paid at time and one-half (11/2) the adjusted,
computed hourly wage base as determined for the work period.)
   D.   Schedule Provided To Employees: Supervisors shall inform employees of
their work schedules and applicable work period. Employees are expected to be
at work and ready to commence work at the start of their shift or established
work schedule, and to remain working in work activity until either an approved
break, or at the end of their scheduled work day or shift. Employees wishing to
leave at other times are required to check with and obtain approval of their
supervisor.
   E.   Recording Time Required; Violations: Supervisors and employees are
required to record all time spent in the performance of work duties in a manner
consistent with the established work periods, and with other applicable
policies regarding compensation. Violations of this policy shall result in
disciplinary action up to and including termination. (Eff. 6-1-1996)
6-3: FLEXIBLE SCHEDULING; TIME-OFF PLANS:
It is the policy of the city to provide work scheduling tools to supervisors
and department directors to help adequately manage their work force and direct
the scheduling of work in their respective departments. The city encourages the
use of flexible scheduling and time-off plans by supervisors and department
directors in order to meet workload demands and fulfill work requirements given
the limitations of funds, staff and other resources available to their
respective departments.
   A.   Flexible Scheduling: Flexible scheduling allows supervisors and
department directors to schedule one or more employees to come to, or leave,
work earlier during the normal work week, than the time normally allotted for
their positions or within the department. Examples of flexible scheduling are:
      1.   Example A: An employee has worked forty (40) hours in three (3)
days, and is normally scheduled to work another two (2) days in the remaining
portion of the work week. The employee is directed to leave work and not report
for those days remaining in the work week.
      2.   Example B: An employee normally starts work at eight o'clock (8:00)
A.M., gets a one-half (1/2) hour meal break and leaves work at four thirty
o'clock (4:30) P.M. The employee is told to report to work at six thirty
o'clock (6:30) A.M. for a training session, to take off work from twelve
o'clock (12:00) P.M. to two o'clock (2:00) P.M., and to return and work from
two o'clock (2:00) P.M. until five o'clock (5:00) P.M., increasing the total
number of hours worked in the day by one-half (1/2) hour, to a total of eight
and one-half (81/2) hours. (The employee may be eligible for overtime pay for
this pay period.)
   B.   Time-Off Plans: As stated in the compensatory time policy in this
manual, time-off plans are a tool available to supervisors and department
directors to direct and control the flow of work and work scheduling in an
effort to comply with budgetary restraints and still meet work demands. As
allowed under the fair labor standards act (FLSA), Ogden City's policy allows
the supervisor of a nonexempt employee to schedule the employee to work a
differing number of hours during a pay period. This generally means the
employee works more hours during one portion of a pay period, and less hours
during another portion of the same pay period. Time-off plans are designed to
control or limit the accumulation, accrual or payment of earned compensatory
time and/or overtime by one or more employees. Employees benefit with reduced
hours worked while still earning their full-time compensation. (See
compensatory time policy in this manual.) (Eff. 6-1-1996)
6-4: SUBSTITUTING; TRADING TIME:
   A.   Sworn Fire Personnel: The city allows only sworn fire personnel to
trade their scheduled hours or shifts of work under certain limited, qualifying
conditions. These employees must request and obtain approval from their
immediate supervisor and their department director in order to trade a
scheduled shift or work duty with another.
   B.   Overtime Not Permitted: Since overtime calculations must be made by the
city, as the employer, trading shifts or schedules of work will not be
permitted when any consequential overtime might occur. The fire chief is
responsible to keep accurate and current records on all trading time and must
accurately reflect such trading hours in time records submitted to the payroll
department.
   C.   Conditions Not Allowed: At no time will the city approve of any trading
of scheduled work or duty when either:
      1.   Proper approval has not been obtained; or
      2.   The safety and protection of the public would direct otherwise,
given the mission and duty of the department. (Eff. 6-1-1996)
6-5: REST AND MEAL PERIODS:
   A.   Rest Period: Each workday, most full-time nonexempt employees are
provided with up to two (2) rest periods. In some cases, department directors
may not allow for two (2) rest periods, due to the nature of the work. In such
cases, employees may be allowed to have beverages and even certain snacks at
their desk(s) throughout the work period. Supervisors will advise employees of
the regular rest period length and schedule. To the extent possible, rest
periods will be provided in the middle of work periods. Since this time is
counted and paid as time worked, employees must not be absent from their work
stations beyond the allotted rest period time.
   B.   Meal Period: All full-time regular employees are provided with one meal
period of thirty (30) to sixty (60) minutes in length each workday. Supervisors
will schedule meal periods to accommodate operating requirements. Unless
specifically designated as part of scheduled work time, employees will be
relieved of all active responsibilities and restrictions during meal periods.
When employees are relieved of all active responsibilities, they will not be
compensated for that time. (Eff. 6-1-1996)
6-6: TRAVEL TIME:
Reasonable travel time for call-back duty, emergency response, traveling
between work sites or traveling out of town on business during the normal work
schedule or working hours is compensable time and shall be payable to the
employee subject to the applicable terms and conditions of the federal fair
labor standards act. (Eff. 6-1-1996)
6-7: PAYDAYS:
   A.   Established: Employees are paid every other Friday (biweekly).
Generally, equivalent monthly/annual compensation is based on biweekly paydays.
Except where a work period differs from the pay period (e.g., sworn fire
personnel), each paycheck will include earnings for all work performed during
the work period as reported through the end of the previous payroll period.
   B.   Automatic Payroll Deposit: The city has established an automatic
payroll deposit program, which provides automatic transfers of an employee's
pay directly to the employee's bank account on each payday. This program
provides a benefit to all employees, in that they do not have to be physically
present to accept their paycheck on regularly scheduled paydays.
   C.   Weekends And Holidays: However, in the event that a regularly scheduled
payday falls on a day off, such as a weekend or holiday, then employees will
receive pay on the last day of work before the regularly scheduled payday.
   D.   Check Provided Only To Employee; Exceptions: Except in the case of a
compelling circumstance as determined by the city, it is the policy of the city
not to provide any employee's check to anyone other than the employee, if a
paycheck is to be picked up, rather than automatically deposited to the
employee's bank account.
   E.   Written Permission: With proper, advance notice and written record, an
employee may give written permission for someone else to pick up his/her
paycheck. Employees wishing to find out about this procedure should check
directly with payroll. (Eff. 6-1-1996)
6-8: PAY ADVANCES:
The city does not provide pay advances on unearned wages to employees. The city
believes that it provides reasonable incentives in its benefit and compensation
package. These benefits serve as the foundation and basis of certain income
security for employees. The city does not believe pay advances are in the best
interests of furthering an employee's work production or income security. Pay
advances would create additional, administrative work load and burden on the
city's administrative and accounting staff, which would be cumbersome and
increase the cost of operations. (Eff. 6-1-1996)
6-9: PAY DEDUCTIONS AND SETOFFS:
   A.   Required Deductions: The law requires that the city make certain
deductions from every employee's compensation. Among these are applicable
federal and state income taxes. The city also must deduct social security taxes
on employee's earnings up to a specified limit that is called the social
security "wage base". The city matches the amount of social security taxes paid
by the employee. Sworn police and firefighters are exempt from social security.
   B.   Voluntary Deductions: Voluntary pay deductions, such as health
insurance, life insurance and other benefits, are made at the written direction
of the employee. Voluntary deductions of this type can have restrictions placed
on the effective date and/or amount of the deduction. Such restrictions are
determined and controlled by the terms and conditions of the applicable plans,
benefits/policies for which the deductions are made.
   C.   Setoffs: Pay setoffs are court-ordered pay deductions that are taken by
the city and forwarded to another party who is authorized to receive them.
   D.   Questions: If you have questions concerning why deductions were made
from your paycheck or how deductions were calculated, your supervisor or the
payroll office can assist in having your questions answered. (Eff. 6-1-1996)
6-10: ADMINISTRATIVE PAY CORRECTIONS:
The city takes all reasonable steps to ensure that employees receive the
correct amount of pay in each paycheck and that employees are paid promptly on
the scheduled payday. In the unlikely event that there is an error in the
amount of pay, the employee should promptly bring the discrepancy to the
attention of the payroll office so that corrections can be made as quickly as
possible. To the extent the law allows, the city reserves the right, upon
discovery, to correct errors in pay and benefits by offsets in payroll or
through civil action(s). (Eff. 6-1-1996)
6-11: DIRECT DEPOSIT:
It is city policy that all employees are paid by direct deposit to their
respective checking or savings account. (Adm. Order 97-6, 7-21-1997)
6-12: TELECOMMUTING:
The city recognizes the benefits and limitations of telecommuting.
Telecommuting is an alternative work arrangement that may be appropriate for
some positions, at certain times, and in certain departments. Telecommuting is
at the sole discretion and convenience of the city and will not be allowed in
situations where the public or fellow employees may be unduly inconvenienced.
This policy allows executive directors to authorize employees to telecommute
for up to two (2) days of the employee’s workweek. In order to allow this
accommodation, both the employee as well as the employee’s current position
must be taken into consideration. If any exceptions to this policy need to be
made, these exceptions must be outlined in writing, approved by the executive
director and submitted to HR for the employee’s personnel file.
   A.   Definition: Telecommuting occurs when a city employee engages in either
short term or long-term city-required office work at a location other than his/
her primary work site. The alternative site may be the telecommuter's home, or
another location properly suited for such activities within the state of Utah.
Occasional off-site work assignments do not constitute telecommuting.
   B.   Eligibility: Individuals who desire to have a telecommuting agreement
must obtain written approval from the division director, and the department
executive director, prior to any telecommuting. Approvals must be documented
and agreed to by the employee on the standard telecommuting agreement form that
is available from the human resources office. By signing the form, the employee
agrees to abide by this policy as well as certain other conditions regarding
the telecommuting assignment.
      Before entering into any telecommuting agreement, the employee and
division director, with the assistance of the department executive director,
will evaluate the suitability of such an arrangement by considering the
following factors among other things.
      1.   Employee suitability: Do the employee’s needs and work habits meet
the criteria customarily recognized as appropriate for successful
telecommuters?
      2.   Reasoning: Teleworking is not an employee “right” but may be granted
when mutually beneficial to the employee and the City.
      3.   Balance: What is the correct balance for an employee to telecommute?
How often do the employees duties require that they be in the office?
      4.   Job responsibilities: Are the employee’s job responsibilities
appropriate for telecommuting.
      5.   Equipment needs, workspace design considerations and scheduling
issues: What are the employee’s physical workspace needs? Is the employee’s
proposed telecommuting location an appropriate and safe location for the
telework?
      6.   Tax and other legal implications: The employee must determine any
tax and legal implications under IRS, state, and local government laws, and/or
restrictions of working out of a home-based office. Responsibility for
fulfilling all obligations in this area rests solely with the employee.
   C.   Approval Procedures: If the employee, division director, and department
executive director agree, a telecommuting agreement will be prepared and signed
by all parties. As part of the telecommuting agreement, the division director
will develop work outcome measurements and objectives based on the employee’s
job description and duties to make sure that the telecommuting agreements do
not result in lower work productivity. After the agreement has been signed, a
three-month trial period will commence based on the terms of the agreement.
      1.   Trial period – During the first three months of the telecommuting
agreement, the employee and the division director will meet at least once a
week to discuss work quantity and quality. At the end of the three months, the
employee, division director, and department executive director will evaluate
the arrangement and determine whether the arrangement can continue, and/or
provide direction for modifications in expectations of the arrangement.
      2.   Long Term Telecommuting – After the trial period, the employee must
keep a running report of the employee’s time spent on daily tasks as well as
measurements and objectives. Telecommuters may work remotely for two days of
their workweek, and the remaining days in the City office. Employees will
provide their worklogs to their manager weekly. If the employee does not turn
in their weekly worklogs as well as other agreed upon measurements, the
division director may terminate the employee’s telecommuting agreement and/or
employ disciplinary measures.
   D.   Safety Considerations: Worksites are expected to be safely maintained.
Care shall be taken to ensure that office equipment does not overload
electrical circuits, and that circuit breakers and surge protectors are used
where appropriate. The city retains the right to make on-site inspections of
designated work sites at mutually agreed upon times.
   E.   Security: Consistent with the city’s expectations of information
security for employees working in the office, telecommuting employees will be
expected to ensure the protection of proprietary and customer information
accessible in their telecommuting work site. All sensitive information must be
stored in locked file cabinets. Regular password maintenance must be maintained
along with any other risk mitigating factors for all city information.
Telecommuters must also take appropriate action to protect the City’s equipment
from damage or theft. Upon termination of employment and/or termination of the
telecommuting agreement, all city property and all city equipment must be
returned to the employee’s division director or the IT director within seven
days.
   F.   Equipment and Costs: The telecommuting agreement will specify the
equipment, if any, that the city will provide for the telecommuter's
alternative work location. Each employee should procure necessary office
supplies through normal city procedures and must keep such equipment and
supplies separate from personal property. Employees are responsible for
ensuring reliable internet connectivity at the alternative work location. All
software used for telecommuting must be properly licensed and approved by the
IT director. Because telecommuting is an accommodation and voluntary for the
employee, Ogden City will not reimburse an employee for personal costs
associated with telework, such as personal phone plans/charges, internet fees,
or other alternative work location fees. The city will not reimburse the
telecommuter for any portion of rent or mortgage costs, related utilities or
commuting costs.
   G.   Travel: Employees will generally be subject to the normal timekeeping
policies while telecommuting. However, the time required to travel to and from
his/her telecommuting location will not be considered work time and will not be
compensated.
      1.   Non-Work: Employees who are telecommuting and perform non-work-
related tasks or attend to non-work-related items must clock out before
participating any non-work-related items. Telecommuters must clock back in upon
returning to the telecommuting work location and/or continuing to work. All
Employee time submissions should be approved through the employee’s division
director, approvals should follow the same guidelines and policies as when
employees are working at a City location.
   H.   Dependent Care: While telecommuting, the employee is responsible for
establishing and maintaining a suitable workspace and for providing a work
environment free of interruptions and distractions that would affect
performance. Telecommuting is not a substitute for dependent care.
Telecommuters with small children or other dependents unable to care for
themselves shall plan for dependent care during scheduled off-site work hours.
The focus of the arrangement must remain on job performance and meeting job
demands. The employee will remain accessible via telephone, email, and/or other
means of communication during agreed upon work hours.
   I.   Hours and Standards: Telework does not alter the basic terms and
conditions of employment including adherence to policies, wages, overtime
compensation, insurance benefits, paid leave, workers compensation, etc.
Employees will generally be subject to the normal timekeeping policies while
telecommuting. However, the time required to travel to and from his/her
telecommuting location will not be considered work time and will not be
compensated. During off-site working hours, the telecommuting employee is
expected to remain accessible via telephone and to notify his/her supervisor of
plans to leave the telecommuting location during the workday.
      All arrangements for childcare, elder care, home maintenance/repair
appointments etc., must be arranged to not interfere with the employee’s agreed
upon work schedule. If while working the employee experiences technical issues
with their computer or internet access that prevent the employee from working
remotely, the employee must notify their manager immediately. Interruptions to
work caused by internet outages may require the employee to work from their
regular city office location for the remainder of the day or until the issue is
resolved.
      Employees who are approved for telework must remain flexible in their
work arrangements. If an in-person meeting is scheduled on a day the employee
is scheduled to telework, the employee may be required to come into the office
to participate in the meeting. Attendance at such meetings is mandatory unless
otherwise directed by your division director. In accordance with city policy,
employees must clock out before commuting to and from the office. If the
manager/supervisor believes that performance standards are not being met or
that the telecommuting arrangement no longer benefits the city, the
telecommuting arrangement may be revoked at any time.
   J.   Exceptions: Exceptions to the limitations of this policy, including
enlargement of the two workdays per week telecommuting limitation, may only be
granted by the Chief Administrative Officer, in writing. Any exceptions granted
shall be documented in the telecommuting agreement entered into by the
employee. A previously granted exception may be withdrawn at the sole
discretion of the Chief Administrative Officer. (Adm. Order 99-6, 9-21-1999;
Adm. Order 2024-5, 10-1-2024)
CHAPTER 7
SAFETY AND WORK CONDITIONS

7-10: Responding To Citizens' Complaints

7-14: Responding To Threats And Violence
7-1: SAFETY:
   A.   Responsibilities: The city recognizes that each department within the
city, as well as the administration and all employees, have certain
responsibilities to uphold the integrity and value of the safety program for
the city. These responsibilities are designed to enable everyone to better
understand and enforce the procedures and purposes of the safety program.
   B.   Communication: The city provides information to employees about
workplace safety and health issues through regular internal communication
channels such supervisor-employee meetings, bulletin board postings, memos or
other written communications.
   C.   Training: Employees and supervisors receive periodic workplace safety
training. The training covers potential safety and health hazards and safe work
practices and procedures to eliminate or minimize hazards. This training may
consist of on-the-job training, equipment and hazards training, first aid and
CPR training; and may also include formal classroom training either on or off
the job.
   D.   Supervisor Responsibilities: Supervisors shall assume the
responsibility of thoroughly instructing their personnel of safe practices to
be observed in their work situations. They shall consistently enforce safety
standards and requirements, set the example of good safety practices and act
positively to eliminate any potential hazards within the activities under their
jurisdiction. Safety records shall be measured along with other phases of
supervisor performance. In discharging their responsibilities for safety,
supervisors shall:
      1.   Enforce all safety regulations in effect and make employees aware
that violations of safety rules may be cause for disciplinary action.
      2.   Ensure all injuries and/or accidents are reported promptly.
      3.   Conduct thorough investigations of all accidents and prevent
reoccurrence by implementing proper employee safety education, changes in
operating procedures, and/or appropriate modification of equipment.
      4.   Before work begins, provide employees with adequate and appropriate
safety instructions regarding their duties, obligations and functions with
respect to the work.
      5.   Before placing new or relocated equipment into operational service,
conduct careful examination and safety checks of the equipment and area of
service.
      6.   Ensure that equipment is properly stored when not in use, and
properly maintained and serviceable when in use.
      7.   On a regular and frequent basis inspect for unsafe practices and/or
conditions of work in progress and the work environment, and take appropriate
corrective action as applicable to ensure safe work practices and safe work
environments.
      8.   Maintain high standards of cleanliness and orderliness within the
work force and the work environment in all areas of operations under his/her
supervision.
      9.   Ensure proper and safe equipment and protective devices for each job
or work duty are available and in use based on knowledge of applicable safe
work standards and practices.
      10.   Conduct safety briefings at organizational meetings and encourage
employee implementation of safety suggestions as appropriate.
      11.   Provide full and active support to all safety procedures,
activities and programs within his/her area of supervision and influence.
   E.   Employee Responsibilities: Each employee is expected to obey safety
rules and to exercise caution in all work activities. Employees must
immediately report any unsafe condition to their supervisor or to the
appropriate supervisor. Employees who violate safety standards, who cause
hazardous or dangerous situations, or who fail to report or, where appropriate,
remedy such situations, may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and
including termination of employment. As examples of job responsibilities to
uphold safe work standards, employees shall:
      1.   Properly use safety equipment provided for work activity and the
completion of work assignments.
      2.   Where necessary or required, wear uniforms and safety gear properly.
      3.   Use or operate tools, equipment and machinery only when adequately
trained and proper orientation has been received for the safe use of such.
      4.   Report defective or hazardous equipment or maintenance problems
immediately to a supervisor. Assist where appropriate and directed to properly
tag or secure such items until proper repair or replacement procedures have
begun.
      5.   Refrain from the use or operation of unsafe tools, equipment or
vehicles until such has been properly replaced or repaired and placed back into
service by the employee's division manager or department director through
established procedures.
      6.   Warn coworkers and others as appropriate of unsafe conditions or
practices in which they may be engaged that are hazardous or could lead to harm
or injury.
      7.   Report dangerous, hazardous or unsafe work environment or physical
conditions that exist throughout the workplace or the city. Such conditions may
include, but not be limited to: defective sidewalks, obstructed traffic signs
or areas, broken curbs, hanging limbs in public access areas, open manholes and
missing or damaged pedestrian, school or traffic signs.
      8.   Report all injuries, mishaps or accidents to the supervisor
immediately, regardless of the perceived seriousness or severity, so that
appropriate correction or resolution can occur.
      9.   Protect the public and coworkers from unsafe or hazardous conditions
resulting from city work or work in progress.
      10.   Use all tools (either hand or power-driven) in an appropriate and
safe manner in the proper performance and application of the purpose for which
the tool was made.
      11.   In the case of accidents that result in injury, regardless of how
insignificant the injury may appear, employees should immediately notify their
appropriate supervisor. Such reports are necessary to comply with various laws,
city policies and initiate workers' compensation claims procedures. (Eff. 6-1-
1996)
7-2: RISK MANAGEMENT GUIDELINES:
   A.   Functions And Responsibilities: The risk management division shall be a
resource for the development, organization, coordination and implementation of
safety programs and safety education. Risk management functions may include
work-site inspections, hazard reduction and accident/injury investigations. The
risk management division shall advise department directors, division managers,
supervisors and employees of unsafe conditions and/or problems related to
accident prevention. As additional responsibilities within the functions of
safety program and education, the risk management division shall:
      1.   Prepare and maintain adequate reports, records and written
documentation on all accidents, incidents and injuries reported to the division
and coming under its jurisdiction.
      2.   Provide training records to the city's personnel office pertaining
to safety programs and education.
      3.   Coordinate the development, use and implementation of safety
educational material, program and information.
      4.   Conduct periodic safety inspections with departmental safety
committees, for the purposes of discovering, correcting and resolving any
unsafe conditions, practices or work situations that may exist.
      5.   Provide direct assistance, referral information and analysis to
departments through the department director and the departmental safety
committees.
      6.   Provide advice, guidance, recommendation and follow-up as
appropriate and applicable related to safety program implementation, training
and accident/injury prevention.
   B.   Guidelines: The city has set forth the following as general guidelines
under and around which employees and supervisors are expected to work and
perform their job functions safely and properly. Since these are only
guidelines, the city reserves the right to develop training programs, written
directives and other detailed procedures with which to enforce and expand upon
these general policy guidelines:
      1.   Immediate Job Task/Function:
         a.   In the immediate job task/function area of safety concern in the
workplace, employees need to be aware that safe work practices will ensure
their own safety by lessening the likelihood of injury to themselves, and
provide for the safety of others, both fellow employees and members of the
public.
         b.   All employees are expected to work in a manner which will help
protect themselves from undue back strain, improper bending or lifting, unsafe
or improper use of equipment or operational requirements. This includes the use
of protective wear (e.g., gloves, goggles, face masks) when working in and
around chemicals and/or equipment where such protective wear is required.
         c.   All employees are expected to keep their own work environment
organized and free of unnecessary clutter, spills or exposure(s) to hazardous
chemicals, vapors or materials.
      2.   Immediate Working Environment:
         a.   When working with the city or at any designated work site, and in
the performance of job tasks or functions, all employees are responsible to
keep the general working environment or area free from unnecessary risk to
their own and other's safety and health. All employees are directed to report
to their own, or the nearest supervisor, whichever is most appropriate, any
unsafe or potentially unsafe condition or circumstance with respect to their
general working environment.
         b.   Employees are required to wear proper protective and safety
clothing, articles, equipment and accessories when performing functions related
to potentially hazardous circumstances, chemicals, vapors or other conditions.
This includes the use of safety eye wear, face masks, respiration protection
equipment, hearing protection equipment, etc.
         c.   By way of an example of proper reporting requirements, if a floor
is observed to be wet and/or slippery, the employee making such an observation
has a duty to communicate that knowledge or perception to the nearest and most
appropriate supervisor right away. Likewise, if an employee notices any noxious
smells, vapors, noise or conditions which are not normal or usual, such should
be communicated right away to the nearest and most appropriate supervisor.
      3.   General Work Environment:
         a.   All employees have a duty and obligation to inform the nearest or
most appropriate supervisor or the department director right away of any
observation or knowledge of any unsafe or potentially dangerous circumstance,
smell, vapor, noise or event; even where such observation and knowledge occurs
outside the employee's own department or area. Likewise, all employees are
responsible for acting in a manner which shall prevent the occurrence of any
unsafe or potentially unsafe condition of any city facility, area or building
where they or others work.
         b.   As an example of expected protective and preventive action(s), if
an employee notices an icy walkway outside any city buildings or property, that
is near to or surrounds the area where others may walk or work, the employee
has a responsibility to report that information to the nearest and most
appropriate supervisor or the department director. (Eff. 6-1-1996)
7-3: TEMPORARY TRANSITIONAL DUTY WORK ASSIGNMENTS:
   A.   Position Qualification Policy: It is the policy of the city that
employees will be permitted to work only in positions for which they are
qualified and in which they are able to perform the job duties, tasks and
essential functions in a safe and proper manner.
   B.   Return To Work Policy: When employees have been off work due to an
injury, illness or disease, it is the city's policy to provide and encourage a
speedy return to work to the extent appropriate and practicable. It is the
experience of the city that employees, who are able to return to work quickly,
even on a limited basis, regain their full health, physical functioning and
abilities quicker and more completely than if they remain inactive and off work
for longer periods of time.
   C.   Limited Or Modified Restrictions: For medical reasons, a physician may
indicate an employee is not able to immediately return to full duty status, and
may release the employee to work with limited or temporary transitional duty
restrictions until the employee is able to completely and safely fulfill all
essential work duties and functions. Notwithstanding a medical report allowing
temporary transitional duty work, the city reserves the right to allow or deny
modified duty work assignments in its discretion.
   D.   Refusal of Temporary Transitional Duty: Refusal of temporary
transitional duty requires an employee to use vacation or compensatory time.
Employees are not able to use sick leave while off work for a workers
compensation injury if transitional duty work assignments are available and are
refused. A temporary transitional duty refusal form is required to be signed by
the employee, department director, and risk management.
   E.   Duration: Any temporary transitional duty assignments must be
immediately documented with a completed temporary transitional agreement form
indicating beginning date of work restrictions. Under no circumstances are
temporary transitional duty assignments to be permanent in nature or to extend
beyond a reasonable period of time. (See medical termination policy found
elsewhere in this manual.)
   F.   Examples: Examples of temporary transitional duty work assignments
include temporary assignments within the employee's department, and temporary
assignments in other city departments. The employee's appointing department
will remain financially accountable for wages for temporary transitional work
assignments.
   G.   Contacting Physicians: Risk Management may contact or request more
information from physicians to determine specific restrictions in providing
temporary transitional duty assignments.
   H.   Departmental Policies: Department directors may adopt department wide
non-work related temporary transitional duty policies not in conflict with city
policy or state or federal law. Such policies are subject to review and
approval by the city attorney and the CAO. (Adm. Order 2012-5, 3-16-2012; Adm.
Order 2023-5, 7-13-2023)
7-4: DISABLED WORKERS:
   A.   Accommodation: The city will consider a reasonable accommodation where
appropriate and necessary for an employee who has presented medical records
which set forth a specific and documented disability for which an accommodation
is requested. Such reasonable accommodation may include changes in the physical
or functional work methods, or the work conditions or environment, so long as
the employee can perform the essential functions of the job.
   B.   Confidentiality: Medical information on individual employees is treated
confidentially. The city will take reasonable precautions to protect such
information from inappropriate disclosure. Managers, supervisors and other
employees have a responsibility to respect and maintain the confidentiality of
employee medical information. Any employee inappropriately disclosing such
information is subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination
of employment. (Eff. 6-1-1996)
7-5: POSITION CERTIFICATION AND LICENSING REQUIREMENTS:
   A.   Loss Of Certification Or License: It is the policy of the city that
employees will be permitted to work only in positions for which they are
qualified and otherwise meet the minimum qualifications and requisites for
which they are employed. An employee is required to immediately report to their
department director the loss of certification or license necessary or required
to perform their job or fulfill the functions of their position. The loss of
any certification or license that is a necessary requisite to perform a job or
fulfill the function of a position in the city may result in discharge from
service with the city.
   B.   Included Losses: A loss of certification to perform a job may include,
but not be limited to, the following:
      1.   Suspension or revocation of a required professional license or
certification;
      2.   A limitation or revocation of a required driver's license; or
      3.   Suspension of a required license or certification to work.
   C.   Driver's Licenses: Employees who are required to operate certain motor
vehicles as part of their assigned duties or job tasks, shall possess a valid
commercial driver's license of the appropriate class to operate said motor
vehicles. They shall also possess a current DOT medical card indicating that
they have successfully completed a required DOT medical examination by a
healthcare provider that is listed on the national registry of certified
medical examiners.
Employees who are required to drive as part of their assigned duties or job
tasks, are required to report to their supervisor or department director as
soon as their license has been suspended, revoked or modified in any way.
Employees may not drive vehicles for which they do not have the appropriate
license, medical card or have not been properly trained. These responsibilities
are a condition of continued employment for any employee required to drive for
the city as part of their job or job function(s). (Adm. Order 2016-2, 4-22-
2016)
7-6: PERSONAL USE OF VEHICLES:
   A.   City Vehicles:
      1.   Subject to the terms and conditions of various city vehicle
policies, employees generally may only operate city vehicles as follows:
         a.   On city business when authorized or directed to do so;
         b.   Between home and work when authorized;
         c.   For minor, infrequent personal use during working hours if
permitted by department policy; or
         d.   For other circumstances as permitted by specific department
policy.
      2.   The city provides the use of city vehicles for personal use, such as
between home and work, at its sole discretion and solely as a privilege to its
employees.
      3.   The city shall not accept any claims of liability should its
equipment or vehicle(s) be used in a manner contrary to its intended purpose,
or outside the scope and controls of this policy.
      4.   The only individuals allowed in and around city operating equipment
or city vehicles are those otherwise approved and necessary within the
functions of the employees' normal scope and duties of their job. The city
prohibits any other individuals from being transported or provided
transportation in city vehicles, including for or in connection with personal
use of city equipment or vehicles. Notwithstanding the above, direct family
members of the employee, limited to spouse and children, may be transported in
the city vehicle to day care, school, or place of employment under the
following limitations:
         a.   All seat restraint laws will be followed.
         b.   Child car seats may be maintained in the trunk (not sure how to
do this with trucks) of the vehicle, but they will not be visible in the
interior of the vehicle unless they are occupied by the child.
         c.   The route is limited to direct travel to/from the residence and
day care, school, or place of employment and while the employee is going to/
from work or work related activities.
   B.   Personal Vehicles: It is the responsibility of each employee, who uses
their personal vehicle, to exercise proper caution, care and safety, with
respect to the use of their vehicle in the conduct of their work or city
affairs, or as an extension of their job function(s) or position. Employees
have a duty and obligation to act in a manner consistent with good citizenship,
respect and courtesy while using their personal vehicles for a business use or
business related activity of the city.
(Eff. 6-1-1996; Adm. Order 2020-2, 3-27-2020)
7-7: USE OF EQUIPMENT AND VEHICLES; REPORTING PROBLEMS, ACCIDENTS:
   A.   Damaged Or Defective Equipment: Equipment and vehicles essential in
accomplishing job duties are expensive and may be difficult to replace. When
using property, employees are expected to exercise care, perform required
maintenance and follow all operating instructions, safety standards and
guidelines.
      1.   It is required that employees notify their supervisor if any
equipment, machines, tools or vehicles appear to be damaged, defective or in
need of repair. Prompt reporting of damages, defects and the need for repairs
could prevent deterioration of equipment and possible injury to employees or
others. The supervisor can answer any questions about an employee's
responsibility for maintenance and care of equipment or vehicles used on the
job.
      2.   The improper, careless, negligent, destructive or unsafe use or
operation of equipment or vehicles, as well as excessive or preventable
accidents or violations, can result in disciplinary action, up to and including
termination of employment.
   B.   Reporting Of Accidents/Investigations:
      1.   Serious accidents, mishaps (including "near misses"), injuries and
traffic violations are required to be reported immediately to the appropriate
supervisor and the risk management office or the city attorney's office. Less
serious accidents, mishaps (including "near misses"), injuries and traffic
violations are required to be reported to the risk management office within two
(2) working days of their occurrence. Department directors and supervisors, as
well as involved employees, are responsible for the timely and accurate
reporting of accidents, mishaps, injuries and traffic violations. (See also
accident review committee policy in this manual.)
      2.   Employees who are directly involved in an accident or injury with
respect to work related activity are to speak only with law enforcement and
appropriate supervisory authority. Employees who witness or discover an
accident or injury with respect to work activity related to the city, may be
asked to assist in completing an incident or investigative report by law
enforcement authority or other appropriate management staff. Employees are to
provide as much as possible a clear and detailed factual report. In no event
should employees admit, or give opinions about, fault, blame or liability. It
is very important that the investigation be based on factual information, not
opinion or speculation.
      3.   It is the intent of the city to provide for prompt and appropriate
investigation, review and other proper action(s) with respect to determining
the cause of any accident or other event which may involve an issue of safety
for our employees, or the public whom we are called to serve. Accordingly, the
city takes seriously any accident or event involving the actual or potential
harm, or threat of harm, to any person(s) or their property.
   C.   Personal Liability: Employees can be held personally liable for any
loss or damage to person(s) or property for which they are responsible. This
liability can extend to the employee irrespective of any insurance coverage or
liability of the city.
   D.   Reasonable Precautions Taken: The city will take reasonable precautions
to avoid accidents or injury, and will act in a manner consistent with safe
work practice to help ensure prompt and appropriate attention to correct work
conditions or related problems so that unsafe conditions are dealt with
properly, and the causes of any unsafe event are determined, addressed and/or
corrected. (Eff. 6-1-1996)
7-8: ACCIDENT REVIEW COMMITTEE:
   A.   Policy Of Investigation; Rating Method: It is city policy to
investigate, review and analyze all accidents involving Ogden City motor
vehicles to determine the preventability of the accident. The city has
established a rating method for city owned motor vehicle accidents to reflect
the preventability of an accident under investigation and review.
   B.   Applicable Equipment: All motorized equipment capable of self-
propulsion, together with any trailer or other equipment attached thereto, that
is involved in an accident while used or employed for use in a work related
city activity or purpose, are included within the scope of this policy. This
includes city owned and personal vehicles as applicable.
   C.   Included Involvement; Reporting: A motor vehicle accident is any event
that results in personal injury or property damage that can be attributed to:
1) the motion of a vehicle or its load; or 2) some other cause, whether known
or unknown, resulting in damage to a vehicle. Any employee involved in a motor
vehicle accident, or who learns of an accident involving a motor vehicle within
the employee's care, custody, or control, is required to report the accident to
his/her supervisor, division manager or department director as soon as possible
after the accident and within twenty four (24) hours of occurrence. Involvement
includes a physical observation of an accident; a direct influence in an
accident; or participatory action in which an individual was directly affected
in an accident, whether or not injury occurred.
   D.   Investigations And Reporting:
      1.   Any employee involved in a motor vehicle accident is required to
remain on the scene of the accident until the proper legal authorities have
arrived, obtained the employee's statement, and have either released the
employee or detained the employee under custody. Any employee involved in a
motor vehicle accident is to provide his/her name, driver's license and
employment data to the driver of any other vehicles involved. Any other
information is to be provided only to proper investigating authority.
      2.   The employee's department director shall have the employee's
supervisor or other designated management member investigate the accident and
review available information and records to obtain factual evidence related to
the reason(s), conditions and preventability of the accident. Within two (2)
working days of the accident the department investigator shall complete the
supervisor's investigation report form and forward the report to the risk
management division and deliver a copy to the fleet division.
      3.   Whenever serious physical injury occurs in, or stems from, a motor
vehicle accident, the supervisor or department director shall report this
information immediately and as soon as possible to the risk management division
or the city attorney's office.
      4.   When any motor vehicle accident results in damage to an Ogden City
vehicle, regardless of damage amount, a vehicle damage report form must be
completed by the applicable employee and supervisor within two (2) days of the
accident and forwarded to the fleet and risk management divisions.
   E.   Review And Action: All accidents shall be reviewed by the accident
review committee, unless the risk manager, in his or her discretion, determines
that a particular accident was clearly nonpreventable. Nonpreventable accidents
shall nevertheless be reported to the risk management committee in the same
manner as preventable accidents. All nonpreventable accidents shall be reviewed
by the risk manager, or his or her designee, for compliance with reporting,
testing and other city policies.
All motor vehicle accidents and attending reports shall be reviewed by the
city's accident review committee. The accident review committee shall review
all motor vehicle accidents referred to it, including all available records,
documents and other evidence pertaining to any motor vehicle accident, to
determine the preventability of the accident. There shall be four (4)
classifications of preventability:
         Preventability Classification
         Nonpreventable
         Preventable - mitigating circumstances
         Preventable
         Preventable - reckless
The term "reckless" is defined as an accident in which city policy was grossly
disregarded, and/or the employee acted with wilful disregard for the
preservation of property and/or safety of self or others, and/or the employee's
actions were intentional.
The recommended disciplinary action for each classification is as follows:
Nonpreventable: No disciplinary action recommended.
Preventable - Mitigating Circumstances: Disciplinary action recommended for a
preventable accident with mitigating circumstances is a minimum of a verbal
warning. The department should consider any other documented disciplinary
actions or extenuating circumstances.
Preventable: Disciplinary action recommended for a preventable accident is a
minimum of a written warning up to a maximum of one day suspension without pay.
The department should consider any other documented disciplinary actions or
extenuating circumstances.
Preventable - Reckless: Disciplinary action recommended for a preventable
accident determined to be reckless is a minimum of a one day suspension without
pay up to a maximum of termination. The department should consider any other
documented disciplinary actions or extenuating circumstances.
   F.   Membership; Appointment: The accident review committee is made up of
five (5) city employees appointed by the chief administrative officer (CAO) who
serve until such time as released by the CAO. The accident review committee may
meet and take official action under the terms of this policy so long as three
(3) or more members are in attendance. Any member of the accident review
committee who believes they may have a conflict of interest shall report to the
rest of the committee such belief and information surrounding the potential
conflict and may refrain from any action with respect to the accident under
review before the committee. A committee member shall automatically be deemed
to have a conflict of interest if the employee being reviewed has a personal or
familial relationship with the employee.
   G.   Investigation Authority: The accident review committee shall have the
authority to initiate any investigation or action it deems necessary to
establish facts surrounding and involving the accident, including visiting the
accident location and interviewing witnesses. The employee involved in an
accident shall be directed to submit to the accident review committee either a
written and signed statement, or personal testimony before the committee, as to
the circumstances and events that were involved in the accident. Notice to the
employee shall be given seventy two (72) hours before the accident review date.
If the employee fails or refuses to provide such information or testimony as
requested, the committee may complete its investigation and render its decision
accordingly, or the committee may mandate that the employee appear at the next
regularly scheduled meeting. Failure to appear as directed by the committee may
subject the employee to disciplinary action to be determined by the employee's
department head.
   H.   Decision: The accident review committee shall issue a written decision
to the risk management committee that shall include findings of fact,
conclusions as to the cause of the accident under review (including determining
the preventability of the accident), and recommendations about what, if
anything, could have been done to prevent the accident, or might be done in the
future to prevent its reoccurrence. The committee shall also report whether all
applicable policies were carried out by the employee's supervisor, including
whether the fitness for duty policy related to drug and alcohol testing was
properly administered.
   I.   Risk Management Committee Consideration: The risk management committee
shall consider the findings of the accident review committee and forward same
along with their own findings and recommendations, when deemed appropriate, to
the employee, the employee's department director, division manager and the
personnel office. Preventable accidents shall be subject to disciplinary
action, up to and including termination, as deemed appropriate by the
employee's department director.
   J.   Confidentiality: Records, evidence and testimony of the accident review
committee and the risk management committee pertaining to accident
investigations and decisions shall be confidential. Discussions about and
pertaining to any ongoing investigation shall be confidential, and information
shall be provided to other management members of the city who have a legitimate
need to know within the scope of their authority and functions. (Adm. Order
2006-5, 5-9-2006)
7-9: LIFE THREATENING ILLNESSES IN THE WORKPLACE:
   A.   City Support; Conditions: Employees with life threatening illnesses,
such as cancer, heart disease and AIDS, often wish to continue their normal
pursuits, including work, to the extent allowed by their condition. The city
supports these endeavors as long as employees are able to meet acceptable
performance standards. As in the case of other disabilities, upon request the
city may make reasonable accommodations in accordance with all legal
requirements, to allow qualified employees with life threatening illnesses to
perform the essential functions of their jobs.
   B.   Confidentiality Of Medical Information: Medical information on
individual employees is treated confidentially. The city will take reasonable
precautions to protect such information from inappropriate disclosure. Managers
and other employees have a responsibility to respect and maintain the
confidentiality of employee medical information. Anyone inappropriately
disclosing such information is subject to disciplinary action, up to and
including termination of employment.
   C.   Questions: Employees with questions or concerns about life threatening
illnesses are encouraged to contact the personnel office or the city's employee
assistance program for information and referral to appropriate services and
resources. (Eff. 6-1-1996)
7-10: RESPONDING TO CITIZENS' COMPLAINTS:
It is the policy of the city to hear and respond in a reasonable, courteous and
open manner to all complaints from its citizens about services and functions of
the city, and treatment received from or by city employees. When an employee of
the city receives a complaint from a citizen, the employee is expected to
assist in a positive and appropriate resolution of the complaint and/or
correction of the problem to the degree the complaint or problem falls within
the scope and functions of the employee's job with the city. (Eff. 6-1-1996)
7-11: USE OF ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATIONS AND MAIL SYSTEMS:
   A.   Telephone Use:
      1.   To assure effective telephone communications, employees should use
an approved greeting and speak in a courteous and professional manner.
Information received from the caller should be confirmed. If the caller can be
better served by another city employee, the call should be transferred to that
employee in a courteous manner. Calls should not be disconnected until the
conversation is appropriately completed.
      2.   Personal use of telephones for long distance and other toll calls is
generally not permitted without reimbursement. The city reserves the right to
limit the frequency and length of personal telephone calls. The employee's duty
to serve the public must take priority over an employee's personal business.
Personal calls that are excessive and/or unnecessary are not acceptable and may
result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination.
   B.   Cellular Phone And Pager Use:
      1.   City assigned cellular phones and pagers, when provided, are for
official city business. Although employees may occasionally need to utilize
this equipment for personal reasons, personal use of cellular phones and pagers
should not be abused and is generally not permitted without reimbursement to
the city.
      2.   Cellular phones should not be used when landlines are available.
Calls made to cellular phones issued to employees should be limited to
important, critical or emergency circumstances.
      3.   The use of city assigned cellular phones and pagers is subject to
auditing and/or review by department directors and other city officials.
Employees who violate this policy may be subject to disciplinary action, up to
and including termination.
   C.   USPS Mail Use: The use of city paid postage for personal correspondence
is not permitted. In the interest of security and safety for all employees and
members of the public, all mail and parcels are subject to search and may be
opened and inspected at any time. Employees who do not wish to have personal
mail subject to inspection by others are advised not to allow such mail or
parcels to be sent from or delivered to the city.
   D.   Computer Use: City owned computer equipment is provided for city
purposes and is generally not to be used for personal business or use.
Employees abusing the privilege of the use of the city's computer equipment may
have the privilege withheld and may be subject to disciplinary action, up to
and including termination.
      1.   Employees should be aware that all systems and information are the
property of the city and will not become the private property of any city
employee. The city owns all legal rights to control, transfer, or use all or
any part of its systems. The city reserves the right to monitor, trace, review,
audit, access, intercept, log, block, resist, screen, delete, recover, restore,
publish, or disclose any information or network activity at any time without
notice, including electronic mail and all website communications and internet
browsing, and therefore, users should have no reasonable expectation of privacy
in the use of these resources.
      2.   Employees shall not allow unauthorized persons to use the city's
equipment or access unauthorized databases. Employees shall not move, alter, or
repair computer software, equipment or wiring, or connect any device to the
city's system without authorization from the information technology division
(IT).
      3.   Employees may transfer data files from work to home and back.
However, employees may not bring software to work from home or from other
sources. The city is committed to provide employees with software that is
necessary to perform their job requirements and will assume no liability
resulting from the use or misuse of unauthorized software on city owned
systems. Such unauthorized software may be removed upon detection without
notice.
      4.   All electronic files that are loaded from any sources into city
owned computers are to be scanned for viruses. Antivirus scanning software is
available for each computer workstation. Since employees may transfer data
files from work to home and back, the city has also acquired license to
distribute antivirus scanning software to employees for use on their home
computers to protect both employee's home computers and the city equipment from
viruses.
      5.   Employees are prohibited from using city computers or the city
computer network to:
         a.   Download, copy or play electronic games or similar forms of
entertainment;
         b.   Engage in personal commercial activities;
         c.   Engage in any activity which may compromise the security of any
city host computer;
         d.   Engage in any political, fundraising or lobbying activity. (Only
city authorized lobbying of federal or state government concerning municipal
issues is permitted);
         e.   Access accounts within or outside the city's computers and
communications facilities for which the employee is not authorized or does not
have a business need;
         f.   Knowingly or inadvertently spread computer viruses;
         g.   Distribute junk mail such as chain letters and commercial
advertisements;
         h.   Distribute confidential information without proper authorization,
including the distribution of private, protected or confidential records under
GRAMA (government records access management act) or section
2-7-3 of the Ogden municipal code;
         i.   Copy, disclose, transfer, examine, rename or change information
or programs belonging to another user without the user's permission;
         j.   Log on as another user, exchange network passwords, or read
another's electronic mail unless specifically authorized to do so;
         k.   Engage in any other similar activity after having been notified
that such activity constitutes an unacceptable use of the city computer system.
      6.   Occasional and incidental personal use of city computer equipment is
permitted so long as it does not interfere with the employee's regular work, or
violate any use restrictions provided in this policy. (Adm. Order 2015-1, 4-29-
2015)
   E.   Electronic Mail Use:
      1.   Electronic mail is the transmission of memos and other electronic
documents over electronic networks, including, but not limited to, the city's
computer network. Employees are advised that the confidentiality of electronic
mail cannot be guaranteed and should not consider such communication to be
private. The city may choose to monitor e-mail messages at any time and without
prior notice. Employees should always properly identify themselves to e-mail
recipients. Employees should only transmit e-mail messages to those city
employees and others that need such information. The content and tone of such
messages should be respectful and comply with all city policies governing
communication.
      2.   The city has the authority and responsibility to manage, control,
and delete junk mail to prevent the unnecessary or inappropriate use of
bandwidth and to ensure that illegal, unwanted, and unsolicited advertisements
are not received on the city network.
      3.   The city e-mail systems shall not be used for the creation or
distribution of any disruptive or offensive messages, including offensive
comments about race, gender, personal appearance, disability, age, sexual
orientation, religious beliefs and practices, political beliefs, national
origin, or in violation of the city sexual harassment policy. Employees who
receive any e-mails with this content from any employee should report the
matter to their supervisor immediately. Additionally, city e-mail services
shall not be used as a personal e-mail account, to send chain letters or jokes,
or to sign up for newsletters/promotional offers except as approved for
business purposes. City business requiring a mass mailing from a city e-mail
account shall be coordinated through IT.
      4.   City e-mail accounts shall not send or receive e-mails or
attachments larger than industry standards.
      5.   Employees shall not access e-mail accounts other than their own
unless approved by the department director, city attorney, CAO, or mayor.
      6.   Employees shall not spread spam e-mail from their city e-mail
account and shall not open e-mail from unknown senders. If an employee receives
spam e-mail they should notify IT immediately.
      7.   Employees shall not publish their city e-mail address in public
websites or in bulletin boards or forums, other than for city business.
      8.   City employees shall be responsible for classifying and storing
electronic documents according to the city's document retention policy.
      9.   The retention of this information is retained until administrative
need ends and then destroy.
      10.   City employees shall utilize e-mail encryption whenever
transmitting sensitive information outside Ogden City. (Adm. Order 2016-1, 1-
19-2016)
   F.   Internet Use:
      1.   General Policy: The internet is comprised of thousands of
interconnected networks, which provide digital pathways to millions of
information sites. The internet provides for file transfer, remote login,
electronic mail, news and other services. Ogden City employees are encouraged
to use the internet to its fullest potential to further the city's mission, to
provide services of the highest quality, to accomplish job responsibilities
more effectively, to discover new ways to enhance service, to promote staff
development, and to develop skills and knowledge. While the city recognizes
that these services are an effective means for making city departments more
efficient, accessible, and responsive to the public's needs, their availability
is open to abuse. Accordingly, the purpose of this policy is to give employees
guidance for the appropriate use of the internet.
      2.   Objectionable Material: There is a wide variety of information
available on the internet. Some individuals may find some information offensive
and objectionable. Employees should be aware that the city has no control over
and cannot, therefore, be responsible for the content of information available
on the internet.
      3.   Permitted Internet Uses:
         a.   City employees are encouraged to use the internet to locate
current and historical data from multiple sources worldwide for use in their
decision making processes.
         b.   The internet may be used by employees to conduct the city's
business within the city, with other governmental agencies, and with the
public. It can be used to publish the city's mission, function, structure,
goals, authority, address, phone numbers, information required by law, and
other information of general interest to the public.
         c.   Employees may use the internet to provide and exchange
information, to communicate with one another, to perform duties of a job more
effectively and less expensively, and to provide better service to taxpayers.
The internet may also be used to disseminate information, announcements, or
schedules with other employees, government agencies, businesses or the public.
         d.   Employees may retrieve data files from the internet.
         e.   Occasional and incidental personal use is permitted so long as it
does not interfere with the employee's regular work, or violate any use
restrictions provided in this policy.
         f.   Streaming media may be used only for city business. Streaming
entertainment content such as audio from radio stations or video from sites
such as YouTube.com is prohibited except for valid city business purposes such
as research or training. Request for temporary access to streaming
entertainment content shall be coordinated through an employee's department
director.
      4.   Unacceptable Internet Uses: It is unacceptable for any employee to
use, download, submit, publish, display, or transmit any information via any
city computer or network which:
         a.   Violates or infringes on the rights of any other person,
including the right to privacy;
         b.   Contains defamatory, false, inaccurate, abusive, obscene,
pornographic, profane, sexually oriented, and/or threatening language or
images;
         c.   Violates the city sexual harassment policy;
         d.   Restricts, inhibits, or disrupts other employees from using the
system or the efficiency of the computer systems;
         e.   Encourages the use of illegal or controlled substances;
         f.   Violates any federal, state, or local statute or policy;
         g.   Contains an offensive, harassing statement or statements which
disparage others based on race, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age,
disability, or political or religious beliefs;
         h.   Violates current copyright laws;
         i.   Is personal in nature, more than infrequent, interferes with an
employee's regular work, or is an application or service not authorized by an
employee's supervisor, including, but not limited to, unauthorized use of
Facebook, Twitter, blogs, video and audio streaming, and similar applications
or services.
   G.   Use Of Wireless Devices While Operating A Vehicle:
      1.   Ogden City does not require nor encourage its employees to use
portable wireless devices (e.g., cellphones, computers, or pagers) while
operating a vehicle for city business.
      2.   In the event an employee makes or receives a call prior to arriving
at his or her destination, the employee shall utilize a "hands free" system, or
safely pull off the roadway and/or stop the vehicle (e.g., at a traffic light)
prior to using the wireless device.
      3.   Pursuant to state law, text messaging is prohibited while operating
a vehicle. In addition, Ogden City prohibits using keyboard functions to dial,
or access electronic mail or the internet while operating a vehicle.
      4.   If an employee's use of a wireless device in violation of this
section is found to contribute to a preventable accident while operating a
vehicle for city business, disciplinary action may be taken, up to and
including termination.
      5.   This policy applies to an employee driving a personal or city owned
vehicle on city business.
      6.   This policy does not apply to the operation of handheld/eight
hundred (800) mhz radios or Nextell devices by emergency personnel or police
officers.
      7.   Employees may "sign out" a wireless headset from the IT department
that functions with cellphone voice dial capabilities. Supervisor approval is
required.
   H.   Electronic Message (Instant Messaging And Texting):
      1.   Electronic messaging is the transmission of business related
