correspondence that is routine or transitory and does not offer unique
information about agency functions or programs.
      2.   Electronic messaging content and use are subject to the same rules
as e-mail in terms of content and professionalism.
      3.   City employees shall be responsible for classifying and storing
electronic documents according to the city's document retention policy.
      4.   The retention of this information is retained until administrative
need ends and then destroy.
   I.   Penalties: Employees violating this and/or related policies may be
subject to corrective and disciplinary action. Violations will be reviewed on a
case by case basis. Discipline up to and including termination may be
appropriate depending on the nature of the violation and any other relative
facts and circumstances. A first time violation could result in termination and
in appropriate instances, civil action may be initiated. Additionally,
violators may be prosecuted criminally under city, state and federal law.
   J.   Questions: These guidelines do not address technologies that have not
been invented or implemented within the city, but may be used in the future.
Suggestions or questions regarding this policy should be directed to the IT
manager at 629-8722. (Adm. Order 2015-1, 4-29-2015)
7-12: NO SMOKING POLICY (UTAH INDOOR CLEAN AIR ACT):
   A.   Prohibited: In keeping with the Utah indoor clean air act and to
promote a safe and healthy work environment, it is city policy that smoking is
prohibited in all enclosed indoor places of public access and publicly owned
buildings and offices. No smoking signs shall be conspicuously posted on all
entrances or in a position clearly visible on entry into any public area or
building. As city vehicles are often considered places of employment, it is
city policy that smoking is also prohibited in all city vehicles.
   B.   Outdoor Smoking: Outdoor smoking is permitted only in designated
smoking areas at least twenty five feet (25') from any public access entry or
exit; and at least twenty five feet (25') from any open window where others are
commonly working and around which the public has access to enter or exit.
   C.   Applicability: This policy applies equally to all employees and members
of the public. Any employee, who observes someone violating this policy, is
required to bring the matter to the attention of their immediate supervisor or
department director. Supervisors and department directors have the
responsibility for enforcing the smoking policy of the city. (Eff. 6-1-1996)
7-13: SECURITY INSPECTIONS:
The city has adopted certain policies regarding the possession of illegal drugs
and alcohol and the possession of dangerous weapons or materials on the city's
premises. The city has provided desks, lockers and other storage devices for
the convenience of employees, as well as vehicles for the use of employees.
Such storage devices and vehicles remain the property of the city. Accordingly,
they, as well as any articles found within them, can be inspected by any agent
or representative of the city at any time, either with or without prior notice.
(Eff. 6-1-1996)
7-14: RESPONDING TO THREATS AND VIOLENCE:
The city maintains a zero tolerance policy toward any act of workplace
violence, or threats of violence, by any of its employees or the general
public.
   A.   Workplace Violence Defined: "Workplace violence" may include, but is
not limited to, verbal harassment or intimidation, threats to inflict physical
harm, unwarranted physical contact, vandalism, or any other act that creates a
hostile, abusive or intimidating work environment. Possession of dangerous
weapons or materials, such as firearms or explosives, except as required or
authorized within the employee's scope of employment, may also constitute
workplace violence. Workplace violence does not include reasonable force in the
defense of property, self or others.
   B.   Prohibited Conduct: Examples of prohibited conduct include, but are not
limited to:
      1.   Hitting, shoving, or physically restraining an individual.
      2.   Threatening to harm an individual or his/her family, friends,
associates, or property.
      3.   Making or sending harassing or threatening telephone calls, letters,
e-mails, or other forms of written or electronic communication.
      4.   Intimidating or attempting to coerce an employee to do wrongful acts
or acts that are contrary to the best interests of the city.
      5.   Harassing surveillance, stalking, and the wilful, malicious, and
repeated following of another person while making a credible threat with the
intent to place the other person in reasonable fear of his/her safety.
      6.   Making a suggestion or otherwise intimating that an act to injure
persons or property is appropriate.
      7.   Bizarre or offensive comments regarding violent events or behavior.
      8.   Unauthorized possession or inappropriate use of firearms, weapons,
or any other dangerous devices on city property.
   C.   Prevention Of Workplace Violence: The city is committed to providing a
safe work environment for its employees, which is free from intimidation,
threats, or violent acts. Prevention efforts include, but are not limited to,
advising employees of this policy through its inclusion in the employee manual,
informing employees of the sanctions for violating this policy, providing a
means to report incidents of violence without fear of reprisal, and developing
a procedure for investigating and enforcing this policy.
   D.   Reporting Workplace Violence:
      1.   Any city employee who is subjected to any of the behaviors listed
above or who observes or has knowledge of any violation of this policy shall
immediately report the incident to his/her supervisor or any management member
of the city administration. The employee should be prepared to identify (or
describe) the parties involved and disclose any information regarding the event
or situation without fear of reprisal. An employee should contact proper law
enforcement authorities directly and immediately if he/she believes that there
is a serious threat to her/her own safety or the safety of others.
      2.   Any supervisor or management member of the city administration who
becomes aware of a possible violation of this policy, whether firsthand or
through a subordinate, shall promptly advise the management services director
or his/her designee.
      3.   Notwithstanding the above, employees and supervisors are encouraged
to identify and defuse problems and conflicts as they arise in the workplace,
treating individuals with honesty and respect, utilizing open communication and
other techniques, as deemed appropriate under each particular circumstance.
   E.   Investigation Of Threats And Violent Incidents:
      1.   Complaints about city employees will be promptly investigated under
the direction of the management services director.
      2.   Investigations of criminal acts, whether perpetuated by city
employees or the general public, will be conducted by appropriate law
enforcement personnel.
      3.   In addition to ascertaining the actions of each involved party to
determine the appropriateness of disciplinary action or criminal prosecution,
the investigating authority shall also evaluate the response by city employees
and recommend security measures to prevent similar incidents in the future.
   F.   Penalties: If an employee is found to have violated this policy,
disciplinary action, up to and including termination, may be taken. See section
9-3 of this manual for more information about the disciplinary process. (Adm.
Order 99-6, 9-21-1999)
CHAPTER 8
DRUG AND ALCOHOL USE AND FITNESS FOR DUTY POLICY
SECTION:
8-1: Terms And Definitions
8-2: Drug And Alcohol Free Workplace Policy
8-3: Prohibited Activities; Zero Tolerance
8-4: Drug And Alcohol Testing
8-5: Fitness For Duty
8-1: TERMS AND DEFINITIONS:
   A.   Terms And Definitions: The following terms used in this chapter shall
be defined as follows:
   ADULTERATED: A specimen that contains a substance, which is not expected to
be present in human urine, or contains a substance expected to be present, but
is at a concentration so high that it is not consistent with human urine.
   ALCOHOL: The intoxicating agent in beverage alcohol, ethyl alcohol, or other
low molecular weight alcohols including methyl and isopropyl alcohol.
   ALCOHOL TESTING: Testing by a certified breath alcohol technician, using a
department of transportation (DOT) approved breath testing device or a DOT
approved initial screening device. Blood and urine alcohol testing may also be
used at the discretion of the city when breath alcohol testing is not
available.
   ALCOHOL USE: The drinking, swallowing or consuming of any beverage, liquid
mixture or preparation (including any medication), containing alcohol.
   CONTROLLED SUBSTANCE OR DRUG: Any prescribed or nonprescribed drug or
substance included in schedules I, II, III, IV, or V of Utah Code Annotated
section 58-37-4, and also includes a drug or substance included in schedules I,
II, III, IV, or V of the federal controlled substances act, title II, PL 91-
513, or any controlled substance analog, homologs, and synthetic equivalents.
   DILUTE: A urine sample or specimen having a specific gravity less than 1.003
and creatinine level less than twenty milligrams per deciliter (20 mg/dl) shall
be deemed to be dilute.
   DRUG TESTING OR DRUG TEST: The scientific analysis for the presence of drugs
or their metabolites in specimens from the human body. Analysis will include
separate screening and confirmation tests.
   EMPLOYEE: Any person or officer in the service of the city for compensation.
   INVALID: A drug or alcohol test sample or specimen that fails to comply with
the minimum laboratory standards for a valid sample or specimen, as determined
by the laboratory.
   MEDICAL REVIEW OFFICER (MRO): A licensed physician with knowledge of drug
abuse disorders, who is retained by the city to determine and verify if a
legitimate or medical explanation exists for a positive, adulterated,
substituted or invalid drug test result.
   ON DUTY: All working hours including meal or break periods, regardless of
whether the employee is on the city premises, and at any time the employee
represents the city in any capacity, including operating city equipment or
vehicles.
   POSITIVE ALCOHOL TEST: The drug test levels on both the screening test and
the confirmation test are at or above the cutoff level recognized as positive
by the U.S. department of health and human services in its mandatory guidelines
for federal workplace drug testing programs, U.S. Department of Transportation
49 CFR § 40, or the standard cutoff levels set by the laboratory; and the MRO
has verified the test result as positive.
   POSITIVE DRUG TEST: The drug test levels on both the screening test and the
confirmation test are at or above the cutoff level recognized as positive by
the U.S. department of health and human services in its mandatory guidelines
for federal workplace drug testing programs, or the standard cutoff levels set
by the laboratory; and the MRO has verified the test result as positive.
   PROSPECTIVE EMPLOYEE: Any person who has made a written or oral application
to become an employee of the city.
   REASONABLE SUSPICION TESTING: Testing based on articulated belief, based on
recorded specific facts and observations, and reasonable inference drawn from
those facts and observations, that an employee is in violation of this policy.
   SAMPLE OR SPECIMEN: Typically, any sample of urine or breath; the city
reserves the right to use blood, oral fluid or hair for drug or alcohol
testing.
   SUBSTITUTED: A specimen with creatinine and specific gravity values that are
so diminished or divergent that they are not consistent with human urine.
   USE: To consume, sell, purchase, manufacture, distribute, be under the
influence of, report to work under the influence of, or be in the possession of
drugs or alcohol. The term use shall also include the presence of drugs or
alcohol in the body of an employee, including the presence as a metabolite, the
use, distribution, or solicitation of a prescription drug without a valid
prescription from a healthcare provider and failure to use a prescription drug
as prescribed by the authorizing healthcare provider. (Adm. Order 2005-10, 8-1-
2005; amd. Adm. Order 2022-9, 12-6-2022)
8-2: DRUG AND ALCOHOL FREE WORKPLACE POLICY:
   A.   Policy: Ogden City is committed to providing a workplace that ensures
safety and encourages the personal health and productivity of its employees.
Ogden City recognizes that substance abuse in the workplace is a threat to the
safety, health and job performance of its employees. Ogden City has established
this policy to detect and remove abusers of alcohol and drugs from the
workplace.
   B.   Scope: This drug and alcohol free workplace policy applies to all
departments, officials, employees, contract employees, job applicants and
volunteers of the city. Employees are required to abide by this policy as a
condition of employment. This policy is not intended to create or alter any
existing contract, written or verbal, between the city, and its employees,
contractors or job applicants. This policy does not change the at will
employment status of employees.
   C.   Report To Work; Condition: It is the city's desire to provide a drug
free, healthful and safe workplace. To promote this goal, employees are
required to report to work in appropriate mental and physical condition to
perform their jobs in a satisfactory manner.
   D.   Alcohol Or Drug Use Prohibited: While on the city premises and while
conducting city business related activities off the city premises, all
employees must be fit for duty and no employee may use, possess, distribute,
sell or be under the influence of alcohol or illegal drugs. Employees may not
use, possess, distribute, sell or be under the influence of illegal drugs while
off duty. The legal use of prescribed drugs or nonprescription drugs is
permitted on the job only if it does not impair an employee's ability to
perform the essential functions of the job effectively and in a safe manner
that does not endanger the employee or other individuals in the workplace.
   E.   Contract Employees; Volunteers: Contract employees, temporary employees
and volunteers providing goods or services for and on behalf of the city shall
also be subject to the terms and conditions of all policies and procedures
involving drug and alcohol testing, including the cancellation or refusal of
continued services or work of said volunteer(s) or contract employee(s), who
are found to be in violation of these policies.
   F.   Employee Responsibilities: Employees bear certain responsibilities and
obligations owed to the city as a consequence of the privileges and benefits
provided by the city under the terms and conditions of employment. Employees
are required to:
      1.   Comply with all the terms and conditions of the policies in this
manual related to the prohibition of the sale, possession, use or distribution
of illegal drugs, alcohol or substances, and appropriate use of prescription
drugs, whether connected directly to work activity or in connection with being
on call for work while in an off duty status.
      2.   Report to their supervisor any use of prescription medication which
may affect the employee's judgment, performance or behavior.
      3.   Comply and cooperate with the request to take any alcohol or drug
test or medical examination which is requested in accordance with this and
other related policies in this manual.
      4.   Report to their supervisor any use of alcohol or drugs which may
affect the employee's judgment, performance or appropriate behavior when called
to work from off duty status.
      5.   Notify supervisors whenever they witness or have information about
accidents, injuries or another employee's ability to adequately and safely
perform their job duties. Employees who act in good faith to appropriately
identify behavior to their supervisor which may indicate another employee may
not be fit for duty will be defended, indemnified and held harmless by the city
for any and all damages claimed or sustained in the event of litigation.
      6.   In instances where required by this policy, enter into and comply
with a return to work agreement and where required as an ongoing condition of
continued employment whether or not directly connected to any disciplinary
action or event.
   G.   Prescription And Over The Counter Drugs: The use of prescription or
over the counter medications that may impair the employee's ability to safely
and competently perform his/her duties must be reported to his/her supervisor.
Employees should read any warning label on a medication (prescription or over
the counter) and report the use to his/her supervisor, if the label warns of
possible impairment. The use of some medications may require reassignment or
temporary leave of absence without pay. Employees must take all medication as
directed on the label and heed any listed warnings and/or side effects. The
city may require the employee to provide medical information about such
prescribed drug and/or the employee's condition to ensure a safe and adequate
work environment for the employee and others, including members of the public.
(See medical information and examinations policy found in this manual.)
If you take a controlled substance (Utah Code Annotated Section 58-37-4) or
have a medical cannabis recommendation card and your assigned duties require
operation of equipment (small tools, equipment, driving) you must report use of
the controlled substance or the medical cannabis recommendation card to your
supervisors.
As prohibited by Federal law, the use of marijuana, a Schedule 1 controlled
substance, is expressly prohibited under this policy for employees who hold a
Commercial Driver's License and employees whose position requires the employee
to carry a weapon as their primary job function. This restriction applies, even
if its medical use is authorized under state law. Employees who use medical
marijuana in connection with a disability should discuss their use with their
supervisor or the human resources office to find other means of accommodating
the disability in the workplace.
   H.   Implementation: The human resources officer is responsible for
implementing, maintaining and answering questions regarding this policy. The
human resources officer or their designee will receive test results and make
required decisions in the testing and evaluation process. If an employee is
found by the human resources officer to be in violation of this policy, the
employee shall immediately be removed from duties, and the matter shall be
referred to the employee's supervisor or department director for disciplinary
action consistent with the zero tolerance policy described in this chapter and
determination of leave status pending discipline.
   I.   Employee Assistance Program: The city provides an employee assistance
program (EAP) for its employees. The EAP provides confidential counseling and
referral services to employees for assistance with such problems as drug and/or
alcohol abuse or addiction. (See employee assistance program policy in this
manual.) Employees with questions or concerns about substance dependency or
abuse are encouraged to use the resources of the employee assistance program.
They may also wish to discuss these matters with their supervisor or the human
resources office to receive assistance or referrals to appropriate resources in
the community. It is the employee's responsibility to seek assistance from the
EAP prior to reaching a point where his or her judgment, performance or
behavior has led to imminent disciplinary action. Participation in the EAP
after the testing and disciplinary process has begun may not preclude or stop
disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment. An employee
must obtain a work release from the EAP, counselor or treatment provider before
returning to work from any drug or alcohol treatment program.
   J.   Treatment Programs; Unpaid Time Off: Employees with drug or alcohol
problems that have not resulted in, and are not the immediate subject of,
disciplinary action may request approval to take unpaid time off to participate
in a rehabilitation or treatment program through the city's health insurance
benefit coverage. Leave may be granted if the employee agrees to abstain from
use of the problem substance; abides by all the city policies, rules and
prohibitions relating to conduct in the workplace; and if granting the leave
will not cause the city any undue hardship. (See related discussion under
employee assistance program [EAP].)
   K.   Government Contracts Or Grants: Under the drug free workplace act, an
employee who performs work for a government contract or grant must notify the
city of a criminal conviction for drug related activity occurring in the
workplace. The report must be made within five (5) days of the conviction.
Employees who are required to drive in their jobs and are involved in any
alcohol or drug related traffic violation or criminal charge stemming from
such, must report such information to their department director. (See use of
equipment and vehicles policy in this manual.)
   L.   CDL Holders: In addition to terms of this drug and alcohol free
workplace policy, certain employees holding a commercial driver's license shall
be subject to additional drug and alcohol testing requirements:
      1.   Employee drivers who hold a commercial driver's license (CDL) are
subject to federal department of transportation (DOT) and federal motor carrier
safety administration (FMCSA) regulations, 49 CFR part 40 and part 382
respectively. The city shall administer drug and alcohol testing of CDL holder
employees consistent with DOT and FMCSA regulations, which are incorporated
herein by reference.
      2.   Employees holding a CDL must also be in compliance with this drug
and alcohol free workplace policy, even though it may be more restrictive than
DOT and FMCSA federal regulations. CDL holder employees are subject to all drug
and alcohol testing requirements of this drug and alcohol free workplace
policy.
      3.   Federal regulations require that any employee in a position
requiring a valid CDL as a requisite or qualification for their job shall be
subject to random testing for the presence of drugs and/or alcohol. Random
testing requires that a mandated minimum percentage of employees in CDL
required positions, as determined by a random selection, be tested at least
once a year. The actual selection of the individual employees to be tested is
made in a random manner and method.
      4.   Federal regulations also require a postaccident drug and/or alcohol
test of CDL drivers in certain circumstances, and allow testing for reasonable
suspicion.
      5.   If drug and/or alcohol testing of an employee is required in the
same instance by both federal regulations and the policies of this chapter,
both the federal regulations and these policies shall be complied with
separately, with the federal requirements being complied with prior to city
requirements. Samples collected for CDL drug and/or alcohol testing may not be
split or divided for use in city required testing; rather, a separate sample
must be collected from the employee for city required testing.
      6.   A CDL holder who occupies a safety sensitive position shall be a
member of separate random selection pools for CDL holders and safety sensitive
positions, and shall be subject to random testing according to the regulations
and policies applicable to either pool.
      7.   The prohibited activities and zero tolerance policy described in
this chapter shall apply to employees who are discovered to have engaged in
prohibited activities through CDL testing procedures.
   M.   Private And Confidential Records:
      1.   Sharing Information: In all cases involving testing for the presence
of substances as detailed and provided for in this and other applicable
policies in this manual, test results and records related to specific testing
methods, steps and procedures shall be released to the city. Such results,
records and other material related to the testing and results are and shall
remain the property of the city. Testing information and results shall be
shared by the city only with interested parties and only otherwise on a need to
know basis. Such need to know basis shall exist with respect to sharing
confidential records with department directors or immediate supervisors who
shall be entrusted with disciplinary action, evaluation procedures and other
direct responsibility over the employee.
      2.   Employee's File; Method Of Recording: Specific test results and
specific records related to the test method(s), procedure(s) and related
medical process shall be kept in separate and confidential records apart from
the employee's personnel file. Reference to the existence of such results and
records shall be made in an employee's file with respect to any record of
disciplinary action taken or terms and conditions of continuing employment
stemming from or arising out of a testing procedure, request or outcome. The
only exception to such reference shall occur with respect to the restoration of
an employee back to duty whenever a hearing decision and order provides for
such restoration and directs the expunging of such record or reference.
   N.   Notification To Law Enforcement: Part of the city's procedures include
supervisors notifying the police or other appropriate law enforcement official
(s) whenever they believe or suspect an employee is in possession of, selling
or transferring illegal controlled substances.
   O.   Consult With Appropriate Agencies: Additionally, the city's procedures
direct supervisors to consult with the human resources office or the mayor,
contact the police department and make other arrangements as necessary or
appropriate for confiscation of illegal materials, drug or alcohol testing,
transportation to testing sites and other direction(s) and activities necessary
for the enforcement of the city's policy against drugs and alcohol in the
workplace.
   P.   Right To Change Or Terminate Policy: As stated elsewhere in this
manual, nothing in this or any other policy is intended to constitute a
contract of employment. Nothing in this or any other policy constitutes a term
of contract nor is there any express term or condition of employment to be
inferred from this or any other policy. The city reserves the right to amend,
replace and/or terminate this policy at any time.
   Q.   Interaction With Other Policies: The policies in this chapter describe
the city's guidelines and procedures involved with upholding, supporting and
enforcing its policies on fitness for duty, drugs and alcohol in the workplace
and drug and alcohol testing. It is the intent of the city to also uphold and
enforce other applicable policies which deal with the conditions and terms of
employment with the city, including, but not limited to, the city's policies
and practices related to disciplinary action for violations of its employment
conditions, terms and standards.
   R.   Federal Law: Nothing contained in this policy is intended to violate or
supersede the intent or provisions of the federal drug free workplace act,
which, among other provisions, compels self-publication of conviction(s) based
on the illegal activity or use associated with illegal drugs or alcohol. Any
inconsistencies between or within this policy or this manual and the drug free
workplace act shall be resolved in favor of the provisions of said act.
   S.   Alcohol Use At Social Events: The city recognizes that occasions will
arise in the normal course of employment, when employees may be called upon to
attend receptions or other social events where alcohol is served. This and
other related policies are not intended to prohibit the legal consumption of
alcohol during receptions or social events, unless the event occurs during or
directly connected with the employee's working hours or work activity, or will
cause the employee to report to work in a condition that violates this policy.
Nonetheless, the city does not condone an excessive consumption of alcohol at
social gathering(s) or event(s). The city reserves the right in its sole
discretion to limit the consumption of alcohol and to intervene to provide an
employee with transportation home and prohibit an employee from driving any
vehicle or equipment, when reasonable suspicion exists to believe the employee
is under the influence of alcohol. Excessive consumption of alcohol at or
involving functions related to the interests of the city or the representation
of the city may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination.
   T.   Employee Disability (ADA): Alcoholism may be considered a disability
under the Americans with disabilities act (the "ADA"). The city will make
reasonable accommodations under the ADA for employees who suffer from
alcoholism, including encouraging an employee to participate in rehabilitation
programs. However, the city will hold an alcoholic employee to the same
performance standards as other employees and will discipline an employee, up to
and including termination, if the employee's alcohol use violates this policy,
adversely affects the employee's job performance, or is considered to be a
safety hazard.
   U.   Labels: Pursuant to Utah Code Annotated (1953) section 34-38-14, an
employee or prospective employee whose drug or alcohol (except as modified by
the Americans with disabilities act) tests are confirmed and verified positive
in accordance with the provisions of this program, shall not, by reason of
those results alone be defined as a person with a "handicap" or "disability"
for purpose of Utah Code Annotated title 34, chapter 35, known as the Utah
antidiscriminatory act.
   V.   Employees with questions on these policies or other issues related to
drug or alcohol use in the workplace should raise their concerns with their
supervisor or the human resources office without fear of reprisal. (Adm. Order
2005-10, 8-1-2005; amd. Adm. Order 2022-9, 12-6-2022)
8-3: PROHIBITED ACTIVITIES; ZERO TOLERANCE:
   A.   Prohibited Activities: The following activities are strictly prohibited
during working hours by all employees and illegal use of drugs is prohibited at
any time. It is a violation of city policy for an employee to:
      1.   Work with the presence of drugs or alcohol in his/her body (as
determined by a drug or alcohol test), including their presence as a drug
metabolite, unless the drug is legally prescribed to the employee.
      2.   Sell, use, purchase, distribute, manufacture or be in possession of
an illegal drug or drug paraphernalia at any time.
      3.   Sell, use, purchase, distribute, manufacture or be in possession of
drugs, including prescription medications which are controlled substances, at
any time, unless the prescription medication is legally prescribed to the
employee.
      4.   Operate any vehicle or machinery while under the influence of any
drug, including prescription or over the counter medications, which render the
employee incapable of safely and competently operating a vehicle, machinery or
performing any other job duties.
      5.   Use alcohol, in any form, while on city time or business, or to
report to work under the influence of alcohol. An employee is considered to be
in violation of this policy when he or she is working and has a breath, blood
or urine alcohol result greater than or equal to 0.02.
      6.   To consume or use alcohol, in any form, within eight (8) hours prior
to a scheduled work period, including when "on call".
      7.   Refuse to submit a specimen for drug or alcohol testing.
      8.   Have a verified, positive drug test.
      9.   Tamper with, substitute or adulterate any specimen collected for
drug or alcohol testing. Any sample reported by the laboratory or medical
review officer as substituted or adulterated will be considered a "refusal to
test" or a refusal to submit a valid sample.
      10.   Obstruct or not fully cooperate with specimen collection or testing
procedures.
      11.   Fail to comply with and complete all treatment and aftercare
recommendations made by a counselor, or treatment provider after a violation of
this policy.
   B.   Zero Tolerance Policy: Upon completion of any required predetermination
hearing, if it is determined that an employee tested positive for use of drugs
and/or alcohol in violation of the policies of this chapter, or engaged in the
prohibited activities described in this chapter, that employee shall have his/
her employment terminated with the city. An employee should not expect to be
granted a second chance to comply with these policies. Nevertheless, the city
and its officers retain discretion to impose discipline of lesser severity than
termination where unusual or extraordinary mitigating circumstances exist that
justify lesser discipline.
   C.   Right Of Review: Employees who are subject to review for serious
discipline or possible termination as a consequence of any action or result
within the scope of this policy shall have a right of review through applicable
grievance procedures. (See predetermination hearing and appeals procedures
policies in this manual.) (Adm. Order 2005-10, 8-1-2005)
8-4: DRUG AND ALCOHOL TESTING:
   A.   Scope Of Testing: Job applicants and employees may be asked to provide
body substance samples (such as urine and/or blood) to determine the abuse,
illicit or illegal use of drugs and alcohol in violation of this policy.
Refusal to submit to drug testing may result in disciplinary action, up to and
including termination of employment, consistent with the city's zero tolerance
policy.
   B.   Situations Or Conditions For Conducting Drug And/Or Alcohol Tests: In
keeping with the city's commitment to provide a safe and productive work
environment for all employees and to protect the public, drug and/or alcohol
testing may be conducted within the guidelines established by this policy. Drug
tests may be conducted under any of the following situations or conditions:
      1.   Preemployment Testing: As a prequalification to assuming any
position, prospective employees are required to provide body substance samples
for drug and alcohol testing. The drug and alcohol test shall occur first in
connection with a preemployment medical examination. Likewise, a preemployment
test shall be conducted for all current employees applying for other positions,
excluding transfers or accommodation relating to reductions in force. Any
applicant who tests positive will be denied employment, unless otherwise
allowed elsewhere in this and related policies. A current employee who has a
positive test or "refusal to test" for preemployment drug or alcohol test,
shall be subject to discipline up to and including termination, consistent with
the zero tolerance policy of this chapter.
      2.   Postaccident Testing: Any current employee who is involved in an
incident or accident while on duty, whether on or off the city's premises, and
involving damages to any property, or results in any personal injury reasonably
requiring medical attention, may be required to provide body substance samples
for the purposes of performing tests for the presence of drugs and/or alcohol.
Testing shall be administered when employee drug use, negligence, and/or an
unsafe act is likely to have contributed to the incident. In these cases, a
drug test can accurately identify what substance caused the impairment. If
testing is deemed unnecessary due to circumstances, non-testing must be
approved through the human resources / risk manager. Except where determined
already by existing evidence or competent authority, the city requires two (2)
confirming opinions by supervisors and/or department directors to determine the
value of any property damage, negligence, or an unsafe act. CDL holders may
also be subject to separate postaccident drug and alcohol testing as required
by department of transportation (DOT) regulations. An employee involved in any
incident or accident while on duty shall not consume alcohol for eight (8)
hours thereafter, or until after submitting to a drug and alcohol test,
whichever occurs first.
Physical injury sustained by a police officer in effecting an arrest, in which
the arrestee resisted arrest, shall not be required to undergo chemical testing
unless reasonable suspicion otherwise exists.
      3.   Reasonable Suspicion Testing: Reasonable suspicion drug and/or
alcohol testing will be conducted in cases where there is a reasonable belief
or suspicion by a supervisor that an employee may be using a controlled
substance, using alcohol while at work, reporting to work under the influence
of alcohol or controlled substances, using prescription drugs illegally, or
violating any other provision of the city's drug and alcohol free workplace
policy. Reasonable suspicion may be the basis for testing a group or groups of
employees for which there is reasonable suspicion that one or more individuals
within the group or groups are in violation of the drug and alcohol free
workplace policy.
      4.   Random Testing: Random testing shall be conducted for employees who
occupy safety sensitive positions or who are required to hold a commercial
driver's license. Selection for random testing will be computer generated. All
employees will have an equal chance of selection in each selection period. The
frequency and annualized rate of random testing shall be determined by the
city.
         a.   Employees occupying safety sensitive positions shall be subject
to random drug and/or alcohol testing. A "safety sensitive position" means any
city position which directly affects the safety of city employees, the general
public, or positions where there is access to controlled substances, as defined
in title 34, chapter 41, Utah Code, during the course of performing job duties.
Safety sensitive positions shall be designated by the human resources officer
and such designation shall be incorporated into applicable job descriptions.
Any existing employee who is newly designated as holding a safety sensitive
position shall be notified in writing of the designation by the human resources
office. The actual selection of the individual employees to be tested is made
in a random manner and method.
         b.   CDL Holders: A CDL holder who also occupies a safety sensitive
position will be subject to separate random testing for CDL holders consistent
with federal regulations.
      5.   Periodic Testing: Preannounced and preselected drug and alcohol
testing of all employees or identified groups of employees on a regular
schedule may be implemented by the city.
      6.   Rehabilitation Testing: Employees returning to work after
participating in a drug or alcohol education and/or treatment program, whether
voluntarily or as part of return to work agreement, will be subject to
unannounced follow up rehabilitation drug and/or alcohol testing. An initial
return to duty drug test shall be required after evaluation by the EAP/
counselor and after the EAP/counselor has determined that the employee has
successfully complied with prescribed education and/or treatment. The test
results must be negative before the employee may return to duty. Thereafter,
the employee shall be subject to follow up rehabilitation testing according to
a schedule determined by the EAP/counselor or the city. Follow up
rehabilitation testing will include, as a minimum, six (6) unannounced drug
and/or alcohol tests in the first twelve (12) months after return to duty.
Follow up testing can be extended to a maximum of sixty (60) months after
return to duty. The employee will also be subject to all other required types
of testing, including random testing.
   C.   Designated Employer Representative (DER): The human resources officer
shall serve as the designated employer representative (DER). If the human
resources officer is unavailable, the director of management services or their
designee shall serve as the DER. The DER is required to make required decisions
in the testing and evaluation process and to take immediate action to remove
employees from duties whenever there is a positive test result or a refusal to
test and refer the matter to the employee's supervisor or department director
for disciplinary action and determination of leave status pending discipline.
Other DER duties include implementing and answering employee questions
regarding this policy; transmitting the list of employees to the third party
administrator for random selection; and receive and maintain confidentiality of
all test results and other information generated by this policy.
   D.   Specimen Collection Procedures:
      1.   All specimen collections will be conducted in conformity with this
policy and in accordance with the requirements of title 34, chapter 41 of the
Utah Code Annotated.
      2.   From time to time, the city shall designate certified urine
collectors and breath alcohol technicians to carry out testing and/or a third
party administrator to assist in setting up and administrating the drug and
alcohol testing program.
      3.   Urine and breath alcohol samples will be collected by individuals
trained to follow the department of transportation's collection and testing
procedures, and in accordance with specific laboratory collection procedures
not covered by DOT procedures.
      4.   All drug tests, alcohol tests and sample collection procedures shall
be performed under reasonable and sanitary conditions and in such a manner as
to respect the privacy of the individual being tested, as well as prevent
tampering or misidentification of the sample.
      5.   Breath alcohol tests with a result greater than or equal to 0.02
will be reported immediately to the DER by the technician or the third party
administrator. No MRO review will be done on breath or blood alcohol tests.
Urine alcohol positive results will be reviewed by the MRO.
   E.   Observed Collection Of Specimens:
      1.   Observed collection of urine specimens may be required if the
collector observes any clear evidence that the specimen donor tried to tamper
with or will try to tamper with the sample. The city may require observed
collection of urine samples if city officials have clear evidence that the
specimen donor tried to tamper with or will try to tamper with the sample.
      2.   Observed collections must be performed by a collector of the same
sex as the donor. A city official may do the observation, if the collector or
collection site does not have someone of the correct sex to observe the
collection.
      3.   Any suspicion of an attempt by an employee to adulterate or
substitute a specimen will be reported to the city. The collector should
instruct the donor that a second specimen will be collected where the
individual's act of urination is observed by the collector to ensure against
tampering with the specimen. Observed tests will only be conducted with
knowledge of the DER/city and at the request of the city. When DOT regulations
require the test collection must be "observed", the city will be notified, but
the test must be "observed" regardless of city prior knowledge or request.
   F.   Test Standards And Results: The city may test for the presence of
alcohol and other chemical substances in the body. Screening tests shall be
conducted by an immunoassay test procedure, or other procedure used by the
laboratory meeting industry standards. Confirmation tests shall be according to
the gas chromatography and mass spectrometry (GC/MS) test procedure or other
procedure used by the laboratory meeting industry standards. The levels, or
results, obtained in each test for each substance are listed in the tables
below. The listed results represent the level at which the applicable test
result shall be determined "positive" for the presence of the listed substance.
The city reserves the right to test for other drugs not on the below list, use
specimens other than urine and breath for testing and to change cutoff levels
as necessary to meet the goals of this program. If industry standards call for
lower screening and confirmation cutoff levels, as disclosed by the MRO or the
laboratory, the city shall apply the lower industry standard cutoff levels.
      1.    Screening And Confirmation Test Cutoff Levels: Screening and
confirmation test cutoff levels for drug testing and alcohol testing shall be
set at or above the cutoff level recognized as positive by the U.S. department
of health and human services, in its mandatory guidelines for federal workplace
drug testing programs, as adopted, or the standard cutoff levels set by the
laboratory.
      2.   Positive Results: Positive test results shall be used as the basis
of taking appropriate action under other applicable city standards and policies
relating to job performance, safety, equipment and vehicle use, employee
conduct and behavior, drug and alcohol testing and procedures, and fitness for
duty requirements.
   G.   Medical Review Officer (MRO): In the case of positive, adulterated,
substituted or invalid test results, the employee or prospective employee shall
be so advised by the MRO by telephone, on a confidential basis, prior to the
reporting of the results to the human resources office. The employee shall have
the right to discuss and explain the results, including the right to advise the
MRO of any medication prescribed by his/her physician, which may have affected
the results of the test. The MRO shall also review the chain of custody
documentation to ensure compliance with normal procedures. The MRO may report a
nonnegative test to Ogden City, without interviewing the employee/applicant,
if:
      1.   An individual has expressly declined the opportunity to discuss the
test result with the MRO; or
      2.   The human resources office has successfully made and documented a
contact with the employee and instructed them to contact the MRO and more than
seventy two (72) hours have passed since that time; or
      3.   If neither city nor MRO, after making and documenting all reasonable
efforts, has been able to contact the employee within ten (10) days of the date
on which the MRO receives the confirmed test result from the laboratory.
   H.   Split Specimen Procedure (Contesting A Drug Test):
      1.   Urine samples shall be separated into two (2) containers at the time
of collection (split specimen collection), consisting of an "A" bottle and "B"
bottle. The primary laboratory will only test the "A" or primary bottle. The
"A" bottle of a nonnegative sample will be kept in frozen storage at the
laboratory for a minimum of one year.
      2.   An employee or prospective employee who has a positive, adulterated
or substituted test result shall have the right to request within seventy two
(72) hours of notification by the MRO, to have the "B" or split bottle of his/
her urine sample independently reanalyzed by gas chromatography/mass
spectrometry at a second SAMHSA certified laboratory of his/her choice at his/
her expense. If the reanalysis is "negative" the employee, or prospective
employee, shall be allowed to return to work immediately, compensated for lost
wages and be reimbursed for the cost of split specimen test, provided the
employee is not in violation of any other policy.
      3.   The city will split the cost of split specimen reanalysis, on a
fifty/fifty (50/50) basis, with an existing employee. Prospective employees/
applicants will pay the entire cost of split specimen reanalysis.
   4.   An employee who has tested nonnegative shall have the right to request
from the city, a copy of the laboratory and MRO report. Any request must be
written and made to a DER.
   I.   Dilute Specimen Procedures: Drug and/or alcohol tests which the
laboratory reports as "dilute", having a specific gravity less than 1.003 and
creatinine level less than twenty milligrams per deciliter (20 mg/dl), shall
not be acceptable, and a new sample will be required. The employee/prospective
employee will be required to give a second specimen as soon as possible and
without prior notification. He/she will be directed and required to minimize
the amount of liquids consumed prior to giving the second specimen. The second
specimen will be considered the final result. In the case of prospective
employee only, a dilute final result will be deemed a refusal to submit a
specimen for drug or alcohol testing, unless the MRO determines that a
legitimate medical explanation exists for the dilute drug or alcohol test
result.
   J.   Adulterated Or Substituted Specimen: Any specimen reported by the
laboratory or medical review officer as substituted or adulterated will be
considered a "refusal to test" or a refusal to submit a valid sample.
   K.   Random Testing: Testing of body substances for the presence of drugs
and/or alcohol shall be administered at random to employees selected from a
pool of safety sensitive employees. Employees are selected at random using a
method and procedure similar to that approved by the U.S. department of
transportation or other governing authority. Employees selected at random shall
be notified through either their department director, division manager,
supervisor, or the city human resources office and shall be required to submit
to the testing procedures upon such notification.
      1.   Random tests can be collected on site or at designated collection
facilities. Random selection of employees for testing will be performed by a
third party administrator and will be computer generated using software which
ensures each individual eligible for random testing has an equal chance of
being selected. Random selections may be done on a monthly, bimonthly or
quarterly basis.
      2.   The human resources officer will forward the list of eligible
employees to the third party administrator at the beginning of each random
selection period. The random drug testing rate and random alcohol testing rate
shall be determined by the human resources officer. The human resources officer
may periodically change the random testing rates to better meet the goals of
this program.
      3.   The third party administrator will inform the designated city
officials which employees were selected for random testing. The human resources
office or third party administrator will coordinate the collection of samples
at the worksite, or the city may send employees to a prearranged collection
site.
      4.   Employees will be notified by a supervisor or the human resources
officer of the requirement to take a random drug test and should then proceed
immediately to the designated collection site. Employees must not be given any
advance notice/warning when random test is required. If the employee refuses to
go to the collection site, refuses to provide a sample or admits drug or
alcohol misuse, the DER and the third party administrator should be immediately
notified and the employee immediately removed from duty without pay.
      5.   Safety sensitive employees with a CDL will be a member of separate
random selection pools for CDL holders and safety sensitive positions.
   L.   Reasonable Suspicion: If reasonable suspicion exists to believe that an
employee is using, consuming or is under the influence of alcohol or drugs
(whether such are legal or illegal) while engaged in work activity or work
related purpose or event, the employee shall be required to immediately undergo
a test for the presence of alcohol or drugs in the system at a medical or
testing center authorized and designated by the city. Any supervisor of an
employee is authorized to require the test and invoke both transportation to
the test site, as well as the testing procedure under this policy.
      1.   Transportation To Collection Site; Positive Result: The employee
shall be taken to the collection site at a medical or testing center by the
supervisor or a designee of the supervisor. An employee who has a positive drug
or alcohol test, and whose test results are confirmed, shall be subject to
disciplinary action, up to and including termination, consistent with the
city's zero tolerance policy. The employee may be referred to counseling and
rehabilitation in addition to any disciplinary action. In no case will any
treatment, counseling, care or rehabilitation, which is allowed or permitted by
the city, abrogate or set aside the city's right to take whatever disciplinary
action it deems appropriate in its sole discretion.
      2.   Reasonable Suspicion Defined: As defined under terms and definitions
in this policy, "reasonable suspicion" includes an articulable belief and
reasonable inference that an employee is under the influence of, or is impaired
by or is abusing drugs or alcohol. Circumstances which constitute a basis for
determining reasonable suspicion include, but are not limited to, the
observation or knowledge of the following:
         a.   A pattern of abnormal or erratic behavior. Unclear thinking as
communicated by the employee when asked questions about what they are doing.
This may include inability to list or follow a series of consecutive events or
directions in a predictable and/or logical manner.
         b.   Information provided by a reliable and credible source that
indicates the employee was observed directly ingesting a controlled substance,
or taking excessive amounts of even legal drugs (e.g., 4 to 5 diet pills every
morning, smoking marijuana in a vehicle, etc.).
         c.   A work related incident or accident. This may include the
observation and/or knowledge of behavior which violated known or expected safe
work standards. An example might be an employee who is using a welding torch or
a saw to threaten or "tease" another individual, even if such did not result
directly in immediate harm.
         d.   Direct observation of drug or alcohol use.
         e.   The presence of physical signs and symptoms of drug or alcohol
use. By way of example, the burnt, sweet, acrid odor of a marijuana "joint"; or
the clear odor of alcohol on a person's breath; slurred speech, unsteady walk,
uncontrolled shaking or small tremors in the hands, arms, legs, etc.; poor
coordination and/or reflexes; and glossy or bloodshot eyes.
         f.   The discovery of drug paraphernalia or other clear signs of drug
or alcohol use in a controlled workplace environment creating reasonable
suspicion that a certain employee or group of employees with access to the
controlled environment is in violation of this drug and alcohol free workplace
policy.
         g.   Admission of drug or alcohol use or other activity in violation
of this drug and alcohol workplace policy.
      3.   Record: Within twenty four (24) hours of the test or before the test
results are available, the supervisor shall complete a reasonable suspicion
record form, a copy of which is on file in the human resources office, to
document the reasonable suspicion determination.
      4.   Suspension: Any employee that is tested for drugs or alcohol under
the conditions of a "reasonable suspicion test" may be suspended, with or
without pay, pending the result of the drug or alcohol test.
      5.   Refusal: A refusal to submit to or undergo an examination or test
referred to in this and related policies in this manual shall be interpreted as
a violation of these policies and, in addition to being treated as a positive
test result, may include an interpretation of insubordination depending upon
the involved employee's actions and behaviors in the circumstances. In either
case, the employee shall be subject to disciplinary action up to and including
termination.
      6.   Documentation:
         a.   Detailed Records: It is an essential element of this policy and
its enforcement that the supervisor and any other management member, who was
involved in evaluating the employee, make a detailed record of all actions,
observations, statements and other pertinent facts related to their basis of
reasonable suspicion and their perception of an impaired worker or an employee
who was unfit for duty.
         b.   Information And Facts Required: The documentation shall include
specific facts related to the date, time, location and observations known to
exist at the time a reasonable suspicion was first formed, and what other
information was known or believed to exist at the time a determination was made
that the employee was potentially unfit for duty.
         c.   Form Available: A form for this purpose is available from the
human resources office for supervisors to use as a guideline on which to base
proper documentation. Any witnesses who also were involved should be
identified, and their statements taken as soon as possible.
      7.   Observed Sale, Use Or Possession:
         a.   Notification Required: If any employee observes the sale,
distribution, solicitation, use or possession of alcoholic beverages, illegal
drugs or drug paraphernalia by any other employee on the city's time or
premises, or observes the presence of illegal drugs or drug paraphernalia, the
employee is required to notify their supervisor immediately. Notification to
the police department is also required if clear and present knowledge exists
that a violation of a law has occurred. An example of the latter case would be
the observation of an employee driving a city vehicle under the influence of
alcohol, when the employee was first observed drinking and then driving. In
such a case, management and the police shall conduct appropriate investigation
and take appropriate action.
         b.   Evidence: Upon instruction or advice from the police department
or other law enforcement authority, any drug and drug paraphernalia shall be
turned over to them and a signed receipt should be obtained acknowledging that
the evidence was provided. Additionally, if the police request or suggest it,
any supervisor or employee shall be required to allow the police to inspect
city property. (See security inspections policy in this manual.)
      8.   Hearing Request: Upon written request to the human resources office,
an employee who was the subject of a positive, verified (confirmed) test
result, or who refused to comply with the testing requirement or other
provisions of this and related policies stemming from a reasonable suspicion or
work related accident or incident, may request a grievance hearing in
accordance with the procedures described elsewhere in this manual.
   M.   Postaccident Testing: Postaccident drug tests must be conducted within
thirty two (32) hours of the accident. Postaccident alcohol tests should be
conducted within two (2) hours of the accident, and must be conducted within
eight (8) hours. If the time limits have passed, the city should cease attempts
to collect the sample. If an on site postaccident test collection is needed,
the third party administrator should be contacted immediately. While waiting
for postaccident drug or alcohol test results, the employee shall not consume
any alcohol whether on duty or off duty, and the employee may be removed from
his/her duties until the alcohol test is reported as less than 0.02 and the
medical review officer (MRO) verifies that the employee tested negative for
drugs.
   N.   Payment For Tests: All drug and alcohol tests required by the city will
be paid for by the city. All tests conducted on employees will be considered
compensatory time by the city. Preemployment tests will be conducted on
prospective employees on their own time. The cost of preemployment tests will
be paid by the city. The exception is that reanalysis of nonnegative samples
will be paid for, by the prospective employee, at the time split sample
reanalysis is requested. Employees will be required to pay fifty percent (50%)
of the cost of the reanalysis at the time split sample reanalysis is requested.
(See split sample procedure [contesting a drug test] subsection of this policy
for complete details.) (Adm. Order 2005-10, 8-1-2005; amd. Adm. Order 2022-9,
12-6-2022)
8-5: FITNESS FOR DUTY:
   A.   Fitness For Duty Policy: It is the policy of the city to protect the
health and safety of employees by providing an environment where all employees
and volunteers are "fit for duty" when performing on the job. Subject to the
terms and conditions of this policy and other related policies in this manual,
the city will not allow or permit any employee to perform work or service, when
there is a concern that they are not able to do so safely and effectively.
   B.   Definition: "Fit for duty" means that an employee or volunteer is able
to perform that job for which he or she was hired in a safe and effective
manner, unimpaired by some medical or psychological conditions, personal
problems, medication, alcohol or drugs.
   C.   Applicability: This policy applies in all aspects of the working
condition, environment and service perimeters for the city. Accordingly, this
includes time performing work or service, whether paid or not, as well as at or
during rest or meal breaks. This policy and its related policies in this manual
may be applied to all persons providing services to the city as an independent
contractor.
   D.   General Guidelines:
      1.   Fit For Duty Required: All employees must be "fit for duty", as
defined herein, in order to be permitted to perform work or service for the
city.
      2.   Work Not Permitted Until Determination: When there is a concern or
situation where an employee is not able to perform safely and effectively, he/
she will not be permitted to work until fitness is determined.
      3.   Determining Fitness: In order to determine fitness, the city may
authorize immediate medical (including psychological) examinations, evaluation
or tests to be conducted at a location or site at the direction and discretion
of the city as established through normal procedures and processes.
      4.   Drug And Alcohol Use: Upon reasonable suspicion of employee
violation of the drug and alcohol free workplace policy, the employee shall be
subject to drug and/or alcohol testing provided for in this chapter and shall
be subject to the city's zero tolerance policy related to drug and alcohol use.
      5.   Refusal: An employee shall not be forced to undergo a fitness for
duty examination. However, if an employee appears unfit for duty and refuses to
undergo a medical fitness for duty examination or evaluation when requested to
do so, he/she may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including
termination. If the individual is a contractor or other person providing
service and is not a bona fide employee, he/she will be denied access to city
facilities/property as a provider of services pending further administrative
review.
      6.   Unfit Employee: If an employee has been found to be unfit for duty
and is subsequently able to return to work after successfully undergoing
recommended therapy and/or rehabilitation, the employee's work performance
shall be monitored and will be subject to further assessment techniques,
including medical examination and testing, as well as any recommended group or
individual counseling or therapy. If required as a part of discipline, the
employee shall enter into a return to work agreement before returning to work.
The agreement form shall be similar to, or emulate, the format obtained through
the human resources office. Specific content and format of any agreement will
be tailored to the individual circumstance(s) as determined to be appropriate
and necessary by the city and any involved medical practitioner and/or
counseling agent or firm.
      7.   City Assistance: In order to maintain safe and effective job
performance, the city may assist any employee with respect to resolving or
correcting any concerns, issues or problems which interfere with the employee's
work performance. Such assistance shall not deny nor abrogate the right of the
city to investigate any/all incidents or performance issues, take disciplinary
action, notify professional licensing agencies, seek or obtain legal
involvement or remedy, and otherwise act in support of its own interests and to
protect the safety and health of all employees and the public.
      8.   Medical Release; Fitness For Duty: Whenever a positive test or
examination result has occurred as the result of a fitness for duty concern or
issue as described and controlled under this policy, a supervisor shall require
that the affected employee obtain a medical release from the city authorized
medical facility or testing center indicating the employee's fitness for duty
as a condition of both returning to work and continued employment.
   E.   Identification Of Unfit Conditions: In order to properly provide for
safe and adequate working conditions for employees and the public, both
employees and supervisors are required to fulfill certain responsibilities in
this policy dealing with proper identification of employees who may be unfit
for duty.
      1.   Reporting To Supervisor: Employees are required to report to their
supervisor any behavior or situation which appears to have the potential to
negatively impact the health or safety of the public or other employees, or the
public's perception of the city. This latter condition may occur with respect
to behavior or situations which could occur in a social setting connected to
the work roles or representations of an employee of the city. Employees are
required to keep confidential their information and reports of information
about any other employee, and to tell only appropriate supervisors.
      2.   Indemnification For Employee: Employees who act in good faith to
appropriately identify behavior to their supervisor which may indicate another
employee may not be fit for duty will be defended, indemnified and held
harmless by the city for any and all damages claimed or sustained in the event
of litigation.
      3.   Action: Supervisors are required to follow through and act timely
and properly upon first knowledge or report of a possible impaired worker or
unfit condition. Supervisors are required to investigate all claims, issues and
situations related to enforcement of this policy. Such investigation shall
include the confidential identification of all witnesses involved with any
impaired worker. Such investigation shall also include obtaining a witness to
assist in the evaluation of any employee's behavior and in proper notification
of any impaired employee to the human resources office.
      4.   Confidentiality: Supervisors shall hold confidential all information
about a reported concern or issue related to enforcement of this and related
policies, and share such confidential information only with other superiors who
need to know to enforce this and related policies in this manual.
   F.   Investigation Procedures:
      1.   Suspension: Pending a determination of an employee's fitness for
duty, the employee may be suspended from any work activity or duty. Except in
the case of a positive drug or alcohol test, refusal to test, some other policy
violation justifying withholding of pay, the employee will generally receive
pay during the suspension pending investigation. This suspension is an
important safety valve and should be used whenever possible and practicable.
Employees on suspension are not permitted back on the job until and unless the
suspension has been lifted. Employees are to be notified by the supervisor on
duty of the initial suspension. Determinations as to whether or not a
suspension will be lifted shall be made after the conclusion of other
procedures described in this and related policies in this manual, and then
through the human resources office or supervisor to the involved employee.
      2.   Immediate Suspension: Employees who refuse to take examinations or
tests shall be warned that failure to comply and cooperate with the city's
policies and procedures will subject them to possible disciplinary action, up
to and including termination. The employee who still refuses to comply and
cooperate with the testing procedures and process shall be suspended
immediately, with or without pay.
      3.   Transportation Of Suspended Employees: Suspended employees who are
perceived to be potentially unfit for duty shall not be allowed to leave their
place of work and/or return home unaccompanied in their own transportation.
Management has the responsibility to ensure safe transportation home for the
employee. If the employee refuses to let the supervisor or their designee take
them home, the supervisor is required to notify the appropriate law enforcement
authorities if it appears that the employee may violate law by operating a
vehicle in an unfit condition.
      4.   Investigation During Suspension: During a suspension, a fair and
thorough investigation shall occur with respect to ensuring the adequate and
thorough compilation of all facts, records and evidence (including test
results) pertaining to the reason(s) and cause(s) for the action of supervisors
to suspend the employee. The human resources office shall coordinate the
functions of the investigation and shall assist in the process.
      5.   Decision: Upon conclusion of an investigation and upon obtaining the
applicable test or examination results, a decision will be made by the
department director regarding the employment and/or conditions of employment of
the involved employee.
      6.   Applicable Policies And Civil Service Rules: Applicable city
policies and any civil service rules and regulations related to the procedures
and steps regarding suspensions and their time frames and/or limitations shall
apply.
   G.   Responsibility For Expenses: The expense of any fitness for duty
evaluations, examination or testing requested or required by the city under
this and related policies in this manual shall be paid by the city. The
expenses for any treatment or rehabilitation, be such recommended, volunteered
or mandatory, shall be the responsibility of the employee. The employee may
avail themselves of existing benefit programs, if any, for which they are
otherwise eligible. Examples of such programs may be employee assistance
program, medical and health insurance benefit coverage (to the extent
rehabilitation is a covered benefit), or a flexible spending account. Any
benefit programs available are subject to the terms and conditions of city
sponsored plans and applicable plan providers and their limitations to the
extent that expense payment or reimbursement are available under any plan.
   H.   Right Of Review: Employees who are subject to review for serious
discipline or possible termination as a consequence of any action or result
within the scope of this policy shall have a right of review through applicable
grievance procedures. (See predetermination hearing and appeals procedures
policies in this manual.) (Adm. Order 2005-10, 8-1-2005; amd. Adm. Order 2022-
9, 12-6-2022)
CHAPTER 9
EMPLOYEE CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINARY ACTION

9-3: Other Unlawful Harassment Or Discrimination

9-7: Conflict Resolution
