5-7:      ON CALL DUTY PAY:
A.   Applicable Employees: This policy applies to employees of the City who are
required to serve in an "on call" status and be available for a call back to
work for up to a week at a time during otherwise unscheduled, off duty hours.
These employees are generally assigned communication devices and procedures,
and are allowed to drive City vehicles home after working hours to aid in
response time for any call to work. On call employees are expected to comply
with the City's fitness for duty policy during this on call period. (See also
overtime policy, Administrative Policy Manual, as applicable.)
B.   Compensation: It is the policy of the City to pay these specifically
designated on call employees a minimum of sixteen (16) hours of overtime for
each week in which they serve in a paid on call or callback status. If the
employee serves less than one (1) full workweek in this status, the number of
hours of applicable overtime will be prorated. When and if an employee in this
capacity performs actual work and service as a result of being called back to
work, they will be paid any additional overtime for hours worked in excess of
the first sixteen (16) hours. Information Technology Division nonexempt
employees will receive two (2) hours of overtime for being on call from 17:00
to 08:00 and three (3) hours for being "on call" from 08:00 to 08:00 (full 24
hours). When and if an IT employee in this capacity performs actual work and
service as a result of being called back to work, they will be paid any
additional overtime for hours worked in excess of the first two (2), or three
(3), hours of overtime, as specified above.
   Departments and/or divisions may have additional on call or callback
procedures if department policy is approved and on file with the human
resources office. Policy must be approved by the department director and Chief
Administrative Officer in conjunction with the human resources division. (Adm.
Order 2012-17, 12-7-2012; Adm. Order 2019-6, 9-10-2019; Adm. Order 2020-8, 12-
24-2020)
 
 
   January 2021
5-8   5-9
5-8:      CALLBACK DUTY PAY:
Sworn public safety and merit employees shall receive a two (2) hour minimum
amount of paid work time for any call back to duty during an otherwise
scheduled off duty workday, except that police officers providing scheduled
telephone testimony shall receive a one (1) hour minimum amount of paid work
time. If such callback time places the employee in an overtime situation, then
overtime is otherwise payable. Telephone calls from work to an off duty
employee are not considered callback duty, however, calls of fifteen (15)
minutes or longer may be eligible for compensation as paid work time. (See also
compensatory time off policy, work schedules and compensation plan policies in
this manual.) (Adm. Order 2017-2, 4-17-2017; Adm. Order 2019-6, 9-10-2019)
5-9:      OVERTIME:
A.   Authority: When operating requirements or other needs cannot be met during
regular working hours, employees may be scheduled to work overtime hours. When
possible, advance notification of these mandatory assignments will be provided.
All overtime work must receive the Supervisor's prior authorization. Overtime
assignments will be distributed as equitably as practical to all employees
qualified to perform the required work.
B.   Disciplinary Actions; Conditions: Failure to work scheduled overtime or
overtime worked without prior authorization from the Supervisor may result in
disciplinary action, up to and including possible termination of employment.
C.   Eligible Employees: Overtime compensation is paid to all nonexempt
employees in accordance with Federal and State wage and hour restrictions. The
Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) sets forth certain conditions and procedures
under which overtime is to be determined. However, certain positions as defined
by FLSA may not require the payment of overtime, even if the employees in these
positions work over forty (40) hours in a week. Classification under FLSA must
be approved by the human resources office. Notwithstanding the above,
Lieutenants in the Police Department, who are regularly assigned to work as
watch commanders, shall receive overtime compensation equal to sworn police
officers for any work period in which such assignment as a watch commander is
effective. Lieutenants not assigned as watch commanders (i.e., Staff
Lieutenants) shall be treated as other exempt employees.
D.   Rate Of Pay: All work and service activity performed for the City under
the direction and with the approval of supervisory staff shall be considered
compensable hours of work for the purposes of determining hours of work and
 
January 2021
5-9   5-9
   overtime calculations. Overtime shall be paid at a rate of time and one-half
(1 1/2) the equivalent hourly, base wage rate.
E.   Calculation Basis; Actual Hours Worked: Overtime pay is based on actual
hours worked. Paid time off, such as sick leave, vacation leave, holidays or
any other leave of absence will not be considered hours worked for purposes of
performing overtime calculations. Additional compensation, such as callback
duty pay or holiday pay that does not reflect actual hours worked or additional
compensation for special duty that already reflects overtime compensation shall
not be used to calculate additional overtime pay. Notwithstanding the above,
the following time may be used in the calculation of hours worked for purposes
of overtime:
   1.   Employees subject to callback and call out requirements in their job,
shall be allowed to include reasonable travel time directly associated with
travel to perform emergency or additional duties in the computation of hours
worked.
   2.   See also snow removal and overtime policies, Administrative Policy
Manual, as applicable.
F.   Work Periods:
   1.   Sworn Fire Personnel: Sworn fire personnel (i.e., those employees hired
to provide direct fire suppression and emergency relief services) shall be paid
overtime based on FLSA guidelines for those hours over ninety one (91) actually
worked in a twelve (12) day work period. Overtime for these employees will be
paid on the first regularly scheduled payday falling at least one (1) week
after the end of the twelve (12) day work period in which the overtime
occurred.
   2.   Sworn Police Officers: Sworn police officers are paid overtime based on
FLSA guidelines for those hours over forty (40) actually worked in a seven (7)
day work period.
   3.   Other Nonexempt Employees: Other nonexempt employees (except sworn fire
personnel) are paid overtime based on those hours over forty (40) actually
worked in a seven (7) day work period. (See also work schedules; work periods
policy in this manual.) (Adm. Order 2012-17, 12-7-2012; Adm. Order 2019-6, 9-
10-2019; Adm. Order 2020-8, 12-24-2020)
 
 
   January 2021
5-10   5-10
5-10:      COMPENSATORY TIME:
A.   Development Of Policy: This compensatory time policy has been developed
through management-employee discussions and review. This policy reflects the
final "understanding" of management and employees regarding the City's existing
compensatory time policy.
B.   Defined: "Compensatory time" is defined as the accrued time credits an
employee may use as paid time off work, subject to department and City policy,
at the employee's normal, regular base pay rate. Like the cash equivalent under
the City's overtime policy, employees earn one and one-half (1½) hours of
compensatory time for every hour worked after minimum overtime requirements
have been met.
C.   Payout Option: Accumulated compensatory time may be paid out annually. Any
accumulated compensatory time that has not been used as of the final day of the
pay period which includes March 15, or December 15, depending on which date is
designated by the Department Director, may be paid out to the employee at his/
her regular base pay rate on the payday following the pay period which includes
March 15 or December 15. Department Directors shall designate in writing which
payout period is in effect for each division eligible to receive compensatory
time in lieu of overtime. Compensatory time may be carried forward to a new
calendar year or fiscal budget cycle but cannot exceed the stated maximum as
outlined below.
D.   Merit Employees: Department Directors may choose by division to compensate
merit employees for overtime worked with cash or compensatory time. Eligible
employees accrue compensatory time in one-fourth (¼) increments at one and one-
half (1½) times their regular base pay rate for hours worked over forty (40) in
a workweek. Compensatory time for merit employees is allowed to accumulate up
to a maximum of one hundred (100) hours. When this maximum is reached, all
additional overtime hours worked must be paid in the payroll period in which it
was earned.
E.   Sworn Police Officers: Full time sworn police officers accrue compensatory
time in one-fourth (¼) hour increments at time and one-half (1½) of their
regular base pay rate for hours worked over forty (40) in a work week.
Compensatory time for Police Department employees is allowed to accumulate up
to a maximum of one hundred twenty (120) hours. When this maximum is reached,
all additional overtime hours worked must be paid in the payroll period in
which it was earned. Accumulated compensatory time may be used at any time
pursuant to department leave usage requirements.
 
October 2023
5-10   5-11
F.   Full Time Public Services Employees: Compensatory time off is only accrued
in one-fourth (¼) hour increments at a rate of one and one-half (1½) times the
employee's base rate for hours worked over forty (40) in a workweek.
Compensatory time off is allowed to accumulate up to a maximum of two hundred
(200) hours. When this maximum is reached, all additional overtime hours worked
must be paid in the payroll period in which it was earned.
G.   Time Off Plans:
   1.   As allowed under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), Ogden City's
policy allows the Supervisor of a nonexempt employee to schedule the employee
to work a differing number of hours during a pay period. This generally means
the employee works more hours during one (1) portion of a pay period, and less
hours during another portion of the same pay period. Time off plans are
designed to control or limit the accumulation, accrual or payment of earned
compensatory time or overtime pay by one (1) or more employees. Employees
benefit with reduced work periods while still earning their full time
compensation.
   2.   Department Directors can implement time off plans for one (1) or more
of their respective employees as a tool to better manage the time, staff, money
and other resources available to their department.
   3.   The following is an example of a time off plan:
   If the employee works fifty (50) hours in the first week of the pay period,
the first forty (40) hours are at straight time pay and the remaining ten (10)
hours must be credited at time and one-half (1½), or fifteen (15) hours
equivalent to straight time pay. In the second week of the pay period, the
employee is scheduled to work twenty five (25) hours only, and is off the rest
of the week. The employee earns full compensation, since fifteen (15) hours of
equivalent straight time pay is carried into the second week from the first
week. (Adm. Order 2017-2, 4-17-2017; Adm. Order 2019-6, 9-10-2019; Adm. Order
2020-8, 12-24-2020; Ord. 2021-2, 7-13-2021; Adm. Order 2022-8, 11-15-2022; Adm.
Order 2023-3, 5-4-2023)
5-11:      OTHER COMPENSATION CONSIDERATIONS:
A.   Additional Work And Service: Employees who are eligible for overtime
compensation may be required to perform additional work and service outside
their regular job duties that relate to and support the functions of their
primary job duties and the needs of the department.
 
   October 2023
5-11   5-13
B.   Approval; Assignment: Additional work and service outside regular job
duties may be approved and assigned through established authority and performed
while at work and/or during scheduled work times. Such additional work or
service shall be compensated as part of the employee's regular pay or
compensation and is subject to applicable overtime based on the employee's
regular, base pay rate. While not all inclusive, examples of additional duties
and services are: training or instruction (on a formal or informal basis);
assisting another employee in completion of their own duties; or, temporary
work performed outside the normal duties and functions within an employee's job
description. A special consideration is given to police officers who train,
handle and board a member of the City's Canine Corps on their own time and at
their own residence. (See Canine Corps pay policy in this manual.) (Eff. 6-1-
1996; Adm. Order 2019-6, 9-10-2019)
5-12:      CANINE CORPS PAY:
A.   Rate Of Compensation: The City provides additional compensation to police
officers who are assigned the care, training and handling of any member(s) of
the City's Canine Corps. This compensation is based on an overtime pay rate of
time and one-half (11/2) the employee's regular, base pay rate. The assigned
officer is compensated at a rate equivalent to five (5) hours of overtime each
week, which is otherwise stated as seven and one-half (71/2) hours of
equivalent straight time pay.
B.   Pay Irrespective Of Hours Worked: Since the care, training and handling of
any member(s) of the Canine Corps generally occurs at the police officer's
place of residence, and includes hours outside the normal work schedule, the
City pays this equivalent overtime rate each week irrespective of the actual
hours the employee works, and irrespective of whether the employee is on
vacation or other paid time off during each week. (Eff. 6-1-1996; Adm. Order
2019-6, 9-10-2019)
5-13:      DIFFERENTIAL PAY:
A.   Rate of Compensation: The city provides additional compensation to
employees who are assigned specific afternoon and graveyard shifts. This
compensation is a percentage based on the employee's base pay wages.
Definitions of a primary, afternoon, and graveyard shift schedules are
determined by the Department Director and approved by the Chief Administrative
Officer.    
 
January 2023
5-13   5-14
B.   Approval; Assignment: Differential compensation may be approved and
assigned through established authority and subject to budgetary restrictions.
For the purpose of implementation and clarification of the differential policy,
a department policy may be established, if it is not in conflict with this
policy and is approved in writing by the Chief Administrative Officer. (Adm.
Order 2019-6, 9-10-2019)
5-14:      TOTAL REMUNERATION:
It is the policy of the City that employees are compensated based on an adopted
pay plan and approved compensation and benefits. Each compensation rate
established in the pay plan for any position shall represent the total
remuneration for that position, exclusive of any other additional pay,
reimbursement or compensation authorized by City policy or ordinance. Employees
shall receive pay from the City based on the compensation authorized in the pay
plan and in compliance with applicable policy/ordinance, for services rendered
by the employee, either in the discharge of the employee's ordinary duties or
of any additional duties that may be assigned. No employee shall be paid based
on any service or activity which the employee may volunteer to perform outside
those authorized and approved by established policy or procedure. Likewise, no
employee shall be allowed or suffered to work in his/her assigned job or duties
without receiving or being paid applicable compensation for such work. These
restrictions shall not prevent payment of funds to, or for the benefit of,
employees for retirement benefits, medical insurance or any other benefit
approved in the Ogden City budget. (Eff. 6-1-1996; Adm. Order 2019-6, 9-10-
2019)

PREFACE
This Administrative Policy Manual of Ogden City, as supplemented, contains
policies effective through November 25, 2025. Policies of the City effective
after said date supersede the provisions of this manual to the extent that they
are in conflict or inconsistent therewith. Consult the City office in order to
ascertain whether any particular provision of the manual has been amended,
superseded or repealed.
American Legal Publishing
Cincinnati, Ohio

code and they may not show the original policies in their entirety. Please
contact the office of the clerk if there are any questions concerning the
policies listed.
TITLE 1
INTRODUCTION
POLICY 1000
PURPOSE OF ADMINISTRATIVE POLICY MANUAL
SECTION:
1000-1: Purpose
1000-2: Policy
1000-3: Responsibilities
1000-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide uniform information to all departments
regarding administrative policy. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1000-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to establish a citywide
administrative policy manual that is a systematic arrangement of information on
organization, administrative policies, operational procedures, rules and
regulations. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1000-3: RESPONSIBILITIES:
   A.   It is the responsibility of all Ogden City employees to:
      1.   Become aware of and apply all policies presented in this manual.
      2.   Maintain a positive attitude in meeting the needs and expectations
of all residents of this community.
   B.   It is the administrative responsibility of Ogden City to:
      1.   Ensure that this manual presents clearly defined policies and
procedures.
      2.   Provide a process by which policies and procedures are initiated,
properly reviewed, enacted and disseminated.
      3.   Foster a high level of morale and the development of each employee's
skills. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1010
MAINTENANCE OF ADMINISTRATIVE POLICY MANUAL
SECTION:
1010-1: Purpose
1010-2: Policy
1010-3: Responsibilities
1010-4: Procedures
1010-1: PURPOSE:
The purposes of this policy are to:
   A.   Establish general responsibilities as they relate to the construction
and maintenance of the administrative policy manual.
   B.   Initiate procedures for distributing new and/or revised policies to all
administrative policy manual holders.
   C.   Provide an explanation of the numbering and organization system
utilized in the manual.
   D.   Clarify title changes that have occurred since the adoption of this
manual. (Eff. 3-14-2007; Eff. 11-19-2024)
1010-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to:
   A.   Maintain an operating administrative policy manual consisting of the
citywide policies and procedures of Ogden City.
   B.   Establish a consistent numbering system which will allow easy access
and maintenance of the administrative policy manual. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1010-3: RESPONSIBILITIES:
   A.   Mayor: Approve and sign the operating policies and procedures of Ogden
City.
   B.   Chief Administrative Officer:
      1.   Review, for approval, recommendations from the department executive
directors for policy and procedure change.
      2.   Ensure that all policies and procedures adopted are consistent with
Ogden City's administrative code and ordinances as well as the overall
philosophy of Ogden City.
   C.   Department Executive Directors:
      1.   Adhere to all adopted policies and procedures.
      2.   Recommend changes or enhancements for any policy or procedure to the
chief administrative officer, providing input and background information for
the policy under review. (See Policy 1020, "New or Revised Policy And Procedure
Development", of this manual.)
      3.   Develop departmental procedures for line operations which are
consistent with the policies and procedures contained in this manual and other
Ogden City manuals.
      4.   Inform employees of new or revised policies and procedures.
      5.   Distribute the policies and procedures within their department to
all administrative policy manual holders.
   D.   City Recorder: Keep original policy and procedure documents stored and
filed as part of Ogden City official documentation process.
   E.   Administrative Policy Manual Holder:
      1.   Ensure that the administrative policy manual is maintained and kept
up to date as policies and procedures are adopted or amended.
      2.   Ensure availability of the administrative policy manual to all Ogden
City employees working within the department.
   F.   Employees: Adhere to all policies and procedures as outlined in this
manual. (Eff. 3-14-2007; Eff. 11-19-2024)
1010-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Numbering And Placement:
      1.   Once a policy has been signed by the mayor, it will be assigned a
policy number depending on the policy content.
      2.   The policy will be added to the administrative policy manual index
sections arranged for holders' convenience, in alphabetical, numerical, and
subject order and placed in the proper manual section.
   B.   Distribution:
      1.   A copy of the new or revised policies shall be sent to the
administrative policy manual holders.
      2.   Along with the policy, a list of remove and insert directions will
be attached to all policy updates.
   C.   Title Changes: Effective upon passage of the FY25 budget, dated August
6, 2024, every reference in this administrative policy manual to a division
manager or a manager of a specified division, shall hereafter mean a division
director or director of the specified division. Every reference in this
administrative policy manual to a department director or a director of a
specified department shall hereafter mean a department executive director or an
executive director of the specified department. (Eff. 3-14-2007; Eff. 11-19-
2024)
POLICY 1020
NEW OR REVISED POLICY AND PROCEDURE DEVELOPMENT
SECTION:
1020-1: Purpose
1020-2: Policy
1020-3: Responsibilities
1020-4: Procedures
1020-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to outline a format for the development of new or
revised policies and procedures. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1020-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to initiate and maintain a process
for developing and/or revising policies and procedures to comply with the
format of this manual. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1020-3: RESPONSIBILITIES:
   A.   Employees:
      1.   Make upper management aware of concerns and/or changes needed within
their department or citywide.
      2.   Suggest solutions to current policies or undeveloped policies that
may help in alleviating unsafe or inefficient workings.
   B.   Supervisors/Division Managers:
      1.   Review all suggestions and resolve any immediate conflicts
communicated by employees.
      2.   Research all concerns and determine if there is a need for specific
policy revisions and/or development of new policy either outdated or
nonexisting.
      3.   If necessary, submit to the department director requests for changes
or development of a policy, providing to the department director information of
all research obtained.
   C.   Department Directors:
      1.   Review all requests for policy/procedure development originating
within department to determine if change is needed.
      2.   Forward recommended policy development, including a brief outline of
the problem and the proposed policy/procedure solution, to the chief
administrative officer for consideration.
   D.   Chief Administrative Officer:
      1.   Review all requests for policy/procedure development recommended
from the department director. After review, forward the originating request
with concerns/suggestions to the requesting department.
      2.   Aid in developing final changes of policy/procedure development,
forward final draft to the mayor.
   E.   Mayor:
      1.   Review all policy/procedure requests which have been reviewed and
recommended from the chief administrative officer and involved department
director.
      2.   Sign the approved policy for effectiveness and implementation. (Eff.
3-14-2007)
1020-4: PROCEDURES:
All requests for the development of a new or revised policy and/or procedure to
be included in the administrative policy manual shall be processed as follows:
   A.   Requests for policy/procedures changes can originate from any employee
in Ogden City. Through direct communication or in writing any problem shall be
presented to supervisor or division managers. All problems shall include an
outline of the problem and proposed solutions.
   B.   Supervisor and/or division managers shall remedy any immediate problems
as soon as possible. If problem needs to be changed through policy/procedures a
written statement shall be developed outlining the problem to be addressed by
the proposed policy/procedure. The statement shall include proposed solutions
to the problem as well as reference to any existing policies and/or procedures
which may be affected through the request. Research to solutions shall also be
included.
   C.   The written statement shall be forwarded to the department director.
   D.   The department director shall review the statement and determine if the
request should be forwarded to the chief administrative officer for
consideration. The department director shall notify the requesting individual
of the director's decision.
   E.   If the department director determines that the policy/procedure
development request should be forwarded, the department director shall ensure
that the chief administrative officer is provided with the appropriate
background information regarding the request.
   F.   The chief administrative officer will review the request for
consideration. The CAO will then ensure that the policy/procedure development
request is not conflicting to the administrative codes of Ogden City. The CAO
will then return the request to the department director for changes before
forwarding to the mayor.
   G.   The mayor shall review the final policy/procedure development request
for approval or disapproval. If approved, the policy will be signed by the
mayor and distributed and enforced through the proper procedures. (Eff. 3-14-
2007)
TITLE 2
FINANCIAL SERVICES
POLICY 1120
PETTY CASH FUND
SECTION:
1120-1: Purpose
1120-2: Policy
1120-3: Procedures
1120-1: PURPOSE:
The purposes of this policy are to:
   A.   Establish procedures for creating a petty cash fund.
   B.   Assign responsibility for the petty cash fund to the department
director of the department in which the fund is located. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1120-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to establish petty cash funds only
where necessary for the most efficient operations of the department's financial
accounts. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1120-3: PROCEDURES:
   A.   The department director desiring a petty cash fund shall submit a
petition to the director of management services demonstrating a need and
requesting that a petty cash fund be established.
   B.   A requisition is then prepared by the finance manager for the amount
approved.
   C.   The department director establishes control over the fund within the
department. A written control plan will be submitted to the finance manager and
kept on file for future reference, as necessary.
   D.   Cash is replenished by requisitioning the amount spent to the
purchasing division. Receipts must accompany the requisitions and only the
amount that can be accounted for on the receipts will be replenished.
   E.   Petty cash funds will be audited during the year by the finance
manager.
   F.   When the need for petty cash no longer exists (e.g., seasonal
operations), the petty cash fund will be returned to the city cashier to be
receipted and deposited after verification by the finance manager. (Eff. 3-14-
2007)
POLICY 1130
RECEIPT OF MONEY
SECTION:
1130-1: Purpose
1130-2: Policy
1130-3: Responsibilities
1130-4: Procedures
1130-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to explain the procedures for all departments
receiving money, keeping proper money collection records, and delivering money
to the treasury division. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1130-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to:
   A.   Place accountability for money received within each department and to
set guidelines for departmental record keeping.
   B.   Forward all money paid to Ogden City to the city's bank via armored car
service or to the city cashier in the treasury division on a daily basis. (Eff.
3-14-2007)
1130-3: RESPONSIBILITIES:
   A.   It is the responsibility of every employee who is authorized to receive
any fees to keep a record such as cash register tape, receipt book or cash
ledger, containing as much detailed information as practical.
   B.   Department directors shall be accountable for all fees and monies
collected by or paid to them or any employee within their department.
   C.   It shall be the responsibility of the department director to ensure
safeguards against employee fraud; including placement of individuals involved
in the receipt of money. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1130-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Each department receiving money paid to Ogden City, transfers all
deposits directly to the city cashier in the treasury division. All checks and
cash received will be deposited into the bank on a daily basis. Receipts or
other evidence of payment shall be issued on forms provided or approved by the
city treasurer or his/her designee for all fees and monies paid into the city
treasury, consistent with state and city codes.
   B.   The city cashier shall prepare an accounting of all checks and cash,
and prepare a receipt which is filed by the cashier for future reference.
   C.   Departments working later than the city cashier deposit their money in
the bank on a nightly basis.
   D.   The city cashier ensures that the department's deposit sheet balances,
the amounts are then entered into the necessary account through the city's EDEN
software system. The city cashier records and files the department's deposit
sheet for future reference.
   E.   The city cashier prints a daily reconciliation of recorded receipts
from the EDEN software system. The daily receipt reports are filed for future
reference. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1140
BUDGET REVISIONS
SECTION:
1140-1: Purpose
1140-2: Policy
1140-3: Procedures
1140-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to formulate proper documentation and flow of
information for requesting budget revisions. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1140-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to control revisions to the budget
and maintain a balanced budget throughout the year by setting requirements for
all budget revisions. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1140-3: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Division Managers:
      1.   Determine if there is a need for a budget revision.
      2.   Provides recommended use of additional revenue or funding source of
additional expenditure.
      3.   Complete a "request for budget transfer" form found on the intranet
(http://theinsider/) by locating "forms", "finance". These forms have the
routing and approval functions identified.
      4.   Obtain department director's approval.
      5.   Forward requests to comptroller division.
   B.   Budget Accountant:
      1.   Verify balances.
      2.   Check form for completeness of other data.
      3.   Complete reference line and forward to finance manager.
   C.   Finance Manager:
      1.   Review justification.
      2.   Forward recommended budget revision to director of management
services for review.
   D.   Director Of Management Services: Review and recommend budget revision
requests within a department and other budget revisions to the chief
administrative officer.
   E.   Chief Administrative Officer: Review for approval all requested budget
adjustments and take any necessary action.
   F.   Mayor: Take the following actions for a budget revision:
      1.   Review for approval revisions between departments and those
involving nondepartmental or capital improvements.
      2.   Review and recommend revisions involving a change in total revenues
and/or total expenditures.
      3.   Propose expenditures from the contingency fund.
   G.   City Council: Take the following actions for a budget revision:
      1.   Review for approval all transfers between departments, new
appropriations, and the general fund contingency.
      2.   Set a public hearing for the budget revisions requiring a change in
revenue or expenditures by fund or in total.
      3.   Propose expenditures from the contingency fund.
   H.   Corporation Counsel: Prepare all ordinances or resolutions required for
council action to amend the budget from information furnished by the
comptroller division.
   I.   Budget Accountant:
      1.   Verify that all necessary signatures are obtained and a copy of
council action is attached, if council action was necessary,
      2.   Forward a copy to the accounting technician for posting to line
items.
   J.   Accounting Technician: Post approved revisions. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1150
GOODS ON CONSIGNMENT
SECTION:
1150-1: Purpose
1150-2: Policy
1150-3: Procedures
1150-4: Other Items
1150-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to maintain proper audit trails and provide
proper requests for the disbursement of funds. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1150-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to control the disbursement of funds
and maintain proper backup to support such disbursements. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1150-3: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Department:
      1.   Receive and inspect consigned goods.
      2.   Complete "consignment agreement" form found on the intranet (http://
theinsider/) by locating "forms", "finance", including mailing address, social
security or federal ID number, and required signatures.
      3.   Obtain Ogden City PO number from purchasing.
      4.   Distribute copies of form as required.
      5.   Process a "receiving and inspection report" found on the intranet
(http://theinsider/) by locating "forms", "purchasing", for payment per terms
of agreement.
      6.   Maintain a record of items sold and items remaining.
   B.   Purchasing:
      1.   Process payment of items on "receiving and inspection report".
      2.   Maintain a record of items sold and items remaining.
   C.   Treasurer: Mail payment to consignor.
   D.   Division Manager: Return all unsold goods or obtain a new agreement at
the end of the consignment period and notify purchasing. (To ensure
accountability, it is recommended that the consignment period be 3 months or
less.) (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1150-4: OTHER ITEMS:
It is imperative that an accurate record of consignments be maintained and that
payment is mailed promptly to consignees in accordance with terms of the
consignment agreements. (Eff. 3-14-2007)

POLICY 1170
EMPLOYEE COST SAVINGS PROGRAM ADMINISTRATIVE POLICY
SECTION:
1170-1: Purpose
1170-2: Policy
1170-3: Procedures
1170-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to implement the employee cost savings program,
intended to provide a cash incentive for city employees to submit suggestions
for improved government services, cost reductions through increased
efficiencies, or other savings in the operation of the city. (Eff. 3-17-2009)
1170-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of the city that implementation of the employee cost savings
program be done according to guidelines and procedures established by the city.
(Eff. 3-17-2009)
1170-3: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Employee Eligibility: Any full time or part time employee, or a team of
eligible employees, may participate in the program. Elected officials, the CAO,
the executive director of the city council, and department directors, are not
eligible for an award under this program. Employees are ineligible to receive
monetary awards for suggestions that fall within the employee's normal job
duties, responsibilities, or assigned tasks.
   B.   Suggestion Eligibility: Eligible suggestions are ones that are useful,
practical, constructive and beneficial to the city. A suggestion must result in
realized cost savings or net revenue to the city to be eligible for a cash
award.
      1.   Eligible suggestions may include, but are not limited to,
suggestions which:
         a.   Reduce expenditures;
         b.   Increase revenue;
         c.   Eliminate waste or duplication;
         d.   Improve a service or product;
         e.   Conserve energy;
         f.   Increase productivity; or
         g.   Improve safety.
   C.   Suggestion Ineligibility:
      1.   Certain suggestions are typically ineligible, such as:
         a.   Complaints and grievances related to the suggester or another
employee;
         b.   Criticisms of other employees or their performance;
         c.   Proposing items already purchased be used for their intended
purpose;
         d.   Changing salary, position, classification, employee benefits,
holidays, leave benefits, retirement compensation, or any other compensation to
an employee;
         e.   Enforcement of existing laws, policies, procedures, regulations,
rules, etc.;
         f.   Ideas that propose unclear or nonspecific practices;
         g.   Suggestions to reduce expenditures that are already
discretionary;
         h.   Suggestions that are already under active consideration, or that
have already been implemented;
         i.   Suggestions outside the scope of appropriate government services
or activities;
         j.   Suggestions that require a capital investment that the city is
unwilling or unable to undertake;
         k.   Suggestions for which the cost savings or revenue cannot be
calculated or determined; and
         l.   Suggestions to raise revenue by raising taxes or fees.
   D.   Filing A Suggestion: Suggestions shall be considered in the order of
the date and time by which they are officially received by the city recorder's
office, and shall be submitted on a form provided by the recorder's office.
Suggestions shall be specific about the nature of the suggestion and how the
suggestion will improve city operations. The suggester shall include a detailed
analysis of cost savings or net revenue, taking into consideration costs of
implementation. Once filed, suggestions shall be forwarded to the management
services director.
   E.   Employee Cost Savings Review Committee: The CAO shall appoint
individuals to serve on the employee cost savings review committee. Members
shall, at a minimum, include the following individuals: the management services
director, or his or her designee, who shall serve as chair; the comptroller, or
his or her designee; and the department director, or his or her designee, of
the department through which the proposed suggestion is most likely to be
implemented. The city attorney, or his or her designee, shall attend meetings
and provide counsel to the review committee. The employee cost savings program
review committee shall by way of a written decision: 1) determine the
eligibility of a suggestion; 2) determine whether a suggestion should be
recommended to the administration for implementation; 3) verify the cost
savings or net revenue to the city of any suggestion chosen for implementation;
and 4) determine the amount of the cash award to the suggester. Decisions of
the review committee are discretionary. All suggestions approved for
implementation become the property of Ogden City.
   F.   Amount And Payment Of Award: The maximum dollar award shall be twenty
percent (20%) of the first year realized cost savings or net revenue and ten
percent (10%) of the second year realized cost savings or net revenue.
Employees with suggestions that result in improved operations of city
government may be recognized with a letter of commendation in their personnel
file and on their next performance evaluation, regardless of whether the
suggestion results in cost savings or net revenue to the city. Where a cash
award is applicable, such award shall be made after the suggestion has been
successfully implemented and savings realized or revenue gained. Suggestions
that do not result in realized cost savings or net revenue within two (2) years
from the time the suggestion becomes fully operational, and suggestions that
are not implemented within two (2) years of being recommended by the review
committee for implementation, are not eligible for a cash award. Award funds
shall be drawn from the existing appropriation of the department benefitting
from the employee's suggestion. If the suggestion reduces costs from a
nondepartmental fund, an award may be paid from the benefitting fund or
account. An award under this program shall not change the base pay of the
suggester, and shall not be prohibited by other ordinances. The suggester must
be employed by Ogden City at the time of payment of the award to be eligible to
receive the award.
   G.   Reconsideration: A suggester may request that the CAO reconsider a
decision of the review committee. To be valid, an appeal must be filed in
writing, with the city recorder's office, within fifteen (15) calendar days of
the review committee's decision. For a request for reconsideration to be
accepted, new evidence or pertinent information must be provided. The decision
of the CAO is a management prerogative and is final. The use or nonuse of
employee suggestions by the city shall not be the basis of further claims of
any kind by the suggester or the suggester's heirs or assigns.
   H.   Annual Report: On or before November 1 of each year, the management
services director shall prepare and file a report with the city council. The
report shall include the number, types and sources of suggestions; cost savings
and improvements realized; number and amount of awards; and may include
recommendations for adjustments or revisions to the program. (Eff. 3-17-2009)
POLICY 1180
INVESTMENT POLICY
SECTION:
