      5.   When Bid Security Is Necessary: Any construction or demolition bids
that are over twenty five thousand dollars ($25,000.00) must have a bid bond
submitted with the bid. A bid bond usually consists of five percent (5%) of the
total bid made out in the name of "OGDEN CITY CORPORATION" either in the form
of a cashier's check, bank draft, bid bond, or money order. Exceptions to the
bid security requirement may be made by the purchasing agent in consultation
with the legal department.
Other projects may also require that a bid bond be included regardless of the
bid price.
      6.   Time Factors: It is important that enough time is given to the
bidder to respond properly to the request. It is recommended that all bids
under five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) be given three (3) to seven (7) days,
bids over five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) and less than twenty five thousand
dollars ($25,000.00) be given a minimum of five (5) working days and any bid
amounting to twenty five thousand dollars ($25,000.00) and over should be out
for a minimum of fourteen (14) working days.
         a.   Any complicated or elaborate bids should be given approximately
three (3) weeks. If there are any questions regarding the time factor contact
the purchasing division.
         b.   An exact submittal date and time must be set before mailing bids
and no bids are to be accepted after the set time and date.
      7.   Changes In The Bid Or Specifications While Bid Is Out: Sometimes an
error is found in a bid packet in advance of the submittal deadline. When an
error is found, the purchasing division must be notified. Purchasing will
prepare and distribute an addendum.
If a vendor contacts the requesting department and requests more information on
the solicitation, only the bid packet should be discussed. Do not discourage
bidding or add additional information that is not part of the original
solicitation. Any information given to one bidder must be shared with all
bidders.
      8.   Bid Openings: All sealed bids, proposals, or quotes shall be
submitted to and publicly opened by the purchasing agent or by an officer in
the purchasing division who has been duly authorized in writing by said agent
to open such bids.
   B.   How To Prepare A Proposal:
      1.   Requirements: Most of the requirements for bids and quotes will also
apply for proposals. Proposals are designed for the purpose of acquiring
professional services that are not appropriately awarded solely on the basis of
price. This includes services of an architect, artist, consultant, auditor,
etc. Proposal guidelines are available in the purchasing office.
      2.   Advertisements: Proposals are generally advertised to ensure broad
coverage. Contact the purchasing division for advice as to when an
advertisement is not needed.
      3.   Time Factor: The time factors on proposals can be determined the
same way as the bids and quotes. An opening date and time must be set for
proposal as explained in subsection A of this section.
      4.   Priorities: When preparing a proposal, items should be listed
according to the priority that they will take in the final consideration of the
proposal.
      5.   Negotiations: Proposals are designed to allow for negotiations after
the closing of the proposal. Whatever is negotiated with one vendor must be
negotiated with the others.
   C.   Bidders List:
      1.   The purchasing division keeps an updated bidders list on file in its
office. If a department needs information on potential vendors, contact the
purchasing division and it will send a copy of the bidders list that pertains
to the items of concern.
      2.   The purchasing agent may determine and declare a bidder
irresponsible, or for any good and sufficient reason have a vendor removed from
the bidders list. Removal from a bidders list is not permanent but is based on
a reasonable length of time established by the purchasing agent, usually not to
exceed one year.
      3.   For any purchase using federal funds the comptroller shall obtain a
list of disadvantaged business enterprises to be added to the solicitation list
and ensure that the vendor/bidder has not been excluded from providing goods
and/or services for federal award programs by checking the www.sam.gov website.
If a federal or other grant requires stricter procurement requirements, those
requirements shall be followed.
   D.   Rejecting Bids Or Taking Other Than Low Bid:
      1.   The department after reviewing the bids may find that the lowest
bidder does not meet the specification. If this is evident, a written
explanation regarding what is not acceptable must be forwarded to the
purchasing division.
      2.   If the department finds that a bid other than the low bid meets
specifications, justification for each rejected bid must be recorded and
forwarded to the purchasing division for final approval.
      3.   If a department wishes to request accepting other than low bid that
meets specifications, it must be submitted to the chief administrative officer
or designee for approval.
      4.   The department may choose to reject all bids and request a rebid.
Reasons for this may be the bids exceed funding limits, specifications were not
written properly so that the bids are not usable, or in the best interest of
Ogden City it is not expedient to accept any of the offered bids.
      5.   A department may adopt more specific policies to implement goals or
preferences for disadvantaged business enterprises in compliance with federal
or other grant requirements or funding sources.
   E.   Final Approval Of Bids, Quotes, And Proposals:
      1.   The purchasing division will review all bid tabulations and
documents prepared outside of the purchasing division before all final bids,
quotes, and proposals are awarded. Purchasing will send bids to the individual
department for its approval, but the final approval will be made by the
purchasing agent, the director of management services, or the mayor/chief
administrative officer as each case warrants.
   F.   Sole Source Purchases:
      1.   This policy is authorized by and implements section
4-2A-5 of the Ogden municipal code providing an exception to competitive
bidding where: the cost of the supplies or services is negligible in relation
to the costs of purchase by bid; the supplies or services are available from a
single source or bidding procedures are otherwise deemed unlikely to produce a
competitive bid; or circumstances indicate that bidding on the supplies or
services will not be in the best interest of the city.
      2.   Sole source procurement shall be used only if an item is reasonably
available from a single supplier. A requirement for a particular proprietary
item does not justify a sole source procurement if there is more than one
potential bidder or offeror for that item.
Examples of circumstances which may necessitate sole source procurement are:
         a.   Where the compatibility of equipment, accessories, replacement
parts, or service is the paramount consideration;
         b.   Where a sole supplier's item is needed for trial use or testing;
         c.   Procurement of items for resale from the manufacturer;
         d.   Government services or requirements of grants or other funding
sources;
         e.   As required by contract, rule or statute;
         f.   Where transitional costs of changing from an existing vendor or
type of procurement item, including, but not limited to, costs of training,
conversion, compatibility, system downtime, disruption of service, staff time
necessary to implement transition, are unreasonable or cost prohibitive.
      3.   The determination as to whether a procurement shall be made as a
sole source shall be made by the purchasing agent after review by the legal
department. Each request shall be submitted in writing together with a written
justification of the sole source procurement. Sole source approvals may be made
on a fiscal year basis.
   G.   Professional Services:
      1.   Professional services over ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00) shall
be publicly bid as provided in title 4, chapter 2, article B of the Ogden
municipal code unless a mayor's justification is obtained as provided therein.
Professional services costing more than five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) and
up to ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00) may be bid or solicited through written
quotes. A minimum of three (3) written quotes shall be obtained. Quotes may be
made via electronic mail. Record of such written quotes shall be provided to
the purchasing division.
      2.   For professional services five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) or less,
no quotes are required, however, the department or division authorizing the
procurement shall use its best efforts to ensure a competitive rate, for
example, by using a rotation or other system. Departments or divisions are
encouraged to use businesses located within Ogden City for procurement of
professional services five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) or less where
available.
The cumulative threshold for procurement of professional services five thousand
dollars ($5,000.00) or less from the same source is a maximum amount of thirty
thousand dollars ($30,000.00) in a fiscal year. For procurement of professional
services five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) or less that are likely to recur in
a fiscal year above the threshold of thirty thousand dollars ($30,000.00), the
department or division shall follow the appropriate bid process and contract
with a single provider or multiple providers for such professional services for
a period of time not to exceed three (3) years.
      3.   Professional services costing more than five thousand dollars
($5,000.00) and up to ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00) may be obtained as a
sole source upon written request together with written justification of the
sole source procurement. Sole source approvals may be made on a fiscal year
basis. (Eff. 10-22-2015)
POLICY 1230
PURCHASE ORDERS
SECTION:
1230-1: Purpose
1230-2: Policy
1230-3: Responsibility
1230-4: Procedures
1230-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to outline authorizations and procedures needed
for purchase orders and, in compliance with the state's legal standards, to
properly account purchases within the city. (Eff. 6-6-2011)
1230-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to establish purchase orders as a
written verification and/or contract of Ogden City's obligation to pay and the
vendor's obligation to supply a particular service or product. This is the only
legal form of authorization for any purchase made by or for Ogden City
Corporation. (Eff. 6-6-2011)
1230-3: RESPONSIBILITY:
The purchasing division is the only authorized agent to issue a purchase order
to a department, company, or an employee. (Eff. 6-6-2011)
1230-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Unauthorized Purchases:
      1.   It shall be prohibited for any department to split its requirements
for supplies, materials, equipment, or contractual services in order to evade
the proper purchasing procedures, i.e., purchasing in small segments to avoid
advertising, etc.
      2.   When an unauthorized purchase or commitment is made by a department
to a vendor without benefit of a purchase order, the department director
personally may be liable for making payment, not Ogden City Corporation. Any
department making a purchase without a purchase order will be required to
submit a letter of justification to the chief administrative officer prior to
the time of the payment request. Amounts over thirty thousand dollars
($30,000.00) must be approved by the chief administrative officer at the time
of the payment request.
      3.   Unauthorized purchases may not be considered a legal obligation of
the city.
   B.   Contracts:
      1.   Most orders are set up as contracts. They have been bid out in
advance by the purchasing division with a per item unit cost established, e.g.,
chlorine, etc.
      2.   A purchase order does not have a limit on the amount that can be
spent, unless there is a total quantity that has already been established at
the time of the bid.
      3.   The purchasing division retains a complete list of contracts and the
amounts per fiscal year.
   C.   Bulk Or Group Purchasing:
      1.   It is the responsibility of the purchasing division to reduce, to
the maximum extent possible, the number of purchase transactions by combining
into bulk order and contracts the requirements of each department for common
use item or items repetitively purchased, i.e., gasoline, vehicles, etc.
      2.   The purchasing division will, whenever it is in the best interest of
the city, consolidate requirements of using departments into bulk purchases. To
do so, they may hold the requisition of a department until receipt of the other
requisitions calling for like items. This action will be governed by the
urgency in the requesting department.
      3.   The purchasing division may periodically request all departments to
submit estimates of the requirements on common use items for future periods of
time, in order that a tabulation of quantities may be made to determine the
needs for bulk or group purchasing. (Eff. 6-6-2011)
POLICY 1240
EMERGENCY PURCHASES
SECTION:
1240-1: Purpose
1240-2: Policy
1240-3: Definition
1240-4: Responsibility
1240-5: Procedures
1240-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide procedures and guidelines for
purchases in an emergency situation. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1240-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to follow all established emergency
procedures requiring immediate procurement of supplies or contractual services.
(Eff. 3-14-2007)
1240-3: DEFINITION:
EMERGENCY SITUATION: A circumstance or situation threatening injury or damage
as a result of riot mob action, civil disturbance, social disruption, attack,
natural phenomena, technological hazard or happening, or any circumstance which
would delay the work of the city in a manner as to vitally affect life, health
or convenience of the public. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1240-4: RESPONSIBILITY:
   A.   In case of an actual or apparent emergency where goods or services are
required, the mayor/chief administrative officer, department directors, or
other personnel authorized by the mayor or under a city emergency plan, may
approve at the lowest obtainable price, the purchase of any supplies or
contractual services regardless of the amount of the expenditure.
   B.   A full written account of such emergency, together with a requisition
for the material, supplies, or services which were required, shall be submitted
immediately to the purchasing agent with reports available for public
inspection. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1240-5: PROCEDURES:
   A.   If there is a problem that needs to be taken care of immediately, there
are several steps that need to be taken:
      1.   Find the item needed to remedy the situation.
      2.   Call the purchasing division if there is not two (2) sources and
they will supply them.
      3.   After acquiring two (2) competitive prices, contact the purchasing
division and an emergency purchase order will then be issued. The purchasing
division will issue a "confirming" purchase order number to be entered with the
requisition.
      4.   Enter a requisition including the "confirming" purchase order number
within forty eight (48) hours after the purchase.
   B.   The purchasing division is aware that there are times when the
emergency is so great that it is impractical to get competitive prices.
Allowances have been made for this situation. Contact the purchasing division
immediately after becoming aware of an emergency and they will assist you.
   C.   In case of an emergency when the purchasing division is closed,
departments may purchase any item reasonably necessary for and crucial to the
preservation of life, preservation of property, safety of employees and
constituents, and preserving assets of the city. A letter of justification is
to be submitted to the purchasing division within forty eight (48) hours of the
purchase. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1250
INVOICES
SECTION:
1250-1: Purpose
1250-2: Policy
1250-3: Definition
1250-4: Procedures
1250-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to guarantee payment for all goods and services
properly ordered and reviewed. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1250-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to ensure the timely payment of all
invoices incurred on behalf of the city. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1250-3: DEFINITION:
INVOICE: Usually in the process of a delivery (in person or by mail), the
delivery person will leave a slip of paper with the individual that signed for
the order. This is either a packing slip or an invoice. If the paper reads,
"Invoice", or if the slip has prices and totals on it, it should be considered
an invoice. If there are no prices listed on the paperwork, it is a packing
slip. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1250-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Upon receiving a delivery, the department must enter a receiving in the
EDEN system. This will show the department has approved the shipment. (For
procedures on proper completion of receiving slip see policy 1260, "Receiving
And Inspection Reports", of this manual.)
   B.   Delivery slips left with departments should be forwarded to the
purchasing division.
   C.   Any statements or invoices mailed to departments are to be forwarded to
the purchasing division. Do not throw them away.
   D.   The purchasing division will not make payment for an item received
until it receives a billing, invoice and receiving. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1260
RECEIVING AND INSPECTION REPORTS
SECTION:
1260-1: Purpose
1260-2: Policy
1260-3: Responsibility
1260-4: Procedures
1260-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to verify all expenditures made on behalf of
Ogden City. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1260-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to ensure that all purchases are
received completely and in good condition. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1260-3: RESPONSIBILITY:
Each department is responsible for approving and receiving any shipment for
their department. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1260-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Departments: The following procedures are the general steps used for
receiving and inspecting deliveries. Each department may have a variation in
procedures due to the deliveries received and may need to make changes to suit
the different demands:
      1.   As each shipment is received by the department, a receiving is
entered in the EDEN system.
      2.   Always check the packing slip with the actual order. On occasions
what the packing slip describes is not what actually received. If there are any
variances between the two, state such on the packing slip.
      3.   When an order is completed, mark the receiving as complete.
      4.   Because of the size of some of the orders, the purchasing division
may decide to make partial payments. It is important that individual
departments notify the purchasing division when the shipment is completed.
      5.   If a department deletes or returns a part of an order or a total
order, state on the delivery slip or invoice what those items are.
      6.   A purchase order always remains open until the purchasing division
has been notified that the order is complete.
      7.   In some cases, items that have not been received after a certain
time period will be deleted and the purchase order closed. If the department
still wishes to receive the items, the department must reorder them and enter a
new requisition.
   B.   Deliveries: The procedure for deliveries is as follows:
      1.   All requisitions should state where the department wants a delivery
made.
      2.   When purchasing places the order, they will inform the vendor of the
proper delivery location and any other particulars such as a contact person or
to call in advance.
      3.   Upon receiving the delivery, the individual signing for the delivery
is responsible for checking for any defective materials. If they find any
discrepancies at that time, they should notify the delivery person or vendor.
      4.   After receipt of the delivery, a "receiving" (subsection C of this
section) shall be completed in the EDEN system.
      5.   If the shipment is approved and then at a later date found to be
wrong contact the purchasing division. If the payment has already been made,
then it shall be the responsibility of the department to seek a remedy to the
problem.
   C.   Receiving: The procedure for preparing the receiving consists of:
      1.   Date: Day the receiving is generated (should be the same day the
order is received).
      2.   Completion Of Orders: When approving partial shipments, always enter
whether an order is completed or not.
   D.   Partial Receiving And Inspection Reports: Sometimes the vendors will
send only partial shipments. When this happens, enter a receiving for items
received and forward invoices to the purchasing division. Partial payments can
be made in this manner. Purchasing can obtain any discounts that are
applicable, and the city is able to avoid any finance charges that may be
incurred otherwise. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1270
PREPAYMENTS
SECTION:
1270-1: Purpose
1270-2: Policy
1270-3: Definition
1270-4: Procedure
1270-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to make payments in advance for items other than
goods and services (i.e., seminars, publications, lodging) to provide
expedience. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1270-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to make sure that the purchasing
division processes a prepayment check immediately upon receiving the request.
(Eff. 3-14-2007)
1270-3: DEFINITION:
PREPAYMENT: When a department requests a check for services that have not been
received but will be received in the future. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1270-4: PROCEDURE:
   A.   A prepayment will go through the same system of payment as regular
purchase orders.
   B.   The requisition form is always used.
      1.   In the instance of prepayments, fill out all the information
including vendor.
      2.   In the description state the time period that will be covered by the
prepayment and what the service is that will be prepaid.
If there are not invoices, subscription slips, or receipts at the time of the
request for prepayment, fill out the requisition and state in the "special
instructions" "prepay issue check with requisition". This will inform
purchasing that there is a need to pay, that there are no receipts available at
this time, and that the requesting department will be responsible for obtaining
receipts and forwarding them to the purchasing division after monies have been
spent. However, this does not release the department from providing proof of
the expenditure. Proof is required at the time of request for prepayment. (Eff.
3-14-2007)
POLICY 1280
SURPLUS AND OBSOLETE COMMODITY DISPOSITION FOR PERSONAL PROPERTY
SECTION:
1280-1: Purpose
1280-2: Policy
1280-3: Procedures
1280-1: PURPOSE:
The purposes of this policy are to:
   A.   Determine when equipment is considered surplus. As each department
replaces equipment and finds they do not have a use for the old equipment, they
may choose at that time to classify the piece of equipment as surplus,
obsolete, or a waste commodity.
   B.   Set guidelines to be used for the disposition of surplus, obsolete and
waste assets. (Eff. 3-13-2015)
1280-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to provide surplus equipment to
departments in need through trade or transfer and if not needed within the city
to sell it at a public auction. The disposition of all assets must be
accurately recorded. (Eff. 3-13-2015)
1280-3: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Each department director is responsible for obsolete, waste or surplus
equipment that accumulates each year.
   B.   The individual department director must sign and forward a memo and
"surplus inventory" form to the purchasing division stating surplus, obsolete,
or waste commodities that they wish to have removed, sold, or transferred to
another department.
   C.   The purchasing division determines if equipment is considered to be
obsolete, surplus, or a waste commodity. The surplus, obsolete, or waste
commodity list is then passed from the purchasing division to the director of
management services for disposal consideration.
   D.   The director of management services has the authority to dispose of
equipment by one or more of the following means:
      1.   Interdepartmental transfer to the department with the greatest need,
through circulation of departmental memo.
         a.   The transferring department director shall arrange for pick up or
delivery of equipment if it is transferred to another department.
         b.   Interdepartmental transfers of surplus property are at no cost to
the receiving department.
      2.   Trade-ins.
      3.   Sale or irrevocable transfer, usually a public auction.
      4.   Salvage, discard or destruction.
      5.   Surplus revenue generated from the sale of IT equipment shall be
returned to the city tiering expense budget account (1-01-200801-34003) for
distribution back to departments according to currently approved distribution
formulas.
   E.   The "surplus inventory" form is then signed and forwarded by the
director of management services to the purchasing division.
   F.   Purchasing distributes a copy of the "surplus inventory" form to the
fleet division, if appropriate, for authorization to auction and to the
initiating department.
   G.   Personally issued equipment valued up to one thousand dollars
($1,000.00) with a sentimental or other value to the employee, for example,
service firearms and outdated fire protection helmets, may be transferred to
the employee at the discretion of the department director. The equipment shall
be valued and taxed as compensation through payroll. Department directors may
adopt specific policies to implement this program. (Eff. 3-13-2015)
POLICY 1290
PROTESTS, PROTEST STATEMENTS FROM PROSPECTIVE BIDDERS OR PROPOSERS
SECTION:
1290-1: Purpose
1290-2: Policy
1290-3: Procedures
1290-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to adopt rules and regulations pertaining to
protests from prospective bidders or proposers. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1290-2: POLICY:
   A.   In accordance with subsection 4-2A-1C2 of the Ogden municipal code, the
purchasing agency of Ogden City hereby promulgates and adopts the following
rules and regulations pertaining to protests from prospective bidders or
proposers.
   B.   Protest statements will be accepted only from prospective bidders or
proposers whose direct economic interest would be affected by the award of a
contract or by failure to award a contract. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1290-3: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Protests To The City:
      1.   Any protest shall be in writing, submitted to the city's purchasing
agent (CPA) at the address designated in the bid or proposal documents. Any
protest not set forth in writing within the time limits specified in these
procedures is null and void and shall not be considered.
      2.   All protest shall include:
         a.   The name and address of the bidder or proposer;
         b.   The solicitation or project number; and
         c.   A detailed statement as to the nature of the protest and the
grounds on which the protest is made.
      3.   All costs of a protest related to quality or testing shall be the
responsibility of the protestor and undertaken at the protestor's expense.
   B.   Protests Prior To Bid Opening:
      1.   Prior to bid opening, all protests, including protests based upon
alleged restrictive specifications or alleged improprieties in any type of
solicitation, shall be filed with the CPA or designee, not less than seven (7)
calendar days prior to the date of the bid opening.
The CPA, or designee, will promptly make a determination in writing regarding
the validity of the protest and whether or not the bidding process should be
delayed beyond the scheduled date of bid opening. If the CPA determines that
the scheduled date of bid opening be delayed, all respondents to the
solicitation who have furnished their name and address to the authority shall
be notified by written addenda of the delay and the reason thereof. If the
protest is determined to be valid, the CPA, or designee, will respond in
writing to each material issue or issues raised in the protest in a timely
manner prior to proceeding further with the solicitation.
      2.   When a protest has been timely filed with the city through the CPA
prior to award, the city will:
         a.   Not make an award except in the case of an emergency until after
the resolution of the protest, or
         b.   During the pendency of that protest, the city shall not make an
award prior to seven (7) calendar days unless the CPA, or designee, determines
in writing that:
            (1)   The items to be procured are urgently required or that an
emergency exists;
            (2)   Deliver or performance will be unduly delayed by failure to
make an award promptly; or
            (3)   Failure to make a prompt award will otherwise cause undue
harm to the authority.
   C.   Right Of Appeal:
      1.   In the event that a protestor receives an unfavorable decision from
the CPA to its protest, the protestor shall have the right to appeal the
decision of the CPA by submitting a written appeal to the city's mayor, or
mayor's designee, within five (5) calendar days after receipt of the decision
of the CPA. The mayor or mayor's designee, will appoint a protest committee of
at least three (3) members to review the protest and the decision of the CPA.
The protest committee will notify the protestor in writing in a prompt manner
of its decision regarding the protest and the appeal. The city will not make an
award prior to seven (7) calendar days after the decision of the committee,
unless the conditions, supra, are determined in writing to exist.
      2.   If the matter is not resolved after the appeal, the protestor may
continue the protest only by appeal to judicial authority.
   D.   Protest Regarding Award Of Contract:
      1.   If an award of contract is being protested, a protestor shall
protest in writing to the CPA, or designee, as soon as practical, but not later
than five (5) calendar days after the aggrieved person knew or should have
known of the facts and circumstances upon which the protest is based. If the
protest has been timely filed, the CPA, or designee, will promptly make a
determination in writing regarding the validity of the protest and whether or
not the procurement should be delayed.
      2.   If the procurement is delayed, all respondents to the solicitation
who have given their name and address to the city will be notified of the
delay. The CPA, or designee, will respond in writing to each material issue
raised in the protest in a timely manner prior to proceeding further with the
procurement. The city shall not proceed with the procurement prior to seven (7)
calendar days after the decision is rendered by the CPA, or designee, unless
the protestor waives in writing its right to appeal to the mayor, or mayor's
designee, or in the event of an emergency.
      3.   Should a protestor wish to appeal the decision of the CPA concerning
any award of contract, a protestor shall follow the procedures as outlined
above. Failure to follow proper protest procedures shall cause the protest to
be rejected. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1291
TAXPAYER IDENTIFICATION FORM (W-9) REQUIREMENT
SECTION:
1291-1: Purpose
1291-2: Policies
1291-3: Responsibilities
1291-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to formalize the existing requirement for vendors
doing business with the city to provide a completed and signed W-9 IRS tax form
prior to payment being issued. Vendor types include individuals/sole
proprietorships, corporations, partnerships, limited liability companies and
others specified by the internal revenue service. This policy ensures that the
city has on file correct and accurate contact information and taxpayer
identification numbers for vendors so that the city can issue annual tax
statements per IRS requirements. (Eff. 3-8-2010)
1291-2: POLICIES:
All entities doing business with the city must have a completed and signed W-
9 IRS tax form on file with accounts payable. These entities include
individuals/sole proprietorships, corporations, partnerships, limited liability
companies, and others specified by the IRS. The W-9 form must be received prior
to any payment for goods and/or services.
All contracts for goods and services are to contain the following provision:
Furnishing of W-9. Payment under this Agreement is contingent upon Contractor
furnishing City with a signed and completed W-9 IRS tax form. Unless the
Contractor has a current W-9 form on file with the City, one should be provided
to the City at the time of contract routing. Contractor shall cooperate with
City in furnishing any additional information City may need to comply with
rules and regulations of the Internal Revenue Service.
(Eff. 3-8-2010)
1291-3: RESPONSIBILITIES:
Employees responsible for completing contracts shall review the completed/
signed W-9 form to ensure that the contractor/vendor name is identical to the
name supplied on the W-9, and that the form is otherwise signed and complete
prior to routing contract.
Employees processing pay requests shall review the request for payment to
ensure that the payee name, address and SSN/EIN match the information contained
in the W-9 on file prior to processing payment. (Eff. 3-8-2010)
TITLE 4
ALLOWANCES/REIMBURSEMENT EXPENSES
POLICY 1300
VEHICLE ALLOWANCE
SECTION:
1300-1: Purpose
1300-2: Policy
1300-3: Responsibilities
1300-4: Other Items
1300-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish authorization, funding,
responsibility, and liability for vehicle allowances to Ogden City employees.
(Eff. 12-13-2007)
1300-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to provide a vehicle allowance to
individuals designated by ordinance and defined by position. (Eff. 12-13-2007)
1300-3: RESPONSIBILITIES:
   A.   City:
      1.   Determine positions in the city that may be given options for
vehicle allowances and amount of allowance deemed appropriate, as approved by
the chief administrative officer.
      2.   As directed by the chief administrative officer, the department of
management services will process payment of the amount specified as part of the
payroll system.
      3.   The vehicle allowance will be processed as part of a regular payroll
on a monthly basis.
      4.   The method used to provide the vehicle allowance continues to
consider the allowance as income to the employee, under IRS rulings.
      5.   As a compensation item, the gross allowance will be reported through
the payroll system and social security tax will be calculated and deducted. (No
income tax withholding will be processed.)
      6.   The vehicle allowance will be included with the regular W-2 data.
      7.   An employee assigned a city vehicle under the provisions of policy
1530 of this manual may not receive a vehicle allowance.
   B.   Employee:
      1.   Is responsible for all acquisitions and operating expenses of his/
her vehicle including licenses, taxes, insurance, repairs, accidental damage,
gas, oil, tires, etc.
      2.   Is responsible to keep the vehicle in good repair, clean and free
from damage while using on city business.
      3.   Must maintain his/her own records of vehicle expenses to comply with
IRS reporting requirements.
      4.   Is responsible for justification of tax deductions; the city assumes
no responsibility for verification.
      5.   Driver must remain qualified and licensed as per Utah state law and
policy 1520 of this manual.
      6.   Per policy section
1550-3 of this manual, employees must carry automobile insurance that complies
with the state minimum requirements. All employees are required to be in
compliance with state law automobile liability coverage. (Eff. 12-13-2007)
1300-4: OTHER ITEMS:
   A.   IRS rulings dictate how vehicle allowances are to be treated. This
policy provides the simplest, least time consuming process of providing vehicle
allowances.
   B.   The IRS rulings indicate that payment is subject to social security
withholdings and is taxable income.
   C.   Employees receiving a vehicle allowance must also comply with all the
provisions of policy 1550, "Use Of Personal Vehicle For City Business", of this
manual. (Eff. 12-13-2007)
POLICY 1310
TRAVEL ALLOWANCE AND REIMBURSEMENTS
SECTION:
1310-1: Purpose
1310-2: Policy
1310-3: Responsibility
1310-4: Procedures
1310-5: Travel Request Forms
1310-1: PURPOSE:
The purposes of this policy are to:
   A.   Establish citywide policy and procedures regarding travel allowances
and reimbursements for employees conducting Ogden City business.
   B.   Set and maintain guidelines for travel with justification and approval.
(Eff. 10-1-2020)
1310-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to:
   A.   Pay for all reasonable expenses incurred by employees who travel for
the purpose of city business. Travel must have a clear city business purpose
and comply with budgetary guidelines.
   B.   Require all travel to professional activities, outside Ogden City, to
be worthwhile to those attending and beneficial to Ogden City. (Eff. 10-1-2020)
1310-3: RESPONSIBILITY:
The following should be used as general guidelines for travel:
   A.   Department directors and division managers should limit overnight
attendance at out of state professional association conferences to one per year
and in state conferences to two (2) per year.
      1.   Diverse activities and demands within departments may dictate no
travel or more travel each year with justification and approval by the chief
administrative officer.
      2.   Ogden City will support those who choose to hold offices in
professional associations; exceptions to this policy may be granted if the
individual is an officer or on the board of an association.
   B.   Ogden City strives for continuous training and education. There is no
set standard for the frequency of attendance at training sessions. Overnight
seminars, courses and other training need to be justified and approved as
follows:
 
     Attendees      Approved By
Department directors CAO
Division managers    Department directors
Supervisors          Division managers
Other employees      Division managers
 
(Eff. 10-1-2020)
1310-4: PROCEDURES:
Travel allowances and reimbursement requirements are as follows:
   A.   Travel Costs: The city will pay for approved travel costs to include:
      1.   Public transportation (airline, shuttle, taxi, train, bus,
transportation network company, etc.). Travel costs should include local ground
transportation at the travel destination.
         a.   Long distance travel: The city will pay full coach airfare or
mileage (not to exceed airfare) at a maximum of the rate allowed by IRS
regulations. (Employees are encouraged to obtain reduced airfare when
possible.) Airfare should be paid with a department credit card. Use of
employee’s personal credit card is discouraged, but reimbursement for a
personal credit card purchase may be approved by a department director in
exceptional circumstances with adequate documentation.
      2.   Parking for a private vehicle at a public transportation facility
(airport, bus station, etc.) while out of town when a personal vehicle is used
to get to the public transportation facility. Alternatively, the city will pay
for taxi, transportation network company (“TNC”, i.e. Uber, Lyft) or other
commercial transportation to and from the public transportation facility if
such costs are less than the combined costs of parking fees and personal
mileage reimbursement. Multi-day parking should be in long term parking
facilities, unless otherwise justified and approved by department director.
      3.   Mileage at the approved IRS rate for local and out of town travel in
a private vehicle. Employees using a private vehicle for out of town travel
will not be compensated for the first one hundred (100) miles round trip if
they receive a monthly vehicle allowance.
         a.   Local travel: Employee must submit itemized mileage records,
indicating daily mileage driven. (Preferable information would list beginning
and ending mileage but may not always be practical.)
         b.   Out of town: Employee must keep mileage record and/or rental
vehicle receipts to give to the purchasing division.
         c.   Purchasing will pay for mileage reimbursement based on the
current rate allowed by IRS regulations.
      4.   Use of rental vehicles for business purposes is encouraged for
business travel when a city vehicle is unavailable and the department
reasonably determines that the overall travel costs of driving, balanced with
travel time, is less than air travel or otherwise benefits the city’s
interests. Whenever practical, employees should use state contracts and city
contracts for rental vehicles, which include insurance coverage for employee
drivers.
      5.   Parking fees and tolls.
      6.   Transportation costs around the area, in the instance of conferences
and seminars (taxi, bus, etc.).
      7.   The city will pay or reimburse reasonable tips associated with
approved business travel expenses (excluding expenses compensated through per
diem) at a customary rate not to exceed twenty percent (20%).
      8.   An employee may extend their stay before or after approved business
travel in a location, without per diem, provided the employee:
         a.   Stays during non-working days or approved vacation leave; and
         b.   Individually pays for any additional travel expenses incurred for
the extended travel, including food, lodging, and transportation.
         c.   These expenses should be paid separately by employee. In
exceptional circumstances where it is difficult or impossible to separate
payment sources for extended personal lodging, rental car, and similar travel
expenses, an employee may with the pre-approval of a department director be
allowed to reimburse the city for extended personal travel expenses incurred by
the city.
      9.   Receipts must be provided on any one cost of twenty dollars ($20.00)
or more, other than per diem reimbursements. A detailed itemization for those
under twenty dollars ($20.00) will be acceptable, provided the detail includes
date, amount, and purpose.
   B.   Lodging Costs: The city will pay for lodging expense separate from per
diem:
      1.   Lodging costs should be paid with a city credit card, or in
exceptional circumstances, by the employee with reimbursement from the city. An
itemized copy of the billing must be presented to substantiate payment in
either case. Reimbursement is for the actual cost of a reasonable business use
double room (if a room is shared with a nonemployee, the employee is expected
to pay additional cost beyond the double room rate).
         a.   Lodging arrangements are the responsibility of the employee.
         b.   Lodging should usually be paid with a department credit card, but
may alternatively be paid through a properly submitted requisition and purchase
order. Use of employee’s personal credit card is discouraged but reimbursement
for a personal credit card purchase may be approved by a department director in
exceptional circumstances with adequate documentation.
         c.   It is the intent of the city for lodging not to be included in
the per diem rate and is to be paid separately.
      2.   Per diem will be paid at the federally authorized rate for the city
in which the conference, convention, or seminar is located.
         a.   On request for per diem, list the city the employee is traveling
to, the date/time of arrival and departure.
         b.   The federal rate is the amount that can be received and not
justify with receipts. Per diem includes expenses for meals, laundry, cleaning
and pressing of clothing, fees, tips, baggage man and other.
         c.   Generally the city will pay for reasonable amounts above the
federally established rates. However, in order for the city to comply with
federal regulations, the employee must submit receipts for all expenses, not
just for those over the per diem rate, in order for the city to reimburse the
employee for the excess expenses.
         d.   An employee's per diem will not be reduced solely because a
hotel, conference, or seminar offers meals or snacks as a benefit covered in
the general hotel rate or conference/seminar fee, whether or not the employee
participates in the meal. However, if the employee chooses to attend an
optional meal at a conference or seminar for which a separate price is charged,
the employee's per diem will be reduced on a pro-rated basis for the separately
provided meal. An employee's per diem will not be reduced because an employee
is required to attend an occasional meal paid for by the city or a third party
for the purpose of city staff team-building, or marketing, entertaining and
conducting business with outside clients and associates.
         e.   Optional tourist, sporting, social and cultural group
entertainment arranged as part of a conference or seminar but which carry an
extra charge in addition to the conference or seminar attendance fee shall not
be considered a business travel expense. Employees shall individually pay for
any such events, including any travel expenses arising from extension of
business travel for the sole purpose of attending such events. A department
director may grant an exception to this provision by providing a written
justification why the event is a legitimate business travel expense attended by
the employee for the benefit of the city.
         f.   When business travel is for less than twenty four (24) hours but
more than twelve (12) hours and requires traveling more than fifty (50) miles
distance from employee's place of employment and employee's commuting
residence, employee is entitled to per diem allowance and may be provided
lodging upon department director-written pre-approval.
         Per diem allowance is payable to a traveling employee as follows:
 
When travel is:                     Your allowance is:
                                    75 percent of the applicable per diem rate
More than 12 but less than 24 hours for each calendar day you are in a travel
                                    status
24 hours or more, on                 
   The day of departure          75 percent of the applicable per diem rate
   Full days of travel           100 percent of the applicable per diem rate
   The last day of travel        75 percent of the applicable per diem rate
 
   C.   Travel Advances: When deemed necessary, a travel advance may be
requested with a full accounting upon return, with the excess returned or
reimbursement of an additional amount for excess expenditures.
   D.   Receipts: All receipts should be kept and presented to the purchasing
division. For convenience, anticipated expenses may be paid to the traveling
employee in advance if the following information is known:
      1.   Travel cost,
      2.   Room rates,
      3.   Number of days per diem required.
   E.   The city will generally use Federal travel regulations and GSA travel
policies as a guide to resolving per diem allowance questions not specifically
addressed in the city policies and ordinances. A department director may
authorize in writing a variance from Federal guidelines unless the Treasurer's
office determines that a proposed per diem allowance may violate IRS
regulations. (Eff. 10-1-2020)
1310-5: TRAVEL REQUEST FORMS:
   A.   The "Ogden City Travel Authorization" form found on the employee
intranet portal (http://theinsider/) will be used to request payment for travel
expenses. All employees must complete the travel form and have proper approval
before reimbursements will be paid.
   B.   The form provides for payment to outside vendors and city employees.
   C.   Reimbursements may be requested as they occur. Per diem may be
requested up to fourteen (14) days prior to travel by submitting the approved
form to Accounts Payable. (Eff. 10-1-2020)
POLICY 1320
CLOTHING ALLOWANCE
SECTION:
1320-1: Purpose
1320-2: Policy
1320-3: Responsibility
1320-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy to establish procedures and responsibilities for the
acquisition, repairing, cleaning, and replacement of uniforms for employees
required to obtain and wear identifying uniforms. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1320-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to provide a clothing allowance to
individuals designated by the chief administrative officer. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1320-3: RESPONSIBILITY:
   A.   City:
      1.   The chief administrative officer shall determine positions in the
city authorized for clothing allowances.
      2.   The department of management services will process payment of the
amount specified as part of the payroll system, as directed by the chief
administrative officer. An initial clothing allowance will be given to each
individual upon hiring into a position where a clothing allowance is
designated. This initial allowance is a one time payment to help defray the
cost of initial uniform acquisition. This amount will be designated in the
employee handbook.
      3.   The clothing allowance will be processed separately from the regular
payroll on a quarterly basis.
      4.   The clothing allowance is considered as income to the employee as
required by IRS rulings.
      5.   The gross amount of clothing allowances will be reported through the
payroll system and social security tax will be calculated and deducted.
      6.   No income tax will be withheld from clothing allowance payments to
the employee. Nonetheless, each employee may be required by IRS regulation to
pay income tax on a clothing allowance. Each employee is advised to become
familiar with pertinent IRS regulation and/or seek advice from an income tax
preparation service.
      7.   The clothing allowance will be included as a part of gross income on
the regular W-2 form.
   B.   Employee:
      1.   The employee must provide his/her own records of clothing expenses
to comply with IRS reporting requirements. The city's position is that the
clothing allowance is income and not a specific reimbursement of expenses. By
providing payment separately, IRS requirements for deductibility of actual
expenses can be met by the employees.
      2.   Justification of deductions is the employee's responsibility and the
city assumes no responsibility for verification. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1330
EXPENSE REIMBURSEMENT
SECTION:
1330-1: Purpose
1330-2: Policy
1330-3: Responsibilities
1330-4: Procedures
1330-5: Other Items
1330-1: PURPOSE:
The purposes of this policy are to:
   A.   Establish procedures and responsibilities for expense reimbursements to
meet IRS requirements of substantiation and fulfill the city's requirements for
adequate records and justifications of disbursements.
   B.   Establish procedures to reimburse city employees for expenses generated
through performance of their duties and in the fulfillment of employment
requirements. (Eff. 10-5-2020)
1330-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to reimburse employees for bona
fide, necessary, and ordinary out of pocket expenses on the city's behalf and
benefit. (Eff. 10-5-2020)
1330-3: RESPONSIBILITIES:
   A.   Employees are responsible for submitting requests for reimbursements
properly approved and substantiated.
   B.   It is the responsibility of the city to determine whether expenses
submitted are bona fide, necessary, and ordinary in the performance of the
employee's duties and to ensure that the reimbursement is limited to actual
expenditures beneficial to Ogden City. (Eff. 10-5-2020)
1330-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Approved: Permission must be obtained to expend city funds through the
proper authority as follows:
 
  Requested By        Approved By
Department directors CAO
Division managers    Department directors
Supervisors          Division managers
Other employees      Division managers
 
   B.   Expense Reimbursement: Based on IRS substantiated requirements:
      1.   Expenses must all be substantiated with receipts and/or expense
logbook. To comply with IRS regulations the city cannot give blanket
reimbursements except concerning per diem for out of town travel (See policy
1310, "Travel Allowance And Reimbursements", of this title).
      2.   Expenses, other than travel, will be reimbursed upon submission of
receipts attached to a properly executed requisition.
   C.   Travel Per Diem: IRS regulations are very specific on per diem, and
this policy is meant to comply with these regulations.
      1.   Per diem rates established by the federal general services
administration (GSA) will serve as the guide for city per diem rates.
      2.   Per diem rates from the GSA will be used and is to cover expenses
for meals, laundry, cleaning and pressing of clothing, and fees and tips for
services paid to waiters, baggage men, and others.
      3.   Expenses incurred that fall into the per diem expenditure guidelines
that exceed the authorized GSA amount can be reimbursed upon approval as
outlined in subsection A of this section. To qualify for this approval,
substantiation (receipts) for all expenses, not just the excess expenses, must
be submitted.
   D.   The city will generally use Federal travel regulations and GSA travel
policies as a guide to resolving travel reimbursement questions not
specifically addressed in city policies and ordinances. A department director
may authorize in writing a variance from Federal guidelines unless the
Comptroller's office determines that a proposed travel reimbursement may
violate IRS regulations. (Eff. 10-5-2020)
1330-5: OTHER ITEMS:
   A.   This policy is prompted by information that reimbursement items are a
special concern and caution from certified public accountants to monitor this
policy more closely.
   B.   This policy is enacted not only to protect the city from future
problems but, equally important, to protect employees from noncompliance review
by the IRS.
   C.   Substantiation of expenditures is a requirement of IRS regulations and
will be followed to protect the city and employees from unfavorable IRS
scrutiny. (Eff. 10-5-2020)
