POLICY 1350
CELLULAR PHONE STIPENDS
SECTION:
1350-1: Purpose
1350-2: Scope
1350-3: Policy
1350-4: Procedures
1350-1: PURPOSE:
Ogden City recognizes that the performance of certain job responsibilities may
be enhanced by or may require the use of a cellular (cell) phone or a
smartphone. In order to comply with IRS rules regarding the taxable nature of
cellphone usage by employees, as of July 1, 2013, Ogden City will issue a
cellphone stipend for those employees who hold positions where the duties of
that position require the use of a cellphone. The stipend paid to the employee
is taxable. The benefits of such an approach include:
   A.   A call log is not required;
   B.   Monthly reporting is not required;
   C.   A single phone may be used for both personal and business purposes.
(Eff. 7-1-2013)
1350-2: SCOPE:
This policy applies to all Ogden City employees who receive a stipend for their
personal cellphone. (Eff. 7-1-2013)
1350-3: POLICY:
Employees who hold positions that include the need for a cellphone (see
eligibility criteria below) may receive a cellphone stipend to compensate for
business related costs incurred when using their individually owned cellphones.
The city will not own cellphones for the use of individual employees except in
limited situations set forth in subsection 1350-4F of this policy. (Eff. 7-1-
2013)
1350-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Eligibility:
      1.   Employees whose job duties include the frequent need for a cellphone
may receive extra compensation, in the form of a monthly cellphone stipend, to
cover business related costs. An employee is eligible for a personal cellphone
stipend if at least one of the following criteria is met:
         a.   The job function of the employee requires considerable time
outside of the employee's assigned office or work area and it is important to
the department function that the employee is accessible during those times;
         b.   The job function of the employee requires the employee to be
accessible outside of scheduled or normal working hours where time sensitive
decisions or notifications are required;
         c.   The job function of the employee requires the employee to have
wireless data and internet access;
         d.   The employee is designated as a "first responder" to emergencies.
      2.   An employee who only occasionally is contacted for business purposes
is not eligible for a stipend; however, the employee may seek reimbursement for
business related calls pursuant to title 5, administrative policy 1420,
"Wireless Devices Acquisition And Usage", of this manual, as amended.
   B.   Stipend Plan:
      1.   If an employee meets the eligibility requirements for a cellphone,
as outlined above, a stipend may be requested in writing through the employee's
department director.
      2.   Once approved, the stipend amount will be added to the employee's
regular pay. In order to meet IRS guidelines, any amount added for cellphone
service will be identified as a taxable benefit.
      3.   The stipend will be paid as a flat rate per month, based on the
selected service as outlined below. The city will pay only the agreed upon
amount.
      4.   The stipend allowance is neither permanent nor guaranteed. The city
reserves the right to remove a participant from this plan or cancel the stipend
for business reasons.
      5.   The amount of the stipend will be determined based on the type of
plan required of the employee's position to perform the employee's job
responsibilities. A tiered model based on the current market rates includes the
following options:
         a.   Tier 1: Seventy five dollars ($75.00) per month voice and data
(moderate to high use and/or high use of data).
         b.   Tier 2: Fifty five dollars ($55.00) per month voice (moderate to
high use or minimal data).
         c.   Tier 3: Thirty dollars ($30.00) per month voice (low to moderate
use).
      6.   If an employee's job duties do not include the need for a cellphone,
the employee is not eligible for a cellphone stipend.
   C.   Equipment Purchase:
      1.   The city will not pay for the purchase of personal cellphones,
activation or termination fees or insurance.
   D.   Oversight, Approval And Funding:
      1.   Department directors are responsible for identifying employees who
hold positions that include the need for a cellphone. Each department director
is strongly encouraged to review whether a cellular device is necessary, and to
select alternative means of communication, e.g., land lines, mobile radios, or
pagers, when such alternatives would provide adequate and less costly service
to the city.
      2.   The department director is responsible for overseeing employee
cellphone needs and assessing each employee's continued need for a cellphone
for business purposes. The need for a cellphone stipend should be reviewed
annually to determine if existing cellphone stipends should be continued,
modified, or discontinued.
      3.   The CAO shall have final approval authority.
      4.   Stipends are funded by the department submitting the request.
   E.   Employee Responsibilities:
      1.   The employee is responsible for purchasing a cellphone and
establishing a service contract with the cellphone service provider of the
employee's choice. The cellphone contract is in the name of the employee, who
is solely responsible for all payments to the service provider.
      2.   The employee shall make the employee's personal cellphone number
available to city staff and shall carry the telephone and receive city calls
thereon in the same manner and to the same extent as would be expected for a
city issued cellphone.
      3.   Because the cellphone is owned personally by the employee, the
employee may use the phone for both business and personal purposes, as needed.
The employee may, at the employee's expense, add extra services or equipment
features, as desired. If there are problems with service, the employee is
expected to work directly with the carrier for resolution.
      4.   Support from the city's information technology (IT) division is
limited to connecting a personally owned PDA/smartphone to city provided
services, including e-mail, calendar, and contacts.
      5.   An employee receiving a stipend shall provide a copy of the
employee's cellular billing statement within a reasonable time upon request.
      6.   If the employee terminates the wireless contract at any point, the
employee must notify the employee's supervisor within five (5) business days.
      7.   Any cellphone that has data capabilities must be secured based on
current security standards including password protection and encryption. If a
cellphone with data capabilities is stolen or missing, it must be reported to
the employee's supervisor, the wireless device service provider, and to IT as
soon as possible.
      8.   Employees are expected to delete all city data from the cellphone
when their employment with the city is severed, except when required to
maintain that data in compliance with a "litigation hold" notice.
      9.   Given that cellphones and smartphones may be storing and
transferring city records and data, all Ogden City records and computer use
policies are applicable and will be enforced, including, but not limited to,
personnel policies
1-13, "Nondisclosure", and
7-11, "Use Of Electronic Communications And Mail Systems", of the Ogden City
personnel manual; title 5, administrative policies 1430, "Software And
Electronic Data", and 1450, "Computer And Telecommunications Hardware And
Physical Security", of this manual, as amended.
   F.   City Owned Cellphones:
      1.   The city may own and retain a limited number of cellphones for
emergency, disaster recovery, and other business purposes, including wireless
devices assigned to a city function and rotated among on call or on duty
positions in the police, fire, management services and public services
departments.
      2.   Department cellphone equipment shall comply with title 5,
administrative policy 1420, "Wireless Devices Acquisition And Usage", of this
manual, as amended.
   G.   Cancellation:
      1.   Any stipend agreement will immediately be canceled if:
         a.   An employee receiving a cellphone stipend terminates employment
with the city.
         b.   The employee changes position within the city and no longer
requires the use of a cellphone for business reasons.
         c.   There is misuse/misconduct with the phone.
         d.   A decision by management (unrelated to employee misconduct)
results in the need to end the program or there is a change in the employee's
duties. (Eff. 7-1-2013)
TITLE 5
DATA PROCESSING; COMMUNICATION SERVICES
POLICY 1400
PROJECT DEVELOPMENT
SECTION:
1400-1: Purpose
1400-2: Policy
1400-3: Responsibility
1400-4: Glossary Of Terms
1400-5: Procedures
1400-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to:
   A.   Provide guidance to users and the IT Division in proposing,
prioritizing, and implementing technology based projects.
   B.   Make available documentation standards to enable anyone using the
documentation to be able to easily and quickly find information needed. (Eff.
2-28-2019)
1400-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to:
   A.   Provide computer users with technology solutions to satisfy specific
department needs.
   B.   Develop documentation to assist the user in answering questions
regarding the computer system in an efficient and timely manner.
   C.   Consult with IT Division staff when users propose, initiate,
facilitate, review, and implement City technology projects. (Eff. 2-28-2019)
1400-3: RESPONSIBILITY:
   A.   The users and department/division requesting projects are responsible
for engaging IT Customer Account Coordinator (CAC) staff at ideation of each
project, and for the high level decision making, overall planning,
prioritization, and implementation of their projects including overseeing
preparation of any required contractual agreements. If a department/division
fails to notify IT of project initiation or acquisition of equipment, IT may
charge back to the department for the costs associated with making any
modifications.
   B.   The IT Division has the responsibility of managing project activities
under the direction of the requesting user, and providing project consultation,
coordination, facilitation, and technical services to users, making work
assignments, ensuring programming, security, and documentation standards are
adhered to, and providing system hardware and software to run the application.
   C.   Technology projects are proposed, prioritized, approved, and developed
according to approved technology and project governance. (See Ogden City
administrative policies, title 5, Data Processing; Communications Services).
(Eff. 2-28-2019)
1400-4: GLOSSARY OF TERMS:
PROJECT: A temporary endeavor with a defined beginning and end (usually time
constrained, and often constrained by funding or deliverables), undertaken to
meet unique goals and objectives, and to bring about beneficial change or added
value. Typical steps in a project are planning, organizing, implementing,
controlling, and closeout. The temporary nature of projects stands in contrast
with business as usual (or operations), which are repetitive, permanent, or
semipermanent functional activities to produce products or services. (Eff. 2-
28-2019)
1400-5: PROCEDURES:
   A.   All technology projects are submitted to IT management. Projects are
requested, scored, approved, and implemented according to the following
procedures. (See technical standards and operational protocol document for
additional project governance details.)
   B.   Users initiate technology project requests by consulting their IT
Division Customer Account Coordinator (CAC).
   C.   The IT CAC creates a project request and submits it to IT management
for review to assure the request meets City infrastructure, security, and other
associated requirements. In some cases, where IT services are minimally needed,
the user may be directed to proceed with their project without direct IT
involvement.
   D.   The IT Division Manager submits projects to the IT Steering Committee
for review. This committee may adjust project priority. (See technical
standards and operational protocol document details.)
   E.   The IT CAC, in conjunction with the requesting department, undertakes
detailed analysis of the approved request requirements and prepares a written,
detailed project scope document (PSD).
   F.   The completed PSD, which contains a complete scope including
specifications, requirements, project acceptance criteria, scheduling, and
project funding, is submitted to the IT Division Manager and user stakeholders
for approval.
   G.   The IT CAC manages the project development under the direction of the
requesting user and performs thorough testing on the project before turning
work over to the user as a finished product. The user is given an opportunity
to test the product before final acceptance to ensure it meets the acceptance
criterion specifications in the PSD proposal.
   H.   Upon user acceptance user stakeholders and IT signs the project
completion document.
   I.   The IT CAC will record time and costs expended on projects on the PSD.
This data is important for future project budgeting and estimation purposes.
   J.   The IT CAC coordinates compilation of documentation throughout the
process, publishes it in a professional manner for both the IT Division and the
requesting department, and logs it appropriately. (Eff. 2-28-2019)
POLICY 1410
HARDWARE/SOFTWARE PURCHASING
SECTION:
1410-1: Purpose
1410-2: Policy
1410-3: Procedures
1410-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish standards for purchasing and
stocking information technology (IT) supplies, including hardware and software
items. (Eff. 10-3-2013)
1410-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation that city purchased computer
hardware and software are requested and purchased through the IT division. With
department director and IT approval, departments may purchase certain computer
accessory equipment, software, and desktop printers directly from vendors of
their choice as per subsection 1410-3C of this policy. Additionally, with
department director approval, employees may choose to privately purchase
desktop or mobile computing devices or software that they use for city business
purposes. The city shall not participate in private purchases of hardware,
software, or services. Employees conducting city business on privately
purchased computing devices are required to comply with all applicable laws and
policies, including the Utah government records access and management act.
(Eff. 10-3-2013)
1410-3: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Purchases for city purchased hardware and software can be made at any
time; however, the most desirable is at annual budget request time.
   B.   Purchases require the requesting department to complete the request for
IT equipment and services form with required signature approvals.
   C.   With department head and IT approval certain computing equipment and
software may be purchased by the department. Please see http://insider/ for
current list of approved hardware and software. All such purchases shall comply
with all current city purchasing policies and procedures.
   D.   IT shall approve all purchases of computing equipment that will connect
to the city network, be locally loaded with city business applications, or, for
printers, be maintained under the city printer/copier maintenance contracts. IT
shall approve all purchases of software that are considered a city business
application, are accessed via the city network, or are shared by multiple
departments.
   E.   For purchases made through IT, funds will be added to the requesting
department's IT budget or charged to the department's account.
   F.   On a monthly basis, IT will make a list of funds to be transferred to
IT to cover intrayear requests for city IT purchases and submit it to the
comptroller for the appropriate journal entries.
   G.   The cost of software provided by the city, but purchased using an
employee's personal account (such as mobile apps), may be required to be
reimbursed by the employee to the city when the employee leaves city
employment, unless otherwise approved by the CAO.
   H.   City purchased desktop or mobile software may be installed on privately
purchased hardware for city business purposes as approved by department
directors.
   I.   Private purchases for hardware and software used for city business,
such as apps for iPads, speakers, and language learning software, may be made
by an employee at any time and from any vendor and installed on city purchased
hardware as approved by department directors (see policy 1430 of this title).
The city will not reimburse for such private purchases. City resources shall
not be used in making private purchases.
   J.   All city purchased computer equipment and software is eligible for city
technical support. Technical support of personally purchased computer equipment
and software used by city employees for personal or city business is the
responsibility of the individual and not the city unless authorized by the
director of management services or CAO. (See policy 1460 of this title.)
   K.   Purchasing division has the responsibility to put in place such
controls as are necessary to meet the policies outlined for the purchasing of
computer software and hardware. All city provided hardware and software
purchases must comply with Ogden City's purchasing procedures.
   L.   Because technology changes rapidly this policy is subject to revision
at any time. (Eff. 10-3-2013)
POLICY 1420
WIRELESS DEVICES ACQUISITION AND USAGE
SECTION:
1420-1: Purpose
1420-2: Policy
1420-3: Procedures
1420-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide procedures for the acquisition and
administration of city owned wireless devices, such as cellular phones, to set
standard usage guidelines, and to establish processes for the dissemination of
wireless phone numbers and services. (Eff. 7-1-2013)
1420-2: POLICY:
Ogden City recognizes the benefits of providing state of the art communications
tools to its employees for the benefit of the citizens. Therefore, it is the
policy of Ogden City Corporation to provide city owned wireless devices to
selected personnel for the convenience of the city and the individual(s) in the
performance of their official duties. It is the general policy of Ogden City
that no more than one city owned wireless device will be provided per
individual, unless incidental to other approved IT equipment. It is also the
policy of Ogden City Corporation that wireless device usage should be based
upon cost effective practices that are applied consistently and comply with all
other city policy, procedures, rules and regulations. It is the policy of Ogden
City Corporation to guarantee payment of cellular services for exclusively city
owned phones. This policy of Ogden City Corporation will be administered by the
IT division under the guidance of the director of management services. (Eff. 7-
1-2013)
1420-3: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Acquisitions:
      1.   All requests for wireless devices should be made during the
development of the budget and be subject to the budget review process.
Department directors determine whom is issued a city cellphone and its
associated service levels and plan.
      2.   In the event requirements arise during the fiscal year that could
not be anticipated during the budget process, all requests for wireless devices
must be made by a department director or division manager to the IT division.
The request will specify by position the number of phones required. A separate
justification for each device will accompany the request clearly demonstrating
the business case for the requested device. Each justification must be approved
by the applicable department director, the director of management services, and
the chief administrative officer prior to submission to the IT division.
      3.   Before any request will proceed, the department or division must
have sufficient money in the appropriate budget accounts to cover both the
acquisition cost and the expected monthly charges for the year. The estimated
amount required to cover both the acquisition cost and the expected monthly
charges for the year shall be estimated by the IT division in consultation with
the comptroller.
      4.   The IT division will, in accordance with city purchasing policies,
select vendors for the equipment and make sole determination as to the
available options of type, model, specification, accessory equipment, plan
minutes and coverage area, along with other special features that will be
allowed. Department directors may choose from the established available
options.
      5.   All wireless devices used for city business will use a common
service provider to the extent possible. The final selection of the service
provider is the responsibility of the director of management services. There
are no exceptions to this requirement without written permission from either
the director of management services or the chief administrative officer.
      6.   The phone numbers for all devices paid for by the city are owned by
Ogden City Corporation. The IT division along with the management services
director will determine the release of numbers to individuals upon leaving
employment with Ogden City.
   B.   Usage:
      1.   Each division manager is responsible for the appropriate use of all
wireless devices within the division. Each individual assigned a wireless
device is responsible for the appropriate usage of the device and will be
responsible for repayment to the city through payroll deduction, if necessary,
of any unauthorized or unallowable expenses incurred through the misuse or loss
of the wireless phone provided. Payroll deduction should not be used as a means
to continuously pay for personal use.
      2.   Usage of assigned wireless devices should be for official use only.
It is recognized that some incidental and minimal personal use may be required
in order to save time and make the employee more efficient. This type of use
should be held to a minimum. Personal wireless telephone usage that falls
within the provided service plan, including occasional and minimal downloading
of application software for personal use, where no additional costs are
incurred by the city as a result, is permissible. If an occasion arises in
which there are additional costs, the individual must identify those costs on
the bill and indicate whether they are related to personal or city business.
Personal usage which results in additional charges to the city should be
reimbursed to the city and it is the personal responsibility of the individual
assigned the cellular phone to make such reimbursement in a timely fashion. The
chief administrative officer shall have the discretion to waive reimbursement
when circumstances are deemed beyond the control of the employee or otherwise
in the best interest of the city.
      3.   City owned wireless devices are provided to selected personnel for
the convenience of the city and the individual(s) in the performance of their
official duties. In these instances, wireless telephone and related charges
must be directly billed to the city. The wireless billing plan provided for
each wireless device must be commensurate and adjusted with the anticipated
business needs of the department or division.
      4.   Department directors and division managers will receive access to a
monthly statement of total airtime charges and usage which results in
additional charges above the estimated usage. Department directors or division
managers, as applicable, will be responsible for completing a written
justification or notice of reimbursement for each individual who is over their
plan minutes. Department directors are to review each justification and
determine the appropriate level of use for his or her department. Individual
monthly charges in excess of one hundred fifty dollars ($150.00) will be
audited and reviewed with the chief administrative officer or assigned
representative.
      5.   Wireless devices should not be used when usage might reasonably
result in the user being distracted so as to cause injury to persons or damage
to property. City requirements for employee use of "hands free" equipment while
operating a vehicle are provided in the Ogden City personnel policy manual and
are not intended to be superseded by the provisions of this policy.
      6.   Employees should immediately report any theft or loss of equipment
to the IT division and upon separation from city service, employees must return
equipment to their division or the IT division. Employees are responsible for
coordinating the repair or replacement of city equipment through the IT
division.
   C.   Stipend To Employees For City Use Of Personal Cellular Telephone
Service:
      1.   Certain Ogden City employees are eligible to receive a stipend to
compensate for business related costs incurred when using their personally
owned cellphones. See title 4, policy 1350, "Cellular Phone Stipends", of this
manual.
   D.   Reimbursement To Employees For Cellular Telephone Expenses:
      1.   Employees who maintain personal wireless devices, but who do not
receive a cell telephone stipend, may be reimbursed for charges incurred when
their telephone is used for city business, provided that such usage is
reasonable and falls outside the service plan resulting in additional costs
incurred to the employee.
      2.   In order to receive reimbursement, the employee must provide a copy
of their entire bill covering the applicable billing period including the
charges for which they are seeking reimbursement and clearly identify those
costs on the bill related to city business.
      3.   Reimbursement to an individual should not exceed sixty dollars
($60.00) in any three (3) month period. In such cases it is the responsibility
of the department director or division manager to determine whether the
individual should be issued a city owned cellular telephone or offered a
stipend and make the necessary request. Reimbursement may not exceed one
hundred dollars ($100.00) in any six (6) month period without the approval of
the department director. (Eff. 7-1-2013)
POLICY 1430
SOFTWARE AND ELECTRONIC DATA
SECTION:
1430-1: Purpose
1430-2: Responsibility
1430-3: Scope
1430-4: Need For Policy
1430-5: Glossary Of Terms
1430-6: Policies And Procedures
1430-7: Compliance
1430-8: Enforcement
1430-1: PURPOSE:
To establish a uniform policy for: a) the protection of the city from any
liability as a result of unauthorized (illegal) software copying, b) the
reproduction of or access to any software or electronic data for business or
personal use, c) the prevention of software viruses, d) the purchasing of
personal computer software, and e) the deterrence of personal computer misuse
in the workplace.
The overall objectives of the policies and procedures are to contain costs,
promote quality, ensure compatibility, maintain standards, and to provide
maximum software support. (Eff. 1-8-2016)
1430-2: RESPONSIBILITY:
Information technology division (IT) has the authority and responsibility to
ensure, where possible, that unauthorized copying of or access to software or
electronic data does not occur and shall put in place such controls as are
necessary to limit software piracy, viruses, and other security issues.
Information technology division (IT) shall make the initial determination based
upon the software license agreement, as to whether or not software may be
copied and/or installed on a computer. Additionally, IT shall make the initial
determination based upon electronic data security policies, as to what
electronic data is accessible to certain employees. The final authority for
interpretation of software license agreements and electronic data security
rests with the city attorney's office, or as otherwise set forth in city
policy. IT shall also establish password standards for the city.
Purchasing has the responsibility to put in place such controls as are
necessary to meet the policies outlined for the purchasing of computer software
and hardware. (Eff. 1-8-2016)
1430-3: SCOPE:
This policy applies to all electronic data and software, regardless of the
operating environment or source of that software or electronic data and to all
employees, interns, and volunteers of Ogden City. The term employees, as used
below, includes interns and volunteers. (Eff. 1-8-2016)
1430-4: NEED FOR POLICY:
With the widespread use of computers, the need for policies and procedures has
been apparent. Any duplication of licensed software, except for backup
purposes, may be a violation of the federal copyright law. Purchase of software
without authorization from IT can result in poor quality control, unnecessary
expense, incompatibility, and virus proliferation or other security issues.
Unauthorized access to electronic data may be in violation of city policies.
It is important to note that the software itself is not purchased; a license to
use the software is purchased. Title 17 of the U.S. Code states it is illegal
to make copies of software for any other purpose without the permission of the
publisher. The only exception is the user's right to make a backup copy for
archival purposes. The city and the employee may be held liable for any
violations of the license agreement. (Eff. 1-8-2016)
1430-5: GLOSSARY OF TERMS:
BACKUP/ARCHIVAL COPY: A copy of software that is provided or made in case the
primary copy becomes unusable.
ELECTRONIC DATA: Data and information produced or stored for city purposes
using any desktop, database, or other software product regardless of who
produced it or when, where, and why it was produced.
LICENSE AGREEMENT: A document and the accompanying payment of money to a
vendor, entitling the purchaser to run a software product on his or her
computer. A license contract usually also commits the vendor to provide
assistance and repairs when problems occur, updates to the products, etc., and
provides legal safeguards to prevent the buyer from selling or giving a copy of
the software to someone else.
MOBILE MEDIA: Any computing or data storage device which is physically separate
from the city's computing infrastructure housed in any of its facilities.
"Mobile media" includes, but is not limited to, desktop computers, laptop
computers, tablet/pad devices, cellphones, smartphones, thumb (USB) drives,
voice recorders, mag tapes, CDs, DVDs, cards, etc.
PROPRIETARY SOFTWARE: Computer software that an individual or business retains
exclusive rights to produce and/or sell.
PUBLIC DOMAIN SOFTWARE: Computer software that neither individuals nor
businesses retain a right to sell, produce, or reproduce. Public domain
software is not copyrighted. Often public domain software is developed using
tax dollars.
SOFTWARE: Instructions (computer programs) which operate the physical equipment
of a computer and manipulate data. Software includes compilers, assemblers,
interpreters, operating systems, firmware, and application programs.
SOFTWARE CONTRACTS: Contracts between the users of proprietary software
products and the owners of those products. These contracts generally describe
the user's authority to reproduce and distribute copies of the software
products. (Eff. 1-8-2016)
1430-6: POLICIES AND PROCEDURES:
   A.   Use Of Software: Information technology division (IT) shall purchase
fully licensed copies of computer software from a variety of publishers and
vendors. Licensed and registered copies of software programs are placed on
computers within the company and appropriate backup copies made in accordance
with the licensing agreements and company policies. No other copies of this
software or its documentation can be made without the express written consent
of the software publisher and Ogden City (information technology division).
      1.   Purchase Of Software: The software must be approved by information
technology division (IT) and purchasing prior to the purchase (see policy 1410
of this title). Where applicable, policy 1400 of this title governing project
development shall be applied.
         a.   The purchased software must be registered with the IT division to
be authorized Ogden City software.
         b.   The software distribution media and proof of proper licensing
must be kept on file with the IT division.
         c.   The purchased software must comply with industry standard
security practices and specifications.
         d.   Games and other nonbusiness related software are not allowed or
authorized for use on any city computer.
      2.   Public Domain Software: All public domain software irrespective of
source, including demo software, must be first reviewed and approved by IT.
      3.   Software From Other Sources: Information technology division (IT)
will provide copies of legally acquired software to meet all legitimate
business needs in a timely fashion and in sufficient quantities for all of our
city computers. The use of software obtained from any other source could
present security and legal threats to the company, and such use is strictly
prohibited.
      4.   Additional Copies: In some cases, the license agreement for a
particular software program may permit an additional copy to be placed on a
portable computer or home computer provided only one user uses both
installations. Employees will not make such additional copies of software or
documentation for the software without the approval of information technology
division (IT).
      5.   Unauthorized Copies: The unauthorized duplication of copyrighted
software or documentation is a violation of the law and is contrary to
established standards of conduct for Ogden City employees. Employees who make,
acquire or use unauthorized copies of computer software or documentation will
be subject to immediate discipline up to and including immediate termination of
employment.
      6.   Internal Controls: Information technology division (IT) reserves the
right to protect its reputation and its investment in computer software by
enforcing strong internal controls to prevent the making or use of unauthorized
copies of software. These controls may include periodic assessments of software
use, announced and unannounced audits of company computers to assure
compliance, the removal of any software found on Ogden City property for which
a valid license or proof of license cannot be determined, and disciplinary
actions, including termination, in the event of employee violation of this
policy.
   B.   Protection Of Digital Infrastructure: Ogden City infrastructure must be
protected against unauthorized exposure, tampering, loss and destruction. All
city devices and/or users shall follow city and industry's standards to protect
against external and internal threats.
      1.   Antivirus Software:
         a.   All devices connected to the Ogden City network or networked
resources shall have antivirus software installed and configured so that the
virus definition files are current, routinely and automatically updated. The
antivirus software must be actively running on these devices.
         b.   If an employee receives what he/she believes to be a virus, or
suspects that a computer is infected with a virus, it shall be reported
immediately to the information technology division (IT). The information
technology division (IT) shall remove the virus from the network.
         c.   No employee shall attempt to destroy or remove a virus or any
evidence of that virus without direction from IT.
         d.   Exceptions to this policy may be allowed if a computer device
cannot have antivirus software installed. In these cases, IT shall implement
procedures to protect the device from infection.
      2.   Use Of External Devices:
         a.   External Network Devices: All external unauthorized devices are
not allowed to connect to the Ogden City LAN except as approved by the director
of management services and IT. Information technology division (IT) offers a
"free" external wi-fi connect for these devices.
         b.   VPN Use: Employees shall not connect personal equipment or
devices to the Ogden City network, including using virtual private networks
(VPN).
            (1)   Employees with VPN privileges shall ensure that unauthorized
devices or users are not allowed access to Ogden City internal networks.
            (2)   VPN use shall be controlled in accordance with the city
password policy.
            (3)   Only one network connection per user is allowed.
            (4)   VPN users shall be automatically disconnected from Ogden City
networks after fifteen (15) minutes of inactivity and shall not be connected
longer than twelve (12) hours in succession.
         c.   Data Storage On External Devices:
            (1)   Storage Of Electronic Data: Electronic city data is stored in
files on appropriate drives as outlined by IT. Citywide file shares are
designated for individuals, departments and citywide sharing, and shall not be
stored on personal storage devices.
            (2)   Electronic Media Policies: Employees shall adhere to
electronic media policies as described in subsection 7-11D of the "Ogden City
Employee Policies And Procedures Manual".
      3.   Security Devices:
         a.   Locking Device: When leaving any device, for any length of time,
employees should lock their devices.
         b.   Remote Or Console Access: No remote or console access is allowed
to any servers unless approved by the employee's department director and the IT
division manager.
      4.   Passwords:
         a.   Requirements: Employees shall be required to use passwords to
access networks and software applications. Passwords shall be kept private and
not shared with other workers. Employees shall receive automated requests every
three (3) months to change their passwords and will be allowed a grace period
for such changes. Password requirements are as follows:
            (1)   Minimum length: Eight (8) characters.
            (2)   Minimum complexity: Passwords should use at least three (3)
of the following: lower case, upper case, numbers, special characters (!, @, #,
$, %, ^, &, *, etc.).
            (3)   Password history: Ten (10) unique passwords required before
an old password may be reused.
            (4)   Maximum password age: Ninety (90) days.
            (5)   Account lockout threshold: Three (3) failed login attempts.
            (6)   Account lockout duration: Thirty (30) minutes.
            (7)   Rules that apply to passwords also apply to passphrases which
are used for public/private key authentication.
         b.   Application And Software Passwords: The information technology
division (IT) captures and retains all internal and external city application
and software passwords. The information technology division (IT) will follow
industry standards for changing and storing application, software, and hardware
passwords.
         c.   Access Approval: IT shall not access an employee's workstation
without the employee's approval or the approval of the employee's department
director, management services director, or CAO.
   C.   City Electronic Data And Information:
      1.   Ownership Of Electronic Data And Files: All electronic data and
files created by city employees are owned by Ogden City. Employees shall adhere
to electronic media policies as described in subsection 7-11D of the "Ogden
City Employee Policies And Procedures Manual".
      2.   Data Security: The IT division controls general security and access
to electronic data for the protection and risk of the city. Department and
division managers determine those employees allowed to access electronic data.
         a.   Employees with rights to electronic data and information are
responsible to assure that only approved persons view or use such data and may
not grant access rights to any other person without approval of their manager/
supervisor.
         b.   Employees shall not leave screens and/or reports containing
electronic data visible to unauthorized persons and are required to secure such
electronic data and lock their computer to prevent access to such data.
         c.   Should employees discover or suspect unauthorized access to
electronic data they should report this immediately to their supervisor/
manager.
      3.   Backing Up Of Data: Electronic data is backed up on a regular basis
by IT and has specific retention periods. Data backups are intended for
recovery only and not for permanent storage.
         a.   Requests for data recovery shall be submitted to the IT help desk
and must provide the full directory path location, the full file name, and the
date and time the file was lost, deleted, overwritten, or corrupted.
            (1)   Due to the possible existence of multiple file versions a
partial loss of work may occur depending on the state of the file during the
backup and the amount of work done on the file between the last successful
backup and the point of failure.
            (2)   Occasionally recovery problems preventing a file from being
restored do occur. These include, but are not limited to, network outages, file
corruption, the file being in an "open" state when it is backed up, or the
file's age.
            (3)   Every attempt will be made to recover a file that has been
backed up and that is recoverable within a reasonable period of time. This can
take from several hours to several days.
         b.   The city IT division captures and retains backup data as per the
following:
            (1)   Cellphones: No cellphone data is captured or retained.
            (2)   Desk Phones: No call records or call detail is captured or
retained.
            (3)   E-mails: Daily backups are retained for the most recent one
month. (If an e-mail is received and then physically deleted prior to being
backed up at the end of the day then that e-mail is not retained.)
            (4)   Network Data - H, X, And Y Drives: Rolling three (3)
consecutive day backup. Rolling weekly backup. Rolling monthly backup. Rolling
quarterly backup. We retain the past two (2) full quarters. Thus, worst case
scenario would be a two (2) month old data file.
            (5)   C Drives: Not backed up or retained.
            (6)   Internet Activity: All internet traffic is captured by IP
address and user name and retained for two (2) months, excepting VPN user
internet traffic. We do not capture VPN internet traffic or any internet
traffic outside of the city network.
            (7)   Document Retention Policy: City employees shall be
responsible for classifying and storing electronic documents according to the
city's document retention policy.
      4.   Database Access:
         a.   All databases, tables, views, jobs, logins, permissions, etc.,
shall be created and maintained under the direction of the IT division manager.
         b.   All users of city data shall be associated with active directory
groups and no single login shall be permitted without approval of the IT
division manager.
         c.   To maintain the integrity of city equipment, databases, and
networks, administrative permissions shall not be granted to user accounts
unless approved by the employee's department director and the IT division
manager.
         d.   No remote or console access is allowed to any database servers
unless approved by the employee's department director and the IT division
manager.
         e.   All database development shall be done in database test
environments.
         f.   Changes to production databases shall be accomplished via
application software. Direct changes to database data or data structures shall
only be performed by the IT database administrator upon approval of the IT
division manager.
         g.   All databases will follow Ogden City policies for logging data,
monitoring servers, and backup and retention.
      5.   Highly Sensitive Data: Access to highly sensitive data must be
approved by the department director, city attorney, or CAO depending on which
area owns the information.
         a.   When moving or copying sensitive data to or from any mobile
media:
            (1)   The individual that is primarily affiliated with the data
must state in writing that such storage is an essential business need and file
a signed electronic access agreement with the human resources division.
            (2)   The data must be securely encrypted and password protected on
the electronic device or media according to encryption methods established by
the IT division. Security encryption on data device will be maintained by the
owner of said data device.
            (3)   As soon as the data is no longer required, it must be deleted
from the mobile media using secure methods established by the IT division, or
the mobile media upon which it was housed must be destroyed.
      6.   Sensitive Data: Access to sensitive data must be job related and
approved based upon job function.
         a.   When transmitting sensitive data via e-mail:
            (1)   The data must be securely encrypted via e-mail according to
encryption methods established by the IT division.
   D.   Security Breach Notification And Incident Reporting: Individuals shall
promptly report security incident information to appropriate authorities.
Information security events, breaches, and weaknesses associated with
information systems shall be communicated in a manner allowing timely
corrective action to be taken. Incident related information can be obtained
from the IT division. (Eff. 1-8-2016)
1430-7: COMPLIANCE:
Violation of these guidelines may subject you to disciplinary action by your
supervisor, or other appropriate authority, and/or legal action by the software
vendor and the Software Publishers Association. (Eff. 1-8-2016)
1430-8: ENFORCEMENT:
Periodic inventories of software on computers will be made by the information
technology division (IT) to check for authorized and registered software and
compliance with this policy. The IT division may adopt such procedures and
controls as are necessary to ensure conformance with, and enforcement of, this
policy. (Eff. 1-8-2016)
POLICY 1440
WEBSITE POLICY
SECTION:
1440-1: Purpose
1440-2: General Disclaimer
1440-3: External Web Links
1440-4: Links By Other Entities To Ogden City's Website
1440-5: Ogden Area Events Calendar
1440-6: ADA Access
1440-7: Legal Notice
1440-8: Copyright Policy
1440-1: PURPOSE:
The goal of Ogden City's website is to enhance the city's governmental purposes
by providing information about Ogden City and city services of general interest
to residents, businesses, and visitors. Ogden City's website is not a public
forum for the exercise of free speech. (Eff. 4-9-2009)
1440-2: GENERAL DISCLAIMER:
Information contained in Ogden City's website, including information contained
in external links, is provided without any warranties or representations of any
kind as to accuracy, reliability, timeliness, or content. Under no
circumstances shall Ogden City be liable for any acts or omissions based upon
reliance on any information contained in or linked to the website, nor shall
the city be liable for any consequences of such reliance. Links or references
to other information or organizations do not constitute an endorsement by the
city. (Eff. 4-9-2009)
1440-3: EXTERNAL WEB LINKS:
Consistent with the purpose of this website, Ogden City may in its sole
discretion provide external web links to the following: governmental entities
and educational institutions; generally recognized community organizations;
organizations providing information about art, cultural, sporting, and
recreational activities in the Ogden area; entities with which the city has an
existing contractual relationship; entities or events that receive funding from
the city or are otherwise sponsored by the city; entities that contribute to
city initiatives and that the city wishes to acknowledge; the Ogden-Weber
chamber of commerce; the Ogden convention and visitors bureau; and web pages
that provide free information on local conditions for Ogden City, such as
weather or snow conditions. Links may be removed or replaced at the sole
discretion of Ogden City at any time without notice. This policy may be revised
without prior notice. (Eff. 4-9-2009)
1440-4: LINKS BY OTHER ENTITIES TO OGDEN CITY'S WEBSITE:
It is not necessary to obtain advance permission to link to the Ogden City
website, however, Ogden City website content and URLs may change at any time
without notice. Entities and individuals linking to the Ogden City website
shall not capture any of the city's web pages within frames; present Ogden City
content as their own, or otherwise misrepresent Ogden City website content;
misinform users about the origin or ownership of Ogden City website content; or
make any statement or implication that Ogden City is endorsing, recommending,
or favoring, any product, viewpoint, or service. (Eff. 4-9-2009)
1440-5: OGDEN AREA EVENTS CALENDAR:
The Ogden City website provides a link to the Ogden area events calendar. The
city posts Ogden City government events. The city may post external events
consistent with the purpose of the city website and external website links
policy. Other community organizations also post events to this calendar. (Eff.
4-9-2009)
1440-6: ADA ACCESS:
Ogden City is committed to compliance with the Americans with disabilities act.
Upon request, Ogden City will make reasonable accommodations to provide
individuals who have disabilities access to information regarding city
services, programs, or activities set forth on the city's website. (Eff. 4-9-
2009)
1440-7: LEGAL NOTICE:
Communication provided to Ogden City through its website, through e-mail or any
other online messaging system does not constitute legal notice to Ogden City.
(Eff. 4-9-2009)
1440-8: COPYRIGHT POLICY:
All material on the Ogden City website is protected by international and U.S.
copyright law. Distribution, mirroring, modification, or reuse of text,
graphics, photographs or videos is not permitted without the express written
permission of Ogden City. Information contained in the Ogden City website may
be printed for personal use. (Eff. 4-9-2009)
POLICY 1450
COMPUTER AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS HARDWARE AND PHYSICAL SECURITY
SECTION:
1450-1: Purpose
1450-2: Responsibility
1450-3: Scope
1450-4: Need For Policy
1450-5: Glossary Of Terms
1450-6: Policies And Procedures
1450-7: Compliance
1450-8: Enforcement
1450-1: PURPOSE:
To establish a uniform policy for: a) the use and protection of computer
hardware used for city business including mobile and storage devices, privately
purchased devices, and office telephones; b) authorized access to data centers;
and c) new hire and termination computer procedures.
The overall objectives of the policies and procedures are to contain costs,
promote quality, ensure compatibility, maintain standards, protect
infrastructure, and to provide maximum support. (Eff. 5-6-2015)
1450-2: RESPONSIBILITY:
The information technology (IT) division has the authority and responsibility
to ensure, where possible, that computer hardware, telephones, and
infrastructure are cared for and protected and shall put in place such controls
as are necessary.
IT shall initially determine which personal and mobile computing devices may be
used to access city networks, the type of telephone hardware and service that
is provided to the city, and the level of physical security for city computer
infrastructure.
Purchasing has the responsibility to put in place such controls as are
necessary to meet the policies outlined for the purchasing of computer software
and hardware. (Eff. 5-6-2015)
1450-3: SCOPE:
This policy applies to all computer hardware and telephones and to all
employees of Ogden City. (Eff. 5-6-2015)
1450-4: NEED FOR POLICY:
With the widespread use of computing devices, the need for policies and
procedures has been apparent. Any misuse of city computer hardware, storage
devices, telephones, or breach of physical security policies may warrant
discipline. Purchase of computer hardware without authorization from IT can
result in poor quality control, unnecessary expense, incompatibility, and
security issues. (Eff. 5-6-2015)
1450-5: GLOSSARY OF TERMS:
HARDWARE: Desktops, laptops, iPad type devices, MTDs, PDAs, DVDs, CDs, magnetic
tapes; peripheral devices such as thumb drives, air cards, external hard
drives, cameras, cellphones, printers, copiers, scanners, external music
devices, external cables, speakers, and any other electronic computing or
storage device, whether city purchased or privately purchased.
MOBILE COMPUTING DEVICE: A portable computing or communications device with a
processor and operating system, such as a laptop computer, iPad type device, or
smartphone.
TELEPHONES: Desk or wall mounted telephones and telephone consoles. (Eff. 5-6-
2015)
1450-6: POLICIES AND PROCEDURES:
   A.   Personal computing and storage devices, including personal mobile
devices and smartphones, may be locally or remotely connected to city equipment
and networks, including data transfer, as approved by department directors, IT,
and the director of management services. Authorized data transfers from city
computers to and from home computers shall use city acquired storage devices.
   B.   City mobile computing devices shall generally be used by city personnel
for business purposes only. See also Ogden City personnel policy manual
provisions on electronic communications, and wireless devices acquisition and
usage policy found elsewhere in this manual. Mobile computing devices that
require access to city networks shall use a secure connection to the networks,
and shall use a screen save lock to prevent unauthorized access.
   C.   Lost or stolen computer and mobile computing equipment used in any way
for city business shall be immediately reported to IT and to the head of the
department to which it was assigned and city equipment shall be replaced by the
department to which it was assigned. Theft shall be reported to appropriate law
enforcement.
   D.   All city equipment/server rooms will remain locked at all times. Access
to city equipment/server rooms in any of its buildings is prohibited unless
authorized and accompanied by IT or fleet and facilities personnel who have
approved entrance authorization.
   E.   Vehicles containing mobile computer equipment or software used in any
way for city business or vehicles used for transporting city computer equipment
or software shall be locked when unattended and shall be parked in secure
areas. Such equipment and software in vehicles should not be exposed to direct
sunlight or other harmful elements.
   F.   All guests and vendors that require access to any Ogden computing
systems and/or communication/computer rooms shall be approved by IT and
escorted by Fleet or IT. They will be required to sign a data access form, wear
a guest badge when on site, and are required to comply with all Ogden City
policies. Upon completion/termination of their work or at the request of Ogden
City, the vendor's or guest's access will be disabled and the vendor or guest
shall surrender all property of Ogden City, including badges, access cards,
equipment, and supplies.
   G.   All new users of city equipment and software shall request equipment
and access by completing a new computer and/or phone account request form and
shall be required to use a user name and password based on city standards.
   H.   Upon termination, city employees shall return all city property to
their manager including any off site devices, laptops, iPad type devices,
cellphones, PDAs, ID cards, keys, smart cards, and air cards. Software costs
provided by the city but purchased using an employee's personal account (such
as mobile apps) may be required to be reimbursed by the employee to the city
when the employee leaves city employment, unless otherwise approved by the CAO.
Additionally, terminated employees shall provide proof of removal of city
provided software loaded on privately purchased hardware. The human resources
division is responsible to notify IT when an employee is terminated. That
notification shall include: name, termination date, department/division,
supervisor name, and any special transition handling. Upon an employee's
termination, IT shall immediately revoke all computer, network, data access,
security, and user accounts of the terminated employee. The terminated
employee's "H" drive and e-mails will be backed up and retained in accordance
with applicable retention schedules or as directed by the city attorney. Three
(3) months after an e-mail account and user name is disabled IT shall remove
them from the network.
   I.   Use of office telephones is intended for business purposes. Personal
use of office telephones shall be occasional, incidental, or for emergencies.
Ogden City has the right to monitor telephone billings and telephone usage. See
also Ogden City personnel policy manual provisions on electronic
communications.
   J.   The IT division shall be responsible for clearing hard drives as
appropriate pursuant to state and federal guidelines. (Eff. 5-6-2015)
1450-7: COMPLIANCE:
Violation of these guidelines may subject you to disciplinary action by your
supervisor, or other appropriate authority, and/or legal action by the software
vendor and the Software Publishers Association. (Eff. 5-6-2015)
1450-8: ENFORCEMENT:
Periodic inventories of computer hardware will be made by IT to check for
authorized hardware compliance with this policy. The IT division may adopt such
procedures and controls as are necessary to ensure conformance with, and
enforcement of, this policy. (Eff. 5-6-2015)

1460-5: COMPUTER EQUIPMENT SUPPORT PROCEDURES:
   A.   All city purchased computer equipment is eligible for city technical

or at helpdeskteam@ogdencity.com for support needs.
   B.   Technical support of privately purchased computer equipment used by
city employees for personal or city business is the responsibility of the
individual and not the city unless authorized by the director of management
services or CAO.
   C.   The IT division shall enter into vendor hardware maintenance agreements

frame.
      3.   Managing the customer's request in a tracking system.
      4.   Providing the needed support or notifying the customer of scheduled
support.
      5.   Providing postsupport follow up to assure equipment performance.
   E.   In the event the IT division cannot immediately repair a piece of
hardware, IT will schedule the repair and notify the customer of the estimated
completion date.
   F.   The IT division shall immediately provide customers with a "loaner", if
available, in the event a piece of desktop or laptop equipment is taken out of
service for repair. (Eff. 10-3-2013)

   C.   The IT division shall enter into vendor software maintenance agreements

frame.

      5.   Providing postsupport follow up to assure equipment performance.

1460-7: COMPUTER EQUIPMENT REPLACEMENT (TIERING) PROCEDURES:
   A.   All city purchased computer equipment is eligible for replacement as
scheduled by the IT division and approved by department directors.

      1.   Desktops.

from IT division budgets when funded during the budget process.
