      1.   Servers.
      2.   Switches and routers.
      3.   SAN (storage).
      4.   Communications cabling.
      5.   Other nondesktop computer equipment.
   H.   Funding for infrastructure computer replacement under this policy will
come from IT division budgets. (Eff. 10-3-2013)
POLICY 1470
CITY SPONSORED SOCIAL MEDIA
SECTION:
1470-1: Purpose
1470-2: Policy
1470-1: PURPOSE:
Ogden City recognizes that social media has changed the way people communicate
with each other, and that the use of social media can enhance communication
between city government and citizens, particularly citizens who do not access
traditional media. The city encourages the use of social media to further the
mission of the city and its departments where appropriate. This policy sets
forth guidelines for the establishment and use of social media by the city for
the dissemination of information to the public.
For purposes of this policy, "social media" means any facility for online
publication and commentary including, without limitation, blogs, wikis, content
hosting sites such as YouTube, and social networking sites such as Facebook,
Google+, Instagram, LinkedIn, Snapchat, and Twitter. (Eff. 3-13-2015)
1470-2: POLICY:
Ogden City departments may utilize social media and social network sites to
enhance communications with citizens and program participants subject to the
following rules and guidelines:
   A.   Ogden City administration social media sites shall be approved by the
chief administrative officer. City council social media sites shall be approved
by the council executive director. The director of each department shall
designate a public information officer (PIO) who is responsible for the content
and upkeep of each social media site maintained by that department.
   B.   Ogden City social media sites shall generally be used for: 1)
marketing/promotional channels which increase the city's ability to broadcast
its messages to the widest possible audience; 2) public information updates;
and 3) the dissemination of time sensitive information as quickly as possible
(example: emergency information).
   C.   Department PIOs shall coordinate with Ogden City IT to ensure that
department webpages and social media sites are accessible from the main Ogden
City website. The main city website, rather than department social media sites,
should be used for in depth information, forms, documents or online services
necessary to conduct business with Ogden City.
   D.   Employees representing the city via social media outlets must conduct
themselves at all times as a representative of the city and in accordance with
all appropriate Ogden City policies and standards, including, but not limited
to, the employee handbook. Employees found in violation of this policy may be
subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.
   E.   City social media sites shall be used only for communication of city
related information in accordance with the city's mission and shall not be used
for personal purposes.
   F.   City social media sites shall comply with federal, state and local
laws, regulations and administrative rules.
   G.   City social media sites are subject to Utah public records laws. The
department maintaining the site is responsible for responding completely and
accurately to any request for public records on social media sites, in
coordination with the city recorder's office. If the information requested is
available on the social media site, referral of the requester to the site will
generally constitute compliance with the request. Content related to city
business shall be maintained in an accessible format so that it can be produced
in response to a request. Wherever possible, such sites shall clearly indicate
that any articles and any other content posted or submitted for posting are
subject to public records laws. Users shall be notified that requests for
public records should be directed to the appropriate departmental records
representative or the city recorder's office.
   H.   Utah law and relevant Ogden City records retention schedules apply to
social media formats and social media content. Unless otherwise addressed in a
specific social media standards document, the department maintaining a site
shall preserve records required to be maintained pursuant to a relevant records
retention schedule for the required retention period. Appropriate retention
formats for specific social media tools shall be determined by the city
recorder's office.
   I.   Users and visitors to social media sites shall be notified that the
intended purpose of the site is to serve as a mechanism for communication
between city departments and members of the public. Ogden City social media
sites are moderated forums. Ogden City social media site articles and comments
containing any of the following forms of content shall not be allowed:
      1.   Comments in support of or opposition to political campaigns or
ballot measures;
      2.   Profane language or content;
      3.   Personal attacks;
      4.   Content that promotes, fosters, or perpetuates discrimination on the
basis of race, creed, color, age, religion, gender, marital status, status with
regard to public assistance, national origin, physical or mental disability or
sexual orientation;
      5.   Sexual content or links to sexual content;
      6.   Solicitations of commerce;
      7.   Conduct or encouragement of illegal activity;
      8.   Information that may tend to compromise the safety or security of
the public or public systems;
      9.   Content that violates a legal ownership interest of any other party;
or
      10.   Comments not topically related to the particular social medium
article being commented upon, including random or unintelligible comments.
   J.   The guidelines described above should be displayed to users or made
available by hyperlink. A copy of any content removed based on these guidelines
must be retained, including the time, date and identity of the poster when
available.
   K.   The city reserves the right to restrict or remove any content that is
deemed to be in violation of this social media policy or any applicable law.
   L.   The social media tools that are currently approved for use by Ogden
City are Twitter, Facebook, Instagram and city sponsored blogs. If any city
department desires to use any other social media tool, such use must be
approved by the chief administrative officer or council executive director as
appropriate.
   M.   All content created or posted on a city social media site as well as
all city profile and home pages shall belong to the city.
   N.   Department directors may adopt departmental policies pertaining to
social media that are not in conflict with the provisions of this policy. (Eff.
3-13-2015)
POLICY 1480
TECHNOLOGY GOVERNANCE
SECTION:
1480-1: Purpose
1480-2: Responsibility
1480-3: Policies And Procedures
1480-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to describe key elements of city technology
governance and specify who is responsible for their creation, maintenance, and
enforcement. (Eff. 4-29-2015)
1480-2: RESPONSIBILITY:
The IT steering committee is responsible for overseeing all city technology
governance, management, initiatives, and budgets.
The IT division is responsible, under the direction of the IT steering
committee, for recommending, coordinating, managing, and enforcing all city
technology governance, including project schedules and implementation,
standards, policies, and budgets. (Eff. 4-29-2015)
1480-3: POLICIES AND PROCEDURES:
   A.   The Ogden City technology mission is to provide a unified and vibrant
technical infrastructure, secure data and networks, robust information sharing
and analysis tools, and software applications that are reliable, long term, and
financially viable and secure to support city goals and strategic directions
by:
      1.   Establishing a reliable and scalable technology infrastructure.
      2.   Prudently integrating "Cloud" hardware and software solutions.
      3.   Evaluating software solutions on a buy then build basis.
      4.   Providing a user friendly dashboard and reporting infrastructure.
      5.   Implementing user selection and managed solutions.
      6.   Promoting mobile computing and geographical solutions.
      7.   Researching leading edge technologies.
      8.   Prioritizing projects.
   B.   The chief administrative officer shall establish and maintain an IT
steering committee, and the IT steering committee may establish and maintain
other technology user committees as needed, to provide direction,
recommendation, ideation, and liaison support to the information technology
division. User committees shall work under the direction of the IT steering
committee.
   C.   The IT division, under the direction of the IT steering committee,
shall establish, maintain and enforce a technology operating methodology that
describes the roles, responsibilities, and decision rights of IT and
departments.
   D.   The IT division, under the direction of the IT steering committee,
shall establish, maintain and enforce technology standards and operating
protocols for all computer equipment, software, and technology project
development.
   E.   The information technology division shall maintain a current list of
technology services offered to departments.
   F.   The IT division, under the direction of the IT steering committee,
shall establish, maintain, and enforce technology policies for areas including,
but not limited to, project development, computer equipment and software
acquisition, cellphones, software and electronic data, website and social
media, computer equipment and facility security, computer equipment and
software replacement and support, and technology governance.
   G.   The IT division, under the direction of the IT steering committee,
shall establish, maintain, and enforce a technology governance model that
partners the information technology division with department users to create
and implement technology solutions, policies, standards and budgets. (Eff. 4-
29-2015)
POLICY 1490
POLICE DEPARTMENT SOCIAL MEDIA
SECTION:
1490-1: Purpose
1490-2: Policy
1490-3: Definitions
1490-4: Legal Considerations
1490-5: Procedures
1490-1: PURPOSE:
To establish department-wide standards for administering and moderating of
official Ogden Police Department social media platforms, ensuring compliance
with the First Amendment and other relevant laws, public trust, and operational
integrity. (Eff. 9-17-2025)
1490-2: POLICY:
The Ogden Police Department uses social media to disseminate information,
promote public safety, and engage with the community. Department social media
accounts are designated as limited public forums, where public comments are
permitted in accordance with clearly defined, viewpoint-neutral content
moderation standards. Users should know that social media posts made by the
police department, comments to those posts, and any direct or private messages
may be public records subject to applicable public records release.
All moderation of comments or user interactions shall be conducted
consistently, constitutionally, and with proper documentation.
Please Note: Police department social media accounts are not constantly
monitored and should not be used to seek emergency services. Those in need of
emergency help should call 9-1-1. (Eff. 9-17-2025)
1490-3: DEFINITIONS:
 
COMMENTS:             Content posted to the Ogden Police Department social
                      media by users.
LIMITED PUBLIC FORUM: A platform opened for public discussion on designated
                      topics, subject to reasonable, viewpoint-neutral rules.
                      Content (text, images, audio, links, or video) created or
                      shared by Ogden police department and communicated on
SOCIAL MEDIA:         Department online accounts through platforms that allow
                      sharing, commenting, and other engagement. Examples of
                      social media accounts include Facebook, X, Instagram,
                      YouTube, and LinkedIn.
UNPROTECTED SPEECH:   Speech categories not protected under the First
                      Amendment.
USER:                 A member of the public engaging with official Ogden City
                      Police Department social media.
VIEWPOINT-NEUTRA L:   Rules enforced without regard to the commenter's opinion.
                      (Eff. 9-17-2025)
 
1490-4: LEGAL CONSIDERATIONS:
The Ogden City Police Department's social media pages are considered limited
public forums governed by the First Amendment, meaning the Department may
impose reasonable, viewpoint-neutral restrictions on public comments to
preserve public safety, civility, and relevance. The Department will not hide
or delete comments solely because such comments are critical of our
organization, its officials, or its employees.
Courts have ruled that while speech may not be removed solely because it
criticizes the Department, city officials, or public employees, the Department
may moderate or remove comments that pose legitimate concerns. Comments may be
removed if they include:
   Repetitive comments posted within a short period of time,
   Commercial advertising or solicitations,
   Criminal threats of violence or harm,
   Incitement unlawful actions,
   Obscenity, which is defined as sexually explicit and/or pornographic content
that is patently offensive, appeals to prurient interest, and lacks serious
literary, artistic, political, or scientific value,
   Actual defamation against a person, and
   Comments containing links to malware and/or malicious content that affects
the normal functioning of a computer system, server, app, or browser.
Comments may be moderated using clear, consistently applied rules aligned with
the forum's purpose regardless of viewpoint.
Repeated violations (on three or more occasions within a 12-month period) may
result in the user being blocked to maintain forum integrity. All moderation
actions will be documented with the reason for the removal, and the affected
individual will be notified of the action and rationale whenever practicable.
Individuals retain a right to due process and may appeal moderation decisions.
Official Department posts are government speech, may be modified or removed,
and are not subject to public comment rights. (Eff. 9-17-2025)
1490-5: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Monitoring And Moderation:
      1.   Department social media pages shall be monitored by designated
personnel trained in First Amendment compliance and this policy.
      2.   Moderators are authorized to hide or delete user comments that
violate the content restrictions identified in subsection D.
      3.   All moderation decisions must be made without regard to viewpoint,
political affiliation, or the identity of the speaker. Criticism alone is not
cause for removal.
      4.   Moderators shall ensure that enforcement of this policy is
consistent, documented, and neutral in application.
      5.   Whenever a comment is hidden/removed or a user is blocked, the
supervisor of the moderator must be informed and approve of the action.
      6.   In circumstances where the interpretation or appropriateness of a
social media post, comment, or engagement is unclear, the moderator must seek
guidance prior to taking action. All such cases should be referred to the Chief
of Police and/or Ogden City Legal Counsel for review and direction.
   B.   Documentation And Recordkeeping:
      1.   Whenever possible, every moderation action taken under this policy
shall be recorded. At minimum, documentation shall include:
         a.   The full text or image of the moderated comment;
         b.   The date and time of the action;
         c.   The platform on which the action occurred;
         d.   The rule or policy provision violated; and
         e.   The identity of the staff member who performed the action.
      2.   These records shall be retained according to the Utah Government
Records Access and Management Act (GRAMA) and applicable city retention
schedules.
   C.   User Notification And Appeals:
      1.   Whenever practicable, the affected user shall be notified that their
comment was removed or hidden and given a brief explanation of the reason.
      2.   Users may appeal moderation decisions by sending a written request
to example@ogdencity.com within five (5) business days of the action.
      3.   Appeals will be reviewed by the Chief of Police and Ogden City legal
counsel. The reviewer will determine whether the original moderation action was
lawful under the First Amendment, other relevant laws, and this policy.
      4.   If an appeal is upheld, the Department will make reasonable efforts
to restore the comment or permit the user to repost. If the appeal is denied,
the user will be provided with a brief written explanation of the decision.
   D.   User Restrictions And Blocking:
      1.   A user who violates this policy on multiple occasions (three) within
a rolling twelve (12) month period, or whose conduct is deemed so egregious
that action is warranted, may be temporarily or permanently restricted from
accessing the Department's social media accounts.
      2.   Prior to blocking or banning a user, the Department shall verify and
document each violation and ensure that lesser alternatives (e.g., warnings,
temporary restrictions) have been considered or attempted where appropriate. If
a user is blocked or banned, reasonable attempts must be made to notify the
user and describe the violation.
      3.   A user who has been blocked or banned may appeal that decision using
the process described in subsection C.
      4.   If the appeal is upheld and the user has fewer than three valid
violations on record within the past twelve months, access shall be reinstated.
   E.   Terms And Conditions For Users:
      1.   A Social Media Terms and Conditions notice shall be published and
maintained on all Department social media accounts, either through a visible
hyperlink, "About" section text, or pinned post.
      2.   The Terms and Conditions shall:
         a.   Identify the platform as a limited public forum;
         b.   State that comments are moderated in accordance with the First
Amendment and other relevant laws;
         c.   List examples of prohibited content categories;
         d.   Inform users of the appeals process;
         e.   State that comments may be subject to public records law; and
         f.   Remind users not to use social media to request emergency
assistance.
      3.   Any user-generated content submitted to Department social media
accounts may be treated as a public record, subject to disclosure under
applicable law.
   F.   Training And Review:
      1.   All personnel authorized to manage or moderate Department social
media accounts shall receive annual training on this policy, the First
Amendment, and applicable platform-specific tools and limitations.
      2.   This policy shall be reviewed every two years or as necessary to
reflect changes in constitutional law, case precedent, or Department practices.
(Eff. 9-17-2025)
TITLE 6
VEHICLES, PROPERTY AND EQUIPMENT
POLICY 1500
OGDEN CITY VEHICLE AND EQUIPMENT MAINTENANCE OPERATIONS
SECTION:
1500-1: Purpose
1500-2: Policy
1500-3: Responsibility
1500-4: Procedures
1500-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish procedures for upkeep and
maintenance of all city owned vehicles. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1500-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City to reduce costs and improve safety in the
operations and maintenance of city vehicles. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1500-3: RESPONSIBILITY:
These policies and procedures are to be the responsibility of each operator/
driver. Training for operators/drivers should be provided on a regular basis by
supervisors and division managers. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1500-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Equipment Operations:
      1.   Daily:
         a.   Check oil level (engine and transmission).
         b.   Check coolant level.
         c.   Check lights.
      2.   Weekly:
         a.   Tires and wheels: Check pressure and do a visual check for wear,
splits, bulges, etc.
         b.   Battery: Check the water level and the terminals for corrosion.
         c.   Power steering: Oil level.
         d.   Brake and clutch: Fluid levels.
         e.   Belts: Check for fraying and tension.
         f.   Air brakes: Drain tanks.
         g.   Hydraulics: Oil levels.
         h.   Interior and exterior: Should be cleaned weekly.
         i.   Check preventative maintenance (PM) sticker (front window top
left corner).
   B.   Care Of Equipment:
      1.   Do not leave a vehicle unattended with the engine running.
      2.   Do not leave a vehicle idling for more than three (3) minutes for
gas engines and ten (10) minutes for diesel engines.
      3.   Do not leave material/equipment loose in vehicles. This can cause
serious injury.
      4.   Do not leave an unattended city vehicle unlocked.
   C.   Detection Of Malfunctions Or Defects:
      1.   The care of Ogden City's vehicles and equipment is the
responsibility of each operator/driver.
      2.   It is unwise for you to operate a vehicle/equipment with a known
defect or malfunction. If there is a problem with the vehicle/equipment, please
report it as soon as possible to the fleet division.
   D.   Procedures For Initiating Repairs:
      1.   If a vehicle accident has occurred follow the reporting accidents
and damage to Ogden City vehicle policy 1510.
      2.   Call or drive vehicle to fleet division.
      3.   Complete fleet work order request form (fleet form: policy 1510).
(Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1510
REPORTING ACCIDENTS AND DAMAGE TO CITY VEHICLES AND/OR PROPERTY
SECTION:
1510-1: Purpose
1510-2: Policy
1510-3: Responsibility
1510-4: Procedures
1510-1: PURPOSE:
The purposes of this policy are to:
   A.   Establish guidelines for reporting, investigating, repairing and
properly accounting for accidents and damages involving city owned, leased or
operated vehicles.
   B.   Establish guidelines for reporting, investigating, repairing and
properly accounting for accidents and damage involving Ogden City property or
those other than vehicles. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1510-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City to:
   A.   Report all motor vehicle and/or property accidents, regardless of the
severity, immediately upon their occurrence. All vehicle accidents must be
reported to the Ogden City police department. Any damage or accident involving
hazardous conditions (i.e., downed traffic signs, damaged fire hydrants, etc.)
should be reported to the appropriate department or to the dispatch center for
proper notification.
   B.   Follow Ogden City's employee injury policy if a city employee is
injured as a result of an accident, or has the possibility of injuries
resulting from an accident.
   C.   Complete, sign and forward all damage report forms to the appropriate
division within twenty four (24) hours.
   D.   Follow all necessary repair procedures.
   E.   Follow the guidelines for reimbursement from the responsible third
party for damages of city property. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1510-3: RESPONSIBILITY:
It is the responsibility of all employees, supervisors, division managers,
department directors, the fleet division and the risk management division to
follow the procedures developed in this policy for accidents and/or damage
involving an Ogden City vehicle and/or property. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1510-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Notify Police Department: Employees must call the police department
immediately and remain at the scene of the accident. If a police vehicle is
involved another law enforcement agency shall be called to investigate.
City employees involved in motor vehicle accidents are to discuss the accident
only with the investigating police department or city officials. The driver may
give his name, driver's license and employer's name to the driver(s) of the
other vehicle(s) involved.
   B.   Notify Supervisor: Employees must notify their immediate supervisor of
damage incurred to any Ogden City vehicle and/or property as soon as possible.
All city employees involved in an accident may be required to take a drug and
alcohol test as provided for in the drug and alcohol/fitness for duty policy
and guidelines. The immediate supervisor of the employee involved in the
accident or a supervisor designated by the department will conduct an
independent investigation and shall complete and forward the "supervisor's
investigation report" form to the risk management division within two (2)
working days of an accident.
   C.   Risk Management/Legal Department: If the accident is of a severe nature
(involving bodily injury or extensive property damage), the affected department
shall immediately advise the city's risk management division or legal
department. (See policy 1600, "Employee Work Related Injury Requiring Medical
Treatment", of this manual.)
   D.   Property Damage Report Form: The employee and employee's supervisor
must complete an Ogden City vehicle or property damage report form (risk
management form: policy 1510) applicable to the accident. This must be
completed, signed and forwarded. In the event a report will be delayed, the
appropriate division(s) must be notified by telephone.
   E.   Vehicle Repairs:
      1.   Damaged Ogden City vehicles must be taken to the fleet division by
the employee or employee's supervisor within two (2) working days, where a
fleet work order form (fleet division form: policy 1510) must be completed.
This is necessary to begin vehicle repairs.
      2.   If the vehicle is unable to be driven contact the fleet division for
towing arrangements.
      3.   Arrangements for a substitute or replacement vehicle should be made
with the employee's department. If approved by the supervisor, substitutes or
replacements can be arranged through fleet or motor pool.
      4.   The Ogden City fleet division will be solely responsible for all
estimates and repairs to Ogden City vehicles.
   F.   Property Repairs:
      1.   The affected division is responsible for all property damage repairs
and shall also be responsible to work with risk management to obtain
reimbursement for damages to property caused by a third party. These
reimbursements are intended to be deposited in the department's account and
used to make repairs.
      2.   The department responsible for repairing the damage shall also be
responsible to gather all other relevant information (i.e., police reports,
statements, costs of repair) required to assign reimbursement costs and return
the vehicle to city service.
      3.   After all information is gathered and estimates or repairs have been
made, the affected division forwards all documentation to the risk management
division to coordinate billing procedures with the treasury division. (Eff. 3-
14-2007)
POLICY 1520
DRIVER'S LICENSE CHECK
SECTION:
1520-1: Purpose
1520-2: Definition
1520-3: Policy
1520-4: Procedures
1520-1: PURPOSE:
The purposes of this policy are to:
   A.   Upon hire, annually, and as needed check the driver's license status of
Ogden City employees who may be required to operate a city owned vehicle or
personal vehicle on city business.
   B.   Ensure all city drivers are legally allowed under state law to operate
a motor vehicle and are conscious of safe driving practices. (Eff. 4-22-2016)
1520-2: DEFINITION:
SERIOUS TRAFFIC VIOLATION: Excessive speeding (15 mph or more above the posted
limit), reckless driving, improper or erratic lane changes, following a vehicle
too closely, traffic offenses committed in connection with fatal traffic
accidents, driving without obtaining a valid driver's license. (Eff. 4-22-2016)
1520-3: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation:
   A.   To reduce motor vehicle accidents by maintaining a periodic check of
drivers' license status of all Ogden City employees who may be required to
operate a vehicle on city business.
   B.   To establish minimum criteria for an unacceptable driving record so
that employees have a clear understanding of the expectation that employees
drive in a safe and responsible manner both on and off the job and maintain a
good driving record.
   C.   To make employees who drive for Ogden City aware of their
responsibility to report any changes in the status of their driver's license.
   D.   To verify the validity of all city employees who drive any motorized
vehicle on city business. (Eff. 4-22-2016)
1520-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Driver's license information is public information and the employer has
a right and responsibility to periodically check the status of its drivers.
   B.   Upon hiring, annually, and as needed, or when requested by a
supervisor, employees are required to sign a motor vehicle record check
authorization form.
   C.   Criteria that may indicate an unacceptable driving record include, but
are not limited to:
      1.   Two (2) or more serious traffic violations in the past twenty four
(24) months;
      2.   Two (2) or more at fault accidents in the past thirty six (36)
months. Contributing factors such as weather or mechanical problems may be
taken into consideration;
      3.   One or more DUIs/DWIs in the past thirty six (36) months;
      4.   Leaving the scene of an accident in the past thirty six (36) months;
      5.   Any combination of accidents and/or moving violations.
   D.   Employees who drive for Ogden City (city owned vehicles or personal
vehicles) have a responsibility to notify their supervisor immediately if their
license has been revoked, suspended or modified in any way, and shall not drive
for Ogden City until verification of driving privileges have been established.
Employees who drive for Ogden City (city owned vehicles or personal vehicles)
have a responsibility to notify their supervisor immediately each time they are
convicted of a moving violation.
   E.   Supervisors should be careful not to request an employee without
driver's license or with an invalid driver's license to drive on any Ogden City
business (errands, etc.).
   F.   No action should be taken regarding driver's license status if an
employee is not required to drive for Ogden City as a part of their job
description.
   G.   Supervisors may request to see an employee's driver's license at any
time. However, requesting a motor vehicle record (MVR) from the motor vehicle
division is the most accurate method to assess the driving status of an
employee. Currently, MVRs may be obtained at no charge in the risk management
division. An employee or supervisor may request and obtain a copy from the
motor vehicle division for a nominal fee.
   H.   Because the motor vehicle division has time gaps in updating
information onto the state computer, Ogden City will take the position that if
an employee's driver's license or violation status is questionable the employee
will not be allowed to drive on city business until the employee clears the
matter and brings in a current motor vehicle record (MVR) indicating current
status to both his/her supervisor and the risk management division.
   I.   Employees who fail to notify their immediate supervisor of change in
the status of their driver's license or drive without a valid driver's license
on city business shall be subject to disciplinary action, including possible
termination. Any employee without a valid driver's license will not be allowed
to operate a city vehicle or drive on Ogden City business. If driving is a
necessary job function and the employee cannot reasonably be accommodated, the
employee may be terminated. Supervisors along with department directors and
division managers are responsible for implementing disciplinary action.
   J.   When an employee driving record is found to be unacceptable, the
driving record will be referred to the risk management committee for review.
Each situation will be evaluated and the risk management committee will
recommend appropriate disciplinary action to the department for implementation.
(Eff. 4-22-2016)
POLICY 1530
EMPLOYEES ASSIGNED AN OGDEN CITY VEHICLE
SECTION:
1530-1: Purpose
1530-2: Policy
1530-3: Responsibility
1530-4: Procedures
1530-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish procedures and requirements for
Ogden City vehicles assigned to employees for on duty and off duty use. (Eff.
8-21-2012)
1530-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to designate assigned city vehicles
to the appropriate personnel and to establish responsibilities and standards
for vehicle usage. (Eff. 8-21-2012)
1530-3: RESPONSIBILITY:
   A.   All employees assigned a city vehicle are responsible for following the
procedures outlined in this policy.
   B.   The employee's department director or division manager shall be
responsible for the enforcement of this policy. (Eff. 8-21-2012)
1530-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Approval For Use: All assigned city vehicles for off duty use must have
approval by the department director and chief administrative officer.
      1.   Assigned city vehicles shall be designated to those in positions
where there is:
         a.   A job related need;
         b.   A purpose for the assignment of a vehicle that benefits the
operation of the city and/or the department; thus meeting a legitimate business
need; and
         c.   A finding that the assignment of the vehicle is the most cost
effective option for meeting the legitimate business need.
      2.   Only employees required to immediately respond to callbacks and
emergency situations will be assigned a city vehicle.
   B.   Limitation: Employees may only operate assigned city vehicles on city
business, between home and work (when authorized) and for minor infrequent
personal use during working hours as permitted.
   C.   Cost For Personal Use:
      1.   Employees receiving compensation (on call pay) and those assigned
police vehicles will not be charged "commuting value", as outlined in IRS
regulations.
      2.   The cost for personal use at three dollars ($3.00) per day will be
deducted from the employees' gross income when such deduction is required for
the purpose of meeting IRS requirements regulations (for those not compensated,
as indicated in subsection C1 of this section).
      3.   Employees using police vehicles will be charged in accordance with
the police vehicle policy.
   D.   City Employees In City Vehicles: Only assigned Ogden City employees may
operate or be allowed in city vehicles, except for circumstances within the
course of employment and directly related to job responsibilities.
   E.   Regular Duty Clothing: Clothing of the type typically worn while on
regular duty is required while driving an Ogden City vehicle.
   F.   Radio Contact: Radio contact with dispatch shall be maintained while
operating assigned vehicle.
   G.   Maintenance And Repairs: The assigned employee is responsible for all
routine maintenance, scheduling regular maintenance and scheduling any
necessary repairs with the city fleet division as established in policy 1500,
"Ogden City Vehicle And Equipment Maintenance Operations", of this manual.
   H.   Misconduct Or Misuse: Employee misconduct or misuse of an assigned
vehicle will be considered conditions for disciplinary action.
   I.   IRS Guidelines And Requirements: To comply with IRS guidelines and
requirements, the three dollars ($3.00) per day added to the employee's gross
income will have appropriate federal and state taxes withheld. Forms will be
provided to report daily use. The three dollars ($3.00) per day is for one-way
or round trip.
   J.   Vehicle Allowance: An employee assigned a city vehicle may not receive
a vehicle allowance under policy 1300 of this manual.
   K.   Monitoring: Employees should be aware that all city vehicles are always
the property of the city and not private property of any city employee. The
city reserves the right to monitor, trace, review, track, audit, access, and
recover vehicle use or patterns at any time without notice, and therefore
employees should have no reasonable expectation of privacy in the use of city
vehicles. (Eff. 8-21-2012)

POLICY 1575
ENGINE IDLING AND PARKING BRAKE POLICY
SECTION:
1575-1: Purpose
1575-2: Definitions
1575-3: Applicability
1575-4: Idling Limitation
1575-5: Exemptions
1575-1: PURPOSE:
Ogden City is adopting an engine idling and parking brake policy in an effort
to reduce emissions and to protect city and private property from damage due to
the unintended movement of unoccupied vehicles.
Exhaust from vehicles is a substantial source of carbon monoxide, toxic air
contaminants and greenhouse gases. The city recognizes that air pollution is a
major health risk created in large part by emissions from automobiles and
trucks. Air pollution can cause or aggravate lung illnesses such as acute
respiratory infections, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, and lung cancer.
Diesel emissions have been identified as a pollutant that disproportionately
affects low income urban neighborhoods. Evidence suggests that diesel exhaust,
particularly particulates, contributes to this urban health problem.
An additional benefit from this policy will be lower fuel consumption and less
wear and tear on vehicles. Studies have shown that turning off and starting an
engine uses less fuel than letting the engine run for thirty (30) seconds and
that engine wear is greater at prolonged idle than during normal operation.
City employees can play an important role in improving air quality, reducing
the consumption of petroleum products, and improving safety by limiting the
amount of time city vehicle engines are allowed to idle and utilizing parking
brakes in an appropriate manner. (Eff. 8-31-2011)
1575-2: DEFINITIONS:
DRIVER: Any person who drives, operates, or is in actual physical control of a
vehicle.
EMERGENCY VEHICLE: Any fire apparatus, ambulance, police vehicle or any vehicle
performing similar functions.
EQUIPMENT: All equipment and all nonroad vehicles.
EQUIPMENT OPERATOR: Any person who is in actual physical control of equipment.
IDLING: The engine is running while the vehicle is stationary or the equipment
is not performing work.
NONROAD VEHICLE: Any self-propelled vehicle not required to be registered or
have a license plate by the department of motor vehicles.
OFFICIAL TRAFFIC CONTROL DEVICE: Any sign, signal, marking or device placed or
erected by authority of a public body or official having jurisdiction, for the
purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic, but does not include
islands, curbs, traffic barriers, speed humps, or other roadway design
features.
VEHICLE: Any self-propelled vehicle that is required to be registered and have
a license plate by the department of motor vehicles. (Eff. 8-31-2011)
1575-3: APPLICABILITY:
There is hereby established a policy to be known as the ENGINE IDLING AND
PARKING BRAKE POLICY that applies to the operation of all vehicles and
equipment owned or leased by Ogden City, except as provided in section
1575-5 of this policy. (Eff. 8-31-2011)
1575-4: IDLING LIMITATION:
   A.   A driver:
      1.   Must turn off the engine and set the parking brake upon stopping at
a destination; and
      2.   Must not cause or allow an engine to idle at any location for:
         a.   More than thirty (30) consecutive seconds; or
         b.   A period or periods aggregating more than five (5) minutes in any
one hour period.
   B.   An equipment operator:
      1.   Must, if the equipment is equipped with a parking brake, set the
parking brake when the equipment is not in motion; and
      2.   Must not cause or allow an engine to idle at any location for:
         a.   More than thirty (30) consecutive seconds; or
         b.   A period or periods aggregating more than five (5) minutes in any
one hour period.
   C.   Supervisors shall ensure that drivers and equipment operators, upon
employment and at least once per year thereafter, are informed of the
requirements of this policy. (Eff. 8-31-2011)
1575-5: EXEMPTIONS:
This policy does not apply to drivers or equipment operators for the period or
periods during which:
   A.   An emergency vehicle is allowed to idle during an emergency.
   B.   Idling is necessary or the parking brake is not set while stopped:
      1.   For an official traffic control device;
      2.   For traffic conditions over which a driver or operator has no
control, including, but not limited to: stopped in a line of traffic, stopped
at a railroad crossing or stopped at a construction zone; or
      3.   At the direction of a peace officer or other official traffic
controller.
   C.   Idling is necessary for testing, maintenance, repair or diagnostic
purposes.
   D.   Idling is necessary to ascertain that the vehicle and/or equipment is
in safe operating condition and is equipped as required by all provisions of
law and established safety policies.
   E.   The vehicle or equipment is not expected to restart due to mechanical
or electrical problems.
   F.   Idling the engine is required to power auxiliary devices other than a
heater or air conditioner (for example, computer, communication device, hoist,
lift, safety lighting) when necessary to conduct city business.
   G.   Idling is necessary to operate defrosters, heaters, air conditioners or
other devices to prevent a safety or health emergency, but not solely for the
comfort of the driver or passengers. (Eff. 8-31-2011)
POLICY 1577
VEHICLE BACKING POLICY
SECTION:
1577-1: Purpose
1577-2: Definitions
1577-3: City Trucks And Heavy Equipment
1577-4: Parking City Vehicles
1577-5: Backing Trailers
1577-6: Department Policies
1577-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish safe practices to ensure city
vehicles are safely moved when operating in reverse mode. (Eff. 4-22-2016)
1577-2: DEFINITIONS:
CITY TRUCK: Any city owned pickup truck, utility truck or one ton truck.
HEAVY DUTY CITY TRUCK/EQUIPMENT: Any city owned dump truck over one ton,
flatbed truck, truck mounted equipment, or heavy equipment.
PARKED VEHICLE: An unoccupied vehicle shall be considered parked regardless of
the time the operator is out of the vehicle, unless the operator is engaged in
stop and go work practices such as reading water meters, delivering door
hangers, etc., involving multiple stops within a very short time period.
SPOTTER: A spotter is responsible for guiding the driver and ensuring that any
potential hazards are avoided. (Eff. 4-22-2016)
1577-3: CITY TRUCKS AND HEAVY EQUIPMENT:
   A.   Supervisors shall ensure each city truck is equipped with a safety cone
to comply with this standard.
   B.   Drivers shall place a safety cone behind any city truck considered
parked, unless they are parked in a parking lot and are able to leave the
parking space without backing.
   C.   Whenever a city truck is parked along a roadway, the safety cone shall
be placed at the rear and on the street side of the vehicle.
   D.   When backing a parked city truck is necessary, drivers shall walk
completely around their vehicle before getting in, pick up the cone, and then
use mirrors and/or look over their shoulder while backing.
   E.   When backing a heavy duty city truck, another employee should "spot"
the driver whenever possible. Every effort should be taken to locate and
utilize a "spotter". When a spotter is not available, drivers shall walk
completely around their vehicle before getting in, pick up the cone, and
carefully watch the area they are backing into.
   F.   Operation of all vehicles shall be in accordance with applicable laws
and regulations.
   G.   Failure to follow this policy will be treated as a violation of city
policy and may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination.
(Eff. 4-22-2016)
1577-4: PARKING CITY VEHICLES:
City vehicles should be backed into a parking space or positioned forward in a
pull through parking space. However, city vehicles should not back into an
angled parking stall. (Eff. 4-22-2016)
1577-5: BACKING TRAILERS:
Employees should avoid situations requiring the backing of a vehicle with a
trailer. When backing a vehicle with a trailer is necessary, the driver should
locate and utilize another employee as a "spotter". (Eff. 4-22-2016)
1577-6: DEPARTMENT POLICIES:
Department directors may adopt departmental policies pertaining to vehicle
backing that are not in conflict with the provisions of this policy. (Eff. 4-
22-2016)

POLICY 1590
POLICE VEHICLE DONATIONS AND ACKNOWLEDGMENTS
SECTION:
1590-1: Purpose
1590-2: Policy
1590-3: Procedures
1590-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to set forth administrative policies and
procedures for Ogden City's acceptance of police vehicle donations and the
city's acknowledgment of donor contributions. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1590-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to accept donations of police
vehicles by qualified donors and acknowledge such donations with language
placed on donated vehicles stating the donor's name and/or logo for the
duration of the donation period, subject to the procedures, terms, conditions,
limitations and criteria provided herein. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1590-3: PROCEDURES:
   A.   The city may accept donations of police vehicles from qualified donors
subject to the following procedures, conditions and limitations:
      1.   The donor must be a qualified donor as defined herein.
      2.   The donation of a vehicle may occur in any of the following forms:
         a.   Donor payment of vehicle lease payments for one or more years for
a police vehicle leased by the city.
         b.   Donor payment of vehicle installment purchase payments for one or
more years for a police vehicle purchased by the city.
         c.   Donor purchase and conveyance of a police vehicle to the city,
free of liens or encumbrances.
      3.   Any donation of lease or purchase payments is subject to the city's
approval and acceptance of all lease or purchase agreement terms, at the sole
discretion and business judgment of the city. Likewise, donation of vehicles
conveyed by donors to the city is subject to the city's approval and
acceptance.
   B.   Any qualified donor of a police vehicle may be honored by the city by
written acknowledgment of the qualified donor's name and/or proprietary logo on
the donated vehicle, according to the provisions set forth below:
      1.   The acknowledgment language shall state as follows:
Ogden City thanks [insert name and/or logo] for the donation of this vehicle.
      2.   The acknowledgment shall be limited to the qualified donor's name
and logo, and shall not include advertising slogans or catch phrases or other
language promoting any specific product, service or viewpoint of the qualified
donor.
      3.   The qualified donor's name placed in the acknowledgment shall be the
registered entity name of the donor or the donor's registered trade name or
DBA. Any logo placed in the acknowledgment shall be the proprietary logo or
trademark of the donor. A logo shall consist of a symbol or symbols, including
letters, but shall not include complete words or phrases except words
designating the donor's name, trade name or DBA. The logo shall not include
advertising slogans or catch phrases.
      4.   If a logo is used in the acknowledgment, the logo shall be no larger
than one hundred twenty (120) square inches. The area of the logo, measured in
square inches, shall be equal or less than the area of the accompanying
acknowledgment text.
      5.   The acknowledgment shall be adhered to both sides of the donated
police vehicle on the rear side panel of each side of the police vehicle.
      6.   The dimensions, font, text size and style of acknowledgments shall
be standardized and similar to all other acknowledgments placed upon donated
police vehicles.
      7.   The acknowledgment shall remain on the donated vehicle for the full
donation period, which shall be the time period in which the qualified donor
makes scheduled lease or purchase payments for the vehicle. For vehicles
purchased outright and conveyed to the city, the donation period shall endure
as long as the vehicle is owned by the city. Ogden City may remove the
acknowledgment after the donation period has expired.
   C.   Qualified donors shall be those donors not excepted below who convey a
vehicle to the Ogden City police department or cover the lease or purchasing
installment payments for such vehicle for a one year donation period. Except,
the following persons and organizations shall not be considered qualified
donors:
      1.   Those businesses a majority of whose business consists of the
manufacture, distribution, or marketing of alcohol, tobacco, explosives, or
related products.
      2.   Sexually oriented businesses as defined in Ogden City ordinances,
which have been recognized in law as generally producing harmful secondary
effects.
      3.   Organizations whose significant focus is the promotion of a
viewpoint related to politics or political issues, or who are otherwise
involved in matters of political controversy.
      4.   Organizations whose significant focus is the promotion of a
viewpoint relating to religion.
      5.   Organizations whose significant focus is the expression of a
viewpoint with respect to promotion, change, or development of legal doctrines,
precedents, or policies.
      6.   Persons or organizations with significant involvement in litigation
in the federal or state courts, including, but not limited to, attorneys, bail
bondsmen, expert witnesses, bounty hunters, and private investigators, and
associations of such persons.
      7.   Those businesses that are integral in assisting public safety
officers in the provision of roadside towing and emergency services.
      8.   Any donor whose affiliation with the city might detract from or
undermine the city's ability to perform its legal duties.
   D.   If the number of qualified donor participants exceeds the city's need
or capacity under this program, preference in participation shall be granted to
the following donors in the order set forth:
      1.   Qualified donors whose principal place of business is within the
boundaries of Ogden City.
      2.   Qualified donors which are city vendors, ranked according to the
amount of business they conduct annually with the city. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1594
FIRST AMENDMENT EVENT GUIDELINES
SECTION:
1594-1: Purpose
1594-2: Policy
1594-3: Responsibility
1594-4: Rules And Regulations
1594-1: PURPOSE:
Pursuant to the authority set forth in section 6-1-1 of the Ogden Municipal
Code, the purpose of this policy is to establish guidelines for First Amendment
events within Ogden City. (Eff. 12-14-2020)
1594-2: POLICY:
Ogden City recognizes the rights of citizens to hold an event consisting of a
public demonstration or rally for the purpose of expressing opinions and views
("First Amendment Event").
The City also has a responsibility to promote public safety, health and general
welfare, protect City resources and property, and prevent conflicts with other
special events and programs including First Amendment Events.
It is the policy of Ogden City to exercise its authority under the United
States Constitution to adopt reasonable, content-neutral, time, place, and
manner guidelines for First Amendment Events to occur.
These guidelines apply to First Amendment Events, whether or not a Special
Event Application has been filled out and approved. (Eff. 12-14-2020)
1594-3: RESPONSIBILITY:
The Arts, Culture and Events Division is responsible for carrying out these
guidelines. The Ogden Police Department has the authority to enforce these
guidelines. Pursuant to section 6-1-10 of the Ogden Municipal Code, violations
of these rules and regulations are subject to criminal penalties as set forth
in title 1, chapter 4 of the Ogden Municipal Code. (Eff. 12-14-2020)
1594-4: RULES AND REGULATIONS
   A.   Groups of three (3) or more persons desiring to hold a First Amendment
Event are required to fill out a Special Event Application for routing and
approval by the City.
   B.   In the event the Mayor adopts an Administrative Order establishing
demonstration zones, the designated locations, and any special restrictions or
guidelines established by the Administrative Order will apply.
   C.   No fees or insurance will be required for First Amendment Events.
   D.   The person filling out the Special Event Application is required to
provide contact information and will be considered the group coordinator.
   E.   The coordinator should use the coordinator's best efforts to notify all
participants of these First Amendment Event Guidelines before the start of the
Event.
   F.   The coordinator should keep a copy of the Special Event Application on
site of the Event. The Special Event Application and any addenda state the
approved parameters of the event. The approved application, and/or approval via
email, is considered the permission for the Event.
   G.   Special Event application timelines are waived, however, groups are
encouraged to fill out an application several business days in advance of the
Event to avoid conflicts with previously approved special events, Ogden City
events or programs, or other First Amendment Events.
   H.   Special Event applications for First Amendment Events are approved for
no longer than ten (10) calendar days.
   I.   A group with an approved Special Event Application will displace a
group without an approved Application. The group without an approved
Application will be asked to move to a non-conflicting location.
   J.   A First Amendment Event may not conflict with another previously
approved special event, Ogden City event or program, or another First Amendment
Event. (Ogden Municipal Code section 6-5-17.)
   K.   Where a conflict exists between a previously approved special event,
Ogden City event or program, or another First Amendment Event, the City may
request the First Amendment Event move to a non-conflicting location.
   L.   In the event the conflicting Event is a "counter" First Amendment
Event, the City may relocate one or both Events to locations where conflicting
messages can be heard and seen, but the City's interests in public safety,
health and general welfare, and protecting City property are met.
   M.   The City reserves the right to immediately revoke approval for a First
Amendment Event at any time should this become necessary in the interest of
public safety, health and general welfare, and protecting City property.
   N.   The following general guidelines apply:
      1.   No smoking or vaping is permitted in any Ogden City park or within
the Municipal Gardens and perimeter sidewalk.
      2.   First Amendment Events are subject to Municipal Gardens or Ogden
City park operating hours, from dawn to dusk or as otherwise noted.
      3.   The group acknowledges that the event is for nonviolent purposes;
violent acts will NOT be tolerated in any manner.
      4.   Event participants must carry any signs by hand, or signs shall be
supported by lathe-type sticks only.
      5.   Event participants may not interfere with pedestrians or vehicular
traffic. Groups may not remain in a roadway unlawfully (Ogden Municipal Code
sections 10-7-12, 11-5-4). Groups may not detain vehicles and may be subject to
charges for unlawful detention and kidnapping (Utah State Code § 76-5-301; §
76-5-304.)
      6.   The group acknowledges the constitutional right of anyone to ignore
or not listen to the group and ignore or not read any information literature
that the group may be passing out; if people do not stop to listen to the
event, event participants may not insist that they do so. Specifically, event
participants may not grab or attempt to physically restrain or touch visitors
of the businesses or residences in the area or any person on public or private
property.
      7.   Event participants may not block or attempt to block any entrance or
driveway. (Ogden Municipal Code Section 11-5-4.)
      8.   The group agrees to be responsible to leave the areas of the event
clean, and that all objects such as: signs, sticks, leaflets, or candles will
be removed by the group.
      9.   Any City property damaged by or as a result of the group will be
replaced or repaired at the cost of the group.
      10.   Interfering with public meetings or public areas is not permitted.
(Utah Code Ann. § 76-9-102.)
      11.   Event participants may not obstruct the free passage of
pedestrians, vehicles, block driveways, entrances, or exits to any business or
building, and may not enter onto private property without the permission of the
property owner.
      12.   Structures, including tents and portable pavilions may not be
erected.
      13.   Electrical power will not be furnished nor will generators be
allowed.
      14.   Events are not permitted to make excessive noise in violation of
Ogden Municipal Code; any portable public address system being used will be so
adjusted to accommodate only those people in the immediate area.
      15.   Event participants shall abide by all pertinent local, state, and
federal ordinances and laws while conducting the activity. (Eff. 12-14-2020)
POLICY 1595
ACQUISITION, DISPOSITION AND LOANS OF UNION STATION MUSEUM COLLECTIONS
SECTION:
1595-1: Purpose
1595-2: Policy
1595-1: PURPOSE:
This policy serves as the framework for management of the Museums at Union
Station’s permanent collection of artifacts and historical information. The
ultimate priority for this policy is the safe, ethical management of
collections in coordination with the Museum’s mission and the public good.
(Eff. 8-28-2024)
1595-2: POLICY:
   A.   It is the policy of the city that the Museums at Union Station
collections management will be carried out in accordance with The Museums at

   B.   The Museums at Union Station Collection Management Protocol will govern
