practices. (Eff. 8-28-2024)
POLICY 1596
MUNICIPAL GARDENS
SECTION:
1596-1: Purpose
1596-2: Policy
1596-3: Responsibility
1596-4: Rules And Regulations
1596-1: PURPOSE:
Pursuant to the authority set forth in section
6-1-1 of the Ogden municipal code, the purpose of this policy is to establish
rules and regulations necessary for the use, control, management and protection
of the public grounds within the Municipal Gardens block (which is located
between 25th Street and 26th Street and between Washington Boulevard and Grant
Avenue, including adjacent sidewalks and walkways and paths therein). (Eff. 10-
13-2009)
1596-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City to provide for the maximum public use and
benefit of the public grounds within the Municipal Gardens block for
recreational and community activities, and special events, while allowing for
the protection of public property and the public safety, health and welfare,
and the economical operation and maintenance of the Municipal Gardens. (Eff.
10-13-2009)
1596-3: RESPONSIBILITY:
The police department shall be responsible for enforcing the rules and
regulations established herein for the Municipal Gardens. Pursuant to the
penalty provision set forth in section
6-1-10 of the Ogden municipal code, any person who violates any of these rules
and regulations shall be deemed guilty of a class B misdemeanor and, upon
conviction thereof, shall be punished as set forth in title 1, chapter 4 of the
Ogden municipal code. (Eff. 10-13-2009)
1596-4: RULES AND REGULATIONS:
   A.   Smoking: No smoking shall be permitted on any portion of the public
grounds within the Municipal Gardens.
   B.   Alcohol:
      1.   As defined in Ogden municipal code section
11-5-1, no person shall consume an "alcoholic beverage", or keep, carry or
possess any "open container" containing an alcoholic beverage within the
Municipal Gardens, except when consumption occurs as part of a special event
for which a special event permit has been issued pursuant to the Ogden
municipal code.
      2.   No person shall be under the influence of alcohol, a controlled
substance, or any substance having the property of releasing toxic vapors, to a
degree that the person may endanger themselves or another within the Municipal
Gardens.
   C.   Animals: Animals brought into the Municipal Gardens, other than as part
of a special event or other permitted activity, shall be adequately restrained
at all times and shall not be permitted to run at large.
   D.   Hours Of Operation: Other than in conjunction with a special event or
other permitted activity, no person shall remain upon any portion of the public
grounds within the Municipal Gardens after ten thirty o'clock (10:30) P.M. or
before five o'clock (5:00) A.M., except police, fire, and parks maintenance
personnel in furtherance of their duties.
   E.   Signs: No signs shall be placed within the Municipal Gardens unless
permitted pursuant to title 18 of the Ogden municipal code.
   F.   Skateboarding And Similar Devices: No person on rollerskates, in-line
skates, skateboards or riding on or by means of any coaster, toy vehicle or
similar device, shall use such devices within the Municipal Gardens, other than
for emergency or law enforcement purposes, as part of a special event or other
permitted activity, or as intended for the exclusive use of a person with a
physical disability.
   G.   Littering: No person shall throw, deposit, place, or discard litter in
any manner within the Municipal Gardens, except in containers or areas lawfully
provided therefor. No person shall expectorate, or urinate or defecate except
into a toilet for that purpose.
   H.   Camping And Related Activities: No person shall camp, lodge, sleep,
cook, make a fire or pitch a tent, fly, lean to, tarpaulin, umbrella, or any
other type of ground cover or shelter, or place sleeping bags, bedding or any
other type of camping or sleeping equipment upon any portion of the Municipal
Gardens, nor shall any person using or benefiting from the use of any of the
foregoing shelter or camping or sleeping equipment fail to remove the same from
the Municipal Gardens for more than five (5) minutes after being requested to
do so by any police officer. This provision shall not apply to picnicking, or
short time, casual sleeping, or where a temporary exception has been issued
pursuant to section
15-1-13 of the Ogden municipal code.
   I.   Noise: Making excessive, unnecessary, unusually loud, or amplified
noises in violation of Ogden municipal code title 12, chapter 14, unless a
special permit has been issued pursuant to code section
12-14-8.
   J.   Nuisances: No person shall within the Municipal Gardens: create any
nuisance, or commit any offense that is in violation of state law or city
ordinance; or scratch, cut, injure or deface any of the buildings, fences,
structures or other property; or foul any of the fountains or any other
improvements; or cut or injure flowers, flowerbeds, or other landscaping; or
create or utilize any path or shortcut other than a city designated path in any
garden or landscaped area, other than to cross an open lawn area.
   K.   Disorderly Conduct: Pursuant to Utah Code Annotated section 10-8-50, no
person shall engage in disorderly conduct, as defined in Utah Code Annotated
section 76-9-102, or disturb the peace by using obscene or profane language
within the Municipal Gardens.
   L.   Aggressive Solicitation: As defined in Ogden municipal code section
11-5-5, no person shall solicit money or other things of value, or solicit the
sale of goods or services in an aggressive manner within the Municipal Gardens.
   M.   Obstructing Walkways And Paths: It is unlawful for any person to remain
standing, lying or sitting on any walkway or path within the Municipal Gardens
for a longer period than two (2) minutes in such a manner as to obstruct the
free passage of foot travelers thereon.
   N.   Posted Orders: No person shall enter any area designated by signs as a
rehabilitation or restoration area, or violate any provision or instruction on
any sign, except enforcement or parks maintenance personnel in furtherance of
their duties.
   O.   Waiver Of Rules: As determined by the city attorney, a waiver of the
rules and regulations contained in this order may apply for activities
protected by the first amendment of the United States constitution.
   P.   Implementation: This policy shall be implemented consistent with
applicable city ordinances and policies and Utah and federal law.
   Q.   Private Property Rights: Additional private property rights may apply
to leased or licensed premises within the Municipal Gardens. (Eff. 10-13-2009)
POLICY 1597
UNMANNED AERIAL SYSTEMS (UAS)
SECTION:
1597-1: Purpose And Scope
1597-2: Policy
1597-3: Privacy
1597-4: Prohibited Use
1597-5: Retention Of UAS Data
1597-6: Data Collected By Private Citizen
1597-1: PURPOSE AND SCOPE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish guidelines for City use of unmanned
aerial systems (UAS) and for the storage, retrieval and dissemination of images
and data captured by UAS.
This policy applies to all City departments and divisions, including employees,
vendors and volunteers working on behalf of the City.
The Ogden City Police Department, the Ogden City Fire Department, and the Ogden
Airport may adopt separate policies for UAS use in accordance with State and
Federal law and regulations not inconsistent with this policy. (Eff. 2-28-2018)
1597-2: POLICY:
   A.   Ogden City departments or divisions may use UAS to enhance City
services through the efficient use of City resources.
   B.   Ogden City departments or divisions shall coordinate UAS use with the
Ogden Police Department UAS Program Coordinator, including participation in any
public notification database, following established safety protocols,
coordinating approval of UAS use within a restricted area, and processing and
redacting data.
   C.   Any City use of UAS will be in strict accordance with State and Federal
law and regulations and Ogden City policy. To review Federal Aviation Authority
(FAA) requirements for the registration and use of UAS by the City, please
refer to: https://www.faa.gov/uas/.
   D.   Engaging in the unauthorized use of a UAS or unauthorized use of data
captured by a UAS may subject an officer or employee to discipline, up to and
including termination of employment.
   E.   City employees operating UAS for City purposes shall sign a form
acknowledging that they have read and understand this policy. Such forms shall
be made available and kept on file by the UAS Program Coordinator.
   F.   Authorized City uses of UAS include uses for public safety, disaster
response and recovery, emergency response, search and rescue, construction
management, environmental monitoring and documentation, inspections, mapping,
marketing, and special events.
   G.   Departments or divisions may operate a City-owned UAS in compliance
with this policy or utilize the services of an approved contractor maintained
by the Program Coordinator.
   H.   City employees may not operate UAS for City purposes other than City-
owned UAS in conformance with this policy.
   I.   City employees may not collect or obtain UAS footage for City purposes
other than in conformance with this policy.
   J.   City-owned UAS must have a global positioning system. The software and/
or firmware used to operate a UAS must be up to date and maintained.
   K.   UAS must be operated in a safe manner. UAS should not be operated in a
way that causes personal injury or property damage. UAS may not have features
(e.g., lights, coloring) or be used in a way that distracts drivers or other
aircraft. UAS that lose GPS signals should be set to hover in place.
Additionally, UAS that lose a signal to a remote operator or when low power is
detected should be set to return to home/origin.
   L.   UAS operators must obtain a remote pilot certification from the FAA and
must comply with all other FAA requirements.
   M.   UAS may not be used within five (5) miles of an airport, in any FAA no-
fly zone, or in any other restricted areas unless approved by the appropriate
authority. City UAS operations must comply with FAA rules.
   N.   Ogden City shall maintain appropriate insurance coverage for UAS use.
   O.   Divisions or departments purchasing UAS shall notify Ogden City Fleet
and Facilities Division of such purchase, together with the intended use of
UAS, as well as any sale or surplus of UAS. (Eff. 2-28-2018)
1597-3: PRIVACY:
Departments or divisions using UAS must have an authorized purpose to collect
information using a UAS, or to use UAS- collected information. Should
information be incidentally collected that could be used to identify persons or
private information, the department or division must remove all personal
identifiable information from raw data footage. (Eff. 2-28-2018)
1597-4: PROHIBITED USE:
UAS equipment shall not be used to conduct random surveillance activities or to
target persons based solely on individual characteristics, such as, but not
limited to race, ethnicity, national origin, religion, disability, gender or
sexual orientation. (Eff. 2-28-2018)
1597-5: RETENTION OF UAS DATA:
Data collected by UAS shall be classified and retained consistent with City
records policy and the Utah Government Records Access and Management Act, Utah
Code Annotated 63G-2-101 et seq.
A department or division may not maintain archives of raw, unprocessed UAS data
once the business purpose is accomplished.
A department or division must restrict access to any raw UAS footage it retains
to authorized staff.
Distribution of raw UAS data is restricted to authorized persons for the
purpose of redacting and processing data only. In all other circumstances, the
City may not exchange raw, unprocessed UAS-collected data between departments
or disclose such data to the public except for exigent public safety needs or
as required by law.
Departments or divisions may store raw, unprocessed UAS data up to a maximum of
one year. Exceptions to this retention schedule must be supported with
documentation and a clear rationale, and approved by the City Recorder and
Legal Department. (Eff. 2-28-2018)
1597-6: DATA COLLECTED BY PRIVATE CITIZEN:
Except as authorized by Utah law for public safety purposes, in order to ensure
data is legally obtained and used with permission, departments or divisions may
not accept or review data captured by a private citizen. The use of any UAS
data captured by a third party must be through an approved vendor consistent
with this policy. (Eff. 2-28-2018)
POLICY 1598
BODY WORN CAMERAS
SECTION:
1598-1: Purpose
1598-2: Policy
1598-3: Definitions
1598-4: Procedures
1598-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide procedures to ensure the proper use,
maintenance and storage of body worn camera (BWC) recordings and equipment. The
BWC recording serves as a third party witness and may reduce the need for court
appearances, as well as protect the Code Enforcement Division or citizens from
complaint. The BWC footage will be primarily used for administrative purposes
rather than evidentiary value. (Eff. 2-28-2019)
1598-2: POLICY:
The policy of the Ogden Code Enforcement Division will be that all Code
Officers with BWC recording equipment will use proper procedures when using,
storing and maintaining the audio-video equipment.
The use of BWC is not intended to replace traditional means of documenting a
case through photographs, drawings, notes, diagrams, interviews, etc., but to
enhance the interaction with the public and safety and training for Ogden City
employees. (Eff. 2-28-2019)
1598-3: DEFINITIONS:
BODY WORN CAMERA (BWC): Means a video recording device that is carried by, or
worn on the body of, a Code Officer and that is capable of recording the
operations of the Code Officer.
"Body worn camera" does not include a dashboard mounted camera or a camera
intended to record secretive investigation activities.
CODE ENFORCEMENT ENCOUNTER: Means:
   A.   A Code enforcement site visit requiring entry on or adjacent to the
property;
   B.   A Code complaint investigation;
   C.   Execution of an administrative warrant (with police escort), including:
      1.   Abatements;
      2.   Investigation of property (inside or out).
   D.   Any other contact that becomes adversarial after the initial contact in
a situation that would not otherwise require recording. (Eff. 2-28-2019)
1598-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Operating Procedure:
      1.   The BWC equipment will be operated in accordance with manufacturer's
recommendations.
      2.   At the beginning of each shift, Code Officers will verify that the
BWC is properly functioning as is reasonably within the Code Officer's ability.
Any time the equipment is found to be not functioning properly, a supervisor
will be notified. Code Officers shall not remove, dismantle, or tamper with any
hardware and/or software component or part of the BWC, with the exception of
the batteries and utility cords.
      3.   Code Officers shall wear the BWC so that it is clearly visible to
the person being recorded.
      4.   Code Officers shall activate the BWC prior to any Code Enforcement
Division encounter; including entry to apartment complex, private residential
dwelling, business, or as soon as reasonably possible after that encounter is
initiated.
      5.   Code Officers shall record in an uninterrupted manner until after
the conclusion of a Code Enforcement Division encounter. This will include
entry to apartment complexes, private residences, and businesses, except as an
interruption of a recording is allowed under the conditions of subsection A9 of
this section.
      6.   When going on duty and off duty, a Code Officer who is issued a BWC
shall record on the BWC the Code Officer's name, case number, address, and the
current time and date.
      7.   If a BWC was present during a Code Enforcement Division encounter,
the Code Officer shall document the presence of the BWC in any code case, or
other official record of a contact; including the case history.
      8.   Once a BWC has been activated the Code Officer shall not deactivate
the BWC until the Code Officer's direct participation in the Code Enforcement
Division encounter is complete, except as provided in subsection A9 of this
section.
      9.   A Code Officer may deactivate a BWC:
         a.   To consult with a supervisor or another Code Officer;
         b.   During a significant period of inactivity; and
         c.   During a conversation with a sensitive victim of crime, a witness
of a crime, or an individual who wishes to report or discuss criminal activity
if:
            (1)   The individual who is the subject of the recording requests
that the Code Officer deactivate the Code Officer's BWC; and
            (2)   The Code Officer believes that the value of the information
outweighs the value of the potential recording and records the request by the
individual to deactivate the BWC.
         d.   If a Code Officer deactivates a BWC during a Code Enforcement
Division encounter, the Code Officer shall audibly announce why the recording
is being stopped prior to deactivating the BWC and then document the reason for
deactivating the BWC in a written report.
      10.   When a Code Officer with a BWC enters an apartment complex, private
residence, or business, the Code Officer shall give notice, when reasonable
under the circumstances, to the occupants and guests that a BWC is in use
either by:
         a.   Wearing a BWC in a clearly visible manner; or
         b.   Giving an audible notice that the officer is using a BWC.
      11.   Code Officers are prohibited from covertly recording other code
personnel without written permission of that Code Officer, or at the direction
of the management.
      12.   The BWC shall not be used to record non-work related activity and
shall not be activated in places where a reasonable expectation of privacy
exists, such as locker rooms, dressing rooms or restrooms.
      13.   Code Officers are prohibited from:
         a.   Reviewing, playing or showing a video made in the course of Code
Enforcement Division work to anyone who is not directly involved in the
investigation or outcome of the recorded event, including members of the
department, without the permission of their supervisor;
         b.   Using a BWC for personal use;
         c.   Making a personal copy of a recording created while on duty or
acting in an official capacity as a Code Officer;
         d.   Retaining a recording of any activity or information obtained
while on duty or acting in an official capacity as a Code Officer;
         e.   Duplicating or distributing a recording except as authorized by
management;
         f.   Altering or deleting a recording in violation of this policy.
      14.   Video may be reviewed by supervisors for the purpose of
investigating a complaint, internal investigations, reviewing for training
purposes, looking for evidence, or other legitimate reasons that in the best
judgment of the supervisor will enhance the training, performance or
professionalism of the Code Officer or the department.
      15.   Video may be reviewed by supervisors for the purpose of
investigating a complaint, internal investigations, reviewing for training
purposes, looking for evidence, or other legitimate reasons that in the best
judgement of the supervisor will enhance the training, performance or
professionalism of the Code Officer or the department.
      16.   Code Officers may view their own BWC recordings as they relate to:
         a.   Their involvement in a case for the purposes of completing an
investigation and preparing official reports.
         b.   Prior to court, or administrative hearing, to refresh
recollection. Code Officers will ensure that the prosecuting attorney is aware
that the BWC recording was reviewed.
      17.   It shall be deemed a violation of this policy for a supervisor to
review recordings for the sole purpose of searching for violations of
department policy or law not related to a specific complaint or incident.
   B.   Control And Management:
      1.   The assigned Code Officer is responsible for assuring that proper
care and storage of each video is accomplished according to policy.
      2.   Code Officers shall be aware of the maximum capacity of the BWC. It
is a Code Officer's responsibility to ensure that the BWC is uploaded to the
appropriate server before it is full.
      3.   Code Officers are required to enter the appropriate classification
coding for the BWC recording for each incident that is recorded. Unintentional
recordings, when a camera is activated accidentally and the video serves no
evidentiary purpose, should be marked "No Evidentiary Value" by the Code
Officer. All videos, regardless of how they are categorized, will be downloaded
and remain on the network for a minimum of sixty (60) days before they are
archived by the evidence/property custodian. If deemed needed for evidentiary
purposes camera footage will be downloaded to a disk or other appropriate
storage within sixty (60) days.
      4.   The evidence/property custodian will archive video from the network
on a weekly basis. Video will be retained for eighteen (18) months unless
otherwise directed by the City Attorney.
      5.   The release of audio-video copies to any agency, individual or
company not already described in this policy will be done in accordance with
Federal, State, and local laws, policies and procedures governing the release
of Code Enforcement Division records and together with any fees that may apply.
(Eff. 2-28-2019)
POLICY 1599
USE OF RADIO
SECTION:
1599-1: Purpose
1599-2: Policy
1599-3: Procedure
1599-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to ensure uniformity in radio procedure and to
ensure code service radio transmissions are on a professional level. (Eff. 8-
30-2019)
1599-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of the Code Services Division to adhere to the rules of the
Federal Communications Commission and to maintain highly professional standards
while operating the radio. It is the responsibility of all supervisors to
ensure that this policy be adhered to. (Eff. 8-30-2019)
1599-3: PROCEDURE:
   A.   Hand-Held Portable Radios:
      1.   Each Code Service's Officer is issued one (1) hand-held radio, one
(1) spare battery, and one (1) desk charger. Each officer must sign an
acknowledgment of receipt. The equipment will then become the responsibility of
the officer.
      2.   All Code Services Officers will maintain their radio at functional
readiness at all times. Batteries are to be kept charged to ensure functional
readiness. Radio issues are to be reported to the appropriate personnel to be
immediately rectified.
      3.   While on duty, field personnel will ensure immediate availability of
their radios. Dispatching and radio procedures will continue as described in
this policy.

   C.   Radio Communications: In order to better satisfy the demands placed
upon the radio system, the following procedures are to be followed.
      1.   General Guidelines: Radio communications are under operational
control of the dispatchers, subject to Federal Communications Commission rules,
departmental policy and directives, and supervision by the OPD duty officer.
Employees should be attentive to all transmissions, bearing in mind the fact
that our channels are monitored by the FCC, other public safety agencies and
many private citizens.
         2.   Accuracy:
         a.   The usefulness of information is limited by its accuracy. Be sure
before you broadcast that the information you will be giving is as accurate as
possible. Use the 10-code and standardized clear speech terminology when
practical. Word your message so that it conveys your exact meaning. Do not use
slang terms or "CB" jargon.
         b.   If in doubt about a message received, ask for a repeat or
clarification.   
      3.   Brevity:
         a.   Radio transmissions must be brief and concise, keeping in mind
that other units are on the air at the same time and that an emergency may
occur at any moment. Use the 10-code and standardized terms for clear speech in
order to say what needs to be said in as few words as possible. Avoid
unnecessary personal communications.
         b.   If a lengthy conversation of a non-emergency nature is called
for, use the telephone or meet with the other person at a convenient location.
When broadcasting any message of more than 30 seconds in length, break the
transmission about every 15 seconds to allow for priority traffic. Superfluous
politeness such as "please," "thank you," etc., should be avoided, as should
any unnecessary justifications or explanations. When the message you want to
convey is covered by the 10-code or a clear speech phrase, it is sufficient to
give only the code or phrase without a detailed explanation.
      4.   Clarity: A radio message that is not clear and easily understandable
may result in the loss of valuable time, tying up the radio with requests for
clarification or misunderstanding of important information with consequent
exposure of officers or citizens to unnecessary hazards.
         a.   To ensure the clarity of radio transmissions, decide what you are
going to say before you begin transmitting. Use the 10-code whenever
applicable. Pronounce the 10-code fully; i.e., "10-28" or "10-29" rather than
"28" or "29." Choose words that are distinct or easily understandable. When
spelling, use the phonetic alphabet.
         b.   Speak slowly and distinctly, without emotional wording or
inflections that may tend to distort your voice or obscure the message. Avoid
unnecessary words, slang, humor, or excessive emphasis.
         c.   Speak across the microphone, not directly into it, while holding
the microphone two to six inches from the mouth and speaking in normal tones.
Be cognizant of background noises. This applies to the radio handsets with
built-in microphone as well as those with detachable lapel microphones. To be
sure that your entire transmission is heard, be certain that the transmit
switch is fully depressed for one to two seconds, waiting for beep tone to
clear before you begin to speak and continue to hold it until transmission is
completely finished. If the system is busy, the radio will emit a tone when the
transmit switch is depressed. When this occurs, release the transmit switch,
wait for one or two seconds, and depress the transmit switch again.
      5.   Routine Procedures:
         a.   When called by the dispatcher or another unit, respond by giving
your location. Example: "1-4, 2400 Washington."
         b.   When calling the dispatcher or another unit, address the intended
receiver, then identify yourself using your designated radio call number or
code. Example: "Weber, 2F 1-4" or "2F Sierra 3, 2F Delta 9."
         c.   When going off the air for any reason, sign out and state your
location.
         d.   Anytime a Code Services Officer will be off their normally
assigned channel, the officer will notify the dispatcher; and again notify
dispatch when the officer returns to their normal working channel.
      6.   Information Requests: The following information services are
available from or through the dispatcher:
         a.   Registration checks on vehicles licensed in Utah
         b.   Stolen vehicle information
         c.   Warrants on persons
         d.   NCIC listings of persons, vehicles and other items
         e.   Missing Persons
         f.   NLETS (National Law Enforcement Telecommunications System, also
known as TWX)
         g.   Utah driver license information by exact name spelling and DOB or
by driver license or Social Security Number   
         h.   OPD records on persons. Privacy laws prohibit the discussion of
criminal records by radio but the fact of the existence of a record and its
file number are not restricted from police radio traffic   
         i.   Recent bulletins and extra patrol requests
         j.   City directory   
         k.   Telephone directory   
         l.   Locations of city streets   
         m.   An index (rolodex file) of businesses, churches, and schools with
names and telephone numbers of persons to be contacted in emergencies. This
information will not normally be broadcast by radio. Calls will be placed by
the dispatchers
         n.   Telephone numbers of public safety and social service agencies in
the local area
         o.   A direct telephone line to ambulance, tow truck and taxi cab
services
         p.   A log of cases handled by this department, arranged numerically
and chronologically for the current year
         q.   A roster of OPD personnel and reserve officers, including ID
numbers. For obvious reasons, this information should not be discussed by radio
   Since radio communications is such an integral part of day-to-day
operations, a great deal can be accomplished toward the goal of true
professionalism by proper use of the radio and the proper utilization of the
services provided by the communications center. We can streamline radio
procedure by eliminating superfluous, useless talk and by not asking
dispatchers to do anything that can be accomplished elsewhere or that you can
do yourself.
   Before requesting information by radio, consider whether the request is
necessary at that particular time. If it is practical to obtain the information
from the Records Bureau at a convenient time, or by a little extra
investigative effort, please do so. Remember that the dispatchers are
frequently very busy and anything, within reason, that can lighten their
workload will contribute to the efficiency of departmental operations.
   Because Code Services case notes are regarded as public records, Code
Services Officers should ensure that any sensitive information from an
investigation or query for information such as account numbers, SSN's, criminal
history, or any other normally guarded or private information is not placed in
the official case notes.
      7.   Technical Problems:
   Radios, like any other electronic device, are subject to occasional
breakdowns, often without warning. If you suspect a malfunction in your radio,
first check the power and squelch controls and the channel selector to make
certain that they are properly set. Check the microphone to be sure that the
switch is not stuck in the open position.
   To test your radio, call "Weber" (or any unit), "2F 1-4, radio check." If no
more than three such attempts are unsuccessful, make no further attempts for
you may be blocking priority traffic.
   Having determined that your radio is malfunctioning, switch the set
completely off and telephone the dispatcher as soon as possible advising her of
the situation. Always contact the dispatcher before going out of service for
repairs.
      8.   FCC Rules:
         a.   The police radio is primarily authorized to transmit
communications directly relating to public safety and the protection of life
and property, communications essential to official police activities, and
communications essential to other official activities of the licensee.
         b.   Any other use is in violation of law, as is the transmission of
superfluous communications or signals, or communications containing profane or
obscene words, language or intent.
         c.   Any person violating FCC rules is subject to a fine of not more
than $10,000, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year, or both.
         d.   It should always be borne in mind that a communications system is
a tool. Like any other tool, it is valueless if it isn't used correctly or is
not understood or practiced.

      11.   Overview Of Current System:
         Code Services and OPD utilize a portable radio system with the
capacity to communicate with all Weber County area law enforcement agencies.
These channels are connected to a repeater system, called Smart Zone, which
strengthens the signal and allows access from nearly every part of the county.
This is a shared network of transmitter and receiver sites all connected
together by microwave to a central electronics bank. With this system and a
consolidated dispatch facility, you will have access to every county and state
agency along the Wasatch Front, and eventually the entire State of Utah.
         Narcotics or other special function officers may be assigned and
equipped from time to time to utilize other channels.
      12.   Call Numbers: The designation for Ogden Code Services is "2F Hotel"

      13.   Emergency Notification Button: The orange button on top of the
radio is an emergency notification button that will set off an alarm and
identify on the dispatch console the Code Services Officer assigned to that
radio. Dispatchers will immediately attempt to locate that officer to determine
the nature of the emergency. At this time, the system does not have GPS
capability. In the event of an error, the officer will immediately notify
Dispatch, of the officer's status; the alarm notification will be cleared from
the screen at the dispatch center.
      14.   Communications Center: Sometimes problems occur with radio
transmission activities, whether it is the fault of the dispatcher or the Code
Services Officer. It is the responsibility of the duty lieutenant to correct
any radio problem as soon as he becomes aware of it. If the problem stems from
Code Service personnel, the duty lieutenant must handle that directly. If the
problem or complaint concerns the dispatcher or dispatch procedure, the duty
lieutenant will immediately deal with the on-duty dispatch supervisor. It is
also the responsibility of the duty lieutenant to determine what needs to be
addressed and what is frivolous, nit-picky and should not be addressed. The
division commanders and the dispatch committee will monitor this process. If
the duty lieutenant hears something on the radio that needs correcting, he
corrects it, and if any of our personnel have a complaint or concern about the
dispatching, they must take it immediately to the duty lieutenant. (Eff. 8-13-
2019)
TITLE 7
RISK MANAGEMENT
POLICY 1600
EMPLOYEE WORK RELATED INJURY REQUIRING MEDICAL TREATMENT
SECTION:
1600-1: Purpose
1600-2: Policy
1600-3: Definitions
1600-4: Procedures
1600-5: Other Items
1600-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to inform Ogden City employees of procedures for
work related accident/illness requiring medical treatment. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1600-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to designate a medical facility and
to provide procedures for treatment to all employees for work related accident/
illnesses requiring medical treatment. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1600-3: DEFINITIONS:
LIFE THREATENING EMERGENCIES: Those situations when life is in danger if
immediate treatment is not received. These include unconsciousness,
uncontrolled bleeding, severe respiratory distress, major burns, spinal cord
injury, shock or life threatening poisonings. In a life threatening emergency,
call
9-1-1, go to McKay-Dee Hospital emergency room or to the nearest emergency
facility.
URGENT SITUATIONS: Those requiring immediate care but are not life threatening.
Examples include fractures or injuries which may require sutures. (Eff. 3-14-
2007)
1600-4: PROCEDURES:
The following are the procedures for work related accident/illness requiring
medical treatment:
   A.   Employees injured on the job requiring medical treatment are requested
to report to the WorkMed facility located at 1355 West 3400 South (by the Ogden
Hinckley Airport). Hours are weekdays from seven thirty o'clock (7:30) A.M. to
five thirty o'clock (5:30) P.M. (WorkMed phone number: 627-1273).
   B.   For minor injuries occurring on the job after WorkMed hours, report to
WorkMed during their business hours or call to schedule an appointment.
   C.   For minor injuries occurring on the job after WorkMed hours and
seriousness of condition is questionable, call the McKay-Dee Hospital emergency
room number 625-2020 to discuss injury and receive further instructions. Do not
go to hospital emergency room unless directed to do so by emergency room
person.
   D.   In urgent situations call WorkMed at 627-1273, during their business
hours or the McKay-Dee Hospital emergency room number 625-2020 if after WorkMed
hours to receive instructions.
   E.   Life threatening accident/illness requiring emergency treatment during
WorkMed hours, should report directly to McKay- Dee Hospital emergency room at
3939 Harrison Boulevard, or the nearest emergency facility. If seriousness is
questionable call WorkMed, 627-1273, for instructions to proceed to emergency
room or WorkMed facility. Always notify emergency room staff that patient is an
employee of Ogden City and WorkMed is Ogden City's designated medical facility.
   F.   Life threatening accident/illness requiring emergency treatment after
WorkMed hours should report directly to McKay-Dee Hospital emergency room at
3939 Harrison Boulevard or nearest emergency facility. Always notify emergency
room staff that patient is an employee of Ogden City and WorkMed is Ogden
City's designated medical facility. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1600-5: OTHER ITEMS:
In accordance with Utah worker compensation laws, Ogden City is allowed to
designate a medical provider for work related accident/illness. Ogden City has
selected WorkMed and McKay-Dee Hospital emergency room. Payment to other
physicians for industrial accidents will not be made unless referred by
WorkMed, the McKay-Dee Hospital, or a "change of physician" form is completed
in the management services department and approved by the Utah state industrial
commission. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1620
SAFETY AND HEALTH
SECTION:
1620-1: Purpose
1620-2: Policy
1620-3: Definitions
1620-4: Safety Program/Accident Control
1620-5: Responsibility
1620-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide information and guidelines to all
departments initiating and maintaining a complete accident prevention program
that will provide safe and healthful working conditions as well as stimulate
employees to work in a safe manner. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1620-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to provide a safe and healthy
workplace for every employee of Ogden City and to minimize the hazards to the
citizens of our community. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1620-3: DEFINITIONS:
ACCIDENT: An event that results in physical harm to a person or damage to
property.
INCIDENT: Any event that could or does result in a loss.
LOSS: Any incident that could negatively impact the municipal assets and
finances of Ogden City.
NEAR MISS: An incident which, under slightly different circumstances, could
have resulted in personal injury or property damage.
RISK MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE: A committee comprised of the city attorney, director
of management services and the risk manager and may include department
directors, division managers and staff personnel when appropriate.
UNSAFE CONDITION: A hazardous physical condition or circumstance which could
directly permit the occurrence of an accident. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1620-4: SAFETY PROGRAM/ACCIDENT CONTROL:
To ensure a comprehensive accident control program Ogden City has established
five (5) fundamental requirements for all departments.
   A.   Management Leadership: Assume leadership responsibility for the safety/
accident control programs. Communication, responsibility, accountability, and
support are key elements that must be addressed by each individual department
in developing an effective program.
   B.   Accident Analysis: All departments must analyze and determine hazards
and/or hazardous conditions and cooperate in all investigations. Departments
must take actions needed to eliminate or control accidents or incidents that
result in personal injury, property damage or interruption of normal
operations.
   C.   Employee Selection And Training: Include selection, retention, and
promotion of employees as criteria for safety/accident control effectiveness.
   D.   Safe Working Conditions: Require that specific attention be paid to
control of design, engineering, condition and use of all equipment, facilities,
process, methods and procedures to eliminate hazards and minimize work related
losses and potential private citizen injury or property damage.
   E.   Incentive Activities: Provide incentive awards or other specific
recognition for accident control accomplishments to individual employees,
groups of employees, divisions and departments through available resources.
(Eff. 3-14-2007)
1620-5: RESPONSIBILITY:
   A.   Administration:
      1.   Communicate the importance and necessity of safe and healthful work
practices.
      2.   Provide consistent procedures and decision processes.
      3.   Outline general responsibilities as they relate to the safety
program.
      4.   Provide information and guidelines to all departments.
   B.   Departments: The department director is responsible for:
      1.   Ensure the health and welfare of each employee in the department
through the establishment and maintenance of safe and healthful working
conditions and practices.
      2.   Provide the proper training of employees, including detailing job
hazards, safety procedures and training on all equipment, tools, etc.,
necessary for the performance of the employee's job duties.
      3.   Ensure personal protective equipment is provided and used in
accordance with safety standards and practices.
      4.   Encourage reporting of hazardous conditions and immediate
consideration of same. (See policy 1650, "Reporting Hazardous Conditions", of
this title.)
      5.   Schedule division safety/accident control meetings as often as
necessary to effect safety practices and work methods. Records of these
meetings will be retained for inspection with a copy forwarded to the risk
management office for review.
      6.   Conduct periodic safety inspections of all facilities, equipment and
vehicles.
      7.   Maintain vehicles and equipment assigned to their department in a
safe operating condition.
      8.   Ensure that all accident reports and industrial injury reports are
forwarded to risk management within forty eight (48) hours of the incident.
      9.   Establish an intradepartmental safety committee if deemed
appropriate and necessary.
      10.   Establish and maintain reporting requirements sufficient to
determine if the program is being effectively implemented.
      11.   Establish objective measures of safety performance evaluations.
   C.   Supervisor: Supervisors shall assume the responsibility of thoroughly
instructing their personnel on safe practices to be observed in their work
situations. They shall consistently enforce safety standards and requirements,
set the example of good safety practices and act positively to eliminate any
potential hazards within the activities or areas under their jurisdiction.
Injury records and safety related accomplishments shall be measured along with
other phases of supervisor performance. The principal duties of supervisors in
discharging responsibilities for safety are as follows:
      1.   Enforce all safety regulations in effect and make employees aware
that violations of safety rules may be cause for disciplinary action.
      2.   Ensure all injuries accidents are reported by phone within one hour
of the injury, and accidents not involving injuries are reported within forty
eight (48) hours of the incident.
      3.   Conduct thorough investigations of all accidents and take necessary
steps to prevent reoccurrence through employee safety education, operating
procedures or modification of equipment.
      4.   Provide employees with complete safety instructions regarding their
duties prior to employee placement in potentially hazardous jobs.
      5.   Conduct regular safety checks of the area, including a careful
examination of all new and relocated equipment before it is placed into
operation.
      6.   Ensure that equipment is properly maintained.
      7.   Continuously inspect for unsafe practices and conditions and
promptly undertake corrective action.
      8.   Maintain high standards of personal and operational cleanliness
throughout all operations.
      9.   Provide safety equipment and protective devices for each job based
on knowledge of applicable standards or on recommendation of risk management.
      10.   Conduct safety briefings at organizational meetings and encourage
employee use of safety suggestions.
      11.   Give full support to all safety procedures, activities and
programs.
   D.   Employees: Each employee is expected to place safe work practices and
identification of unsafe conditions in their highest priority while performing
their daily tasks. Each employee's safety commitment shall include, but is not
limited to, the following:
      1.   Using the safety equipment which has been provided in performing his
daily work assignments.
      2.   Wearing the prescribed uniform and safety items as required.
      3.   Not operating equipment or using tools for which training or
orientation has not been received.
      4.   Reporting defective equipment or maintenance problems immediately to
a supervisor.
      5.   Refraining from operating an unsafe vehicle or equipment until fixed
or deemed to be safe by the employee's division manager or department director.
      6.   Warning coworkers of unsafe conditions or practices they are engaged
in which could lead to or cause an accident.
      7.   Reporting dangerous or unsafe conditions that exist in the workplace
as well as throughout the city. This includes defective sidewalks, broken
curbs, hanging limbs, loose handrails, open manholes, missing or damaged signs,
etc.
      8.   Reporting of all injuries and accidents regardless of severity.
      9.   Protecting from potentially hazardous situations resulting from city
work or activities.
      10.   Taking care not to abuse tools and equipment.
      11.   Adequately securing items or loads when driving city vehicles to
prevent falling off in transit. If appropriate, this includes sweeping rocks or
debris from truck bed or tailgate.
   E.   Risk Management: Risk Management shall be a resource for the
development, organization, coordination and implementation of safety programs
and safety education. Risk management functions may include worksite
inspections, hazard reduction and accident/injury investigations. Risk
management shall advise the department directors, division managers,
supervisors and employees of unsafe conditions and/or problems related to
accident prevention. In addition risk management shall:
      1.   Prepare and keep adequate records of all accidents, incidents, etc.
      2.   Prepare and keep adequate records of all training relevant to
vehicle and equipment operation.
      3.   Coordinate the development of safety educational material.
      4.   Conduct periodic safety inspections with departmental safety
committees.
      5.   Assist departments with safety committees as needed.
      6.   Provide wherever possible advice, guidance, and assistance that may
be needed in safety training, accident prevention, or use of potentially
hazardous equipment or products. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1630
SEAT BELT POLICY
SECTION:
1630-1: Purpose
1630-2: Policy
1630-3: Responsibility
1630-4: Other Items
1630-1: PURPOSE:
The purposes of this policy are to:
   A.   Recognize that safety belts are an important effective item of personal
protective equipment, that people needlessly die and are injured due to their
failure to use available safety belts, and that reducing these costly injuries
can better serve the public.
   B.   Establish mandatory belt usage as a citywide policy, and to designate
responsibility for implementation and enforcement. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1630-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to:
   A.   Ensure that all employees and vehicle occupants shall use available
safety belts at all times while traveling on city business in any city owned
vehicle or private vehicle.
   B.   Maintain all safety belt systems so they are clean, easily accessible,
and in good working order. Individual employees are responsible for reporting
any maintenance problems.
   C.   Ensure that the fleet division upgrades and/or repairs any unsafe
safety belt systems in all city owned vehicles.
   D.   Inform all employees on proper safety belt use and Ogden City's
commitment to this policy. Information shall be emphasized through employee
orientation and education programs, driver training, and safety briefings.
(Eff. 3-14-2007)
1630-3: RESPONSIBILITY:
   A.   First line supervisors are charged with the primary responsibility for
general education and enforcement of this policy.
   B.   Safety belt use shall be enforced in the same manner as any other work
rule. Violation of this policy may be viewed as grounds for disciplinary
action.
   C.   The driver of the vehicle is responsible for enforcing proper belt use
by all occupants. The ranking occupant, if other than the driver, shares this
responsibility. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1630-4: OTHER ITEMS:
Exceptions allowed under state law are not covered in Ogden City's seat belt
policy are not allowed by Ogden City's citywide policies but may be granted by
the chief administrative officer or his/her designee and will be upon written
approval. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1650
REPORTING HAZARDOUS CONDITIONS
SECTION:
1650-1: Purpose
1650-2: Policy
1650-3: Responsibility
1650-4: Procedures
1650-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish standards for reporting and
correcting hazardous conditions in the workplace and within Ogden City. (Eff.
3-14-2007)
1650-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to review and take any necessary
actions to correct conditions of potential hazards to employees or the citizens
of Ogden City. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1650-3: RESPONSIBILITY:
It is the responsibility of every Ogden City employee to report hazardous
conditions and/or procedures in the workplace or within the community. (Eff. 3-
14-2007)
1650-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Any employee aware of hazardous conditions and/or procedures should
complete the top portion of the hazard report form (risk management form:
policy 1650), indicating location and description of hazard and action
recommended.
   B.   Employee should immediately forward completed report to his/her
supervisor.
   C.   Supervisor must respond within five (5) days by completing bottom
portion of hazard report form and forwarding it to the risk management
division.
   D.   Supervisors are responsible for assuring all high risk hazards are
corrected immediately. All other hazards are to be corrected as soon as
possible.
   E.   The risk management division will contact the employee to verify if the
reported hazard has been satisfactorily corrected.
   F.   For traffic control device problems complete an Ogden City report of
traffic control device problem form (risk management form: policy 1650) and
forward to the traffic engineer immediately. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1660
CLAIMS FILED AGAINST OGDEN CITY
SECTION:
1660-1: Purpose
1660-2: Policy
1660-3: Responsibilities
1660-4: Procedures
1660-1: PURPOSE:
The purposes of this policy are to:
   A.   Establish procedures concerning claims filed by the general public
against Ogden City or a city employee.
   B.   Establish a process for the investigation and reporting of injuries
and/or property damage claims from the general public as well as procedures for
employees involved in incidents where possible claims against Ogden City may
arise.
Note: Employees involved in motor vehicle accidents must also follow policy
1510, "Reporting Accidents And Damage To City Vehicles And/Or Property", of
this manual. (Eff. 11-16-2007)
1660-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to:
   A.   Allow any person having a claim against the city or against a city
employee to file a written notice of claim with the city within one year after
the claim arises. All claims presented by the general public shall be filed
with the city recorder's office in conformance with the Utah governmental
immunity act.
   B.   Forward all claims filed with the Ogden City recorder's office to the
risk management division for processing.
   C.   File and forward appropriate claim notice and documentation to the
city's insurance carrier or applicable agency, through the risk management
division.
   D.   Require the department/division involved in a claim to obtain the
necessary background information, conduct an internal investigation, and
forward all reports to Ogden City's risk management division.
   E.   Ensure that the risk management committee reviews all claims filed
against the city. (Eff. 11-16-2007)
1660-3: RESPONSIBILITIES:
   A.   Department Director/Division Manager:
      1.   Inform employees that they shall not admit or imply fault to a
citizen or claimant.
      2.   Train employees in proper incident reporting procedures.
      3.   Obtain necessary background information and reports. If applicable,
request copy of any available police reports.
      4.   Review reports and conduct further investigation if warranted.
      5.   Forward all reports to the risk management division.
      6.   Assist risk management division, insurance carrier, or other
applicable agency in their review and investigation of claim.
      7.   Refer unsatisfied citizens or claimants to the risk management
division.
   B.   Risk Management Committee: Shall review all Ogden City accidents,
claims and losses and make recommendations as necessary.
   C.   Chief Administrative Officer Or Designee: The director of management
services is designated on behalf of the chief administrative officer, with
recommendation of the risk management committee and the advice of the city
attorney, to settle disputed or doubtful claims against the city when the total
amount to be paid by the city does not exceed ten thousand dollars
($10,000.00).
   D.   Mayor/City Council: Any disputed or doubtful claims against the city
that exceed ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00) shall be compromised or settled
with the approval of the mayor. The chief administrative officer will provide
the mayor with his/her recommendations. Claim settlements requiring the
expenditure of funds not authorized in the current budget shall require
approval of the city council. (Eff. 11-16-2007)
1660-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   All claims involving personal injury, damage to a vehicle or personal
property presented by the general public shall be filed with the city
recorder's office.
   B.   If a citizen contacts a city department regarding an injury or damage
to personal property, the appropriate city department should investigate and
take necessary corrective actions.
   C.   If a citizen is not satisfied with the situation or corrective action
taken, he/she shall be referred to the city's risk management division to file
a claim against Ogden City.
   D.   The risk management division will instruct the citizen on the
procedures for filing a claim against Ogden City.
   E.   Employees involved in or responding to incidents which may result in a
claim filed against Ogden City shall prepare a written statement detailing the
facts of the incident or occurrence, as known to them and provide this
statement to their supervisor.
   F.   Immediate supervisors shall also prepare a written statement of facts
regarding the incident or occurrence, as known to them. This shall be completed
within twenty four (24) hours of an accident/incident and forwarded with
employee's statement and any other reports and information to the risk
management division.
   G.   Upon review of the supporting documentation the risk management
division shall obtain any additional information that is necessary to process
the claim.
   H.   Once the "claim against Ogden City" form, employee's and supervisor's
statements, police reports and all other necessary information are obtained,
claims may be processed by the risk management division for final settlement.
In addition, the risk management division may forward all information, as
necessary, to the city's insurance carrier for review, investigation and
ultimately the determination regarding settlement of claims.
   I.   Within sixty (60) days of the filing of a claim the city or its
insurance carrier shall contact claimant in writing of its approval or denial.
If a response is not received within sixty (60) days, the claim is considered
to be denied. (Eff. 11-16-2007)
POLICY 1670
INDOOR CLEAN AIR ACT ADMINISTRATIVE POLICY
SECTION:
1670-1: Purpose
1670-2: Policy
1670-1: PURPOSE:
The Utah indoor clean air act (the "act") prohibits smoking in all indoor
places of public access and publicly owned buildings and offices. The act
allows building owners or operators to designate certain outdoor areas as
smoking permitted areas.
The purpose of this policy is to authorize department directors to designate
certain areas outside a city facility as smoking permitted areas, consistent
with the requirements of the act. (Eff. 7-23-2008)
1670-2: POLICY:
Smoking is not encouraged among city employees, and the city offers classes
through the wellness program to assist employees who desire to stop smoking.
Smoking is prohibited inside all Ogden City facilities, and is not permitted
outside a facility within twenty five feet (25') of any entranceway, exit, open
window, or air intake of any city facility.
Department directors may adopt policies in compliance with the act designating
certain areas outside a facility as smoking permitted areas, and prohibiting
smoking in all other areas. Where facilities are shared by more than one
department, e.g., the public safety building, the responsible department
directors shall adopt a joint policy with respect to such facility.
Any department policy adopted pursuant to this administrative policy shall
include a site drawing indicating where smoking is permitted and where smoking
is prohibited, and shall be reviewed and approved by the department of
management services, the division of fleet and facilities, and the legal
department.
Final policies shall be filed with the city recorder. (Eff. 7-23-2008)
POLICY 1680
RISK MANAGEMENT TRAINING AND REQUESTS FOR VOLUNTEERS
SECTION:
1680-1: Purpose
1680-2: Policies
1680-3: Procedures
1680-1: PURPOSE:
The purposes of this policy are to:
   A.   Establish procedures for the planning and approval of necessary risk
management training for city employees;
   B.   Establish a procedure for approving requests for volunteers from
outside agencies, organizations and individuals for risk management purposes.
(Eff. 6-27-2011)
1680-2: POLICIES:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to:
   A.   Balance and coordinate necessary risk management training of city
employees with other governmental activities;
   B.   Make full use of internal city resources before making a general or
specific request for volunteers to outside agencies, organizations and
individuals for risk management purposes, to avoid overtaxing volunteer
resources; and
   C.   Require the management services director and mayor to specifically
approve each risk management training or request for volunteers, except as
exempted herein. (Eff. 6-27-2011)
1680-3: PROCEDURES:
The risk management division manager shall obtain written approval from the
management services director and the mayor prior to planning and scheduling a
risk management training meeting for city employees. The request for approval
shall be in writing and should set forth the purposes for the training, the
timing of the training, the categories of employees involved in the training,
and any other considerations that make the training necessary or advisable. The
management services director or mayor will coordinate with directors and
managers of affected departments and divisions, as necessary, prior to granting
approval.
The risk management division manager shall obtain written approval from the
management services director and the mayor prior to making a request for
volunteer services from outside agencies, organizations and citizens. The
request for approval shall be in writing and should set forth the need for
volunteers, the time, place and activities that such volunteers will be
involved in, the entities that will be requested for volunteers, and an
explanation as to why the services to be provided by the volunteers cannot or
should not be provided through internal city resources. The approval procedures
set forth above shall not be required before requesting assistance of community
emergency response team (CERT) volunteers. (Eff. 6-27-2011)
POLICY 1690
GETS/WPS ACCESS
SECTION:
1690-1: Purpose
1690-2: Scope
1690-3: Responsibilities
1690-4: Policies And Procedures
1690-1: PURPOSE:
Congestion on telephone networks (wire line and wireless) caused by natural
and/or manmade disasters can affect emergency response capabilities by limiting
call completion for public safety responders. The government emergency
telecommunications services (GETS) and the wireless priority service (WPS) were
developed to address the growing need for priority communications. GETS
enhances call completion for select wire line (landline) users when abnormal
call volumes exist. WPS enhances call completion for select wireless (cellular)
users when abnormal call volumes exist. Both services receive priority over
public calls; however, they do not preempt calls already in progress. (Eff. 3-
13-2015)
1690-2: SCOPE:
This policy applies to all Ogden City employees who receive or are responsible
for a GETS/WPS card. Department directors determine who is issued which card
(s). The emphasis are employees or groups who rely on telecommunications
services to perform critical functions, including those areas related to
leadership, safety, finance, logistics, operations and planning. (Eff. 3-13-
2015)
1690-3: RESPONSIBILITIES:
Those employees or groups who are responsible for a GETS and/or WPS card are
required to secure and maintain such card and become familiar with its usage
and limitations. They are also required to test the proper functioning of the
card(s) on a regular basis. This is done by calling the familiarization line,
703-818-3924, or a phone number you may dial in an emergency, as the
destination number. There is an associated fee for calls not made to the
familiarization line. If these calls are short in duration and on a regular
schedule they recognize them as a test and do not charge for them. Those
employees, who are issued a GETS and/or WPS card, must surrender card upon
separation from Ogden City. (Eff. 3-13-2015)
1690-4: POLICIES AND PROCEDURES:
   A.   GETS: Most wire lined phones are connected directly to a telephone
access provider's network and can be used to place GETS calls. However, a dial
tone is required to place a GETS call. If GETS users experience dial tone
delays during call congestion, users can minimize delays by remaining on the
line, rather than hanging up and dialing again. Remaining on the call prevents
interruption of the local exchange carriers (LEC) dial tone queuing process and
provides dial tone in turn to the customer who has been holding for the longest
period of time. GETS calls can be placed from cellular communications devices
that are not subscribed to WPS, however, a GETS card alone will not provide
priority on initial access from a mobile handset to the wireless
telecommunications networks. GETS users should be able to access GETS through
most mobile switching centers (MSCs).
      1.   Making a GETS call:
         a.   Access outside phone line (dial tone) and dial the GETS access
number 710-627-GETS (4387).
         b.   Listen for the GETS tone.
         c.   Enter the twelve (12) digit PIN on the front of your GETS card
(do not enter # after the last digit).
         d.   Listen for prompt: "Please enter your destination number now".
         e.   Enter the ten (10) digit destination number (omit the 1 before
the area code).
         f.   You will hear an announcement: "You are using GETS, AT&T, MCI, or
Sprint". GETS will route your call.
   B.   WPS: WPS calls can be made to other cell phones, landlines, and
satellite phones. The destination wireless device does not need to have the WPS
feature.
      1.   Making a WPS call:
         a.   Ensure you have coverage (1 or more "bars" on the display
screen).
         b.   Dial *272 and the destination number and then push SEND, or green
button, to initiate the call.
         c.   Network will route call to the destination number. It may take
thirty (30) seconds or longer to complete the call during heavy congestion and
there may be intervals of ringing and/or silence; this is normal. On most cell
phones the screen will display *272 and the destination number.
         d.   If the first attempt does not complete, end the call and retry
the WPS call.
   C.   Stipend To Employees For City Use Of Wireless Priority Service:
      1.   Employees who have been issued WPS cards are eligible to receive a
stipend to compensate for business related costs incurred when using their
personally owned cell phones. (Eff. 3-13-2015)
TITLE 8
GENERAL ADMINISTRATION
POLICY 1701
CITY LETTERHEAD
SECTION:
1701-1: Purpose
1701-2: Policy
1701-3: Responsibilities
1701-4: Procedures
1701-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to:
   A.   Establish consistent design standards for letterhead for city
departments, divisions, agencies, boards, commissions and committees. (Eff. 3-
14-2007)
1701-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to:
   A.   Require that all city letterhead be designed according to the standards
included in this policy to ensure a consistent appearance while still allowing
flexibility within each city department and organization.
   B.   Define responsibility for individual departments, divisions, agencies,
boards, commissions and committees concerning the design and use of city
letterhead. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1701-3: RESPONSIBILITIES:
   A.   Management Services Director: Ensure consistent application of the
policy throughout the city.
   B.   Department Directors: Review and approve use of logos on letterhead
used within the department, or used for city agencies, boards, commissions, or
committees for which the department provides administrative support. (Eff. 3-
14-2007)
1701-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   City letterhead must comply with the design elements in this section.
   B.   Use of an approved logo must be used on city letterhead. By default,
the logo to be used is the city seal or the "mountain" logo as maintained by
the management services department. Other logos may be used with the approval
of the department director. Logos must be placed in the upper left corner of
the letterhead, beginning 0.5 inch below the top of the page and 1.0 inch from
the left side of the page.
   C.   Opposite the logo and right justified 1.0 inch from the right edge of
the paper must appear the words Ogden City and the name of the department,
agency, board, commission, or committee. The Ogden City text must be in either
an Old English type font (if the city seal is used) or an Arrus type font (if
the mountain logo is used) in a point size of 16 and in bold type.
   D.   If desired, a particular division may be identified immediately under
the Ogden City line, and should be in a type size of 12 point and in bold type.
   E.   The lines immediately below the name of the department, agency, board,
commission, or committee, should include a complete mailing address, including
ZIP code, phone number, fax number, and, where applicable, an electronic mail
address. No abbreviations may be used in the name and address area. ZIP codes
used may be the five (5) digit ZIP or ZIP+4. In phone and fax numbers, the area
code 801 is to be placed in parentheses. This information should be in a type
size of 12 point and in bold type.
   F.   Paper color used for city letterhead may be white, cream colored, or
grey.
   G.   Letterhead may be printed on laser printers if desired. Color printed
letterhead, the use of color logos, or the use of gold foil for the city seal
logo are permitted.
   H.   Names of elected or appointed officials may only appear on letterhead
that formally represents the officials. For example, the mayor's office
letterhead may include the mayor's name; planning commission letterhead may
include names of commissioners. Letterhead for operating departments may not
use personal names.
   I.   Envelopes used with city letterhead should match the color of the paper
used in the letterhead, but need not include logos. Typestyles used on the
envelope's return address area should be similar to those used on the
letterhead. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1702
ADOPTION OF EMPLOYEE POLICIES AND PROCEDURES MANUAL
SECTION:
1702-1: Purpose
1702-2: Policy
1702-3: Responsibilities
1702-4: Procedures
1702-5: Effect On Interim Personnel Policies And Procedures Handbook And Any
Other Conflicting Policies Or Procedures
1702-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to:
   A.   Effect the adoption of the employee policies and procedures manual.
   B.   Establish responsibilities and procedures for distribution of the
initial copies of the manual as well as copies of future amendments or
additions to the manual.
   C.   Establish a review process for the consideration of future amendments
to the manual. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1702-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation:
   A.   To maintain an operating employee policies and procedures manual which
will describe some of the city expectations for employees and describe and/or
set forth the city policies and programs, as well as the benefits available to
eligible employees. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1702-3: RESPONSIBILITIES:
   A.   Mayor: Approve and sign any changes or enhancements to the employee
policies and procedures manual.
   B.   Chief Administrative Officer:
      1.   Make recommendations for changes or enhancements to the employee
policies and procedure manual.
      2.   Review, for approval, recommendations from the director of
management services for changes or enhancements to the employee policies and
procedure manual.
      3.   Ensure that all other administrative policies and procedures are
consistent with the provisions of the existing handbook.
      4.   Facilitate any changes or enhancements to the employee policies and
procedure manual required by actions by the city council.
   C.   Director Of Management Services:
      1.   Review all proposed changes or enhancements to the employee policies
and procedure manual, considering its relevance, application, precedence,
legality, equity and advisability.
      2.   Coordinate review of all proposed changes, including input from
parties affected by the change or who can assist in its evaluation.
      3.   Commence the review of all existing administrative policies and
procedures and propose any necessary changes to eliminate inconsistencies or
conflicts with the provisions of the employee policies and procedure manual.
   D.   Department Directors:
      1.   Adhere to all adopted policies and procedures contained in such
manual.
      2.   Review all departmental policies and procedures and make such
changes as are necessary to eliminate any conflicts with the provisions of the
manual.
      3.   Develop such departmental procedures as are necessary to implement
the provisions of the manual.
      4.   Maintain at least one current employee policies and procedures
manual in every division, which shall be available for all employees.
      5.   Recommend changes or enhancements to any policies or procedures
contained in the employee policies and procedures manual to the director of the
department of management services.
   E.   City Recorder: Keep the original of the employee policies and
procedures manual, and any amendments thereto, stored and filed as part of the
Ogden City official record.
   F.   Employee Handbook Holder:
      1.   Ensure that the employee policies and procedures manual assigned to
the division is maintained and kept up to date as changes or additions are
distributed.
      2.   Ensure availability of the employee policies and procedures manual
to all Ogden City employees working within the division. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1702-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Distribution:
      1.   A copy of the initial employee policies and procedures manual shall
be provided to every employee, a receipt of which shall be acknowledged in
writing and made a part of the employee personnel file.
      2.   A copy of amendments to the manual shall be distributed to each
employee; provided that it shall be up to each employee to update their
individual manuals.
      3.   Each department shall receive a sufficient number of copies of the
initial manual so that a copy will be available for each division in the
department. Any amendments to the division copy of the employee policies and
procedures manual shall be provided with a list of remove and insert
directions.
   B.   Amendment: All amendments, changes or enhancements to the employee
policies and procedures manual shall first be submitted to the director of the
department of management services, who shall coordinate the appropriate review
of the proposal. The proposed change, along with the recommendations of the
director of management services shall be submitted to the chief administrative
officer. If the CAO concurs and action is required, the recommendation shall be
sent to the mayor for approval. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1702-5: EFFECT ON INTERIM PERSONNEL POLICIES AND PROCEDURES HANDBOOK AND ANY
OTHER CONFLICTING POLICIES OR PROCEDURES:
   A.   The employee policies and procedures manual adopted herein, replaces
and supersedes the provisions of the "Interim Personnel Policies And Procedures
Handbook", as of the effective date of this administrative order.
   B.   Any provision contained in any existing administrative policy or
procedure, which is in conflict with the provisions of the employee policies
and procedures manual, is hereby superseded.
   C.   The provisions of any departmental policy or procedure which are in
conflict with the provisions of the employee policies and procedures manual are
hereby superseded and repealed, as of the effective date of this manual. (Eff.
3-14-2007)
POLICY 1703
MINUTES FORMAT
SECTION:
1703-1: Purpose
1703-2: Policy
1703-3: Procedure
1703-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide uniform guidelines to all departments
regarding the format to be used for minutes of official city meetings,
including committees, commissions and boards. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1703-2: POLICY:
Title
3-2-1 of the Ogden municipal code outlines the general rules for boards,
commissions and committees, and stipulates such committees are subject to the
provisions of the Utah Open and Public Meetings Act, which law requires written
minutes to be kept of all meetings of public bodies.
It shall be the policy of Ogden City Corporation that clear, concise, accurate
and informative minutes shall be kept of all official city meetings; including
committees, commissions and boards, and that such minutes will document how
recommendations are reached, why decisions are made, why specific actions are
taken, and provide a historical record of city business.
It also shall be the policy of Ogden City Corporation that a standard minute
format shall be followed by all city staff and committee members providing
minutes of meetings to ensure uniformity and that all requirements of the Utah
Open and Public Meetings Act are being met.
Minutes are permanent public records and should be prepared on acid free paper
and kept in an official minute book or binder. Copies of approved and signed
minutes are to be provided to the city recorder for filing. (Eff. 9-25-2024)
1703-3: PROCEDURE:
   A.   A heading shall be provided at the top of each page which will indicate
the type of meeting, date of the meeting, and the minutes page number.
   B.   The beginning paragraph of the minutes shall give all the necessary
information about the type of meeting, date of the meeting, time of the
meeting, and where it was held, etc.
   C.   The roll call shall list the names of all members present, those absent
or excused, as well as city staff present.
   D.   Agenda item titles should be capitalized or underlined without the
agenda item number.
   E.   The text of the minutes should be single spaced, with paragraphs being
indented, and double spacing between each item in the order of business.
   F.   Motions should be typed in all capital letters, bolded, and made a
separate paragraph.
   G.   Margins shall be no less than 0.75 inch nor more than one inch.
   H.   The last paragraph should indicate the time the meeting adjourns
followed by a signature block for the preparer and the date of approval.
   I.   Approved minutes should be sent to the recorder's office as soon as
possible, and no later than 3 business after their approval.(Eff. 9-25-2024)
POLICY 1704
ENFORCEMENT OF PROPERTY MAINTENANCE VIOLATIONS; CIVIL PENALTIES; ADMINISTRATIVE
ABATEMENT
SECTION:
1704-1: Purpose
1704-2: Policy
1704-3: Responsibilities
1704-4: Administrative Fee
1704-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide certain administrative guidelines for
enforcement efforts under title 1, chapter 4, article B; title 12, chapter 4,
"Property Maintenance Regulations", chapter 8, "Administrative Abatement Of
Public Nuisances"; and title 16, chapter 8, "Code For The Abatement Of
Dangerous Buildings", of the Ogden municipal code. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1704-2: POLICY:
   A.   Although more than one department may have jurisdiction over a
violation, enforcement personnel shall use their best efforts to coordinate or,
if possible eliminate, multiple enforcement activities affecting an individual
parcel or lot, so as to avoid conflicting enforcement orders, confusion on the
part of the property owner, and duplication of enforcement efforts.
   B.   Primary responsibility for enforcement shall be taken in accordance
with the provisions of this policy.
   C.   Administrative abatement of public nuisances by the city pursuant to
title 12, chapter 8 and title 16, chapter 8 of the Ogden municipal code shall
generally be performed by the fleet/facility management division, through use
of division personnel and/or such number of outside contractors as is necessary
for the city to respond effectively to a property owner's failure to abate in a
timely manner.
   D.   In the event the city directly abates the nuisance, reasonable charges
for the city's administrative costs of abatement should also be collected.
(Eff. 3-14-2007)
1704-3: RESPONSIBILITIES:
   A.   Appointed Inspectors: The following officers and employees of the city
shall be appointed as inspectors under the provisions of title 12, chapters 5
and 8 of the Ogden municipal code:
      1.   The employees within the community and economic development
department who are classified as building inspectors, housing inspectors,
zoning inspectors and/or code enforcement officers, and their respective
supervisors and managers; and
      2.   Those officers and employees specifically authorized under section
12-8-2 of the Ogden municipal code.
   B.   Hearing Officers: Unless the city has contracted with a hearing officer
for the hearing of appeals under sections
1-4B-10,
12-8-5,
16-8C-1 of the Ogden municipal code, the division manager, and if needed the
department director and the deputy director, responsible for the applicable
enforcement personnel are authorized to act as hearing officers.
   C.   Primary Enforcement Responsibilities: The city's code enforcement
officers shall have primary responsibility for enforcement efforts, under the
