overall supervision of the community development manager; provided that the
building official, and the building official's authorized representatives,
shall have primary responsibility for any enforcement efforts under title 16,
chapter 8 of the Ogden municipal code.
   D.   Oversight And Supervision Of City Abatement:
      1.   Except for the oversight responsibilities of the inspector as
described in subsection D2 of this section, the fleet/facility manager, or the
manager's designee, shall be responsible for supervising division employees
involved in performing any abatement work and administering contracts with
outside parties performing abatement work.
      2.   If a question arises as to the scope of work authorized under an
abatement order, the fleet/facility manager, or the manager's designee, shall
consult with the inspector, or the inspector's supervisor or manager, for a
final determination. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1704-4: ADMINISTRATIVE FEE:
   A.   An administrative fee, in the amount of fifty dollars ($50.00), shall
be collected covering the reasonable administrative costs of enforcement
efforts.
   B.   Such administrative fee shall be in addition to the expenses incurred
or charged by the fleet/facility management division in performing the
abatement, and any civil penalties assessed against the property owner or other
responsible person. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1705
GRANT APPLICATION AND ACCEPTANCE
SECTION:
1705-1: Purpose
1705-2: Policy
1705-3: Definitions
1705-4: Procedures
1705-1: PURPOSE:
Realizing the magnitude of funding sources available to the city in the form of
grants from various sources, the purposes of this policy are to:
   A.   Ensure that all grant applications and awards are approved by the mayor
or chief administrative officer (CAO). This shall also include all applications
filed via electronic process.
   B.   Ensure that the appropriate administration departments are aware of all
grant applications of the city and the match requirements.
   C.   Ensure that the city council is notified of all grant awards greater
than fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00). Ensure that the city council approves
all grant application requiring a match greater than fifty thousand dollars
($50,000.00).
   D.   Ensure that any grant match requirements are known and the funding
sources identified prior to submission of any application.
   E.   Ensure proper accounting and tracking of awarded grants.
   F.   Establish and identify responsibilities for award compliance. (Eff. 3-
14-2007)
1705-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City to:
   A.   Investigate and pursue grants of all types (federal, state, private,
etc.) that can enhance or supplement other city revenue sources to provide
services to the citizens of Ogden.
   B.   Ensure that all performance and financial aspects are known and
understood by the administration prior to application for such grants.
   C.   Provide for proper accounting and tracking of grant activities to
comply with specific and general reporting requirements.
   D.   Maintain a schedule of active grants as required by the federal single
audit act to ensure proper auditing. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1705-3: DEFINITIONS:
GRANTEE: Applicant organization, grantee organization or agency, recipient,
occasionally subrecipient, is always Ogden City Corporation. Never a department
or agency within the city.
RECIPIENT OR GRANTEE MAILING ADDRESS: 2549 Washington Boulevard, Ogden, UT
84401
SIGNATORY: Signatory official, authorized public official, authorizing officer,
authorized recipient official, authorized representative, other like terms,
refer to the mayor. Signatures of department directors or others are never
authorized. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1705-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Grant Applications:
      1.   Department directors are responsible for identifying potential
grants that may benefit city operations and programs.
      2.   Department directors are responsible for determining if the grant
outcome justifies the time and effort to obtain, implement, and account for the
grant.
      3.   Department directors are responsible for contacting granting
authorities and obtaining grant applications and reporting requirements.
      4.   Department directors are responsible for determining grant operating
and financial requirements and for recommending approval of grants to the chief
administrative officer (CAO). This must include a review by the management
services department to ensure that financial obligations are known in advance
and that provisions for proper reporting are available.
      5.   The CAO will review all grant applications to determine if the city
is interested and can comply with the grant operating and financial guidelines.
Allow for adequate time for the CAO's review, at a minimum of three (3) days,
prior to the filing deadline. In the case of larger grants this review will
take longer and additional time will be necessary.
      6.   Where grant instructions require, the mayor will sign grant
applications. All other grant applications will be signed by the CAO or his
appointed designee.
      7.   Information on grant applications requiring a match greater than
fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00) will require approval from the city council
prior to filing the grant. Understanding that some grants may have a short
application cycle, it is understood that grant acceptance is contingent on
funding the match and grants will not be accepted without council approval of
the match.
      8.   Electronically filed applications are not exempt from the approval
process.
   B.   Grant Acceptance:
      1.   Matching funds will be allocated to the grant as appropriate, with
the city council authorizing the transfer of funds or where necessary, the
appropriation of additional funds.
      2.   All grants received will follow the same approval process as
contracts and then be approved by the mayor or CAO.
      3.   A completed "grants information report", available on the city
intranet, will be submitted to the comptroller division, regardless of grant
size, along with a complete copy of the signed award document for grants. This
will facilitate the project set up and appropriate financial tracking.
      4.   The following information, will be transmitted to the comptroller
division for appropriate financial tracking of all grant activities, regardless
of size:
         a.   Grant Information:
            (1)   Grant name.
            (2)   Grant amount.
            (3)   Source of funding, i.e., federal funds, state funds, other
(specify).
            (4)   Responsible agency.
            (5)   Contract (or other identifying) number.
         b.   Grant Requirements:
            (1)   Description of grant purpose and restrictions.
            (2)   Match requirements.
            (3)   Specifics of match requirements (including source of match
funds).
            (4)   Long term commitment of city funds.
         c.   Grant Administration:
            (1)   Provide name, position (title), division, and phone number of
staff members authorized to requisition funds.
            (2)   Provide name, position, division, and phone number of staff
members submitting or assisting in the filing of grant reports.
            (3)   Name of person submitting information requested above.
   C.   Grant Accounting, Reporting, And Compliance Requirements:
      1.   All grant accounting and financial reporting will be handled and
monitored by the comptroller division of management services department.
         a.   Auditing and reporting of all grants is a necessary part of the
annual audit of city financial records so compliance and financial records must
be maintained in the financial area. Federal single audit requirements A-133
requires the city's auditor to review all federal and state grants. Frequently
private grants request the same verification.
         b.   Grant compliance and financial information and reports may be
handled by other departments of the city, but a copy of such reports must be
provided to the comptroller division.
      2.   As a minimum, all transactions involving grant funds will follow the
same administration procedures as required in other city activities.
         a.   If grant requirements are more restrictive they will be followed,
otherwise city policies and procedures will be followed.
         b.   Auditors are required to verify that grant activity follows grant
and/or city guidelines. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1706
BANNER PROGRAM RULES AND REGULATIONS
SECTION:
1706-1: Purpose
1706-2: Policy
1706-3: Responsibilities
1706-4: Procedures
1706-5: Standards
1706-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish written standard design
specifications and application procedures for the display of noncity banners in
the 2400 block of Washington Boulevard, pursuant to the authority granted to
the mayor in section
7-2-17 of the Ogden municipal code. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1706-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of the city to allow the display of noncity banners in the
2400 block of Washington Boulevard if approved and displayed in accordance with
the conditions, procedures and requirements imposed herein. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1706-3: RESPONSIBILITIES:
The special events coordinator, under the direction of the community services
director, shall be responsible for approving the display of noncity banners in
the 2400 block of Washington Boulevard. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1706-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   All organizations making requests to display banners must submit a
written application as obtained from Ogden City special events no less than
thirty (30) days prior to the requested beginning date of display.
   B.   A fee in the amount of four hundred dollars ($400.00) shall be charged
to cover the reasonable costs of administration, maintenance and hanging.
Special requests resulting in additional costs to the city will be assessed
additional charges, as determined by the special events coordinator. Payment of
the fee must accompany the application. If additional charges are assessed, no
banners will be displayed until such additional charges are paid by the
applicant. Checks should be made payable to Ogden City. If the applicant is
denied, three hundred fifty dollars ($350.00) of the fee shall be returned to
the applicant.
   C.   The application shall include a written description of the banner
(verbiage, colors, etc.) and include a sketch or picture of the proposed banner
display. The applicant must agree to hold the city, its officers, employees and
agents harmless from or against any and all loss, theft or damage that may
occur in the keeping, hanging, display, or removal of the banners.
   D.   Requested display dates will not be reserved until the written
application has been submitted and approved and the payment of all fees has
been received.
   E.   No application shall be approved unless it meets the requirements of
section
7-2-17, title 18, "Outdoor Signage", of the Ogden municipal code, and the
requirements of this order.
   F.   Upon approval of the application, the applicant will provide eight (8)
complete banner sets, meeting the required design standards, to the city for
hanging. No banners will be hung by the applicant. All banners will be
designed, ordered and paid for by the requesting party. In no event shall Ogden
City pay for the cost of such banners.
   G.   Banners will be displayed no more than ten (10) days prior to an event
and will be taken down upon the event's conclusion.
   H.   Banners must be delivered to Ogden City special events no less than
seven (7) days prior to the date to be displayed.
   I.   Banners must be picked up at Ogden City special events no later than
five (5) working days following the display period. Banners left longer will be
discarded.
   J.   Qualifying applications shall be approved on a first come, first served
basis. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1706-5: STANDARDS:
   A.   Banners must meet the following design standards:
      1.   Complete sets consisting of one for the street side and one for the
sidewalk side of each pole.
      2.   Printed on both front and back.
      3.   Have a finished size of twenty nine and three-fourths inches by
ninety two inches (293/4" x 92").
      4.   Have a two and one-half inch (21/2") casing on both top and bottom.
      5.   Have metal grommets on both top and bottom on the pole side of the
banner.
      6.   The banner shall be constructed of a weather resistant material,
such as vinyl, nylon or treated canvas.
   B.   The banner display shall meet all requirements of section
7-2-17 of the Ogden municipal code, including the following:
      1.   The purpose of the banners must meet one of the following purposes
allowed by city ordinance:
         a.   Promoting special occasions, such as charitable, civic or festive
events.
         b.   Promoting the celebration of some event of national, state or
civic significance.
         c.   Honoring a visit from meritorious individuals.
         d.   Promotion of a community oriented event.
      2.   The banners may not incorporate in any manner any political
advertising or advertising of a commercial nature. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1707
INTERNAL CONTROL POLICY
SECTION:
1707-1: Purpose
1707-2: Policy
1707-3: Procedures
1707-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to set forth the policy and procedures regarding
Ogden City's framework for internal control. (Eff. 8-26-2008)
1707-2: POLICY:
Ogden City's internal control is a process affected by the city council, city
administration, and city employees that is designed to provide reasonable
assurance regarding the achievement of objectives in the following categories:
   A.   Effectiveness and efficiency of operations;
   B.   Reliability of financial reporting; and
   C.   Compliance with applicable laws and regulations.
The internal control framework at the city is based on the report of the
committee of sponsoring organizations (COSO) of the Treadway commission
integrated framework. COSO is a voluntary private sector organization dedicated
to improving the quality of financial reporting through ethics, effective
internal controls, and proper governance.
The COSO integrated framework of internal control consists of five (5)
interrelated components as follows:
   A.   Control environment;
   B.   Risk assessment;
   C.   Control activities;
   D.   Information and communication; and
   E.   Monitoring. (Eff. 8-26-2008)
1707-3: PROCEDURES:
The comptroller shall implement all financial related controls and control
systems and shall maintain internal control documentation that is reviewed and
updated annually. (Eff. 8-26-2008)
POLICY 1708
MAYOR'S ADMINISTRATIVE REVIEW MEETING (MARM); RULES AND PROCEDURES
SECTION:
1708-1: Purpose
1708-2: Policy
1708-3: Applicability
1708-4: Procedures
1708-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish the day, time and place where the
mayor will regularly conduct administrative reviews or hearings; and to
establish the rules and procedures for the scheduling, preparation, noticing
and conduct of such reviews and hearings. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1708-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation that administrative reviews or
hearings to be conducted by the mayor shall be heard on a regular basis, at a
fixed day, time and place, in order to:
   A.   Provide efficient and timely review of administrative matters; and
   B.   Ensure that administrative reviews or hearings be conducted in a manner
meeting the requirements of due process. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1708-3: APPLICABILITY:
   A.   The administrative reviews or hearings to be heard during the mayor's
administrative review meeting shall include, but not be limited to, the
following:
      1.   Appeals of administrative decisions where a right of appeal to the
mayor is authorized or required by ordinance. (Example: Landmarks commission
decision regarding certificates of historic appropriateness.)
      2.   Waivers of ordinance provisions where the mayor is vested with such
authority by ordinance. (Example: Variances or exceptions to the requirements
of the subdivision ordinance of Ogden City; waiver of sign ordinance
requirements applicable to historic resources.)
      3.   Site plan reviews where approval of the mayor is required under the
zoning ordinance of Ogden City.
      4.   Review of preliminary and final plans for subdivisions, or
dedication plats.
      5.   Reviews of the mayor under the sensitive area overlay zone
ordinance.
      6.   Subdivision plat amendments and vacations.
      7.   Permits, certificates or licenses requiring mayoral approval.
(Example: Encroachment permits.)
      8.   Temporary exceptions from the zoning ordinance.
      9.   Sales or other conveyance of real property of the city where a
public hearing is required.
      10.   Orders to show cause regarding the abatement of dangerous buildings
through city performance of demolition.
      11.   Other administrative reviews of the mayor which:
         a.   Under ordinance or other provisions of law, require notice and/or
hearing prior to mayoral action (Example: Administrative order approving a
developer payback agreement); or
         b.   May be considered at such time merely on the basis of
convenience. (Example: Administrative orders adopting traffic rules and
regulations; execution of deeds.)
   B.   Scheduling matters as part of the MARM process is intended to be a
convenience to all parties. Consideration of any of the above matters outside
of the MARM process shall not be prohibited, if approved by the mayor. (Eff. 3-
14-2007)
1708-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Mayor's Administrative Review Meeting (MARM); Scheduling: The mayor's
administrative review meeting (MARM) shall be held in the ninth floor
conference room, municipal building, unless another location is directed by the
mayor. The regular MARM shall be held on the Friday following the monthly
regular meeting of the planning commission, although other Fridays may be
scheduled as needed if approved by the mayor's office. In the event of a Friday
holiday or unavailability of the mayor, the regular MARM will be held on Monday
of the following week, at two o'clock (2:00) P.M., unless otherwise directed by
the mayor's office. In the event a regularly scheduled MARM is canceled, the
agenda for that MARM will be continued until the next regularly scheduled MARM,
unless a special MARM is scheduled by the mayor's office. Administrative staff
having matters on the agenda will be available from nine thirty o'clock (9:30)
to ten o'clock (10:00) A.M., prior to MARM to brief the mayor on any matters
appearing on the agenda.
   B.   Minutes: Minutes of the meeting shall be kept by the city recorder's
office.
   C.   Agenda Process:
      1.   Planning Staff Submission Of Items: On the Monday morning prior to
the regularly scheduled planning commission meeting, the planning division
secretary will provide city recorder staff with a listing of all items on the
planning commission agenda subject to final approval of the mayor, which are
temporarily scheduled for the MARM on the following Friday.
      2.   Distribution Of Proposed Agenda: On the Tuesday prior to the next
MARM, city recorder staff will e-mail the proposed agenda to the people listed
below, requesting any additions, deletions, or changes be provided by eleven
o'clock (11:00) A.M. that day:
   Community and economic development director
   Planning manager
   Building official
   Business development director
   Neighborhood development manager
   Public services director
   City engineer
   Traffic engineer
   Assigned legal counsel
   Mayor's executive assistant
      3.   Changes Or Additions: The above listed individuals will provide any
changes or additions to the city recorder staff by twelve o'clock (12:00) noon.
Any changes or additions to the agenda received after twelve o'clock (12:00)
noon on Tuesday must be approved by the mayor.
      4.   Final Agenda Preparation: The agenda will be prepared on the Tuesday
immediately preceding the MARM and will include all pending administrative
matters ready for review, including all matters appearing on the planning
commission agenda for the Wednesday immediately preceding the MARM which are
scheduled for such MARM as indicated in such planning commission meeting. If
persons attending the planning commission meeting are not informed that the
matter will be heard at MARM on the following Friday, the matter will be
scheduled for the next regularly scheduled MARM and the city recorder shall
provide written notice to the petitioner/applicant or other individuals
involved with the matter.
      5.   Submission Of Material To City Recorder: Reports of city staff and
recommendations of any city body previously hearing the matter will be
submitted to the city recorder by twelve o'clock (12:00) noon on Tuesday;
provided that action items from matters scheduled before the planning
commission on the intervening Wednesday shall be submitted by noon on Thursday.
      6.   Distribution: The city recorder will make copies of the agenda and
all agenda backup information and collate the information into agenda packets
for distribution to the following officers:
   Mayor
   Assigned legal counsel
   Community and economic development director
   Planning manager
   Public services director
   Traffic engineer
   City engineer
After the agenda is prepared, city recorder staff will publicly post a copy of
the agenda as a courtesy to the public.
   D.   Procedure:
      1.   Order Of Business: The order of business shall first consider
approval of the minutes from the last MARM and then shall list the items for
consideration in the suggested order of review. The mayor reserves the right to
alter the order of business.
      2.   Review Process: The review of any item of business shall proceed in
the following order:
         a.   Mayor introduces item.
         b.   Presentation of city staff.
         c.   Petitioner/applicant/appellant presentation.
         d.   Any opponents and/or proponents may comment.
         e.   Mayor asks questions.
         f.   Mayor makes a decision.
   E.   Notice:
      1.   Reasonable notice stating time, place and subject matter shall be
given to the parties involved, prior to any hearing. No hearing, or the result
thereof, shall be invalidated by any defect in giving notice to the parties
involved, unless a denial of due process is caused thereby. Unless another
notice requirement is imposed by law or ordinance, reasonable notice may be
made by mailing notice first class, postage prepaid, five (5) days prior to the
applicable MARM.
      2.   In matters involving prior planning commission review, notice of the
time, date and place of the mayor's administrative review meeting will be
announced in Ogden City planning commission notices and/or at the planning
commission meeting.
      3.   Special notice requirements imposed by ordinance shall supersede the
notice requirements imposed herein.
      4.   The city recorder shall not place an item on the agenda unless and
until noticing requirements are met.
      5.   To the extent possible, public hearings on amended plats to be held
by the mayor shall be noticed in advance of the planning commission meeting so
that the matter can be heard on the Friday immediately following the planning
commission meeting. If notice is provided by the planning division, copies of
such notices shall be provided to the city recorder.
   F.   Witnesses: At the request of any party, witnesses will be sworn by the
mayor. At the request and expense of any party, a hearing may be recorded by a
certified shorthand reporter.
   G.   Decisions: The mayor will enter a written order or decision. Approved
written minutes may be considered to be a written order or decision unless an
administrative order, notice, or other formal document is required by law or
ordinance. The city recorder shall forward a copy of any written order or
decision pertaining to a land use decision to the planning manager. Preliminary
subdivision approvals shall also be forwarded to the city engineer. The
planning manager shall be responsible to provide a copy of the written decision
to the applicant. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1709
ELECTRONIC PUBLIC MEETING SECURITY
SECTION:
1709-1: Purpose
1709-2: Policy
1709-3: Responsibility
1709-4: Procedure
1709-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide uniform guidelines to city departments
and divisions regarding electronic public meeting security. (Eff. 8-27-2020)
1709-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City to operate electronic public meetings in a
secure environment while complying with the Utah Open and Public Meetings Act.
(Eff. 8-27-2020)
1709-3: RESPONSIBILITY:
The I.T. Division shall provide training and support to departments and
divisions in establishing electronic public meetings to mitigate the
possibility of individuals joining the meeting and engaging in disruptive
activity.
Disruptive activity includes but is not limited to conduct that substantially
prevents another person from hearing, viewing or meaningfully participating in
the meeting; sharing content of a sexual nature; sharing content that promotes,
fosters, or perpetuates discrimination; using profanity, shouting or otherwise
disrupting the carrying on of the business of the meeting. (Eff. 8-27-2020)
1709-4: PROCEDURE:
The following procedures are general best practices; specific guidance may vary
depending on meeting type.
   A.   Operate electronic public meetings via Zoom, or a comparable platform
with advanced security features.
   B.   Establish settings such that only the meeting host or authorized
participants can share their screen.
   C.   Establish settings such that file transfers are disabled or limited to
prevent sharing of inappropriate or virus-ridden files with other participants.
   D.   Remove participants who are engaging in disruptive activity and
establish settings such that removed participants cannot rejoin the meeting.
   E.   Disable unused meeting features such as Chat or Q/A to prevent misuse.
   F.   Require participants to sign in with a password, when appropriate.
   G.   Use the waiting room feature or webinar feature to allow attendees to
join the meeting as attendees to prevent misuse.
   H.   Establish a co-host for all electronic public meetings, assigned
exclusively to meeting security and administration.
   I.   Check recording settings prior to a meeting to ensure effective
recording by City users and prevent unauthorized recordings by non-City users.
   J.   Use Zoom Webinar, or comparable platform, for electronic public
meetings and events where it is appropriate for attendees to be view only with
camera and microphone disabled.
   K.   Boards and committees should otherwise adopt rules governing electronic
public meetings as required by Utah Code Ann. § 52-4-207. (Eff. 8-27-2020)
POLICY 1710
CITY COUNCIL AND REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY AGENDA
SECTION:
1710-1: Purpose
1710-2: Policy
1710-3: Definitions
1710-4: Procedures
1710-1: PURPOSE:
The purposes of this policy are to:
   A.   Set guidelines and responsibilities for departments pertaining to city
council agenda and/or information items.
   B.   Outline the format and deadlines for these items. (Eff. 5-1-2013)
1710-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of the administration to inform all departments of the city
council agenda and/or information items format. Electronic submittal of all
agenda items is strongly encouraged. (Eff. 5-1-2013)
1710-3: DEFINITIONS:
CITY COUNCIL AGENDA ITEM: An item which requires specific attention and
discussion at a city council meeting. The agenda item is submitted to the chief
administrative officer for review and then discussed at the weekly agenda
meeting. The format and procedures for the item and submittal process is
discussed in detail in this policy.
WEEKLY INFORMATION ITEM: An item that is advantageous to communicate to the
city council but does not require city council action. Weekly informational
items may also include monthly reports by departments, responses to council
inquiries, reports on project progress, etc. These items are submitted to the
chief administrative officer for review and then placed on the weekly
informational item sheet to be sent to the city council. (Eff. 5-1-2013)
1710-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Agenda Items: All departments with agenda items for city council
meeting must comply with the developed format and contain the following
information:
      1.   Title: Ogden City council agenda item.
      2.   Department: Name of the department submitting item.
      3.   Topic: Brief statement of the subject.
      4.   Date: Date of submittal.
      5.   Background: A brief explanation of the origin of the issue, an
analysis of the current situation, alternatives which were considered and
reasons why this recommendation is preferred. Also indicate any existing city
policy or precedence, if applicable.
      6.   Recommendations: Brief paragraph stating departmental
recommendations. Also include financial requirement and source of funding, if
applicable.
      7.   Contact Person: The departmental representative responsible for
item. His or her telephone number should be included.
   B.   Informational Items: All departments with informational items shall
follow the following format and deliver to the chief administrative officer
upon completion:
      1.   Title: Ogden City council weekly information item.
      2.   Date: Date of submittal.
      3.   Department: Name of the department submitting item.
      4.   Topic: Brief statement of the subject.
      5.   Body: Explanation of weekly information item.
      6.   Contact Person: The department representative responsible for item.
His or her telephone number should be included.
   C.   Agenda Meeting:
      1.   All department agenda item reports, except reports from the planning
commission, are to be approved by the chief administrative officer prior to
being delivered to the city council officer for agenda scheduling. Planning
commission reports are to be delivered concurrently to the city council office
and the chief administrative officer as soon as practicable following
commission's actions.
      2.   Ordinances and resolutions will be approved by the legal department
prior to presentation to the chief administrative officer. The legal department
will transmit electronically a conformed copy of the approved ordinance or
resolution to the requestor and to the chief administrative officer. The legal
department will also deliver the initialed, original hard copy of the ordinance
or resolution to the recorder's office. The department director will then
transmit electronically the approved, conformed ordinance or resolution, along
with a transmittal and other supporting documentation, in one package to the
chief administrative officer via electronic mail. Additionally, the department
director will provide three (3) hard copies of the entire packet to the chief
administrative officer during the weekly CAO coordination meeting.
      3.   Chief administrative officer (CAO) coordination meetings are held
weekly on Friday at nine o'clock (9:00) A.M., unless otherwise rescheduled and
will consist of the chief administrative officer, the city recorder and a
representative of the involved departments. City council and/or redevelopment
agency agenda items must be delivered to the chief administrative officer via
electronic mail and in hard copy form before the CAO coordination meeting.
Complex matters and major policy issues should be discussed with the mayor and
chief administrative officer well in advance of the CAO coordination meeting.
      4.   The agenda preparation meeting will be held each Tuesday at eight
thirty o'clock (8:30) A.M. All items which are in need of attention at city
council meeting will be discussed in the agenda preparation meeting. Each item
must be accompanied by a memorandum stating the date desired for city council
consideration and an explanation of the date requested is needed.
      5.   The chief administrative officer will deliver agenda items via
electronic mail and hard copy to the city council executive director. The
executive director may ask a department representative for additional
information to make the item more understandable to the city council.
Department representatives are to provide the executive director with timely
responses to questions and give the appropriate consideration to suggestions
regarding agenda reports.
      6.   The council staff transfers the agenda items to the city recorder's
office via electronic mail on or before Friday.
      7.   The city recorder's office prepares the agenda packets and has them
delivered electronically to the city council staff Friday afternoon.
      8.   Proposals requiring city council action within a known time frame
(i.e., to meet a legal or financial requirement) are to be prepared on a
schedule that permits sufficient time for review by the city council. For
example, if an ordinance needs to be adopted by a defined date, under normal
circumstances, it will not be acceptable to present it at the last scheduled
city council meeting prior to the required adoption date. Scheduling of such
items is to be coordinated with the chief administrative officer and the city
council executive director well in advance of the required action date. (Eff.
5-1-2013)
POLICY 1712
GOVERNMENT ACCESS CHANNEL 17; OPERATIONAL POLICIES AND PROCEDURES
SECTION:
1712-1: Purpose
1712-2: Mission And Objectives Of Channel 17
1712-3: Channel Programming
1712-4: Emergency Response
1712-5: Community Calendar
1712-6: Appeals
1712-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of these operational policies and procedures is to define the
function of the Ogden City governmental cable access channel 17 (channel 17),
provide direction to city staff, and assist the public in understanding the
services offered by channel 17. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1712-2: MISSION AND OBJECTIVES OF CHANNEL 17:
   A.   Channel 17 is designated as a government access channel, as provided
for in the 1994 cable act.
   B.   The mission and objectives of channel 17 are as follows:
      1.   To provide city government information to citizens of the community.
      2.   To inform the public of the activities of the administrative and
legislative branches of city government.
      3.   To disseminate public information regarding the functions and
services performed by the various departments and divisions of city government.
      4.   To notify the public of city sponsored events, activities, and
programs.
      5.   To provide a forum for Ogden City to educate citizens regarding
matters of public concern in the community.
      6.   To notify citizens of events, activities and programs of other
governmental and educational entities. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1712-3: CHANNEL PROGRAMMING:
   A.   Programming Responsibility:
      1.   Ogden City reserves the right to program channel 17 in accordance
with the mission and objectives identified above.
      2.   Programming content and quality is determined at the sole discretion
of the city, and approved by the city television coordinator.
      3.   Ogden City shall follow all FCC guidelines for government access
television.
      4.   Departments are responsible for providing information about city
issues and activities in ready to broadcast form to the city television
coordinator.
      5.   Department directors or their designees must submit information for
broadcast on channel 17 to the city television coordinator. Department
directors or their designees are responsible for approving the content of all
programming provided by their department.
      6.   Requests for test announcements must be received one week in advance
of the desired air date, except in the event of exigent circumstances.
      7.   To accommodate broadcast announcement schedules, requests for video
programming must be received one month in advance of the desired air or
recording date.
      8.   Channel 17 is not a public forum for the purposes of the exercise of
free speech. It is exclusively a medium for broadcasting city programming. No
citizen shall have the right to use this medium for any purpose or
communication.
      9.   Should incorrect information be broadcast over channel 17, Ogden
City Corporation, its officers, employees, agents shall be indemnified and held
harmless to the full extent permitted under the Utah governmental immunity act.
   B.   Programming Categories: All programming on channel 17 shall fall within
one or more of the following categories:
      1.   Governmental Decision Making: Programming which provides direct
coverage of the deliberations of elected or appointed bodies, as well as
coverage of selected public issues forums. Examples of programming in this
category include: city council meetings, election coverage, board and
commission meetings, public use forums.
      2.   Community Information/Affairs: Programming that provides information
about city government and/or issues of local interest in Ogden. This may
include city produced magazine shows such as "Ogden Today", interviews of city
officials, calendar of community events, and special programs on issues
important to the community such as crime prevention, environmental issues,
public safety, neighborhood information, etc.
      3.   Cooperative Community Programming: Programming produced or provided
in cooperation with other governmental organizations that contain useful
information or that celebrates the achievements and accomplishments of Ogden
citizens. Examples include: school events/information, performing arts,
recreation activities, and ceremonies.
      4.   General Interest/Transitional Programming: Programming content of a
general entertainment or informational nature, intended to maintain viewer
interest.
   C.   Prohibited Programming: The following types of programming shall be
prohibited on channel 17:
      1.   Programming which does not comply with the mission and objectives of
channel 17 or fall within the approved programming categories described herein.
      2.   Programming that violates FCC guidelines for government access
television, including: commercial/for-profit making enterprises, trade or
business announcements, obscene, indecent, libelous or slanderous speech, or
other illegal content.
      3.   Programming which exceeds specific limitations on political content
set forth in these policies and procedures.
      4.   Programming for the purpose of fundraising for a nongovernmental
entity.
      5.   The city reserves the right to refuse to transmit all or any portion
of a program which promotes any activity which is illegal under city, state or
federal law or in violation of these policies and procedures.
   D.   Programming Guidelines: All programming on channel 17 must be approved
by the city television coordinator. The Ogden City chief administrative officer
(CAO), or his delegate, shall serve as the city television coordinator.
      1.   All programming on channel 17 must support the channel's mission and
objectives and fall within one of the channel's designated programming
categories.
      2.   All programming on channel 17 must be of local interest and provide
community benefit.
      3.   The city may choose to broadcast externally prepared programs if
they meet city policy and quality requirements and are not in violation of
copyright law. Public requests for broadcast of such information must be made
to the city television coordinator.
      4.   The city television coordinator shall establish allocation of
programming time among the designated categories.
      5.   City council meetings and other public meetings broadcast live or by
tape delay, shall be shown, up to the extent possible, gavel to gavel, without
editing or interruption. However, recesses and delays in such proceedings may
be excerpted from broadcast. Introductory or supplementary information, which
will aid the viewer in understanding the context or issues, may be provided.
      6.   Videotaped coverage of meetings shall not be considered an official
record of said meetings, and there shall be no liability by the city or its
employees for inadvertent erasure or omissions, technical difficulties, or for
inaccurate information stated during an aired event.
      7.   Any city department may cosponsor a programming proposal from the
community with the approval of the city television coordinator.
      8.   The city may cooperate with other media, municipalities and agencies
to acquire additional programming, which meets the mission and objectives of
channel 17.
      9.   All programming produced for channel 17 shall be copyrighted and may
only be reproduced for personal, noncommercial home use by individuals.
Retransmission or any unauthorized use of channel 17 programming (in part or
whole) is strictly forbidden without the written consent of the city television
coordinator.
      10.   Channel 17 has no duty to record channel 17 broadcasts. However,
any recording of channel 17 programming that exists may be subject to access as
provided by the Utah government records access and management act and retention
schedules as established by the city recorder's office. Appropriate fees may be
charged as provided by city ordinance.
   E.   Limitations On Political Content:
      1.   Use of channel 17 by individuals seeking public office or reelection
is prohibited unless participating in city sanctioned public issue forums or
debates. Persons who have filed for candidacy in any local, state, or federal
election will not be eligible to appear on channel 17 prior to such election
unless they appear in a forum in which opposing candidates are given equal
time. This exclusion does not apply to persons who receive incidental airtime
as part of a public meeting or elected officials acting in an official capacity
as part of regular duties.
      2.   Use of channel 17 to disseminate information about any ballot
proposition or election of any candidate in any local, state, or federal
election, caucus, political convention or primary, shall be prohibited except
as provided herein. Either the administration or city council may broadcast a
brief statement about its position on a ballot proposition and the reason for
that position. More detailed factual information about a ballot proposition may
be broadcast to the public, so long as the information grants equal access to
both the opponents and proponents of the ballot proposition. Nothing in this
provision shall limit a city official from exercising his/her free speech
rights related to any political issue in any city council meeting, hearing or
other official city proceeding, although such proceedings may be broadcast on
channel 17.
      3.   The administration or city council may choose to sponsor public
issue/candidate forums or debates where members of city government and/or the
community are invited to discuss contrary viewpoints on issues of concern to
the city and its citizens. Public issue forums or debates carried on channel 17
must relate to the channel's mission and objectives and offer a balanced
perspective on the issues.
   F.   Advertising And Underwriting:
      1.   Commercial advertising on channel 17 is prohibited. At no time will
the city's government channel endorse specific brand names of products for
consumer use.
      2.   Underwriting or in-kind contributions must be approved prior to
solicitation or receipt by the city television coordinator and/or the mayor.
      3.   Contributors may be acknowledged in the program opening/closing
credits or during the body of an underwritten program. The only identifying
information allowed in a credit for underwriting or in-kind support is a
listing of the underwriters/contributor's name and/or logo, phone number and/or
website. At the city's discretion, the credit may use full or partial screen or
program video as background, with or without voice over. The following is an
example of appropriate credit text:
This program was made possible (in part) with funds provided by [name and/or
logo and/or phone number and/or website].
      4.   Editorial and related decisions regarding underwritten programming
will be made by the city television coordinator. The underwriter shall have no
editorial control over broadcast content. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1712-4: EMERGENCY RESPONSE:
Channel 17 may be used at any time for the purpose of emergency communication
and response. In these cases, direction will be taken from the procedures
outlined in the Ogden City emergency operations plan. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1712-5: COMMUNITY CALENDAR:
   A.   The community calendar is designed to provide a source of timely
information about a variety of community activities displayed by the channel 17
character generator system. In addition to including information about city
events and services, the community calendar may also include information about
noncity sponsored events and services that are consistent with the mission and
objectives of channel 17.
   B.   The community calendar consists of textual information to be displayed
throughout the cablecast area on channel 17, twenty four (24) hours a day,
seven (7) days a week, except at those times when other programming has been
scheduled by the city television coordinator, or the channel is experiencing
technical difficulties.
   C.   A request form must be used when submitting messages for display on
channel 17. The form can be obtained from the city television coordinator. The
city television coordinator will make every effort to include appropriate
messages on the community calendar, but inclusion is not guaranteed.
   D.   Community calendar notices are subject to the following guidelines:
      1.   No information shall be transmitted which involves any advertising
to promote the sale of commercial products, activities or services, advertising
on behalf of candidates for public office or political issues, lottery
information, fundraising or obscene or indecent matter.
      2.   If a nonprofit agency's primary service is referral of business to
profit agencies, it shall be excluded from use of the community calendar.
      3.   Event messages must include whether they are free or if there is an
admission fee charged. An information telephone number should be included.
      4.   All information displayed must be consistent with the mission and
objectives of channel 17.
   E.   Should an error result in the cablecast of incorrect information,
neither Ogden City nor the employee responsible shall be liable for the
inaccuracy of the information or the actions taken by anyone as a result of the
inaccurate information.
   F.   The city reserves the right to refuse to transmit all or any portion of
a message which promotes any activities which are illegal under city, state or
federal law or in violation of these policies and procedures. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1712-6: APPEALS:
Any appeal of programming decisions shall be made by filing a written notice of
appeal with the Ogden City recorder. All appeals shall be determined by the
Ogden City mayor or his delegate. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1720
CITIZENS' COMPLAINTS
SECTION:
1720-1: Purpose
1720-2: Policy
1720-3: Procedures
1720-1: PURPOSE:
The purposes of this policy are to:
   A.   Provide accurate and timely response to all citizens' complaints.
   B.   Set guidelines for employees receiving complaints from citizens in our
community. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1720-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to hear and respond to all
complaints by the citizens of Ogden City and to treat them in a timely,
courteous and professional manner. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1720-3: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Because complaints can originate from all areas and to any employee of
Ogden City, an employee receiving a complaint should be courteous and helpful
in dealing with the dissatisfaction of the constituent.
   B.   Employees who receive complaints should try to assist, within their
capabilities, to resolve the complaint immediately or as soon as possible.
   C.   Resolved or unresolved complaints should be reported by the employee to
their supervisor as soon as possible, no later than the end of the day.
Supervisors receiving a complaint should try and resolve the problem or notify
the division manager to resolve the complaint.
   D.   The complaint should be recorded in Better Place with as much
information necessary for the appropriate division in the city to resolve the
issue, respond to and satisfying the citizen.
   E.   Unresolved complaints will be sent to the appropriate department or the
chief administrative officer office for further recommendation and resolution.
   F.   All involved individuals should be notified of the final resolutions.
If resolution cannot be achieved quickly the complainant should be advised and
given periodic updates on progress. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1721
SPECIAL EVENT SPONSORSHIPS
SECTION:
1721-1: Purpose
1721-2: Applicability And Exceptions
1721-3: Definitions
1721-4: Authority
1721-5: Policy
1721-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish clear and consistent guidelines for
special event sponsorships. The city is frequently asked to waive fees or
provide in-kind services for events held at the Union Station, amphitheater,
parks, and other locations within the city. Sponsorship plays a key role in
meeting the city's mission to provide safety, education and lifelong learning,
stable neighborhoods, a vibrant economy, strong infrastructure, healthy
lifestyles, and meaningful connections. This policy provides a process for
community organizations to request city resources and ensures that sponsorship
decisions are made transparently and impartially. Sponsorship approvals will be
guided by this policy to promote the efficient use of taxpayer resources,
ensuring that event organizers contribute to the cost of services and work
toward self-sufficiency. (Eff. 7-15-2025)
1721-2: APPLICABILITY AND EXCEPTIONS:
This policy applies to all private, non-governmental entities, including
nonprofit and for-profit organizations. It does not apply to public entities,
such as political subdivisions, governmental agencies, school districts, or
public institutions of higher education. Any assistance to public entities may
be extended at the discretion of city administration as mutual aid but falls
outside of the scope of this sponsorship policy.
The following are exempt from the requirements of this policy:
   A.   Special events explicitly listed as line items in the current city
budget.
   B.   Services provided by one city department in support of another city
department during a city-organized special event. (Eff. 7-15-2025)
1721-3: DEFINITIONS:
As used in this policy:
"City organized special event" means an event:
   A.   planned and executed exclusively by city staff; or
   B.   executed in partnership with a third-party organization under a written
agreement with the city.
"City sponsored event" a special event that has successfully completed the
city's sponsorship application process and received formal approval from the
CAO or CAO's designee.
"Fee waiver" means the reduction or elimination of standard city fees for
permits, facility rentals, or other charges.
"In-kind services" means non-monetary contributions provided by the city, such
as labor, materials, or use of city-owned equipment.
"Special event" means any organized activity involving the use of, or having an
impact on, public property which is not within the routine and ordinary use of
the property or which, by nature of the activity, may have a greater impact on
city services or resources, neighborhoods, businesses, or the community as a
whole than would have occurred had the activity not taken place, including,
parades, gatherings, arts and crafts shows, fairs, festivals, and athletic
events. The Special Event Coordinator shall determine whether an activity is
considered a special event. (Eff. 7-15-2025)
1721-4: AUTHORITY:
Sponsorships are approved by the CAO or CAO's designee. (Eff. 7-15-2025)
1721-5: POLICY:
   A.   Limitations:
      1.   Sponsorships are limited to fee waivers and in-kind contributions;
cash donations are not permitted.
      2.   Special event business license fees cannot be waived.
      3.   City sponsored events must occur within twelve months of being
approved.
      4.   Submission of a special event sponsorship application does not
guarantee approval. The city retains full discretion to approve or deny
applications based on the priorities outlined in this policy and the
availability of resources.
      5.   Sponsorships approved in one fiscal year for events occurring in a
different fiscal year are contingent upon budgetary appropriations.
      6.   Applicants must comply with all applicable rules, regulations, laws,
and ordinances.
   B.   Evaluation Criteria: Preference will be given to sponsorship
applications that:
      1.   Include a detailed plan for the city sponsored event to become self-
sufficient without city sponsorship in future years;
      2.   Acknowledge the city's support in a meaningful and visible way,
providing public recognition that reflects the value of the city's
contribution;
      3.   Minimize impacts to city staff and public roads, facilities, and
services;
      4.   Create benefits to the local business community;
      5.   Demonstrate a reasonable correlation between the number of attendees
and the cost of city support;
      6.   Are not duplicative of other special events held in the city within
the same calendar year;
      7.   Involve collaboration among multiple community groups;
      8.   Are open to the public;
      9.   Request no more than $3,500 or 50% of total costs, whichever is
less, including:
         a.   In-kind services;
         b.   Fee waivers;
         c.   Any other grants awarded by the city; and
         d.   Any additional costs incurred by the city;
      10.   Are not primarily focused on political or religious purposes;
      11.   Are proposed by individuals or organizations with a demonstrated
record of fulfilling obligations from previous special event or reservation
agreements;
      12.   Do not tax city resources beyond what is reasonably available; and
      13.   Have not received city sponsorship two or more times previously.
   C.   Procedures:
      1.   Sponsorship requests must be submitted in writing using the
designated application form.
      2.   Applications must be submitted at least 90 days prior to the
proposed city sponsored event. Requests submitted less than 90 days in advance
will not be considered.
      3.   Applicants must provide the following financial information:
         a.   For returning applicants: financial expense statements from the
prior year's event, if any, and a proposed budget for the current year's
proposed city sponsored event.
         b.   For first-time applicants: the proposed budget for the current
year's proposed city sponsored event.
      4.   The Special Event Coordinator will forward applications to relevant
departments to evaluate eligibility and estimate fees. The application, along
with department feedback, will then be reviewed by the CAO or the CAO's
designee for action. After the review process, applicants will be notified of
the decision to approve, deny, or partially approve the application.
      5.   Scheduling and use of city facilities are subject to the
availability of the requested facilities and city staff. City sponsored events
do not take priority over city programs, activities, or previous commitments to
third parties. (Eff. 7-15-2025)
POLICY 1725
MEDIA RELATIONS POLICY
SECTION:
1725-1: Purpose
1725-2: Policy
1725-3: Responsibilities
1725-4: Official Releases Of Information
1725-5: Responding To Editorial Information
1725-6: The Government Records And Management Act (GRAMA)
1725-7: Emergency Management Plan
1725-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish guidelines for the release of
information to the media by Ogden City employees. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1725-2: POLICY:
   A.   All information that is a matter of public record will be made
available to the media through proper channels and at appropriate times.
Information which is not a matter of public record and, for legal purposes, is
not normally released, will not be released without the authorization of the
mayor, chief administrative officer, the appropriate department director and/or
the city attorney.
   B.   Employees should always offer facts to the media and refrain from
offering conclusions, assumptions, or opinion except as provided in this
policy.
   C.   The provisions of this policy do not apply to the routine release of
promotional information for city events or programs. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1725-3: RESPONSIBILITIES:
All city employees can expect to be contacted by the media regarding
information about Ogden City. Responsibility for responding to such inquiries
is as follows:
   A.   Mayor And Chief Administrative Officer:
      1.   These positions are expected to respond to media inquiries with
appropriate information and other points of contact.
      2.   In cases where sensitive information (as defined below) is requested
for release, the mayor or the chief administrative officer should determine the
process for the release and should identify the appropriate spokesperson for
the city.
   B.   Department Directors:
      1.   Directors are expected to respond to media inquiries with
appropriate information and/or other points of contact.
      2.   Directors are expected to contact the mayor, the chief
administrative officer, the city attorney or the management services director,
prior to releasing information when possible, in regard to potentially
controversial or sensitive matters, particularly if media attention is expected
or has already occurred. Such incidents include, but are not limited to:
         a.   Controversial statements, accusations or debates occurring in
meetings of advisory boards or commissions.
         b.   Disruptions in city services.
         c.   Personnel matters such as suspensions, terminations and
resignations of employees and possible employee strikes, walkouts or other job
actions.
         d.   Accidents or other incidents resulting in the injury or death of
a city employee.
         e.   Accidents or other incidents that involve city employees or
property that results in the injury or death of a citizen.
      3.   Directors are expected to advise the mayor or the chief
administrative officer of any contact with the media, except in the case of
routine, job related media contacts by the police and fire departments.
      4.   Directors should establish guidelines within their departments
regarding employee contact with the media. These guidelines should include
designated spokespersons for the department, how employees report media
contacts and how this information is reported to other departments.
   C.   City Attorney: The city attorney or his/her designee is the only
employee authorized to release information concerning litigation filed or court
decisions rendered regarding the city.
   D.   Employees:
      1.   Employees are expected to respond to the media only as set out in
this policy and their departmental policies.
      2.   In the absence of a department policy, employees will refer media
inquiries to their department director. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1725-4: OFFICIAL RELEASES OF INFORMATION:
   A.   News Releases:
      1.   The mayor's office will handle most routine news releases for city
departments, excluding the police and fire departments in most cases. Any time
a news release is to be issued, it should be forwarded to the mayor's office
for review and release.
      2.   News releases will follow the format established and from time to
time modified by the mayor's office staff.
   B.   News Conferences:
      1.   News conferences will be arranged by the mayor's office for all
departments excluding police and fire in most cases.
      2.   The mayor's office will be responsible for setting a location,
notifying the media, making sure appropriate personnel are in attendance and
prepared to answer questions, and that handling follow up requests by the media
are met. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1725-5: RESPONDING TO EDITORIAL INFORMATION:
   A.   Letters To The Editor: Employees wishing to write a letter to the
editor that is not in response to another letter to the editor or an editorial,
and that is directly related to the employee's position with the city should
submit the letter for review to his or her department director, who will review
it with the mayor's office prior to the letter being submitted to the
newspaper.
   B.   Guest Editorials: From time to time, employees may be asked by a
newspaper editorial staff to write a guest editorial on a particular topic
related to their position with the city. Before accepting that request, the
employee should consult with his or her department director, and the director
should obtain approval from the mayor's office before the employee accepts the
invitation. The guest editorial must be reviewed by the mayor or chief
administrative officer before it is submitted for publication.
   C.   Responding To Letters To The Editor: When a letter to the editor is
published in the newspaper to which a director feels a need to respond, the
response must be reviewed and approved by the mayor or the chief administrative
officer prior to sending it to the newspaper.
   D.   Responding To Newspaper Editorials Or Editorial Cartoons: When a
director feels that the city needs to respond to a newspaper editorial or
editorial cartoon, the response should be in the form of a "guest editorial"
and must be reviewed and approved by the mayor or the chief administrative
officer prior to sending it to the newspaper. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1725-6: THE GOVERNMENT RECORDS AND MANAGEMENT ACT (GRAMA):
It is the policy of the city to comply with legitimate requests for information
filed under the Utah government records and management act. GRAMA requests are
covered in policies 1800 through 1870 in this manual. For additional guidance
on GRAMA requests, please contact the city recorder's office. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1725-7: EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT PLAN:
The release of information during an emergency or a disaster is addressed in
the city's emergency management plan. The emergency management plan takes
precedence over this policy during an emergency or a disaster. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1730
SECURITY CARD, KEY, AND FUEL KEY ACCESS POLICIES AND PROCEDURES
SECTION:
1730-1: Purpose
1730-2: Definitions And Descriptions
1730-3: Cardkey, Key And Fuel Key Issuance; Eligibility
1730-4: Written Request Required
1730-5: Process For Obtaining Security Cardkeys And Fuel Keys For Full Time And
Authorized Part Time Employees
1730-6: Process For Obtaining Security Access Cardkeys And Fuel Keys For
Temporary Or Seasonal Employees And Volunteers
1730-7: Cardkey Rules And Procedures
1730-8: Responsibility Of Employees, Temporary Employees, Volunteers,
Contractors, Lessees Or Outside Agencies Issued Security Items
1730-9: Lost Or Damaged Cardkeys, Keys And Fuel Keys
1730-10: Misuse Of Cardkeys, Keys And Fuel Keys
1730-11: Retrieval Of Security Items
1730-12: High Security Areas
1730-13: Periodic Updates And Verification
1730-1: PURPOSE:
Ogden City has installed a sophisticated security system to control and monitor
access to city buildings and fuel islands as part of the overall effort to
secure and protect all city assets. The primary responsibility for monitoring
and controlling such access has been assigned to the fleet and facilities
division of the management services department. The information technology
division provides technical support for the security computer system.
This document sets forth Ogden City policies and procedures for issuing and
retrieving security cards and keys used for accessing Ogden City buildings, and
fuel keys used to fuel at Ogden City fuel pumps. (Eff. 3-13-2015)
1730-2: DEFINITIONS AND DESCRIPTIONS:
CARDKEY: A personalized photo identification card issued to a specific user for
the purpose of entering Ogden City buildings.
FUEL KEY: The fuel master fueling system keys that are required to access fuel
at Ogden City fuel islands. (This system requires 2 keys to operate. 1 key is
assigned to a specific vehicle and another key is assigned to a specific
individual. This allows the city to monitor not only the amount of fuel a
particular vehicle is using, but also when a particular individual uses the
pumps.)
GUEST CARDKEY: A nonpersonalized card issued to a division manager for use by
guests, temporary or seasonal employees, or volunteers.
KEY: A normal key used for unlocking doors, gates, etc.
PIN NUMBER: The numbers, unique to each individual user, used in conjunction
with a cardkey or to disarm the security alarm system after entering a
facility.
SECURITY ACCESS ITEMS OR SECURITY ITEMS: Any combination and number of
cardkeys, keys and fuel keys issued to an individual or division. (Eff. 3-13-
2015)
1730-3: CARDKEY, KEY AND FUEL KEY ISSUANCE; ELIGIBILITY:
   A.   Full Time And Authorized Part Time Employees: Full time and authorized
part time employees may be issued building access cards and/or keys for those
areas to which they need access as determined by their assigned duties. Fuel
keys will be issued to full time and authorized part time employees whose job
requirements involve the fueling of city vehicles and equipment.
   B.   Temporary Or Seasonal Employees And Volunteers: Temporary/seasonal
employees from outside agencies or volunteer groups will not be issued access
cardkeys, keys or fueling keys by fleet and facilities. Division managers may
request, in writing, guest cardkeys, keys and/or fuel keys for use by temporary
employees to provide the fueling and building access requirements necessary for
those workers to perform their assigned duties. Procedures for obtaining
cardkeys for temporary or seasonal employees and volunteers are set forth in
section
1730-6 of this policy.
   C.   Authorized Contractors, Lessees Or Outside Agencies:
      1.   Contractors providing services for Ogden City may be issued a
cardkey or guest cardkey and/or keys when: a) the contractor will be providing
ongoing services at times other than regular business hours (e.g., janitorial
services), or b) the contractor's responsibilities to the city includes
responding on an emergency basis to complete repairs (e.g., electrical
services, HVAC services). The division manager managing the contractor shall
determine whether a cardkey or guest cardkey will best meet the needs of the
city and contractor. The division manager shall also identify the doors for
which the contractor will need keys. Background checks may be required before
final authorization is made.
      2.   Lessees who lease space at the Mt. Ogden communications site may be
issued cardkeys, guest cardkeys, and pin numbers to allow access to their
equipment without being accompanied by an Ogden City employee.
      3.   Outside agencies contracting with Ogden City for the purchase of
fuel shall be issued fuel keys as requested by an authorized agent of the
agency. (Eff. 3-13-2015)
1730-4: WRITTEN REQUEST REQUIRED:
Division managers must authorize, in writing, the fueling and building access
requirements for all employees within their division. Access shall be limited
to that necessary for employees to perform their assigned duties. In cases
where an employee requires access to areas that are controlled by more than one
division, the written approval of each division manager must be provided.
Security access is subject to review and override by department heads, the CAO,
and the mayor.
An authorized agent for lessees with leased premises at Mt. Ogden communication
site or Ogden Intermodal Hub shall submit written request for cardkeys or keys
as needed to meet their needs. Background checks may be required before final
authorization is made. (Eff. 3-13-2015)
1730-5: PROCESS FOR OBTAINING SECURITY CARDKEYS AND FUEL KEYS FOR FULL TIME AND
AUTHORIZED PART TIME EMPLOYEES:
   A.   Complete And Forward Written Request: Authorization and request for
building access cardkeys, keys and/or fueling keys shall be completed and
forwarded, via fax, interoffice mail, or e-mail, to the fleet and facilities
office to Ogden fleet and facilities. A security access authorization/request
form, located on the department share "Y" drive under security access, shall be
completed with the employee's full name, Ogden City employee number, the
department by which they are employed and the specific building areas to which
they will be granted access. Any special requirements, such as after hours
accessibility or admittance to sensitive areas must be documented in this
request. (See section
1730-12, "High Security Areas", of this policy.) Fueling keys for those
employees who are required to fuel vehicles or equipment may be requested on
the same form.
   B.   Obtain Employee Photo (For Cardkeys): The employee may report to human
resources or the fleet and facilities division for photo. Photos are processed
on a schedule to be determined by the fleet and facilities division and human
resources.
   C.   Identify PIN Number: Employee may be asked to identify a six (6) digit
PIN that will be required for after hours access to the buildings.
   D.   Pick Up Security Items After Forty Eight Hours: An authorized fleet and
facilities or IT employee will review and enter all information into the system
and create the access cardkey to allow employee into all authorized areas.
   E.   Test Access Items And Report: Employees shall test the security item(s)
as soon as possible and communicate to fleet and facilities whether the item(s)
are working properly.
Employees shall be responsible for protecting all security items. Sharing items
with other employees, family members or others is strictly prohibited and may
be grounds for disciplinary action. (Eff. 3-13-2015)
1730-6: PROCESS FOR OBTAINING SECURITY ACCESS CARDKEYS AND FUEL KEYS FOR
TEMPORARY OR SEASONAL EMPLOYEES AND VOLUNTEERS:
   A.   Complete And Forward Written Request: Authorization and request for
building access guest cardkeys and/or fueling keys shall be completed and
forwarded, via fax, interoffice mail, or e-mail, to the fleet and facilities
office to Ogden fleet and facilities. The security access authorization/request
form, located on the department share "Y" drive under security access shall be
completed. Requests for guest cardkeys and keys above the amount of keys at the
reception desk will require approval of the management services director.
   B.   Issue Cardkey(s) And Fuel Keys On An As Needed Basis: The division
managers or their assigned representative shall be responsible for issuing and
retrieving temporary access cardkeys, keys, and fuel keys and shall maintain
records relating to cardkey, key, and fuel key issuance. Before issuing any
cardkey, key, or fuel key to a temporary employee or volunteer, the following
information shall be obtained and recorded:
      1.   Photocopy of picture identification.
      2.   Current address.
      3.   Current phone number.
      4.   Date of issuance.
This information shall be kept in addition to any other information required by
personnel or risk management as part of the normal hiring process.
   C.   Retrieve Cardkeys, Keys, And Fuel Keys At End Of Employment: All
cardkeys, keys and fuel keys issued on a temporary basis shall be retrieved
prior to the temporary or seasonal employee leaving employment with Ogden City.
(Eff. 3-13-2015)
1730-7: CARDKEY RULES AND PROCEDURES:
As a vital part of our security system, an Ogden City cardkey will be issued to
employees, visitors, contractors and temporary staff. Employees should not
allow access to any individual to any area of Ogden City that requires a
cardkey. Likewise, employees must request any visitor who does not have a
visible cardkey to report to the information desk.
   A.   Ogden City Employees: An Ogden City cardkey with the employee's name,
photo and department will be issued on the first day of employment. The cardkey
is also the electronic key to enter the building and other secured areas as
needed. Every employee is required to have their city issued cardkey in their
possession during working hours while in Ogden City facilities.
Employees are not permitted access to the interior of Ogden City facilities and
other working areas during their off duty hours without prior approval by their
division manager or department director.
Lost or stolen cardkeys should be reported to fleet and facilities or human
resources as soon as possible. A fee of twenty five dollars ($25.00) will be
assessed for all replacement cardkeys after the first replacement. Failure to
possess a cardkey or excessive loss or damage to cardkeys can lead to
disciplinary action.
Upon termination, employees may be asked to return cardkeys to their supervisor
or human resources as part of the exit interview. The supervisor or human
resources will immediately report to fleet and facilities terminated employees
so that the cardkey can be deactivated. Failure to return the cardkey when
requested may result in a charge pursuant to section
1730-11 of this policy.
   B.   Contractors And Temporary Staff: Contractors and temporary staff with
multiple day assignments may be issued a cardkey consistent with section
1730-3 of this policy.
   C.   Visitors: Visitors who have business in the municipal building should
check in at the information desk located on the second floor. Except for
appointments with staff on the second floor, the information desk attendant
will contact the Ogden City employee and verify the appointment and properly
document the visitor's name and the city employee with whom the visitor has
business.
The visitor will then be given a visitor cardkey (identified by a red pouch and
lanyard) which will allow them access to the specific floor they are visiting.
The visitor cardkey must be worn visibly on a lanyard around the neck at all
times. It is the responsibility of the employee with whom the visitor meets to
ensure that the visitor cardkey is properly returned to the information desk
before the end of the day. In the event of a multiple day visit, the division
manager may request that the visitor be allowed to keep the visitor cardkey
overnight. Again, at the conclusion of the visit, it is the employee's
responsibility to ensure the visitor cardkey is returned. Visitor cardkeys not
returned at the end of the day must be reported by the information desk
attendant to the fleet and facilities division prior to the end of the day to
ensure they are deactivated.
   D.   After Hours Access To Ogden City Facilities: Based on business needs,
certain employees will be given access to Ogden City buildings after normal
working hours. Employees will only access the building for legitimate business
purposes.
   E.   After Hours Meetings: Employees who use the municipal building for
meetings that occur outside of normal business hours are responsible for the
attendees of that meeting. The employee will be required to let attendees in
the building and then will be required to ensure they exit the building at the
end of the meeting.
   F.   Additional Security Information: An employee may provide human
resources with additional information that may affect security and/or access to
the building, such as the existence of restraining or protective orders against
a third party. Such information will only be provided to the information desk
attendant for the purpose of preventing the third party access to the
employee's workspace. (Eff. 3-13-2015)
1730-8: RESPONSIBILITY OF EMPLOYEES, TEMPORARY EMPLOYEES, VOLUNTEERS,
CONTRACTORS, LESSEES OR OUTSIDE AGENCIES ISSUED SECURITY ITEMS:
Any individual or agency issued any Ogden City security system item shall:
   A.   Make all reasonable efforts to keep the item(s) in a secure location;
   B.   Use item(s) only for approved purposes;
   C.   Not share with or loan the item(s) to nonauthorized personnel;
   D.   Report lost or missing item(s) immediately. (Eff. 3-13-2015)
1730-9: LOST OR DAMAGED CARDKEYS, KEYS AND FUEL KEYS:
   A.   Cardkeys, keys, or fueling keys shall not be left unsecured. Loss of a
cardkey, key, or fueling key must be reported immediately. Repeated loss or
misplacement of these items may result in loss of privileges or disciplinary
action.
   B.   All instances of cardkey, key or fuel key loss will be noted in the
employee, contractor, lessee's, or outside agency's file.
   C.   The cost to replace a lost or stolen cardkey, key or fuel key is twenty
five dollars ($25.00), which shall be paid by the employee, contractor, lessee,
or outside agency to whom the security item was issued.
   D.   Damaged cardkeys, keys, or fuel keys will be replaced at no charge if
the damage was unavoidable or due to normal wear and tear. If the damage to the
cardkey, key or fuel key was caused by the negligence of the city employee,
contractor, lessee or outside agency employee, the city employee, contractor,
lessee or outside agency employee may be required to pay the twenty five dollar
($25.00) replacement fee. (Eff. 3-13-2015)
1730-10: MISUSE OF CARDKEYS, KEYS AND FUEL KEYS:
   A.   Security items shall be used for authorized purposes only. Misuse of
these items may result in loss of privilege, disciplinary action or
termination. Criminal prosecution may also be warranted.
   B.   Security items shall not be shared with coworkers or others. Failure to
abide by these terms may result in loss of privilege, disciplinary action or
termination.
   C.   Fuel keys shall not be used to fuel vehicles for other than that which
they are assigned. Failure to abide by these terms may result in loss of
privilege, disciplinary action or termination. (Eff. 3-13-2015)
1730-11: RETRIEVAL OF SECURITY ITEMS:
   A.   Full Time And Authorized Part Time Employees: When an employee leaves
Ogden City employment, it is the responsibility of the division manager to
collect all security cardkeys, keys, fuel keys and other Ogden City property in
the possession of the employee. (A copy of the original and any subsequent
security access authorization/request forms identifying the security items in
the possession of the employee may be obtained from the fleet and facilities
division.)
All security items shall be turned in to the fleet and facilities office with a
security release form, located on the department share "Y" drive under security
access, for deactivation. A fee of twenty five dollars ($25.00) may be assessed
the division of the employee for each security item not retrieved. Failure to
complete the form and return all security items may result in a fee to the
employee of the division. The city shall have the right to withhold up to two
hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) from the employee's final pay to cover any
items not retrieved from the employee.
   B.   Temporary Or Seasonal Employees And Volunteers: Upon termination of
employment, the security item(s) shall be retrieved and the retrieval date
recorded. Items may be retained by the division manager for issuance to future
temporary or seasonal employees or volunteers. Items should be kept in a
secured area until issued again.
   C.   Contractors, Lessees, Or Outside Agencies: Division managers
responsible for managing the contract or lease shall be responsible for
collecting all security items from contractors, lessees, or outside agencies.
Guest cardkeys may be retained for future use. Individual cardkeys should be
