OVERTIME: Any time worked during a defined work period for which an overtime
rate of pay is due, at one and one-half (11/2) times the regular rate of pay.
PYRAMIDING: Calculating overtime on hours where the employee is already
receiving premium pay. "Pyramiding" will not be allowed at Ogden City. (This
does not apply to any "holiday pay" provisions as outlined in this policy.)
STANDBY TIME: Time when an employee leaves contact information, but activities
are not restricted.
SUBSTITUTING: When an employee works for another employee but the hours worked
are credited to the scheduled employee not the substitute employee. This
practice is not allowed at Ogden City.
TRADING (Fire Protection And Law Enforcement Personnel Only): Trading time
(shifts) has no effect on the total compensable hours if it is voluntary among
the employees. It must be preapproved by the supervisor and the trade benefits
the employee.
TRAVEL TIME: Reasonable travel time for call back duty, emergency response,
traveling between work sites or traveling out of town on business during
working hours.
VOLUNTEER: An individual working for the city without receiving compensation,
other than ordinary expenses. Any volunteer work performed for the city by an
employee of the city, must be unrelated to the paid work the employee performs
for the city.
WORK PERIOD: A workweek or work period has been identified for all groups of
employees in Ogden City. For all employees, each work week or period stands
alone in computing hours worked. Averaging hours worked over two (2) or more
periods will not be done. (Eff. 12-24-2020)
1790-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Overtime Compensation:
      1.   All covered city employees who are required or requested to work
overtime hours will receive overtime pay or compensatory time at the rate of
one and one-half (11/2) times the amount of overtime worked.
      2.   Overtime compensation will be calculated on actual hours worked.
Holiday, sick leave, vacation, short term military leave, etc., will not be
used in determining overtime pay. If the holiday is worked then the hours will
count toward the actual hours worked for the week. If it is not worked then the
employee will not receive eight (8) hours' credit toward the actual hours
worked in any given week.
      3.   Call back time for police officers will be paid according to the
following schedule:
         a.   Call back duty on an on duty day: A two (2) hour minimum will be
paid; additional time will be paid on actual hours worked. All hours worked
over forty (40) in the seven (7) day work period will be paid at 1.5 times.
         b.   Call back duty on an off duty day: A two (2) hour minimum will be
paid. Hours worked over two (2) will be paid on an "actual time worked" basis.
Only one 2-hour minimum per day will be allowed.
      4.   On call duty for Ogden City employees in divisions such as water,
parks, animal services, fleet and facilities, and public works operations is
required in case of emergencies. (See also on call duty policy in the employee
policies and procedures manual. On call duty for information technology
division employees is separately addressed in the employee policies and
procedures manual.)
         a.   This duty is in addition to a normal forty (40) hour workweek.
         b.   Ogden City will pay a minimum of sixteen (16) hours at 1.5 times
to an employee designated "on call" even if no emergency occurs and the
employee is not called back unless separately addressed under a department
policy or the employee policies and procedures manual and approved by the Human
Resources Manager.
         c.   Employees who are serving on call for a period of less than one
week will have the minimum rate prorated.
         d.   An employee who is called out for actual duty will not receive
additional compensation unless the minimum sixteen (16) hours are exceeded. Any
hours worked beyond the minimum will be paid at the overtime rate of 1.5 times
on an "actual time worked" basis.
         e.   Time taken off for holidays, vacation, sick leave, etc., will not
affect the current policy regarding on call pay unless the employee is
unavailable for a full week. In this case, prorating as outlined in subsection
A5c of this section will take place.
      5.   Overtime will be paid on the next paycheck following the completion
of the two (2) week period.
      6.   A firefighter's work period, consisting of ninety six (96) shift
hours every twelve (12) day work period, requires that overtime compensation at
a rate of time and one half begins when hours worked exceed ninety one (91)
hours within this twelve (12) day work period per FLSA regulations.
      7.   If a firefighter works an extra shift, it will be at 1.5 pay unless
sick or vacation time has been taken that workweek.
      8.   When a holiday (other than a personal preference day) occurs within
a workweek when public services crews are required to perform snow removal,
water utility, or other emergency operations outside of regular working hours,
the holiday hours will be considered to be hours worked for purposes of
performing overtime calculations. (See also snow removal administrative
policy).
   B.   Approval Of Overtime:
      1.   Overtime worked must be approved in writing by the department
director or designee prior to being worked. The department director is
responsible for appropriate and accurate recordkeeping of all overtime and
compensatory time earned.
      2.   Failure to have overtime approved will not prevent the city from
compensating the employee for time worked; however, disciplinary action may be
taken for working unauthorized hours.
   C.   Payment Of Accrued Compensatory Time:
      1.   Use of compensatory time should not create a situation where
overtime of other personnel is necessary to maintain minimum manning levels or
maintain operations without department director approval.
      2.   Compensatory time will be earned, accrued and paid according to the
policies contained in the employee handbook.
   D.   Holiday Pay:
      1.   Eligible employees receive eleven (11) paid holidays per year and
one personal preference day. In addition, when Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve
fall on a Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday, city offices will close at
one o’clock (1:00) P.M.
      2.   Holiday pay will be calculated based on the employee's straight time
pay rate (as of the day of the holiday) for eight (8) hours unless the employee
has already worked forty (40) hours in the week or if the holiday falls on the
employee's regular day off. Police and fire officers will be governed by
departmental policy regarding holidays.
      3.   A recognized holiday that falls on Saturday will be observed the
preceding Friday; holidays falling on Sunday will be observed the following
Monday.
      4.   If the actual holiday falls on a weekend, but the official holiday
is observed on a weekday, an employee who works the weekend as part of a normal
schedule will not receive additional holiday pay.
      5.   If an employee does not work on a holiday, these hours do not count
toward the forty (40) hour week for overtime purposes; however, the employee
will receive eight (8) hours of "straight time" pay for the holiday or 1.5 rate
if it is the employee's regular day off and they are unable to take another day
off in the work week or the forty (40) hour workweek requirement has already
been met.
      6.   When an employee (other than sworn fire personnel working two
thousand nine hundred twelve (2,912) annual hours) is required to work on a
paid holiday, compensation will be time and one-half (1/2) for hours worked and
eight (8) hours for the holiday, which equates to double time and one-half (1/
2).
   E.   Work Periods: A variety of workweeks exist at Ogden City due to the
need for twenty four (24) hour, seven (7) day a week, emergency and public
safety coverage. Departments/divisions are responsible to maintain operating
schedules for their respective areas with approval of the Human Resources
Manager.
      1.   When an employee works a shift that spans two (2) working days,
holiday overtime pay will be calculated and reported on the day that the shift
begins.
      2.   If an employee is called back to work at night, twelve o'clock (12:
00) midnight will be the cutoff time for recording hours worked. (Eff. 12-24-
2020)
POLICY 1791
SNOW REMOVAL
SECTION:
1791-1: Purpose
1791-2: Policy
1791-3: Responsibility
1791-4: Procedures
1791-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to establish procedures for handling the
accumulation of snow on Ogden City streets. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1791-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City to provide public access to city roads as soon
as possible during and following winter snow storms. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1791-3: RESPONSIBILITY:
   A.   Operations division employees, including personnel assigned to
operations from other city departments for snow removal, will be responsible as
follows:
      1.   Responsible for snow removal from city streets. Each employee so
assigned will make every reasonable effort to be available for snow removal or
have made prior notification to his/her supervisor of nonavailability.
      2.   Should "clock in" within forty five (45) minutes of being called.
      3.   Ensure that the snow removal equipment he/she uses is in a safe and
operational condition prior to operation and upon completion of use.
Discrepancies will be reported to the supervisor.
   B.   Supervisors will be responsible as follows:
      1.   Ensure that all employees are trained in the safe and efficient use
of equipment which he/she will operate.
      2.   Tailor the snow removal effort to the condition of the particular
snowstorm; allocating resources as required.
   C.   Operations division manager will be responsible as follows:
      1.   Assume overall responsibility for the safe and efficient execution
of this policy.
   D.   Public works director will be responsible as follows:
      1.   Oversight responsibility for this policy.
   E.   Police department will be responsible as follows:
      1.   Provide notification to the operations division for snow removal
(when conditions warrant) from ten o'clock (10:00) P.M. Friday to seven o'clock
(7:00) A.M. Saturday and from ten o'clock (10:00) P.M. Saturday to seven
o'clock (7:00) A.M. Sunday. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1791-4: PROCEDURES:
   A.   The operations division manager or his designated representative will
initiate snow removal procedures. During off duty hours the operations manager
will receive condition reports from the night crew, the police department and/
or operations division supervisors.
   B.   The operations division has the ability and responsibility of
monitoring snow conditions except during the periods of ten o'clock (10:00)
P.M. to seven o'clock (7:00) A.M. Friday and Saturday nights. The operations
night crew does not work those nights and the police department dispatch is
responsible during those periods to make notification for snow removal. A
current notification list will be provided to the Ogden City dispatch center by
October 1 of each year.
   C.   The salt/sanding crew is normally called out first to deal with slick
hills, major intersections, school crossing, dangerous curves, and other high
priority areas. The plow crew is not normally called out until at least four
inches (4") of snow has accumulated. In addition to the above priorities, major
arterial and collector streets will be plowed first. Other residential streets
may not be plowed until the next normal duty day.
   D.   Snow crews may not exceed fifteen (15) hours of duty time before
receiving eight (8) hours off duty (waivable by the chief administrative
officer or his designated representative). To accommodate this requirement the
public works director may authorize release of snow crews to their home until
called in. Crews sent home during a normal duty day will be considered on duty
for pay purposes.
   E.   When a holiday (other than a holiday taken as a personal preference
day) occurs within a workweek when crews are required to perform snow removal
operations outside of regular working hours, the holiday hours will be
considered to be hours worked for purposes of performing overtime calculations.
(Eff. 3-14-2007)

MAYOR'S DESIGNEES FOR BUSINESS LICENSE HEARINGS AND APPROVALS
SECTION:

   B.   Appoint a designee for the purpose of approving local consent forms,
and approving business licenses requiring approval of the mayor under title 5

It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to:
   A.   Appoint hearing officers for purposes of calling, presiding at, and
conducting hearings to consider the suspension, revocation, denial or approval

   B.   Management Services Director:

         b.   Business licenses requiring the approval of the mayor under title

      2.   The management services director shall provide monthly reports of

   C.   Appeals Related To Assessment Of License Fees And Late Penalties:
Unless the city has contracted with a hearing officer for the hearing of
appeals related to assessment of license fees and late penalties pursuant to
section
5-1A-18 of the Ogden municipal code, the management services director is
designated as the hearing officer responsible for hearing such appeals. If
necessary, the director may delegate such functions to the division manager
responsible for business licensing functions. (Eff. 5-4-2009)
POLICY 1793
WEB PAGE DEPARTMENT AND DIVISION MAINTENANCE
SECTION:
1793-1: Purpose
1793-2: Policy
1793-3: Procedure
1793-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide uniform guidelines to all city
departments and divisions regarding updating and maintaining the Ogden City web
pages (internet and intranet). (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1793-2: POLICY:
To ensure the city web pages provides clear, consistent, timely and accurate
information and serves the needs of citizens by being well organized, user
friendly and updated regularly. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1793-3: PROCEDURE:
   A.   Each department or division that provides information for web pages is
responsible to keep their section up to date at all times.
   B.   Each department or division will assign an employee (web page editor)
to be responsible for ensuring timely, updated and current information update
their department or division web page section.
   C.   Department directors and division managers are responsible for periodic
review and approve all web page information in their respective departments
before forwarding to the web page editor. All web page information is
coordinated through the department or divisional web page editor, who will be
authorized to make changes to the content of the web page information in their
respective areas using the city's approved web content management system only.
   D.   The web page editor is responsible to coordinate the submission and
updates of all web page information to the city webmaster for final approval.
The webmaster will be available to assist web editors on an as needed basis.
   E.   Design or content standards, major additions, changes to the structure
or design will first be reviewed and approved by the web page "steering
committee" and then forwarded to the webmaster and the information technology
division for implementation.
   F.   The web page "steering committee" shall consist of one web editor from
each city department, the city webmaster, and member of the IT division staff
at or above the level of project manager. The city CAO, management services
director and CTO may choose to participate as members of the web page "steering
committee". (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1794
RATE GUIDELINES FOR CITY SERVICES FOR SPECIAL EVENTS
SECTION:
1794-1: Purpose
1794-2: Policy
1794-3: City Services Rate Guidelines
1794-1: PURPOSE:
   A.   Private entities plan and produce numerous public events that take
place on public property throughout Ogden.
   B.   These events frequently require special allocation of traffic control,
police, fire, or other city services.
   C.   Ogden Municipal Code Section 6-5-5 requires an applicant for a special
event to reimburse the city for all charges applicable for any services agreed
to be provided by the city in support of the special event.
   D.   Consistent with Ogden Municipal Code Section 6-5-5, the purpose of this
policy is to establish standardized rates for city services, which rates may
not exceed the reasonable costs of providing such services. (Eff. 4-24-2024)
1794-2: POLICY:
   A.   It is the policy of Ogden City to charge standardized rates to cover
the city's reasonable costs of providing city services for special events.
   B.   Pursuant to Ogden Municipal Code Section
6-5-2, reimbursement is not required for any city event directly organized and
operated by the city. Reimbursement for city services required for special
events operated by a third party under an agreement with the city shall be
governed by the terms of the agreement.
   C.   The special events coordinator shall review such rates annually and
recommend revision or updating as needed. (Eff. 4-24-2024)
1794-3: CITY SERVICES RATE GUIDELINES:
   A.   In an effort to support special events and to cover the city's
reasonable costs of providing services to such events, the following rates are
established for services not otherwise included in the fee schedule set forth
in Ogden Municipal Code Title 4, Chapter 6:
 
Police                            $85 per officer per hour (2 hour minimum)
EMT/Paramedic                     $66.49 per EMT/Paramedic per hour
Staffed ambulance                 $135 per hour
Staffed fire engine               $135 per hour
Parks/Operations personnel        $50 per employee per hour (2 hour minimum)
Electrical hookup/set up services $35 (4 hour maximum)
Extra trash cans                  $15 per can (includes delivery, pick up and
                                  tip fee)
 
   B.   Upon application for a special event permit, the special events
coordinator shall consult with other departments to determine whether city
services are available and what charges are applicable. If applicable, the
special events coordinator shall indicate the rate on the special event permit
application form and provide the appropriate notification to the applicant.
   C.   A waiver of the above rates may apply for certain events pursuant to
Ogden Municipal Code Section 6-5-20.
   D.   This policy shall be implemented consistent with applicable city
ordinances and policies and Utah and federal law. (Eff. 4-24-2024)
POLICY 1795
DELEGATION OF MAYORAL POWERS TO THE CAO WITH RESPECT TO CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS
SECTION:
1795-1: Purpose
1795-2: Policy
1795-3: Procedures
1795-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to delegate and authorize the chief
administrative officer (CAO) to exercise, in the mayor's absence, the statutory
rights and responsibilities of the office of the mayor to attend council
meetings, take part in council meeting discussions, and freely give advice to
the council. (Eff. 6-11-2009)
1795-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of the city that the statutory rights and responsibilities of
the office of the mayor to attend council meetings, take part in council
meeting discussions, and freely give advice to the council pursuant to Utah
Code Annotated section 10-3b-202(1)(d)(vii)(2009), shall not be abandoned,
prohibited or diminished by the mayor's absence at council meetings. Rather, it
is the policy of the city that such rights and responsibilities be delegated to
the CAO, to be exercised in the mayor's absence and on his behalf. (Eff. 6-11-
2009)
1795-3: PROCEDURES:
   A.   In the case of the mayor's absence at all or part of any city council
meeting, the CAO is delegated and authorized to act and speak on behalf of the
mayor in the same manner and to the same extent in which the mayor could act,
speak, or otherwise participate in such meeting.
   B.   The rights and responsibilities delegated to the CAO by this policy
shall include all statutory rights and responsibilities of the office of the
mayor to attend council meetings, take part in council meeting discussions, and
freely give advice to the council pursuant to Utah Code Annotated section 10-
3b-202(1)(d)(vii)(2009), as amended. (Eff. 6-11-2009)
POLICY 1796
GUIDELINES FOR SIDEWALK VENDOR LOCATION ASSIGNMENT
SECTION:
1796-1: Purpose
1796-2: Policy
1796-3: Procedures
1796-1: PURPOSE:
Ogden municipal code subsection 5-13B-6B requires the city to assign a specific
location for each licensed sidewalk vendor cart from among approved vendor
locations. Pursuant to this subsection, the mayor is required to adopt rules
necessary for the administration of such location assignment process. (Eff. 1-
14-2010)
1796-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City to adopt a fair and efficient process for
assigning vendor locations from among approved locations. (Eff. 1-14-2010)
1796-3: PROCEDURES:
   A.   Sidewalk Vendor License Application: Applications for vendor licenses
shall be hand delivered to the Ogden City business license division on or
before the first business day in January. Applications shall contain a minimum
of the following: the name and mailing address of the applicant; a description
of the products to be sold; a description of the cart to be used in conducting
business, including scaled drawings or a photograph and proposed colors,
including signage to be used; the number of carts proposed to be operated.
Individuals desiring to operate more than one cart shall submit a separate
application for each cart. Payment of license fees is not required until after
the selection meeting is held. Applications will be marked with the time and
date received. Applications will be accepted on a first come, first serve basis
until a number of applications equivalent to the total number of approved food
and general vendor locations has been submitted. Additional applications will
be marked with the time and date received and shall be placed on a vendor
waiting list.
   B.   Location Selection Meeting: Initial vendor location assignments shall
be for a three (3) year time period (through December 31, 2012). The director
of management services shall hold a selection meeting to determine vendor
location assignments no later than January 15, 2013, and every three (3) years
thereafter to determine vendor location assignments. The management services
director may hold interim meetings, as necessary.
   C.   Notice Of Selection Meeting: Other than the initial vendor location
assignments, all individuals submitting applications by January 1 before the
selection meeting shall be provided with advance written notice of the
selection meeting, mailed to the address provided in the application. The
applicant, or a person designated by the applicant, shall attend the selection
meeting. Vendors shall be given an opportunity to mutually agree to locations
from among approved locations for a three (3) year time period. In the event an
agreement cannot be reached among those applicants participating in the
selection meeting, the director of management services may conduct a lottery or
solicit bids to determine vendor location assignments.
   D.   Lottery Process (Optional): Each applicant shall be given the
opportunity to draw a number, beginning with the number one, and ending with
the total number of locations then designated by the city council as approved
sidewalk vendor locations. An individual with more than one application shall
be permitted to draw a second number after all applicants have drawn an initial
number. The applicant who draws the lowest number shall be assigned to the
location of his or her choice from among the approved locations for a three (3)
year time period. The applicant who draws the second lowest number will be
assigned to the location of his or her choice out of the remaining locations.
This process will continue down the list until all applicants have an assigned
location.
   E.   Bid Process (Optional): The management services director shall accept
sealed bids from applicants for each desired location from among the approved
locations. The minimum starting bid for any location shall be the amount of the
sidewalk vendor business license. The management services director shall assign
each desired location to the applicant with the highest bid for that location
for a three (3) year time period. In the event there is only one applicant
bidding for a particular location, the selected applicant shall be deemed to
have bid the amount of the sidewalk vendor business license, regardless of the
amount of the sealed bid. Funds received from the bidding process shall be
placed in the general fund.
   F.   Records: The business license division shall maintain appropriate
records to document the vendor assignment process.
   G.   Issuance Of Business License: Initial vendor operators shall on or
before sixty (60) days from the date of city council approval of the vendor
ordinance provide the business license division with all required documentation
and approvals, including a bathroom agreement, as required by the Weber Morgan
health department, and shall pay all Ogden City business license fees, any
outstanding civil penalties, and the required damage deposit. Any remaining
damage deposit may be carried over for the following license year. An applicant
shall not conduct business prior to obtaining a license. In the event an
applicant is unable to meet all requirements within the sixty (60) day time
period, applicant's selected location shall be forfeited, and the applicant may
be reassigned to an open location, if available. Subsequent to the initial
vendor assignments, the sixty (60) day time period shall run from the date of
the location assignment.
   H.   Availability Of Top Five Locations: In the event any of the top five
(5) selected locations come available, the management services director may
choose to hold an interim selection meeting, or if the prior selection was made
by lottery or bid, he or she may contact the applicant who drew the next lowest
number (or the next highest bidder), to determine whether that individual
desires to change locations, continuing down the list until the space is
filled.
   I.   Waiting List: The business license division may assign an available
location (other than the top 5 locations) to an applicant on the waiting list.
All license conditions must be met by the applicant before a business license
may be issued.
   J.   Transfer Of Location; Fee: Currently licensed vendors can move to an
available location during the license year by submitting a new application and
paying a business license transfer fee. All license conditions must be met for
the new location before a business license may be issued.
   K.   New Applications: Any individual applying for a sidewalk vendor license
after assignments have been made shall be assigned his or her choice of any
remaining locations, on a first come, first serve basis, for the remainder of
the three (3) year assignment period. All license conditions must be met by the
applicant before a business license may be issued. In the event that all
approved food or general vendor locations are assigned, new applications will
be marked with the time and date received and placed on the vendor waiting
list.
   L.   Assigned Locations Nontransferable: Locations assigned to sidewalk
vendors are nontransferable. (Eff. 1-14-2010)
POLICY 1797
CITY CONTRIBUTION TO EMPLOYEES' RETIREMENT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2015
SECTION:
1797-1: Reference
1797-2: Purpose
1797-3: Policy
1797-4: Eligibility
1797-1: REFERENCE:
Public employees' retirement act, Utah Code Annotated sections 49-12-409 and
49-13-408 et seq. (as amended). (Eff. 2-12-2015)
1797-2: PURPOSE:
To establish a policy for the purchase of retirement credit for employees
participating in the public employees' retirement plan(s), permitting a
nondiscriminatory participation standard for all eligible city employees. (Eff.
2-12-2015)
1797-3: POLICY:
Ogden City agrees to contribute a maximum of ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00)
for full time employees for the purchase of up to two (2) years of service
credit after accruing twenty eight (28) years of eligible service, pursuant to
the provisions of Utah Code Annotated sections 49-12-409 and 49-13-408 (as
amended). Contribution amounts will be limited to the actual number of years of
service needed to attain a full retirement with no actuarial reduction. Such
contribution shall not exceed ninety five percent (95%) of the total cost of
purchasing the retirement credit as determined by the Utah state retirement
office. (Eff. 2-12-2015)
1797-4: ELIGIBILITY:
In order to be eligible for the city contribution, the person retiring must
meet the following requirements:
   A.   At least four (4) years of city service;
   B.   At least twenty eight (28) years of eligible retirement service credit
(full or part time as required by the Utah state retirement office);
   C.   Be employed currently by Ogden City; and
   D.   Be employed currently in a position subject to reduction in force in
the following fiscal year.
Ogden City shall only contribute toward the purchase of that retirement service
credit necessary to permit the employee to meet the retirement eligibility
requirements under the public employees' contributory and noncontributory
retirement act with no actuarial reduction.
It is not the intent of this policy to restrict the city's contribution toward
the purchase of the retirement service credit to an employee of the city, not
defined as an eligible employee herein, as part of a settlement agreement
related to either an involuntary termination or a settlement of claims related
to employment, but in no event shall Ogden City's contribution under such
agreement exceed the amount that would otherwise be allowed under this policy,
if the employee were an eligible employee. (Eff. 2-12-2015)
POLICY 1798
USE OF AN EMERGENCY NOTIFICATION SYSTEM
SECTION:
1798-1: Purpose
1798-2: Policy
1798-3: Responsibilities
1798-4: Procedures
1798-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide information and guidelines to all
departments in regard to notifying residents of emergent and nonemergent events
that may impact them. Although there are many communication methods available,
this policy is directed at the phone based emergency notification system. The
emergency notification system works geographically. Those informed are based on
landlines assigned to the area as well as a voluntary cellphone registry to
that area. (Eff. 10-18-2013)
1798-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to take appropriate measures to keep
the public informed. This policy will provide guidance when utilizing the
emergency notification system to inform residents of applicable issues in their
neighborhood. Anticipated system uses include, but are not limited to:
disruptions in water service; street closures; lost individuals; etc. It is the
intent of this policy to incorporate other city policies affecting city
communications. This system may not be used for any advertising to endorse
specific entities or for any political purposes or gain. (Eff. 10-18-2013)
1798-3: RESPONSIBILITIES:
If a need arises to notify the public, it is the responsibility of each
department and/or division to determine which communication method would best
serve its purpose. The request to use the emergency notification system will be
made by a division manager or above, except in the case of an emergency (see
below). Final approval for nonemergent use shall be by the mayor or designee.
Weber area consolidated dispatch, Ogden City emergency management, and Weber
County emergency management are authorized to access the system for
notification. (Eff. 10-18-2013)
1798-4: PROCEDURES:
When a division manager decides to utilize the emergency notification system
for a planned event or dissemination of nonemergency information, he or she
shall fill out an "emergency notification request" form (this form can be found
on the Ogden City intranet site at: http://insider/cityforms.html) and send it
electronically to the emergency manager and the fire department administrative
assistant. If the emergency manager is unavailable the administrative assistant
will forward the request to Weber County emergency management or to Weber area
consolidated dispatch. The requestor will have the option to record his or her
own voice message or have it entered into text by emergency management.
In the event of an emergency requiring immediate notification, the OPD duty
lieutenant or OFD battalion chief or designee may immediately contact Weber
area consolidated dispatch to initiate the notification. (Eff. 10-18-2013)
POLICY 1799
ELECTRONIC MEETINGS
SECTION:
1799-1: Purpose
1799-2: Policy
1799-3: Procedure
1799-4: Adoption
1799-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide uniform guidelines to all boards,
commissions and committees regarding the process to hold an electronic meeting.
(Eff. 12-9-2015)
1799-2: POLICY:
Section
3-2-1 of the Ogden municipal code outlines the general rules for boards,
commissions and committees, and stipulates such committees are subject to the
provisions of the Utah open and public meetings act, which permits meetings to
be held electronically in accordance with specified notice provisions.
It shall be the policy of Ogden City Corporation that boards, commissions and
committees may conduct their meetings electronically, in accordance with the
Utah open and public meetings act and this administrative policy. (Eff. 12-9-
2015)
1799-3: PROCEDURE:
Pursuant to Utah Code Annotated section 52-4-207, members of a public body may
participate telephonically or electronically according to the following
provisions:
   A.   If one or more members will participate electronically or
telephonically, public notice of the meeting shall so indicate. In addition the
notice shall specify the anchor location where any members not participating
electronically or telephonically will be meeting and where interested persons
and the public may attend, monitor, and participate in the open portions of the
meeting.
   B.   Notice of the meeting shall be posted at the anchor location and as
further required under Utah Code Annotated section 52-4-202.
   C.   Notice of the possibility of an electronic meeting shall be given to
the members at least twenty four (24) hours before the meeting. In addition,
the notice shall describe how a member may participate in the meeting
electronically or telephonically.
   D.   When notice is given of the possibility of a member appearing
electronically or telephonically, any member may do so and shall be counted as
present for the purposes of a quorum and may fully participate and vote on any
matter coming before the body. At the commencement of the meeting, or at such a
time as any member initially appears electronically or telephonically, the
chair shall identify for the record all those who are appearing telephonically
or electronically. Votes by members who are not at the physical location of the
meeting shall be confirmed by the chair.
   E.   The anchor location, unless otherwise designated in the electronic
meeting notice, shall be the location indicated in the annual meeting schedule
for which public notice has been given in accordance with the Utah open and
public meetings law, Utah Code Annotated title 52, chapter 4, as amended. The
anchor location is the physical location from which the electronic meeting
originates or from where the participants are connected. In addition, the
anchor location shall have space and facilities so that interested persons and
the public may attend, monitor, and participate in the open portions of the
meeting. (Eff. 12-9-2015)
1799-4: ADOPTION:
Any board, commission or committee desiring to conduct an electronic meeting
shall, at a public meeting, adopt the provisions of this administrative policy.
Thereafter, the body may hold electronic meetings in accordance with this
policy and Utah law. (Eff. 12-9-2015)
TITLE 9
RECORDS MANAGEMENT
POLICY 1800
BUSINESS CONFIDENTIALITY CLAIMS WITH REGARD TO RECORDS
SECTION:
1800-1: Purpose
1800-2: Policy
1800-3: Procedure
1800-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide uniform guidelines to all departments
regarding records received from individuals who claim business confidentiality.
(Eff. 3-14-2007)
1800-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation that any person(s) who provides
records to the city that he/she believes should be protected under subsection
63-2-304 of the government records access and management act (GRAMA) shall
provide a written claim of business confidentiality, which claim shall include
a concise statement of reasons supporting the claim of business
confidentiality. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1800-3: PROCEDURE:
   A.   When a person(s) presents a record(s) to the city that he/she believes
should be protected, a business confidentiality claim form is to be completed.
The department director and legal department will review each record and claim,
and notify the person(s) of the classification given to the record(s). This
will be accomplished by completing the administrative review and determination
section of the form.
   B.   If the record is originally classified as public and is later
reclassified as private, the provider of the record shall also be notified. The
notification is to be given by completing the notice of reclassification
section of the form.
   C.   If the record(s) is classified private or protected as requested and
the department director and legal department determine there is no interest in
restricting access to the record(s), or that the interests favoring access
outweigh the interest favoring restriction of access, the record may be
disclosed under the provisions of subsection 63-2-302(2) of GRAMA for private
records and under the provisions of subsection 63-2-304 of GRAMA for protected
records. Refer also to the provisions of section
4-5-15 of the Ogden municipal code.
   D.   The requestor may appeal any decision to classify a record as public.
The same appeal procedure is to be followed as for other appeals to the records
review board (see policy regarding appeals). The subject record may not be
disclosed until the thirty (30) day period in which to file an appeal expires,
or until the end of the appeals process if an appeal is filed, including a
judicial appeal, unless the claimant, after notice, has waived the claim by not
appealing or intervening before the appeals body.
   E.   A copy of the business confidentiality form is to be filed with the
record, where it will remain at all times and will be given the same retention
schedule as the record. A copy of the form will be returned to the requestor
after the administrative determination is made. A third copy will be forwarded
to the city recorder as notification of a potential hearing.
   F.   The city recorder will maintain the duplicate copy for thirty (30) days
and then destroy it. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1810
DENIAL OF REQUESTS FOR RECORDS
SECTION:
1810-1: Purpose
1810-2: Policy
1810-3: Procedure
1810-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide uniform guidelines to all departments
regarding denials of requests received for records. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1810-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation that the city shall provide a notice
of denial to a requestor when a request for records is denied either in whole
or in part. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1810-3: PROCEDURE:
   A.   The city recorder in conjunction with the legal department will review
each written request for records form to determine if the record(s) requested
are classified public, private, controlled or protected (see compliance with
the government records and access management act policy for definitions and
guidelines).
   B.   When a verbal request is received and the records officer determines
that access is denied, the requestor must then complete a request for records
form to provide documentation that the request was received and to begin the
denial and appeal process.
   C.   Upon determination that a requested record, or portions of a record, is
not public, a records request denial form will be completed. The original will
be mailed to the requestor; a copy will be provided to the legal department;
and a copy will be maintained by the city recorder as notification of a
possible appeal. The requestor has thirty (30) days from the date of denial to
file an appeal with the city recorder. (See policy 1870, "Appeal Process For
Denial Of Request For Records", of this title.)
   D.   The city recorder will maintain a copy of the records request denial
forms for one year following final action and then destroy it, unless an appeal
is filed. If an appeal is filed within thirty (30) days, the copy of the denial
form will be maintained with the appeal file in the city recorder's office for
documentation to be given to the records appeal board. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1820
REQUESTS FOR RECORDS
SECTION:
1820-1: Purpose
1820-2: Policy
1820-3: Procedure
1820-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide uniform guidelines to all departments
regarding requests received for records. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1820-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to require completion of a written
request form when the city is unable to provide a record immediately upon
receipt of a verbal request from an individual; or if there is a question as
classification of the requested record. Upon receipt of the written request,
the city has ten (10) working days to respond to the request, or five (5)
working days if it is an expedited request. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1820-3: PROCEDURE:
   A.   Upon receipt of a verbal request for a record by an individual, the
city recorder or department receiving the request can provide the
documentation. Notation of the records request and response should be
documented in a GRAMA log maintained for said purpose.
   B.   If the city recorder or department records officer determines the
requested record is not readily available or in case of question as to
appropriate classification of the record, the requestor must fill out a request
for records form. If the request is made through a department, the requestor
should either be directed or documentation should be provided to the city
recorder's office for official filing. Upon receipt of a request for records,
the city recorder's office will note the date and time the request is received
on the form. The date of receipt determines the deadline date for providing the
requested record.
   C.   The city recorder and legal department will determine whether the
requested record is classified public, private, controlled or protected. (See
policy
1850, "Compliance With Government Records Access And Management Act (GRAMA)",
of this title for definitions and guidelines.)
   D.   Upon identification of the record classification, the city recorder and
legal department determine whether the request can be granted. The city
recorder completes and signs the request for records and provides the
appropriate notification to the requestor. (See also policy
1810, "Denial Of Requests For Records" and policy 1830, "Notice Of Extended
Time For Response To Records Requests", of this title.) The city recorder
maintains the original request form. A copy of the request is returned to the
requestor with the requested records.
If a request is denied, a records request denial form (see policy
1810, "Denial Of Requests For Records", of this title) is completed and a copy
of the request for records form is returned to the requestor.
   F.   The city recorder will maintain the original request for records form
for one year following final action, after which time it may be destroyed.
(Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1830
NOTICE OF EXTENDED TIME FOR RESPONSE TO RECORDS REQUESTS
SECTION:
1830-1: Purpose
1830-2: Policy
1830-3: Procedure
1830-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide uniform guidelines to all departments
regarding notice to be given when extended time is required to provide
requested records due to extraordinary circumstances. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1830-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation that a notice of extended time for
response to records request will be given to the requestor if the city is
unable to comply with a request for records in the required time limits due to
extraordinary circumstances. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1830-3: PROCEDURE:
   A.   After receipt of a request for records form and identification of the
record classification, the city recorder will determine the time required to
provide the requested record. If the time required to fill the request exceeds
the ten (10) day time limit for response, the city recorder will complete a
notice of extended time for response to records request form indicating the
reason for the delay. The original notice of extended time will be provided to
the requestor. The city recorder will maintain a copy of the original request
for records, as notification of a possible appeal.
   B.   The city recorder will maintain the copy of the notice of extended time
for response to records request form for one year following final action,
unless an appeal is filed. If an appeal is filed within thirty (30) days, the
copy will be maintained with the appeal file for documentation to the records
appeal board. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1850
COMPLIANCE WITH GOVERNMENT RECORDS ACCESS AND MANAGEMENT ACT (GRAMA)
SECTION:
1850-1: Purpose
1850-2: Policy
1850-3: Procedure
1850-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to ensure uniform compliance by all departments
with the government records access and management act (GRAMA), chapter 2 of
title 63 of the Utah Code Annotated (1953), and the Ogden City municipal code
which establish policies and guidelines for retention, maintenance and access
of Ogden City records in accordance with GRAMA. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1850-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation that every person has the right to
see, review, examine and take a copy of all public records of the city during
normal working hours upon payment of a lawful fee and pursuant to the
provisions of GRAMA. All records of the city are public unless otherwise
expressly provided by the act. Definitions provided in the act will apply to
Ogden City. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1850-3: PROCEDURE:
   A.   City departments are encouraged to schedule only those unique records
series that are not covered in the general retention schedule. Also,
notification of classification can now be done directly without first
scheduling the record series. GRAMA outlines the records that can be included
in each classification, which is helpful in completing the classification
worksheets.
   B.   City departments will work with the city recorder, as the city's
contact with the Utah state archives, to compile and forward the required
classification report for the city to the Utah state archives.
   C.   These classification worksheets will be the tool used by the city
recorder and legal department when determining whether or not a requested
record should be released, as the appropriate sections of GRAMA or other
statutes justifying the classification have already been determined. (Eff. 3-
14-2007)
POLICY 1851
GUIDANCE ON REASONABLE FEE FOR FILLING GRAMA REQUESTS
SECTION:
1851-1: Purpose
1851-2: Policy
1851-3: Guidance
1851-1: PURPOSE:
Ogden City ordinance sections
4-5-8 and
4-6-1 and Utah Code Annotated section 63-2-203 authorize the city to charge a
reasonable fee to cover the city's actual cost of compiling a record in a form
other than that maintained by the city. Given the variety of records requests,
it would be difficult to establish a standard fee that would cover the city's
actual costs of filling such requests. The purpose of this policy is to provide
uniform guidelines to all departments to assist the city recorder in
establishing reasonable fees consistent with Utah law. (Eff. 3-4-2008)
1851-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation to charge a reasonable fee to cover
the city's actual cost of compiling a record in a form other than that
maintained by the city consistent with Utah law. (Eff. 3-4-2008)
1851-3: GUIDANCE:
   A.   If the city recorder or department records officer determines that a
request has been made for a record in a form other than that maintained by the
city, the requester must fill out a request for records form. If the request is
made through a department, the requester should either be directed or
documentation should be provided to the city recorder's office for official
filing.
   B.   At the time of the request, or as soon thereafter as practicable, the
city recorder shall notify the requester that the city will be charging a fee
to cover the actual cost of compiling the record, and shall provide the
requester with the opportunity to preauthorize the charge up to twenty five
dollars ($25.00). If appropriate, the city shall allow the requester an
opportunity to avoid the fee by searching for and retrieving the documents
without the city's assistance.
   C.   When practicable, the request shall be filled by the lowest paid
employee who has the necessary skill and training to fill the request.
   D.   The city recorder or department records officer shall keep track of the
following:
      1.   The staff time incurred for compiling, formatting, manipulating,
packaging, summarizing, or tailoring the record either into an organization or
media to meet the person's request;
      2.   The staff time incurred for search, retrieval, and other direct
administrative time incurred for complying with a request; and
      3.   In the case of fees for a record that is the result of computer
output other than word processing, the actual incremental staff time incurred
in providing the electronic services and products together with a reasonable
portion of the staff time associated with formatting or interfacing the
information for particular users, and the administrative time as set forth in
subsections D1 and D2 of this section or its successor.
The department records officer shall inform the city recorder of the time
expended as set forth above, and the staff person or persons filling the
request.
   E.   Any employee time spent for the following shall be excluded from the
fee calculation:
      1.   Reviewing a record to determine whether it is subject to disclosure;
or
      2.   Inspecting a record.
   F.   The city recorder shall establish a reasonable fee based on the time
expended, using the following employee categories and associated salaries as a
guideline:
 
Administrative/clerical staff         $12.50
Professional/technical staff          15.00
Division manager/assistant managers   18.50
Department directors/deputy directors 28.00
Other                                 59.50
 
   G.   An hourly charge for an employee's time pursuant to this section may
not exceed the salary of the lowest paid employee who, in the discretion of the
city recorder, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.
   H.   When calculating the fee, no charge shall be made for the first quarter
of an hour of the employee's time.
   I.   Where circumstances require the city to employ an independent
contractor to retrieve or compile requested information due to the
unavailability of a city employee to perform the request, the actual hourly
rate charged by the contractor to the city will be charged to the requesting
party.
   J.   The city recorder will indicate the fee on the request form and provide
the appropriate notification to the requester.
   K.   Certain exceptions may apply pursuant to city ordinance section
4-5-8.
   L.   This policy shall be implemented consistent with applicable city
ordinances and policies and Utah law. (Eff. 3-4-2008)
POLICY 1860
CERTIFICATION OF DOCUMENTS
SECTION:
1860-1: Purpose
1860-2: Policy
1860-3: Procedure
1860-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide uniform guidelines to all departments
regarding certification of documents. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1860-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation that certified copies of original
documents on file within city departments may be provided upon request subject
to: a) the classification of the requested record having been verified to
ensure the record qualifies to be released; and b) payment of the required
fees. Department directors must authorize department employees who are
qualified to certify copies of original documents on file in their department.
(Eff. 3-14-2007)
1860-3: PROCEDURE:
   A.   The requestor must complete a request for certified copy form. The
authorized department employee must verify that: 1) the classification of the
record was checked to ensure the record qualifies to be released; and 2) the
document on file in the department is the original document, as certification
can only be done on original documents maintained by that department.
   B.   The authorized employee certifying a document is to complete the fee
section on the request for certified copy form indicating the amount of the fee
to be charged for copying and certifying the copy of the document (see title 4
of the Ogden municipal code for the fee schedule and subsequent amount to be
charged). A copy of the request for certified copy form will be attached to the
certified copy of the document and given to the requestor.
   C.   The certification statement will read as follows:
I  (Name) , do hereby certify that the foregoing document, namely:  (Complete
description of the document)  is a true and exact copy of the original on file
in the (office/department/division), of the City of Ogden, County of Weber,
State of Utah.

(Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1870
APPEAL PROCESS FOR DENIAL OF REQUEST FOR RECORDS
SECTION:
1870-1: Purpose
1870-2: Policy
1870-3: Procedure
1870-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide uniform guidelines for filing of
appeals for denials of requests for records. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1870-2: POLICY:
It is the policy of Ogden City Corporation that persons aggrieved by the city's
classification or designation of a record, or of an access decision or by a
response to a record request may appeal the determination to the records review
board in accordance with the provisions of section
4-5-25 of the Ogden municipal code. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1870-3: PROCEDURE:
   A.   Upon receipt of a records request notice of denial from the city
recorder, a person may appeal such denial to the Ogden City records review
board.
   B.   The appellant shall complete the notice of appeal section on the
records request notice of denial form, and submit the form to the Ogden City
recorder within thirty (30) calendar days of the date of the denial, either by
mail or in person. The notice of appeal may include a short statement of facts,
reasons, and legal authority in support of the appeal.
   C.   No later than three (3) business days from receipt of a notice of
appeal, the city recorder will schedule a hearing before the records review
board to be held no sooner than fifteen (15) days and no later than thirty (30)
days from the date of the appeal filing.
   D.   The records review board will make a determination of any appeal within
five (5) business days after the hearing, and shall issue a signed order
whether granting the petition, in whole or in part, or upholding the initial
determination by the city. The order of the records review board will include
the following: 1) a statement of reasons for the decision; 2) a description of
the record or portions of the record to which access was ordered or denied,
provided that the description does not disclose private, controlled, or
protected information; 3) a statement that any party to the appeal may appeal
the decision of the records review board to district court within thirty (30)
days after the date of the order; and 4) a brief summary of the appeal and a
notice that, in order to protect its right on appeal, the party may wish to
seek advice from an attorney.
   E.   Appeals to the final decision of the records review board can be made
to the district court. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
POLICY 1880
INTERDEPARTMENTAL ACCESS TO PRIVATE, PROTECTED OR CONTROLLED RECORDS FOR LAW
ENFORCEMENT PURPOSES
SECTION:
1880-1: Purpose
1880-2: Policy
1880-3: Guidelines
1880-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of this policy is to provide guidelines for interdepartmental
access to private, protected or controlled records kept by the city for "law
enforcement purposes". (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1880-2: POLICY:
The city maintains various records within the city that are classified as
private, protected or controlled records under the government records access
and management act (GRAMA). In addition to the purposes of the department or
division originating such records, it is the policy of the city that such
records should also be available to the Ogden police department and other city
departments, divisions, officers and employees responsible for enforcing,
litigating or investigating civil, criminal or administrative law, including
violations or requirements under city ordinance. The provisions of this policy
are not intended to apply to personal health information, the disclosure of
which is governed by HIPAA. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1880-3: GUIDELINES:
   A.   Except as provided in subsection F of this section, the Ogden police
department and other city departments, divisions, officers or employees may be
provided access to the private, protected or controlled records of the city
maintained in another department or division of the city for the following
purposes:
      1.   Identifying and locating persons suspected, charged or convicted of
violating city ordinances and other provisions of local, state or federal law;
      2.   Determining compliance with the requirements of city ordinance,
state or federal law, any city license or permit, or city policies or
procedures; or
      3.   Otherwise enforcing, litigating or investigating violations of city
ordinances and other provisions of local, state or federal law. (Hereinafter
referred to as "law enforcement purpose".)
   B.   Whenever OPD or other city departments, divisions, officers or
employees are provided access to private, protected or controlled records
maintained by another department or division within the city for law
enforcement purposes, the recipient of the record should be informed of the
record's classification as a private, protected or controlled record and the
accompanying restrictions on access.
   C.   If access is being provided through a direct or continued sharing of
data maintained in the city's data processing files, the city's information
technology (IT) division shall be responsible for implementing the guidelines
contained in this policy.
   D.   The legal department shall assist IT and the department or division
originating the record with identifying applicable restrictions on access.
   E.   Nothing contained in this policy should be construed as imposing
additional or more restrictive requirements than contained in the government
records access and management act.
   F.   Personal health information kept or maintained in the records of the
city shall not be disclosed or otherwise accessed under the provisions of this
policy. Any disclosure of personal health information shall be governed by the
provisions of HIPAA. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
TITLE 10
PUBLIC SERVICES
POLICY 1900
ARBORICULTURAL REGULATIONS
SECTION:
1900-1: Purpose
1900-2: Policy
1900-3: Definitions
1900-4: Tree And Shrub Specifications
1900-5: Prohibited And Permitted Tree Species
1900-6: Proper Planting Specifications
1900-7: Standard Methods Of Tree Care
1900-1: PURPOSE:
The purpose of these regulations is to implement the provisions of subsection
6-2-5A of the Ogden municipal code authorizing the adoption of arboricultural
regulations concerning park trees and street trees, as defined below.
Specifically, these regulations are intended to accomplish the following:
   A.   Prohibit the planting and growing of the type or kind of trees prone to
disease and insects or injurious to sidewalks and curbs and designates such
types and kinds of trees and shrubs permitted to be planted hereafter as park
trees and street trees.
   B.   Provide a plan of proper planting and growth of trees for the
beautification of streets in Ogden that allows implementation of any existing
or future street tree plan as adopted by the council as part of the Ogden City
general plan.
   C.   Protect trees from improper care by establishing the standard methods
of tree care for park trees and street trees including guidelines for trimming,
spraying, removal, planting and pruning.
   D.   Prevent trees on city or private property from becoming a public
nuisance. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1900-2: POLICY:
Any and all work performed on street trees or park trees shall comply with
Ogden City's urban forestry ordinances (title 6, chapter 2 of the Ogden
municipal code) and these Ogden City arboricultural regulations.
   A.   Modified; Amended; Extended: These arboricultural regulations may be
modified, amended, or extended in accordance with section
6-2-5 of the Ogden municipal code, at any time that experience, new research,
technology or laws indicate improved methods or circumstances make it
advisable.
   B.   Regulations To Be Reviewed: The urban forester, in conjunction with the
Ogden City urban forestry advisory committee, should review these
arboricultural regulations once every two (2) years in order to update the
methods, procedures, species, cultivars and varieties included in this policy.
Upon review, circumstances indicating a need for change should determine
addition of methods, procedures, species, cultivars and varieties of proven
dependability and value, or removal of obsolete, improper and unsatisfactory
information.
   C.   Urban Forest Management Plan: In the event that the Ogden City urban
forest management plan dictates that individual street blocks are assigned one
or more particular species or varieties of trees, only those trees shall be
planted subject to revision of said plan.
   D.   Public Nuisance: The owner or occupant will correct trees located on
private property declared a public nuisance, under the criteria defined in
section
6-2-10 of the Ogden municipal code.
   E.   General: All work herein described shall be conducted in such a manner
as to cause the least possible interference with or annoyance to others.
      1.   Inadequately or improperly trained personnel shall not be utilized
for work on or with city trees beyond their known capacity or ability to
perform properly or safely.
      2.   Pedestrian and vehicular traffic shall be allowed to pass through
the work areas only under conditions of safety and with as little inconvenience
and delay as possible.
      3.   Adequate barricades and warning devices shall be placed and flagmen
shall be stationed as necessary for the safety of persons and vehicles in
accordance with the "Manual On Uniform Traffic Control Devices".
      4.   It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the private
business of planting, cutting, trimming, pruning, removing, spraying or
otherwise treating city trees, shrubs or plants within the city without first
procuring a business license and a tree permit from the city.
   F.   Cabling And Bracing: Cabling and bracing will only be done when no
other arboricultural practice is a viable solution to the individual tree's
situation. In the case where cabling is an effective method of treatment, it
will only be done on trees of high community value. If the urban forester
recommends cabling, the cabling/bracing operation will only be conducted by
Ogden City forestry personnel or qualified certified arborist. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1900-3: DEFINITIONS:
The following definitions shall apply to these arboricultural regulations:
MAINTENANCE: Those practices and procedures for the normal care of trees and
shrubs as set forth in the arboricultural regulations of the city.
OGDEN URBAN FORESTRY ADVISORY COMMITTEE: The Ogden urban forestry advisory
committee as established in title 3, chapter 23 of the Ogden municipal code.
PARK TREES: Trees, shrubs, bushes and any other woody vegetation located on
city parks or other property belonging to the city, other than streets.
PARKING OR PARKING STRIP: That part of the public street right of way set aside
as a planting strip or open space and located between the sidewalk and curb or
edge of the roadway, or where no sidewalk exists, located within the ten feet
(10') adjacent to the edge of the roadway.
PARKS DIVISION: The division responsible for city parks, which is currently the
parks and cemetery division of the public services department.
PERSON: Individuals, firms, corporations, partnerships and every type of
association.
STREET: Includes any street, avenue, highway, alley or other public
thoroughfare, including the entire width from property line to property line.
STREET TREES: Trees, shrubs, bushes and any other woody vegetation located in
any parking or parking strip.
URBAN FORESTER: The official designated by the community services director to
enforce the provisions of title 6, chapter 2 of the Ogden municipal code and
these arboricultural regulations. (Eff. 3-14-2007)
1900-4: TREE AND SHRUB SPECIFICATIONS:
Unless otherwise specified or approved by the urban forester, all tree species,
cultivars and varieties will conform to American Association of Nurserymen
Standards in size and quality.
   A.   Size: Tree diameter (caliper) shall be measured as it stands in a
natural position, six inches (6") above the appropriate soil line for that
species. Stock used on city property shall meet the minimum and maximum sizes
specified. Larger sizes may be required to ensure survival, provide a designed
landscape effect or produce a desired aesthetic quality in accordance with
certain city ordinances, regulations, or planning pertaining to property
development and/or zoning. However, large trees and plants that have been cut
back in order to achieve specified sizes will not be accepted.
The following are the approved minimum sizes of tree stock to be planted on
city property.
 
Shade tree (residential)     11/2 inches – 21/2 inches
Shade tree (commercial)      2 inches – 21/2 inches
Ornamental trees             15 – 20 gallon containers
Evergreen trees (commercial) 5 feet – 6 feet in height
Shrubs                       5 gallon container
 
   B.   Quality:
      1.   All trees and shrubs shall be of standard quality as set forth by
the American Association of Nurserymen Standards and shall be true to their
names, types and typical of their species, cultivars or varieties. All
publications are available at the Ogden City public ways and parks office,
located at 1875 Monroe Boulevard, upon request.
      2.   All trees and shrubs shall have normal, well developed branches that
exhibit vigorous shoot and bud development. They shall be sound, healthy,
vigorous plants free from defects, disfigurements, knots, cankers, mechanical
or biological abrasions of the bark, sunscald, disease, insects, and all other
forms of infections or objectionable disfigurements. Roots shall be established
but not root bound, they shall be normal, healthy, vigorous systems free from
extensive damage, drying or abnormalities. All plants will be nursery grown
stock unless otherwise specified or approved by the urban forester and shall
have been lifted the fall or winter prior to the planting season.
      3.   All balled and burlapped plants shall have a solid ball of earth of
adequate specified size held in place securely. Ball will be confined securely
with wrapped burlap and tightly bound with twine or rope. The burlap ball shall
be encompassed by a firm wire basket designed for the size and shape of the
ball. Broken, loose, damaged or manufactured balls will be rejected.
      4.   Containerized plants should not be root bound in their containers.
Roots that circle the container can become strangulated roots and hinder future
growth of the plant. Extensive roots that have grown out through the drain
ports of the container may be dried or damaged and become a source for
infection and additional stress for the plant. Any or all abnormalities listed
above shall be reason for rejection.
      5.   Bare root plants shall have abundant root growth, fibrous and
numerous small roots with good color and moisture. Kinked, circling roots or
mechanical/biological abrasions of the roots shall be reason for rejection.
(Eff. 3-14-2007)
